Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 16 Benefits Administration User Guide

Intended Audience This guide is intended for users involved in benefits administration. Unless you have permission to access system-level features, you cannot set up global benefit plans. Before using this guide, you must set up all files, preferences, and information required for system and client administration. This guide assumes that you have some background knowledge of benefits administration and processing.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 17 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans When you set up benefit plans, you create sets of benefits for groups or categories of employees. In general, a group benefit plan contains: • States that offer the plan • Covered plan types (also called tiers) • Premium rates • Billing rates Before you define the benefit plans, you must define the group benefit plan types. You set up group benefit plans at the system level, but you can also administer them at the client level.

Defining Types of Group Benefit Plans Group benefit plans can cover more than one employee coverage situation. For example, an organization can use a benefit plan for single employees, employees who have one child, or employees with large families. Each situation is defined by a group benefit plan type (also called a tier). Each group benefit plan specifies the plan types it covers.

Before defining group benefit plans: l Use the Group Benefit Plan Types form to define the types of group benefit plans.

To define group benefit plan types: 1. Open the Group Benefit Plan Types form.

   Use this option                              To define this
   Type Code                                    The code representing the benefit plan type (for example, ES).
                                                You cannot enter a zero in the Type Code field on the Group
                                                Benefit Plan Types form. If you do, you will get an error
                                                message: Invalid Type Code. Click OK. The zero will be removed
                                                from the Type Code field.

To delete a group benefit plan type: Click Delete to delete the selected Type Code.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 19 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

Note: If an existing Type Code is tied to any of the following, then you cannot delete it. The system displays an error message: There are records associated with (Plan Type). Code cannot be deleted:

l   The Type Code field under the Plan Types section on the Group Benefit Plans form.
l   An Effective Date field set up for the Plan Type on the Billing Rates or Premium Rates forms.
l   The Plan Type field under the Contribution Rules section on the Benefit Rules form.
l   The Plan type field under the Coverage Details section on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form.

Maintaining Group Benefit Plans Use the Group Benefit Plans form to create and maintain group benefit insurance plans.

Actions You can access benefit-related features and settings using the Actions menu : • Audit • Benefits Enrollment Plan Detail: Refer to Benefits Enrollment User Guide • Billing Rates • Clients Assigned To • Copy Benefit Plan • Eligible ZIP Codes • Enrollment Details • Network ZIP Codes: see Setting Benefit Network Locations on page 121 • Payees (refer to the payroll user guides) • Premium Rates

Establishing Basic Parameters for Group Benefit Plans To establish the basic parameters of a group benefit plan, use the Group Benefit Plans panel.

To establish the basic parameters: 1. Open the Group Benefit Plans panel and complete the following:

Use this To define this option Benefit Plan ID A short description of a new or existing benefit plan Plan A more detailed description of the benefit plan. Description

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

Plan The plan description in Spanish. Description (Spanish) Insurance The type of coverage the plan provides (for example, Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Class Insurance, Long-Term Disability). This setting determines which panels open, what fields are available, and the calculation method the system uses to derive the premium for the benefit plan. See Insurance class panels on page 25. Payee ID The ID of the benefits provider that receives the deducted amounts. If you need to define a new payee for this benefit provider, open the Actions menu and select Payees. Auto Enroll Whether the employee can waive the benefit during an enrollment. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) This option must be used with other settings in the system. For more information, see “Setting Up Waive Options” in the Benefits Enrollment User Guide. Auto Enroll One of the following options: • No: The employee has the option to waive coverage in the benefit plan. • Yes: The employee automatically enrolls in the benefit plan and does not have the option to waive coverage. • Company Decision: The system determines the employee waive option based upon settings at the client level. COBRA Whether the benefit plan can be elected for COBRA coverage. Electable 3rd Party Enable this field to allow plans to be flagged when COBRA administration is COBRA handled by third party. State Specify a U.S. state or territory for state continuation of coverage or mini-COBRA Continuation offerings within the Benefit Plan. In PrismHR, this field is for informational purposes only. Marketplace partners retrieve this data from the PrismHR API and use it for state continuation or mini-COBRA offerings through their services.

                 Note: If you set a state in the State Continuation field, we recommend also
                 checking the COBRA Electable option located directly above the State
                 Continuation field. This ensures coordination with federal continuation, where
                 applicable.

Carrier Set this option if the service provider is responsible for updating carrier eligibility Eligibility information such as enrollments, terms, coverage modifications, or other changes Management which may affect carrier eligibility. Once you flag the plans, you can use this information to create a report in Report Center showing a list of plans where the Carrier Eligibility Management option is set.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 21 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

High Whether the benefit plan has a high deductible that may entitle the employee to Deductible participate in a health savings account (HSA). Plan Single Whether the benefit plan is employee-only. When this option is selected, the Coverage employee contribution must be defined as a percentage of the employee’s Gross Wages earnings when the employee contribution rules are set up in the Benefit Rules % form. This option must be enabled in System Parameters with the custom feature code SHOWSINGLEGROSSWAGE. Allow Gross Select this option to set the Percent of Gross Wages as the employee contribution Wage % towards a medical plan (employee premium only). Selecting this option displays a Contribution grid where you can enter an Effective Date and a Percent of Gross Wages, which Method is used as a default setting.

                 Note: To select the Allow Gross Wage % Contribution Method option you must
                 deselect the following options:

                 •     Single Coverage Gross Wage %
                 •     Do NOT Include In ACA Reporting
                 Additionally, you can select this option only if the Cost Basis field is set to either
                 Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly.

PEO Master Whether the Group Benefit Plan is one of the PEO’s Master Benefit Plans. Plan Client Whether the benefit plan is client-sponsored. Sponsored Rate Groups Whether premium rates are maintained separately for each rate group. For Premium Rates Offer Type Select the offer type that classifies the benefit plan. This ensures that the plan displays in the correct form in enrollment workflows. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) The Offer Type field only displays the list of compatible options based on the selection made for the Insurance Class field on this form. When you select an offer type other than Voluntary, the Insurance Class field is automatically assigned to the corresponding insurance class without any manual intervention.

                 Note: Offer Type is now a required field. The system displays a warning in the

Configuring Age Parameters To establish the age parameters in which a group benefit plan is offered, use the Age Parameters panel on the Group Benefit Plans form.

To configure the age parameters in which a plan is offered: 1. Open the Age Parameters panel.

Use this option To define this Age Calculation (Month/Day) • The Age Calculation Month method used to calculate

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 40 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

Use this option To define this employees’ age for insurance premium calculations. • The Age Calculation Day on which employees’ insurance premium ages are based. The drop-down field only displays when you select a valid month (January- December). Dependent’s Age Limit The age at which the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage. If the dependent reaches that age limit before the plan effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage. The selected value determines when the dependent age limit becomes effective: • On Date of Birth (DOB): The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on the dependent’s birth date when the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 6, 2017. If this date falls before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll. • End of DOB Year: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on January 1st of the year the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on January 1, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll. Therefore, the dependent is longer eligible for coverage in the benefit plan even though the dependent’s actual age has not yet reached the age limit specified. • End of DOB month: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective at the end of the month the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25 and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll. If the plan effective date falls before the date the dependent’s age limit becomes effective. For example, if the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30,

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 41 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

Setting Up Wellness Benefit Plans Some clients offer wellness benefits for employees. Wellness benefits can improve and motivate healthy behaviors in your employees while reducing their health care costs. Before approving employees for lower wellness benefit plan rates, they must pass a wellness assessment. In PrismHR, you can: 1. Define a medical benefit plan as wellness banded. 2. Enter the billing and premium rates. 3. Manage employee wellness statuses in bulk, or per employee. For more information, see Changing the Wellness Status for Multiple Employees or Changing an Employee’s Wellness Status. 4. View employee wellness status history. For more information, see Viewing an Employee’s Wellness Status History.

Defining a Wellness Banded Benefit Plan First, you must define a benefit plan as wellness banded on the Group Benefit Plans form. You can only define a Medical (MED) benefit plan as wellness banded.

To define a benefit plan as wellness banded: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Group Benefit Plans. The Group Benefit Plans form opens. 3. In Offer Type, select Medical (MED). 4. In the Other Processing Parameters panel, complete the following:

 Use this option...                         To do this...
 Wellness Banded Rates                      Define the medical benefit plan as wellness banded. The Use
                                            Wellness Rates as Default and Assessment due fields display.
                                            When enabling the Wellness Banded Rates option, the system
                                            disables the following options:
                                                •   Family Rated Premiums
                                                •   Tobacco Banded Rates
                                                •   Gender Banded Rates
                                            If these options are enabled on a benefit plan, the system shows a
                                            confirmation dialog box indicating that they reset when enabling

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 56 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

 Use this option...                         To do this...
                                            Wellness Banded Rates.
 Use Wellness Rates as Default              Set the wellness banded rates as the default for the benefit plan.
 Assessment due                             Define the days or months before or after the open enrollment
                                            effective date when the wellness assessment is due.
  1. Click Save.

Entering Billing Rates After defining a benefit plan as wellness banded, enter the billing rates on the Billing Rates form. For more information, see the following: • Setting Health Plan Billing Rates by Rate Group • Setting Health Plan Billing Rates by Rate Group and Age

Entering Premium Rates After defining a benefit plan as wellness banded, enter the premium rates on the Premium Rates form. For information, see the following: • Setting Health Plan Premium Rates • Setting Premium Rates Based on Rate Group • Setting Premium Rates Based on Network

Changing the Wellness Status for Multiple Employees To manage the wellness status for multiple employees, use the Bulk Change Wellness Status form.

To improve the response time for loading results, you can filter the results with the following criteria: • Control Group • Clients • Plans • Qualify Click Continue. Approving Assessments On the Employee Details form Personal tab, approving assessments: • Changes the employee qualification status to Qualifies • Updates the completion date • Sets the effective date of the change

To approve employee assessments: 1. While holding the Ctrl key, select multiple employees from the list. 2. Click Approve Assessments. The Approve Assessments dialog box displays. 3. In Assessment Completion Date, select a date to mark the employee assessment complete. 4. In Effective Date for Status Change, select a date for the employees’ enrollment in the wellness benefits plan to take effect. The effective date affects employee rates. 5. Click Continue. Declining Assessments On the Employee Details form Personal tab, declining assessments: • Changes the employee qualification status to Does Not Qualify • Updates the completion date • Sets the effective date of the change

To decline employee assessments: 1. While holding the Ctrl key, select multiple employees from the list. 2. Click Decline Assessments. The Decline Assessments dialog box displays. 3. In Assessment Completion Date, select a date to mark the employee assessment complete. 4. In Effective Date for Status Change, select a date for the employees’ enrollment in the wellness benefits plan to take effect. The effective date affects employee rates. 5. Click Continue. To view a report of the changes, click View Report. You can view and download the report at the time you make changes. You cannot access the report after viewing it the first time. To confirm and close the dialog box, click Done.

Resetting Assessments In preparation for open enrollment, you must reset employee assessments every year. On the Employee Details form Personal tab, resetting assessments: • Resets the assessment completion date to blank • Updates the assessment due date based on the open enrollment date

To reset employee assessments: 1. While holding the Ctrl key, select multiple employees from the list. 2. Click Reset Assessments. The Reset Assessments dialog box displays. 3. In Enter the correlating OE effective date, select the open enrollment effective date. 4. Click Continue. To view a report of the changes, click View Report. You can view and download the report at the time you make changes. You cannot access the report after viewing it the first time. To confirm and close the dialog box, click Done.

  1. If the benefit plan is set up as tobacco banded:

Use this option To define this From Age Enter the starting age and the upper age limit. Unless the To Age benefit plan is also set up as age banded by selecting the Age Banded Medical Billing option in Group Benefit Plans, you must enter a one-line “all encompassing” age range in the From Age and To Age fields, for example, 0-99. Non-Tobacco Premium The amount billed to the client for the plan type and age group for non-tobacco using employees. Tobacco Premium The amount billed to the client for the plan type and age group for tobacco using employees. Dependents (Spouse Non-Tobacco) The cost associated with covering an employee’s non- tobacco using spouse for this plan type and age group. Dependents (Spouse Tobacco) If covered, the cost associated with covering an employee’s tobacco using spouse for this plan type and age group. Setting Family Rated Plan Premium Rates To set up premium rates based on the age of individuals covered by the plan, use the Premium Rates form. You must enter a premium for each specific age group. If the plan imposes a surcharge for individuals that are smokers, enter the surcharge in the Tobacco Surcharge column. If the plan does not impose a surcharge, that column blank or enter a zero. If individual rates are the same at the beginning or end of the age range, you do not need to enter individual age rates. For example, assume that the rates start at age 20 and end at 65. For individuals on the plan who are 19 years of age or younger, the system uses the age 20 rate. For individuals who are older than 65, the system charges the age 65 rate.

Setting Family Rated Plan Premium Rates by Rate Groups and Network To set up premium rates based on the age of individuals covered by a plan with networks where billing rates vary by rate group and network, use the Premium Rates form. You must enter a premium for each specific age group. If the plan imposes a surcharge for individuals that are smokers, then enter the surcharge in the Tobacco Surcharge column, otherwise leave that column blank or enter a zero. If individual rates are the same at the beginning or end of the age range, you do not need to enter individual age rates. For example, assume that the rates start at age 20 and end at 65. For individuals on the plan who are 19 years of age or younger, the system uses the age 20 rate. For individuals who are older than 65, the system charges the age 65 rate.

To set family rated premium rates by rate groups and network: 1. Open the Premium Rates form.

Copying Rates from Another Plan Type When premium rates are defined for a plan, you can copy those rates to another plan in the same year using the Premium Rates form. For example, you can copy the rates for the employee and spouse plan to the family plan.

To copy plan rates from another plan type:

  1. In the Actions menu , click Audit and provide the following information:
  2. Select a Plan Type.
  3. Enter a new Effective Date. The Copy from another plan type link displays.
  4. Click Copy from another plan type. A pop-up window opens.
  5. Select the plan from which to copy the premium rates.
  6. Click Copy. The rates populate the table.
  7. Click OK to close the success message.
  8. Make any necessary edits.
  9. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type.
  10. Enter the rates for another plan, either manually or by copying.
  11. Click Close when you are finished.

Establishing Basic Parameters for Group Benefit Plans To establish the basic parameters of a group benefit plan, use the Group Benefit Plans panel.

To establish the basic parameters: 1. Open the Group Benefit Plans panel and complete the following:

Use this To define this option Benefit Plan ID A short description of a new or existing benefit plan Plan A more detailed description of the benefit plan. Description Plan The plan description in Spanish. Description (Spanish) Insurance The type of coverage the plan provides (for example, Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Class Insurance, Long-Term Disability). This setting determines which panels open, what fields are available, and the calculation method the system uses to derive the premium for the benefit plan. See Insurance class panels on page 113.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 108 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

Payee ID The ID of the benefits provider that receives the deducted amounts. If you need to define a new payee for this benefit provider, open the Actions menu and select Payees. Auto Enroll Whether the employee can waive the benefit during an enrollment. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) This option must be used with other settings in the system. For more information, see “Setting Up Waive Options” in the Benefits Enrollment User Guide. Auto Enroll One of the following options: • No: The employee has the option to waive coverage in the benefit plan. • Yes: The employee automatically enrolls in the benefit plan and does not have the option to waive coverage. • Company Decision: The system determines the employee waive option based upon settings at the client level. COBRA Whether the benefit plan can be elected for COBRA coverage. Electable 3rd Party Enable this field to allow plans to be flagged when COBRA administration is COBRA handled by third party. State Specify a U.S. state or territory for state continuation of coverage or mini-COBRA Continuation offerings within the Benefit Plan. In PrismHR, this field is for informational purposes only. Marketplace partners retrieve this data from the PrismHR API and use it for state continuation or mini-COBRA offerings through their services.

                 Note: If you set a state in the State Continuation field, we recommend also
                 checking the COBRA Electable option located directly above the State
                 Continuation field. This ensures coordination with federal continuation, where
                 applicable.

Carrier Set this option if the service provider is responsible for updating carrier eligibility Eligibility information such as enrollments, terms, coverage modifications, or other changes Management which may affect carrier eligibility. Once you flag the plans, you can use this information to create a report in Report Center showing a list of plans where the Carrier Eligibility Management option is set. High Whether the benefit plan has a high deductible that may entitle the employee to Deductible participate in a health savings account (HSA). Plan Single Whether the benefit plan is employee-only. When this option is selected, the Coverage employee contribution must be defined as a percentage of the employee’s Gross Wages earnings when the employee contribution rules are set up in the Benefit Rules % form.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 109 Chapter 1 Setting Up Group Benefit Plans

                 This option must be enabled in System Parameters with the custom feature code
                 SHOWSINGLEGROSSWAGE.

Allow Gross Select this option to set the Percent of Gross Wages as the employee contribution Wage % towards a medical plan (employee premium only). Selecting this option displays a Contribution grid where you can enter an Effective Date and a Percent of Gross Wages, which Method is used as a default setting.

                 Note: To select the Allow Gross Wage % Contribution Method option you must
                 deselect the following options:

                 •     Single Coverage Gross Wage %
                 •     Do NOT Include In ACA Reporting
                 Additionally, you can select this option only if the Cost Basis field is set to either
                 Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly.

PEO Master Whether the Group Benefit Plan is one of the PEO’s Master Benefit Plans. Plan Client Whether the benefit plan is client-sponsored. Sponsored Rate Groups Whether premium rates are maintained separately for each rate group. For Premium Rates Offer Type Select the offer type that classifies the benefit plan. This ensures that the plan displays in the correct form in enrollment workflows. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) This form displays the count of clients who have the selected benefit plan assigned to them in active status. The Status drop-down has the following options: • Active – This is the default option. This option shows a list of clients for whom the selected plan is assigned and is active. • Terminated – This option shows a list of clients for whom the selected plan is assigned but is terminated. • Never Implemented – This option shows a list of clients for whom the selected plan is assigned but was never implemented. • All – This option shows a list of all clients having the selected plan assigned to them in any of the above three statuses. Setting Up Eligible ZIP Codes To enter eligible locations by ZIP code, use the Eligible ZIP Codes form. Use this form only for benefit plans that are not set up to collect network information.

Note: To access the Eligible ZIP Codes form, select Eligible Zip Codes on the Actions menu in the Group Benefit Plans form.

Only employee home locations that match the ZIP codes entered on the plan are eligible for enrollment. If no ZIP codes are entered for the benefit plan, employees can enroll regardless of home location. If the benefit plan is set up for networks (the Collect Network Information option in the Other Processing Parameters panel is selected) you must set up network ZIP codes in the Benefit Network Locations form.

Note: To quickly access the Eligible ZIP Codes import template, select Import Eligible ZIP Codes. You can use the Eligible ZIP Codes import template to import eligible ZIP codes for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To enter eligible locations by ZIP code: 1. Open the Eligible ZIP Codes form. 2. Enter the ZIP Codes to attach to the benefit plan. The City and State displays. You can also click Zip Code and select the ZIP Codes from the Select ZIP Codes selector that displays. On this selector, you can filter the ZIP Codes according to State by using the State drop-down filter. 3. Click Save.

Updating ZIP Codes To attach ZIP codes to a benefit plan, you must first enter them at the system level. If you enter a ZIP code that is not in the system, an error message displays. You can correct this by entering the ZIP code in the Zip Codes form. When the ZIP code record is in the system, you can then attach it to the benefit plan for more information.

Using the Deemed ROTH Field The Secure 2.0 Act includes a mandatory Roth catch-up requirement for Highly Paid Employees (HPE) participating in a 401(k), 403(b), or 457 retirement plan. For the 2026 tax year, employees with $150,000 in prior year, Social Security wages must contribute catch-up on a Roth basis, to the extent they have not previously made Roth contributions during the year. This field allows you to elect plans provision to force Pre-tax contributions to ROTH contributions, Pre-tax Catchup contributions to ROTH Catchup contributions, or both, regardless of whether the 402(g) limit has been met for Highly Paid Employees. Determining a Highly Paid Employee An employee is considered to be an HPE only if the corresponding Retirement Year is defined and the HPE Prior Year field is set to Yes in the Mandatory Roth Catch-up Participant table under the Other tab on the Employee Details form. This drop-down field has the following options: • -Select- – Same as the No (Default) option. • No (Default) – Pre-tax Catchup contributions is taken as pre-tax until total pre-tax contributions equals the 402(g) limit. Once the 402(g) limit is reached, no further Pre-tax or Pre-tax Catchup will be taken for contributions. For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500. Any elected ROTH and ROTH Catchup contributions will continue up to the limits. Any remaining pre-tax Catchup contributions will not be forced to ROTH Catchup contribution. • Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit – Pre-tax Catchup contributions may be taken up to the point when total pre-tax contributions equal the 402(g) limit. Any further catchup contributions will be taken as a ROTH catchup contribution. For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500 with any remaining Catchup contributions taken as ROTH Catchup contribution for the following year (Example: 2026). Please note the following: • If an HPE has a retirement Catchup deductions taken as Roth Catchup, the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code assigned under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section on the

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 128 Chapter 2 Setting Up Retirement Plans

     Retirement Plans form. When there is no code on the Retirement Plans form, then the Roth Catch-up
     Deduction Code assigned at the system level is used as default.
•    When the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code, the deduction displays as a
     ROTH catchup on voucher and on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form.

• Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup before 402(g) limit – Pre-tax Catchup contributions will be taken as a ROTH Catchup regardless of whether the total pre-tax contributions equal the 402(g) limit. For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500. However, all the pre-tax Catchup contributions are taken as ROTH Catchup contribution regardless of whether the total pre-tax contributions equals the 402(g) limit. Please note the following: • If an HPE has a retirement Catchup deductions taken as Roth Catchup, the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code assigned under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section on the Retirement Plans form. When there is no code on the Retirement Plans form, then the Roth Catch-up Deduction Code assigned at the system level is used as default. • When the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code, the deduction displays as a ROTH catchup on voucher and on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form. • Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit – Pre-tax and Pre-tax Catchup contributions may be taken up to the point when total pre-tax contributions equal the 402(g) limit. At this point, all pre-tax elections will be taken as ROTH and all Pre-tax Catchup will be taken as ROTH Catchup contributions. For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500 with any remaining pre-tax contributions taken as ROTH and pre-tax Catchup contributions taken as ROTH Catchup for the following year (Example: 2026). Please note the following: • If an HPE has a retirement pre-tax or Catchup deductions taken as Roth or Roth Catchup, the deduction is taken using the Roth and Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code assigned under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section on the Retirement Plans form. When there is no code on the Retirement Plans form, then the Roth or Roth Catch-up Deduction Code assigned at the system level is used as default. • When the deduction is taken using the Roth or Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code, the deduction displays as a Roth or Roth catchup on voucher and on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form. Please note that currently, the 402(g) limit is equal to the Contribution Limit defined on the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form. The Catch Up Limit is also defined on this form. Additionally, the 402(g) limit and the Catch Up limit can be overridden by defining limits under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section on the Retirement Plans form.

Note: When you check Prohibit Deductions for either of the following on the Retirement Plans form:

• Roth Post-Tax Deduction Code • Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code then, the following options are not displayed in the Deemed ROTH drop-down options: • Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit

After clicking Yes, an on-screen report displays the affected employees, with each employee record, deduction type, and code change (original > updated), which requires you to once again confirm this update in the Retirement Plan and its downstream impacts to Recurring Deduction records: • Clicking Yes: Updates all associated records and provides a list of affected employee enrollments. Once updated, the corresponding Deduction Code displays on the Recurring Deductions form for each associated employee, which the system pulls into the payroll. • Clicking No: Does not update the Retirement Plan setup or the employee Recurring Deduction records. Note the validations for the Prohibit Deductions option: • When you select the Prohibit Deductions or Prohibit Billing option for any of the Deduction or Billing Codes, then that code row clears any existing Deduction Code/Billing Code value and the row is disabled. • When you select the Prohibit Deductions for Employee Loan Deduction Code, then on the Employee Retirement Loans form, when you set up a retirement loan, (Prohibited) text is displayed next to the plan name in the Retirement Plan drop-down options. Additionally, if a loan exists for a retirement plan with Prohibit Deductions option flagged for the Employee Loan Deduction Code row, then while running a payroll, the system does not take the loan deductions. • When you save the form with a Retirement Plan record and if Prohibit Deductions/Billing is not enabled, then: • The record cannot be saved when corresponding Plan-level code is empty and Global Setting is empty. • The record can be saved when either corresponding Plan-level code is not empty or Global Setting is not empty or both values are not empty. • When you save the form with a Retirement Plan record and if Prohibit Deductions/Billing is checked, then: • The record can be saved regardless of whether corresponding Plan-level code is empty and/or Global Setting is empty.

Chapter 3 HSA, FSA, and Section 125 Benefit Plans A health savings account (HSA) is a tax-exempt savings account that, when paired with a qualified high- deductible health plan (QHDHP), can be used to pay for certain medical expenses. Funds deposited are not taxed, nor are withdrawals for qualified expenses. A Flexible Spending Account (FSA) lets employees take home a larger paycheck by reducing their taxable income. Employees enrolled contribute tax-free dollars into an account that can be used throughout the year on qualified medical, dental and vision or qualified dependent care expenses — reducing out-of-pocket costs Section 125 plans enable participating employees to direct a portion of their pre-tax salary to be used to pay for approved premiums, health, dental, and vision care expenses and dependent care expenses. While you can establish FSA and HSA plans under Section 125 settings, PrismHR allows you to maintain your FSA and HSA benefit plans separately. The HSA Plans form is typically used when your FSA and HSA plan years differ.

The subtotal line includes subtotals for Deductions, Company Match, PEO Match, and Reimbursements based on the date range selected. • Summary - For a summary report you just need to indicate the year from the drop-down. The current year shows by default. You have the option of a 10 year look back from the current year. Starting Pay Date Enter the first pay date for the detail report. Ending Pay Date Enter the last pay date for the detail report. Plan Year Accept the default plan year shown or select a different plan year to include in the report. You can type or select the current year and up to 10 prior years. Statement Date This field is optional. Enter the statement date here. Forfeit Balance This field is optional. Check this box if you want the report to indicate that balances will be forfeited (at the end of the plan year). Else leave it unchecked.

Flexible Spending Account Statement Message Use this form to enter text that will appear on the Flexible Spending Account Activity Statement Report. It is a global message setup and applies to all clients and employees when that report is run.

Click Save to save the FSA Statement Message. This message will be displayed on the Flexible Spending Account Activity Statement Report for all clients. 3. Click Delete to delete the FSA Statement Message.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 144 Chapter 4 Configuring the Client-Level Setup

Chapter 4 Configuring the Client-Level Setup You can configure client-level settings to override settings established at the system level.

Setting Up a Benefit Plan To maintain the client’s group benefit, retirement, flexible spending, employer match, and HSA match plans, use the Benefit Plan Setup form. Note: To quickly access the Client Benefit Plan Import form, select Import Client Benefit Plans. (Set the Plan Class to Group Benefit to view this quick link.) You can use the Client Benefit Plan Import form to import the client benefit plan. After that, you must set up a data file and a benefit import definition. Benefit plans must first be set up at the system level. When this is done, each plan offered by the client is established in Benefit Plan Setup.

Note: If your organization is using Benefits Enrollment, the forms for flexible spending plans will display in enrollments only if the plans are set up in Benefit Plan Setup and in the Benefits tab in Client Details. refer to the Client Administration User Guide for more information.

You can access benefit-related features and settings using the Actions menu: • Using a Default Benefit Plan Template (page 178) • Viewing Employees Assigned to a Benefit Plan • Maintaining Benefit Eligibility Groups (page 179) • Setting Up Employee Enrollment Conditions (page 183) • Establishing Eligibility by Benefit Group (page 181): Displays only when you select Flexible Spending in the Plan Class drop-down and select the Use Benefit Groups option. • Clone Benefits: Creates new benefit plans for this client based on the plans for another client.

Establishing Basic Information Establish the basic information for the plan in the Benefit Plan Setup panel.

Note: Different panels display on this form depending on the selected Plan Class. Refer to the appropriate panel descriptions for the plan you are editing.

Applying the Billing Wash Rule For group benefit plans in PrismHR, the billing wash rule determines whether the system charges plan premiums and deductions for a month. This is determined based on where the coverage start or end date falls in relation

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 164 Chapter 4 Configuring the Client-Level Setup

to the wash rule date. The wash rule applies to new hire and terminated employees. The following examples illustrate how the wash rules can affect the benefit deductions of new hire and terminated employees.

New Hire Employees

Scenario 1: No Wash Rule Applied On the Benefit Plan Setup form: • Use Billing Wash Rule? = Enabled • Wash Rule Date On/Before = 15th Day of the Month On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form: • Coverage Starts = 01/08/2021 • Deduction Starts = 02/01/2021 Result: The system performs a benefit adjustment for the full month of January since the employee’s start date (Jan 8) comes before the wash rule date (Jan 15). The system charges the employee their regular scheduled deductions.

Scenario 2: Wash Rule Applied On the Benefit Plan Setup form: • Use Billing Wash Rule? = Enabled • Wash Rule Date On/Before = 15th Day of the Month On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form: • Coverage Starts = 01/29/2021 • Deduction Starts = 02/01/2021 The Deduction Starts field shows Wash Rule applied for 202101. Result: The system does not perform a benefit adjustment for the full month of January since the employee’s start date (Jan 29) comes after the wash rule date (Jan 15). The system does not charge the employee.

Terminated Employees The following is an example of a scenario where the system does not apply the wash rule to a group benefit plan for a terminated employee.

Note: If the Coverage Ends On field is set to “End of Month Following Termination Date” and the Wash Rule date is set to “End of Month”, the wash rule is not applied. However, any other Coverage Ends On Option will result in a full month’s charge upon termination.

On the Benefit Plan Setup form: • Use Billing Wash Rule? = Enabled • Wash Rule Date On/Before = 15th Day of the Month

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 165 Chapter 4 Configuring the Client-Level Setup

On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form: • Coverage Starts = 01/22/2021 • Coverage Ends = 03/05/2021 • Deduction Starts = 02/01/2021 The Deduction Starts field shows Wash Rule applied for 202101. • Deduction Ends = 03/05/2021 The Deduction Ends field shows Wash Rule applied for 202103. Result: The system does not perform a benefit adjustment for the full month of January since the employee’s start date (Jan 22) comes after the wash rule date (Jan 15). The system does not charge the employee. Since the employee was terminated on March 5th (before the 15th day of the month), the system also applies the wash rule to the full month of March.

Setting up Benefit Plan Defaults Use this form to set up the benefit plan defaults for the selected plan. On the Client Benefit Plan Defaults form, click the Plan Defaults hyperlink for a Benefit Plan ID to open this form for the selected plan. You will not be able to find this form using normal search means.

To set up benefit plan defaults: 1. Complete the following fields:

Field Name Description Plan ID This field will be prepopulated. Plan Description This field will also be prepopulated. Billing Rate Group Enter a billing rate group for the selected benefit plan or click the Billing Rate Group selector to select it from the Select Rate Group dialog box which will only populate with Billing Rate Groups that are set up for the selected Benefit Plan. Premium Rate Group Enter a premium rate group for the selected benefit plan or click the Premium Rate Group selector to select it from the Select Rate Group dialog box which will only populate with Premium Rate Groups that are set up for the selected Benefit Plan. Rule Template ID This field is optional. Rule Template ID is used to calculate eligibility, coverage, and employee contributions in the absence of a client or plan specific rule. Enter a Rule Template ID for the selected benefit plan or click the Rule Template ID selector to select it from the Select Benefit Rule Template dialog box. One Month Prepay Check this box if one month prepay is required. You cannot enable Prepay when Billing Wash Rule is used. Add One Month for Prepay Check this box if one month prepay is required. You cannot enable Prepay when Billing Wash Rule is used.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 176 Chapter 4 Configuring the Client-Level Setup

Field Name Description Annual Periods This setting calculates payroll deduction amounts for employee benefit contributions and affects the calculation of weekly, bi- weekly, semi-monthly, or monthly premiums. Select one of the following options: • 48 • 52 48 weeks is generally recommended because the total amount that gets deducted from the client and employee will always equal the same monthly premium (and invoice) from the insurance carrier. However, you can override this setting for any of your individual clients. Use Billing Wash Rule? Check this box if you want to use Billing Wash Rule. You cannot enable Billing Wash Rule when Prepay is used. Cafe Plan Eligible Check this box if this benefit plan is eligible for Cafe Plan. Coverage Ends On Specify the date when coverage ends by choosing one of the drop- downs. Benefit Billing Frequency Specify how often benefits are billed from the following options: • Pay Period • Monthly • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 2 • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 3 • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 4 Pay Deduction Frequency Specify how often benefits are deducted from payroll from the following options: • Pay Period • Monthly • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 2 • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 3 • Monthly, Start Deduction Period 4

  1. Click Save to save the defaults for the selected benefit plan.

Using a Default Benefit Plan Template To have PrismHR automatically generate the Benefit Plan Setup based on the Company Benefit Defaults templates, use the Default Benefit form. The default templates are maintained in the backend system. 1. In the Benefit Plan Setup form, open the Actions menu and select Default Benefit. The system prompts you with a confirmation message. 2. Click Yes to continue. PrismHR creates benefit plans for the client based on the appropriate template. It checks the Cost Center in Client Details. • If there is a cost center set for the client, the system uses the Company Benefit Defaults template for that cost center. • If there is no cost center, it uses the ALL template.

Viewing Employees Assigned to a Benefit Plan Use the Employees Assigned To form to view the employees that are enrolled in the selected Benefit Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form. To access this form, after you have selected a Plan Class on the Benefit Plan Setup form, under the Actions menu, click Employees Assigned To. You cannot find this form using normal search means. This form need to be added to your User Role to access this form.

Note: The Employee Assigned To option under the Actions menu is available only if the Plan Class field is set to Group Benefit on the Benefit Plan Setup form.

• The Active employee count displays the number of active employees based on the active Enrollment Status count. • The Enrollment Status filter displays total number of Active employees assigned to the selected Benefit Plan by default. You can change this to any one of the options from the drop-down. • The grid contains the following columns: • Employee ID: If you click on this hyperlink the Employee Benefits Enrollment modal form is displayed. The Employee and the Benefit Plan fields on the modal form is pre-populated and is in a read-only format. The Employee ID hyperlink is accessible only if you have Full or Inquiry access to that employee in the Employee Benefits Enrollment form. • Employee Name: The employee name is listed here. • Employment Status: The employment status of the employee will display here. • Enrollment Status: The enrollments status of the employee will display here. • Coverage Level: The insurance coverage level of the employee will display here. • You can sort this grid by any of the five headers noted above. • You can scroll to see all employees on a page. There are 11 employees listed per page. If there are more than 11 employees listed, then you can scroll to subsequent pages. • Click Close to close this form and return to the Benefit Plan Setup form.

• Click Report to run a report for the Employees Assigned To. Once the report is run, you can export the data of the employees assigned to the relevant benefit plan. You can download this report into a XLS file on your system.

Contribution Method The calculation method for contribution amounts: • Percentage - The employee’s contribution towards the premium as well as the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is calculated by percentage. • Fixed - The employee’s contribution towards the premium as well as the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is a fixed amount. • Fixed EE, Percent DEP - The employee’s contribution towards the premium is a fixed amount, and the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is calculated by percentage. • Percent EE, Fixed DEP - The employee’s contribution towards the premium is calculated by percentage and the portion of the premium allocated for dependent coverage is a fixed amount.

Calculating Life Insurance Coverage for Commissioned Employees PrismHR has a process for automatically calculating life insurance coverage for employees who are paid on a commission basis or who have a zero pay rate. If the employee Pay Method is set to Commission or their Pay Rate is set to zero on the Pay tab of Employee Details, the system automatically calculates the life insurance coverage amount by extrapolating the year-to-date amounts paid in either the previous or current year. Otherwise, the calculation is based on the employee’s Annual Pay.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 196 Chapter 4 Configuring the Client-Level Setup

If the employee was paid during the previous year, the system uses the amount paid during that year to extrapolate the employee’s annual pay: • If the employee was employed during the entire previous year, the system uses the amount that was paid in that year for the annual pay amount and the life insurance coverage calculation is based on that amount. • If the employee was paid during only part of the year, the system uses that amount to extrapolate the amount that would have been paid over the course of the whole year, and then the system uses that amount for the annual pay. For example, if the employee was paid $25,000 during the last six months of the previous year, the calculated annual pay amount would be $50,000. If the employee was not paid during the previous year, the amount paid year-to-date in the current year is used to calculate the annual pay. If the employee was paid $25,000 for the first six months of the year and that is the year-to-date amount, then the calculated annual pay amount is $50,000. If the employee was not paid in the current or previous year, the calculated annual pay is zero.

Chapter 5 Enrolling Employees in Benefit Plans This section describes the requirements for enrolling employees in group benefit plans. Some of the features found in the Actions menu of Employee Benefits Enrollment are also available in other parts of the system.

Manually Enrolling an Employee in a Benefit Plan To manually enroll an employee in a benefit plan, use the Employee Benefits Enrollment form.

Note: If the employee qualifies for COBRA benefits, the system prompts you to specify whether you want to maintain the COBRA benefits. Click No if you want to edit non-COBRA benefits. Click Yes to edit the COBRA benefit information. The form is very similar to this one; see Enrolling a COBRA Participant on page 240 to learn about COBRA enrollees.

You can access detailed information about the employee’s benefits using the Actions menu : • Benefit Detail Audit (Audit Log) • Benefit Overview: See Displaying an Employee’s Benefit Plans on page 230 • Benefits Adjustment: See Changing an Employee’s Benefit Billing Record on page 260. • CAFE Contribution: See Defining Cafeteria Plan Contributions on page 239. • Dependents: Refer to Human Resources User Guide • Employee Details: Refer to Human Resources User Guide • Employee Flexible Spending Accounts: See Enrolling Employees in Flexible Spending Accounts on page 371. • Employee Flexible Spending Accounts Inquiry: See Employee Flexible Spending Accounts Inquiry on page 375. • Enrollment Audit: See Displaying Enrollment History on page 240. • History: See Displaying Employee Benefit History on page 229 • Retirement Plan Enrollment: See Retirement Plan Enrollment on page 353. • Rule Override: See Overriding a Client’s Eligibility Rules on page 234 • User Fields: Refer to Client Administration User Guide.

• While creating an Employee Benefits Enrollment Detail record for an employee configured with Life Insurance plan for Spouse Age Reduction set as Use Employee Schedule, the system considers the following: • The system displays both the Spouse Coverage Basis and the reduced Spouse Coverage Amount in the Coverage Details section of the Employee Benefit Enrollment form. • If spouse coverage amount is entered then the Spouse Coverage Basis must be set equal to Spouse Coverage Amount. • If the spouse does not meet an age threshold for the reduction schedule and a Spousal Coverage Amount is entered, the Spouse Coverage Amount is stored as the initial coverage amount. • If the spouse meets age threshold for the reduction schedule and a Spousal Coverage Amount is entered, then: • the Spouse Coverage Basis is calculated to reflect the age reduction for the spouse’s age. For example, if spouse is 65 years and reduction to 80% is applied at 65, then for an election of $100,000, the calculated Coverage Basis is $125,000. • if an amount is entered that results in the coverage basis exceeding the Spouse Life Coverage End Amount then an error message is displayed. • While using the Benefits Import tool to import new Benefit Detail Record for Voluntary Life elections, if the Spouse Coverage Amount is imported and the spouse is at or above the first reduction age, then the Coverage Basis is calculated to reflect the appropriate reduction as defined on the plan setup. • If a plan is configured with Employee DOB for Spouse Life field enabled on the Group Benefit Plans form, then the above scenarios should use employee age instead of the Spouse age. • Similarly, the system considers the above scenarios while creating an Employee Benefits Enrollment Detail record for an employee configured with Life Insurance plan for Spouse Age Reduction set as Separate Spouse Schedule. When a spouse covered under an employee life plan crosses a configured Dependent Spouse Age Reduction threshold, then during the payroll process, the system automatically creates a new Life Insurance benefit detail record with the correct Effective Date and reduced coverage amount, using the existing employee age-reduction logic. Please note the following: l The above logic applies when spouse age is calculated from spouse Date of Birth (DOB) or, when configured, from the employee DOB, and continues to respect plans where Dependent Spouse Age Reduction is set to No under the Age Reduction Schedule section on the Group Benefit Plans form. l The Voluntary Life premium calculations now follows the logic that when a plan is configured to

  ReduceCoverage and Premium and Dependent Spouse Age Reduction is enabled with either Use
  Employee Schedule or Separate Spouse Schedule under the Age Reduction Schedule section on the
  Group Benefit Plans form, then the spouse premiums are reduced in line with the spouse coverage
  reduction for manual enrollments.
l Similarly, the Voluntary Life premium calculations include that when a plan is configured with

  ReduceCoverage and Premium and Dependent Spouse Age Reduction is enabled with either Use
  Employee Schedule or Separate Spouse Schedule under the Age Reduction Schedule section on the
  Group Benefit Plans form, then the spouse premiums are reduced in line with the spouse coverage

   amount. Please note that when ReduceCoverage and Premium is not selected, then the spouse premiums

Establishing Billing History To establish and view the billing history for a specific employee/plan along with the ability to select custom date range to review billing history, expand the Billing History section. 1. Expand the Billing History section. Under this section you can perform the following actions: Under the Selection Parameters section, the Defined Ranges drop-down field is available for you to select from a list of pre-defined date ranges or enter your own date range to review billing history. The Defined Ranges drop-down contains the following options: • Current Month (default)- The date range is displayed as the first day of current month and the last day of current month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 6/1/2024-6/30/2024. • Year-to-date- The date range is displayed as the first day of the current year till the current system date. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition displayed on this selection will be 1/1/2024-6/15/2024. • Prior Month- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous month and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 5/1/2024-5/31/2024. • Prior 2 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous two months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 4/1/2024-5/31/2024. • Prior 3 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous three months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 3/1/2024-5/31/2024.

Specifying Whether a Rate Guaranty Applies For life insurance plans, the system displays the rate guaranty for specific date ranges, if it applies to the plan. • The Rate Guaranty Start Date is the start of the guaranty period, and is the date used for Age and Rate. If the plan is an ongoing 5-year guaranty plan, ensure the list includes as many 5-year periods that can possibly apply. Once the employee is out of guaranty periods, the system resumes using the current date for all transactions. • After the final Rate Guaranty End Date passes, the system uses the current Age and Rate for any future calculations.

Displaying Group-Term-Life Taxable Earnings For life insurance plans, the system displays the group-term taxable earnings for the employee, if applicable. • The Benefit Start Date for YTD GTL Taxable is the start date for the employee’s group-term life taxable earnings. • The Tax Year displays the year in which taxable benefits accrued against this plan. • The Taxable Benefit Accrued displays the amount of taxable benefits that accrued against this plan.

Generate / Print COBRA Payment Coupons Use this form to generate or print COBRA Payment Coupons. The COBRA Payment Coupons option provides qualified participants with information to assist with remitting payment for coverage. This process will print COBRA payment coupons for each month in a participant’s COBRA coverage period.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits section, click COBRA Processing. Under COBRA Processing click Generate / Print COBRA Payment Coupons.

To generate or print COBRA Payment Coupons for active participants: 1. Complete the following:

Field Name Description Participant ID Click the Participant ID link and select the code or identifier of an active COBRA participant from the Select Enrollee selector.

  1. Click Run to build the COBRA Payment Coupons for the selected participant. A prompt displays the number of COBRA Payment Coupons created for the selected participant. Click OK to continue.
  2. Click COBRA Payment Coupon Report to display the COBRA Benefits Payment report on screen for the selected participant. If no COBRA Payment Coupon is generated for the selected participant, then this button will remain disabled.
  3. Click Generate Coupons to generate the COBRA Payment Coupons. A Job progress window opens showing the processing steps. Click Open to open the COBRA Payment Coupons generated in a PDF format. You can print them now. If no notice is generated for the selected clients, then this button will remain disabled.
  4. Click Clear to clear the form at any time.

The COBRA Benefits Payment Report has the following columns for the particular Payment Due date: • Benefit Plan ID • Benefit Plan • Premiums • Employer Subsidies

Maintaining COBRA Participant Enrollment This section covers COBRA Participant Enrollment maintenance and includes steps for performing actions such as terminating dependent coverage.

Terminating COBRA Dependent Coverage There are multiple methods for terminating COBRA dependent coverage depending on your practices AND depending on the circumstances under which dependent coverage is terminated. Some of the methods include: l Entering a Coverage End Date on the associated Coverage Detail record. l Adding a new Coverage Detail record for an existing COBRA participant with the same Coverage Effective Date/ Qualifying Event Date. l Adding a new Coverage Detail record for an existing COBRA participant with a new Coverage Effective

 Date/Qualifying Event Date.

l Adding a new Coverage Detail record for a new COBRA participant (where the dependent was previously

 covered under an employer plan but NOT as a COBRA participant.)

The method you choose can determine the way important dates (such as Qualifying Event Date, Coverage Effective Date, and Coverage End Date) are recorded in the system. For more details on how dates are derived and recorded based on the termination method used, see the “How Dates Are Determined When Terminating Dependent Coverage” section of this topic.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 241 Chapter 5 Enrolling Employees in Benefit Plans

   Note: You do not need to switch to COBRA view to perform these steps.

How Dates Are Determined When Terminating Dependent Coverage

When Terminating Dependent Coverage By Entering an End Date on an Existing Coverage Detail Record: l Coverage End Date in the “Dependent [dependent’s full name] was covered before but will not be as of…” message that displays when you enter the End Date on the existing Coverage Detail record and click Save = Coverage End Date you entered on the Coverage Detail record + one day. l Coverage End Date in the “Covered Dependents” section of the Employee Benefits Enrollment record =

 The Coverage End Date you entered on the existing Coverage Detail record.

l New Qualifying Event Date/Coverage Effective Date on the COBRA Participant record (if applicable) =

 Coverage End Date you entered on the existing Coverage Detail record.

When Terminating Dependent Coverage By Adding a New Coverage Detail Record for an Existing COBRA Participant with the Same Qualifying Event Date l Coverage End Date in the “Dependent [dependent’s full name] was covered before but will not be as of…” message that displays when you add the new Coverage Detail record and click Save = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record. l Coverage End Date in the “Covered Dependents” section of the Employee Benefits Enrollment record =

 The date the coverage actually ended, which is the day before the new Coverage Detail record Effective
 Date.

l New Qualifying Event Date/Coverage Effective Date on the COBRA Participant record (if applicable) =

 Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record.

When Terminating Dependent Coverage By Adding a New Coverage Detail Record for an Existing COBRA Participant with a Different Qualifying Event Date l Coverage End Date = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record. l Coverage End Date in the “Covered Dependents” section of the Employee Benefits Enrollment record = The date the coverage actually ended, which is the day before the new Coverage Detail record Effective

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 245 Chapter 5 Enrolling Employees in Benefit Plans

 Date.

l New Qualifying Event Date/Coverage Effective Date on the COBRA Participant record (if applicable) =

 Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record.

   Note: There is no difference between the way the dates are determined when an existing COBRA
   dependent is terminated by adding a new coverage detail record with the same OR different qualifying
   event dates. The system uses this distinction to determine whether to create a new COBRA Participant
   record or update the existing COBRA Participant record (if you selected the option to add the new
   coverage details to a COBRA Participant record.)

   New Qualifying Event Date = New COBRA Participant record. Same Qualifying Event Date = Updated
   COBRA Participant record.

When Terminating Dependent Coverage by Adding a New Coverage Detail Record for a New COBRA Participant l Coverage End Date = Effective Date you entered on the new Coverage Detail record. l Coverage End Date in the “Covered Dependents” section of the Employee Benefits Enrollment record = The date the coverage actually ended, which is the day before the new Coverage Detail record Effective Date. l New Qualifying Event Date/Coverage Effective Date (if applicable) = Effective Date you entered on the

 new Coverage Detail record.

This applies to ASO clients only. Enter the date the client notified the COBRA administrator of the qualifying event. Benefits Expiration Date Enter the date this person’s benefits will expire if not continued under COBRA. COBRA Coverage Period Starts This is the date when the COBRA continuation coverage period begins. The continuation coverage expiration date is calculated from this date.

Field Name Description COBRA Coverage Period Ends Enter the date that the COBRA coverage period will end. This is dependent on the number of months of coverage, based on the qualifying event. Election Notice Due Date Enter the date the initial notification letter is due to be sent. Election Notice Sent Date This field is optional. Enter the date the Election Notice for COBRA continuation coverage was sent to this enrollee. Eligibility Cutoff Date This field is optional. Enter the date by which a decision to enroll must be made. After this date, COBRA benefit eligibility will no longer be active. ARPA Notice This field is optional. This field applies to ARPA notices that were required in 2021. If checked, ARPA-style election notices will generate for individuals whose COBRA coverage start date falls within the assigned start and stop date. If unchecked, the qualifying event date will be used. ARPA Election Notice Sent This field is optional. Enter the date when ARPA election notice was sent. ARPA Extension Notice Sent This field is optional. Enter the date when ARPA extension notice was sent. Continuation Coverage Accepted This field is optional, if the COBRA status is inactive. However, if the COBRA status is active, then this field is required. Enter the date that the participant elected to continue coverage under COBRA. First Premium Due Date This field is optional. Enter the date the first premium is due from this beneficiary. This is normally forty-five days from the date the person elects COBRA continuation coverage. First Premium Receipt Date This field is optional. Enter the date the first premium payment was received from the participant. Termination Notice Printed This field is optional. Applies to terminated enrollees. Certified Letter Reference Number This field is optional. Enter the reference number for the certified or registered initial notification letter sent to this person. Certified Letter Status This field is optional. Select the status of the certified letter sent to this person from the following: • Signed • Returned

COBRA Dependent Participant Questions The COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form is used to gather the information needed to add or update a COBRA Participant record for one or more terminated dependents. The system determines the Qualifying Event Date and Coverage End Date shown on the form depending on for you depending on how the dependent is being terminated. For example, if the terminated dependent was already covered under an existing Coverage Detail record and you are terminating dependent coverage by adding a new Coverage Detail record with a new Coverage Effective Date, the Qualifying Event Date is the same as the Coverage Effective Date and the Coverage End Date is set as the day before the Coverage Effective Date.

To complete the COBRA Dependent Participant Questions form: 1. Select the Qualifying Event. Note: If your access privileges allow, you can also edit the Social Security No. field. Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 268 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

Chapter 6 Importing Benefits The Benefits Import Process enables you to enroll employees in group benefit plans using the information in an external data file. The process requires you to set up a data file and a benefit import definition.

Before you begin: • Set up company benefits and benefit rules. For more information, see the Benefits Administration User Guide.

Setting Up the Data File The data file must be either tab-delimited or comma-delimited. It must include the following columns of information, in any order: • Company ID • Employee ID, Employee SSN, or Employee Clock Number • Offer Type • Benefit Plan ID • Benefit Plan Type • Effective Date • Action Codes

lrImporting Benefit Rates Use this Benefit Rates Import form to initiate a new import or complete an existing import in progress of benefit rates (premium or billing) into PrismHR using a predefined benefit rates import template. You can also view completed benefit rates imports on this form. This benefit rates import process cannot be used to change or overwrite existing benefit rates.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the form, on the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits, click Benefit Imports & Reporting. Under Benefit Imports, click Benefit Rates Import.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 269 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

You can also search for this form on the search box in the main navigation search bar.

This form has the following two sections: • Imports in Progress • Past Imports

Imports in Progress When you access this form for the first time, all the tables will be blank and you should select the New Import button to proceed to the Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import (page 274) screen to define and begin a new benefit rate import.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 270 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

User – This field is a dropdown. By default, the user id of the user who has logged in will display here. You can also select a different user from the drop-down. This section displays all benefit rate imports that are not completed successfully for the selected user. This section will display the last 7 imports in progress at a glance on-screen for the selected user. In case there are more than 7 imports in progress for the selected user, you will see a scroll bar on the right. Scroll to view all the imports in progress for the selected user. The information is displayed in a table that has the following columns: 1. Name – This is the import name that was provided for that benefit rate import. If you click one of the names, it will take you to the Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import (page 274) screen for further action to complete the import. 2. Type – This is the benefit rate type that you are importing for the import. This will be: a. Premium Rates OR b. Billing Rates 3. Plan Used for Template – This is the Benefit Plan ID used for the import template. 4. Last Modified Date – This shows when this import was last worked upon. 5. Last Modified User – This shows the user id of the user who worked on the import last. 6. Status – This shows the status of the import in progress and can be any one of the following: a. Template Defined – When an import has been defined but no import file is uploaded. b. Ready for Import – When an import has been defined AND an import file is uploaded. c. Import Errors – When an import attempt has failed. This will produce a Benefit Rate Import Error Report 7. Error Report – When the Status above is either Template Defined or Ready for Import, this column will display a ‘-’ [dash]. When the Status above is Import Errors, then this column will display a link to open and view the error report for the corresponding import that was not successful. It provides a list of all the errors that this import encountered. You can correct these errors and try again to complete the import. Following is a sample Benefit Rate Import Error Report.

Past Imports This section lists all the benefit rate imports completed successfully for the selected date range. By default, the date range is a calendar month ending on the current date. You can manually change the date range. This section will display the last 7 completed imports at a glance on-screen for the selected date range. In case there are more than 7 completed imports for the selected date range, you will see a scroll bar on the right. Scroll to view all the completed imports for the selected date range. Past Imports that are older than one year (since completion date) are automatically deleted and no longer display in the table. The completed imports are sorted first by Date Completed and then by Name. The latest imports are listed at the top.

Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import Use this Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import form to set up and import new benefit rates (premium or billing) into PrismHR using a predefined benefit rates import template. You also need to use this form to complete existing Imports in Progress. Note:

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 274 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

• You can only access this form from the lrImporting Benefit Rates (page 269) form. From the Benefit Rates Import form: • You can click the New Import button to come to this form, OR, • You can click the Name link of an existing Import in Progress to come to this form.

Using the New Import button When you click the New Import button on the lrImporting Benefit Rates (page 269) form, you come to this form. All fields on this form will be blank. 1. Complete the following fields:

Field Description Import Name Give the import a unique name that does not already exist in PrismHR to identify it. • The name can have alpha-numeric characters but cannot contain special characters. • The import name cannot contain spaces. • Import names must contain at least 3 characters. Which Rate are you Importing? Select one of the following benefit rate types from the following: • Premium Rates OR • Billing Rates Plan ID This link only becomes active after you select a benefit rate type above. This defines the import template for the rest of the procedure. You can enter the Plan ID manually or click the Plan ID link and select a plan as your template builder based on pre-defined defaults and selectable filters.

                                                       Note: You cannot manually enter a Plan ID if the
                                                       Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage Entered
                                                       Manually in the Group Benefit Plans form for that
                                                       plan. Since these plans do not have rate tables,
                                                       there are no rates that can be imported in Group
                                                       Benefit Plans, and they cannot be supported in the
                                                       Benefit Rate Import. These plans will not show up
                                                       when you are using the Select Benefit Plan selector.

Please note that: • If you manually enter a Plan ID and try to save the form without entering a benefit rate type, an error message displays.

  1. Click Save to save your import template once you have provided a valid input for all the three required fields noted above. A line item is listed in the Imports in Progress section on the lrImporting Benefit Rates (page
    1. form. Upon save, the Import Name field and the rate type become read only. However, you can still edit the Plan ID field. A warning displays when you try to edit this field. Please note that: • Import Names must contain at least 3 characters. • Rate type selection is required. • The Plan ID field cannot be blank.

What is the import template builder? Based on the benefit plan that you enter in the Plan ID field, you can import numerous benefit plans that have the same setup. Example: If the Plan ID has Age Banded Medical Rates and Rate Groups for Premium Rates, then a plan with only Age Banded Medical Rates WOULD NOT be included in a Premium Rate Table but WOULD be included in a Billing Rate Table, since Rate Groups for Premium Rates is not used for Billing Rates. If BOTH plans do not have any values checked, then these are considered to match. If you enter an age banded medical plan, any medical, dental and vision plan that is age banded can be imported together. Please note that the benefit plans need to be an exact match. Using the prior example, it cannot be age banded and tobacco banded.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 277 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

Once you save your import template, the following section displays a list of all plans that match the setup as the selected Plan ID. This table is a reference for all the different possible setups. In the example above, we have selected a medical plan that is age banded, so that column is populated below.

Note: If you try to change the Plan ID at this point, the system displays a warning that this action may affect the plans that can be included in this import. If an import file has been uploaded, it will be removed. If you select Yes, then the Plan ID changes and the table of available plans that can be imported based on the plan selection also changes. This would affect what can be included in the import file.

• The updated Plan ID is saved to the import definition template. • The table of available plans is updated based on the newly selected Plan ID. • The Premium and Billing Rate Template available via the links in the Import Template Builder is updated based on the new Plan ID. • If there is an import file already uploaded, the file is removed from the import. • Since this is a change to the import, the Imports in Progress table on the Benefit Rate Import form is updated with Last Modified User and Last Modified Date.

b. If the processing completes with errors, click Close to close the job progress window. The Benefit Rate
