   the corrected import file and continue.

Note: Click Close to close this form at any time. If you close this form before successfully completing an import, then the import will be listed under the Imports in Progress section on the Benefit Rates Import form with the appropriate Status. You can click that import anytime to resume your import from where you left off.

Using the Name link under Imports in Progress If the Status of the Import is: • Template Defined – Continue from Step 1 in the procedure above. • Ready for Import – Continue from Step 5 in the procedure above. • Import Errors – Make necessary corrections to your import file and continue from Step 1 in the procedure above. To validate what was imported, go to the Group Benefit Plans form. Enter the Benefit Plan ID for which you had imported the rates. Select Actions and then select Premium Rates or Billing Rates whichever is applicable. Then complete the information on the form that matches what you imported.

Please make a note of the following errors to avoid while preparing your import file using this template: 1. For Plan ID a. You can only select an active plan for the import. If you select a plan that is terminated you will get an error message stating Plan ID is Terminated. Not valid for Import. b. If the Family Rate Premiums field under the Other Processing Parameters section on the Group Benefit Plans form is checked, then exclude family rated plans from the import. If not you will get an error message stating Plan ID has Family Rated Premiums. Not supported for Import. c. Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported. If you select any other insurance class plans, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is [NAME] Insurance Class. Not supported for Import. d. Plans where the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually in the Group Benefits Plans form are excluded. 2. The following are required values for this import. [Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type, Effective Date, Total Premium, Employee Premium]. If the import file is missing any required values, you will see an error message stating {Import Field Name} is required. 3. If the Benefit Plan ID on the import file a. does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID does not exist. b. is more than 25 characters, you receive an error message stating Benefit Plan ID must be 25 characters or less. c. is NOT in the list of benefit Plan IDs in the Template Builder you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not in the Template Builder and cannot be included in this Rate Template.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 283 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

  1. Multiple lines of age rates are allowed (For example: age 0 - 19, 20-39, 40-59, 60-99). However:
    1. If import file is set up with overlapping From Age and To Age for same Effective Date combination, you will receive an error message stating Age Bands cannot overlap.
    2. Import file should not have gaps between age bands. For example you cannot have age bands like 0-19, 20-29, 31-39 since the To Age of 29 and From Age of 31 have a gap. If there are gaps, you will receive an error message stating Age gaps are not permitted in Age Banded Rates.
    3. The From Age and To Age fields in the import file must be a whole number >=0, otherwise you will receive an error message stating [From Age/To Age] must be a whole number >=0 From Age or To Age = whichever is applicable to error.
    4. The initial From Age in the import file must be 0, otherwise you will receive an error message stating Initial From Age must be 0.
  2. If the Plan Type on the import file does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .
  3. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.
  4. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type and Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.
  5. The rate on the import file has to be a positive number with a maximum of 2 decimals. If the rate on the import file
    1. has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
    2. is negative, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.
  6. Total Bill Amount must equal Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount. If Employee Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then Employee Bill Amount must equal Total Bill Amount, otherwise the import will fail with the following error message:
    1. Plan Type Coverage Class can be found in Group Benefit Plan Types in the Coverage Class field.
    2. Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Bill Amount must equal Total Bill Amount.
  7. If Dependent Bill Amount > 0 is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then the import will fail with an the error message stating Dependent Bill Amount > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .
  8. Dependent Bill Amount is a calculated amount based on Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount.
    1. If Dependent Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class NOT selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the Employee Bill Amount PLUS the Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount. Otherwise, the import will fail with an error message stating Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 284 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

b.    If Dependent Bill Amount is blank on the import file, then Dependent Bill Amount will be imported as a
     calculated amount. (Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount)

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 285 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

  1. The following are required values on the import. [Benefit Plan ID, Rate Group, Plan Type, Effective Date, Total Bill Amount and Employee Bill Amount]. If the import file is missing any required values, you will see an error message stating {Import Field Name} is required.
  2. If the Benefit Plan ID on the import file:
    1. does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID does not exist.
    2. is more than 25 characters, you receive an error message stating Benefit Plan ID must be 25 characters or less.
    3. is NOT in the list of Benefit Plan IDs in the Template Builder you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not in the Template Builder and cannot be included in this Rate Template.
  3. The Rate Group on the import file:
    1. must be an existing Rate Group under the Billing Rate Groups form. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group does not exist.
    2. must be an active Rate Group under the Billing Rate Groups form i.e. the field Inactive must be unchecked. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group is inactive.
  4. If employee Plan Type on the import file does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plan form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .
  5. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.
  6. Age Banded Medical Rates
    1. Only one line of rates is allowed.
    2. If import file is set up with more than one line for an effective date combo then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not setup as age banded. Therefore, only one age band is allowed (0 to 99).
    3. If the From Age and To Age fields are on the import file, then the From Age must be 0 and To Age must be 99. If any other value is entered, you will receive an error message stating From Age must be 0. To Age must be 99.
    4. If the From Age and To Age fields are blank on the import file, then PrismHR will import the values of 0 for the From Age field and 99 for the To Age field.
  7. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type and Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.
  8. If the rate on the import file has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
  9. If the rate is negative on the import file, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 286 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

  1. For Plan Type with coverage class selected as Single (employee) coverage, if Employee Premium is on the import file, then Employee Premium must equal Total Premium. Else, you will receive an error message stating Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Premium must equal Total Premium. Refer to the Coverage Class field selection on the Group Benefit Plan Types form for details.
  2. If your import file has Dependent Premium > 0 for a Plan Type with coverage class selected as Single (employee) coverage, you will receive an error message stating Dependent Premium > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .
  3. Total Bill Amount must equal Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Premium. Dependent Premium is a calculated amount based on Total Premium minus Employee Premium.
  4. If Dependent Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type with coverage class is not selected as Single (employee) coverage, the Employee Bill Amount PLUS the Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount. Otherwise, you will receive an error stating Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount. Note: If Dependent Bill Amount is blank on the import file, then the Dependent Bill Amount will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount)

      1. If import file is set up with overlapping From Age and To Age for same Effective Date combination, you will receive an error message stating Age Bands cannot overlap.
      2. Import file should not have gaps between age bands. For example you cannot have age bands like 0- 19, 20-29, 31-39 since the To Age of 29 and From Age of 31 have a gap. If there are gaps, you will receive an error message stating Age gaps are not permitted in Age Banded Rates.
      3. The From Age and To Age fields must be a whole number >=0, otherwise you will receive an error message stating [From Age/To Age] must be a whole number >=0 From Age or To Age = whichever is applicable to error.
      4. Initial From Age must be 0, otherwise the import will fail with an error message stating Initial From Age must be 0.
  3. If the Plan Type on the import file
    1. does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .
    2. has a Coverage Class of Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefits Plan Types form, you will receive an error stating Spouse coverage is not allowed for Plan Type .
  4. The Rate Group for this import must be an existing Rate Group under the Billing Rate Groups form. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group does not exist. Also the Rate Group for this

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 291 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

import must be an active Rate Group under the Billing Rate Groups form i.e. the field Inactive must be
unchecked. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group <Billing Rate Group> is inactive.
  1. Network ID on the import must exist under the section Plan Networks on the Group Benefit Plan form. If not import line fails with error message stating Network ID does not exist on Plan ID .
  2. If the Employee Gender on the import file does not match up with system gender options (Male or Female), you will receive an error stating Employee Gender is not found.
  3. If the Spouse Gender on the import file does not match up with system gender options (Male or Female), you will receive an error stating Spouse Gender is not found.
  4. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.
  5. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Rate Group (if applicable), Network ID, Plan Type, Employee Gender and Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.
  6. The rate on the import file has to be a positive number with a maximum of 2 decimals. If the rate on the import file:
    1. has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
    2. is negative, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.
  7. Total Bill Amount must equal Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount. If Employee Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then Employee Bill Amount must equal Total Bill Amount, otherwise the import will fail with the following error message:
    1. Plan Type Coverage Class can be found in Group Benefit Plan Types in the Coverage Class field.
    2. Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Bill Amount must equal Total Bill Amount.
  8. If Dependent Bill Amount > 0 is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the import will fail with an the error message stating Dependent Bill Amount > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .
  9. Dependent Bill Amount is a calculated amount based on Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount.
    1. If Dependent Bill Amount is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class NOT selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the Employee Bill Amount PLUS the Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount. Otherwise, the import will fail with an error message stating Employee Bill Amount PLUS Dependent Bill Amount must equal the Total Bill Amount.
    2. If Dependent Bill Amount is blank on the import file, then Dependent Bill Amount will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Bill Amount minus Employee Bill Amount)

Please make a note of the following errors to avoid while preparing your import file using this template: 1. For Plan ID a. You can only select an active plan for the import. If you select a plan that is terminated you will get an error message stating Plan ID is Terminated. Not valid for Import. b. If the Family Rate Premiums field under the Other Processing Parameters section on the Group Benefit Plans form is checked, then exclude family rated plans from the import. If not you will get an error message stating Plan ID has Family Rated Premiums. Not supported for Import. c. Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported. If you select any other insurance class plans, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is [NAME] Insurance Class. Not supported for Import. d. Plans where the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually in the Group Benefits Plans form are excluded. 2. The following are required values for this import. [Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type, Effective Date, Total Premium, Employee Premium]. If the import file is missing any required values, you will see an error message stating {Import Field Name} is required. 3. If the Benefit Plan ID on the import file a. does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID does not exist. b. is more than 25 characters, you receive an error message stating Benefit Plan ID must be 25 characters or less. c. is NOT in the list of benefit Plan IDs in the Template Builder you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not in the Template Builder and cannot be included in this Rate Template. 4. Multiple lines of age rates are allowed (For example: age 0 - 19, 20-39, 40-59, 60-99). However:

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 304 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

a. If import file is set up with overlapping From Age and To Age for same Effective Date combination, you
   will receive an error message stating Age Bands cannot overlap.
b. Import file should not have gaps between age bands. For example you cannot have age bands like 0-19,
   20-29, 31-39 since the To Age of 29 and From Age of 31 have a gap. If there are gaps, you will receive an
   error message stating Age gaps are not permitted in Age Banded Rates.
c. The From Age and To Age fields must be a whole number >=0, otherwise you will receive an error
   message stating [From Age/To Age] must be a whole number >=0 From Age or To Age = whichever is
   applicable to error.
  1. If the Plan Type on the import file does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .
  2. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.
  3. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type and Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.
  4. The rate on the import file has to be a positive number with a maximum of 2 decimals. If the rate on the import file
    1. has more than 2 decimals, then you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
    2. is negative, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.
  5. Total Premium must equal Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium. If Employee Premium is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then Employee Premium must equal Total Premium, otherwise the import will fail with the following error message:
    1. Plan Type Coverage Class can be found in Group Benefit Plan Types in the Coverage Class field.
    2. Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Premium must equal Total Premium.
  6. If Dependent Premium > 0 is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the import will fail with an the error message stating Dependent Premium > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .
  7. Dependent Premium is a calculated amount based on Total Premium minus Employee Premium.
    1. If Dependent Premium is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class NOT selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the Employee Premium PLUS the Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium. Otherwise, the import will fail with an error message stating Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium.
    2. If Dependent Premium is blank on the import file, then Dependent Premium will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Premium minus Employee Premium)

  1. If the Plan Type on the import file does not exist under the section Plan Types on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error stating Plan Type does not exist on the Plan ID .
  2. If the Effective Date on the import file is not in a valid US date format, you will receive and error message stating Effective Date must be in a valid date format.
  3. Only one line of rates per Effective Date is allowed.
    1. If import file is set up with more than one line of rates for an Effective Date, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not setup as age banded. Therefore, only one age band is allowed (0 to 99).
    2. If the From Age and To Age fields are on the import file, then the From Age must be 0 and To Age must be 99. If any other value is entered, you will receive an error message stating From Age must be 0. To Age must be 99.
    3. If the From Age and To Age fields are blank on the import file, then PrismHR will import the values of 0 for the From Age field and 99 for the To Age field.
  4. If a rate on the import file;
    1. has more than 2 decimals, you will receive an error message stating Only 2 decimal places are allowed for Rates.
    2. is a negative value, you will receive an error message stating Negative amounts are not allowed.
  5. If your import file has records which already exist in PrismHR having the same Benefit Plan ID, Plan Type and Effective Date, you will receive an error message stating Effective Date <EFFECTIVE DATE.> already exists for this record. Updates cannot be imported. If a duplicate key exists on the import file, this validation will also present a line error for the second record and any subsequent duplicate records attempted to be imported.
  6. If Employee Premium is on the import file, and the Plan Type has Single (employee) coverage selected in the Coverage Class field on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, then Employee Premium must equal Total Premium. Else, you will receive an error message stating Plan Type has Coverage Class Single. Employee Premium must equal Total Premium. Refer to the Coverage Class field selection on the Group Benefit Plan Types form for details.
  7. If your import file has Dependent Premium > 0 for a Plan Type with coverage class selected as Single (employee) coverage, you will receive an error message stating Dependent Premium > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type . • Total Premium must equal Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium. Dependent Premium is a calculated amount based on Total Premium minus Employee Premium. • If Dependent Premium is on the import file and Plan Type with coverage class is not selected as Single (employee) coverage, the Employee Premium PLUS the Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium. Otherwise, you will receive an error stating Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium.

  6. If Dependent Premium > 0 is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the import will fail with an the error message stating Dependent Premium > 0 is not allowed for Plan Type .
  7. Dependent Premium is a calculated amount based on Total Premium minus Employee Premium.
    1. If Dependent Premium is on the import file and Plan Type has Coverage Class NOT selected as Single (employee) coverage on the Group Benefit Plan Types form, the Employee Premium PLUS the Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium. Otherwise, the import will fail with an error message stating Employee Premium PLUS Dependent Premium must equal the Total Premium.
    2. If Dependent Premium is blank on the import file, then Dependent Premium will be imported as a calculated amount. (Total Premium minus Employee Premium)

a. does not exist in PrismHR, then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID <Plan ID> does not

  1. Age Banded Medical Rates
    1. If Age Banded Medical Rates = No, then only one line of rate is allowed.
      1. If the import file has more than one rate for the same Effective Date then you will receive an error message stating Plan ID is not setup as age banded. Therefore, only one age band is allowed (0 to 99).
      2. If the From Age and To Age fields are on the import file, then the From Age must be 0 and To Age must be 99. If any other value is entered, you will receive an error message stating From Age must be 0. To Age must be 99.
      3. If the From Age and To Age fields are blank on the import file, then PrismHR will import the values of 0 for the From Age field and 99 for the To Age field.
    2. If Age Banded Medical Rates = Yes, then multiple lines of age rates are allowed (For example: age 0 - 19, 20-39, 40-59, 60-99). However:
      1. If import file is set up with overlapping From Age and To Age for same Effective Date combination, you will receive an error message stating Age Bands cannot overlap.
      2. Import file should not have gaps between age bands. For example you cannot have age bands like 0- 19, 20-29, 31-39 since the To Age of 29 and From Age of 31 have a gap. If there are gaps, you will receive an error message stating Age gaps are not permitted in Age Banded Rates.
      3. The From Age and To Age fields must be a whole number >=0, otherwise you will receive an error message stating [From Age/To Age] must be a whole number >=0 From Age or To Age = whichever is applicable to error.
      4. Initial From Age must be 0, otherwise the import will fail with an error message stating Initial From Age must be 0.
  2. If the Network ID on the import file does not exist under the section Plan Networks on the Group Benefit Plans form, you will receive an error message stating Network ID does not exist on Plan ID .
  3. The Rate Group for this import must be:
    1. an existing Rate Group on the Billing Rate Groups form. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group does not exist.
    2. on the Billing Rate Groups form with the field Premium Rate Group checked, otherwise you will get an error message stating Rate Group is not a Premium Rate Group.
    3. an active Rate Group on the Billing Rate Groups form i.e. the field Inactive must be unchecked. Else you will get an error message stating Rate Group is inactive.

Importing Employee Dependents You can import multiple employee dependents for multiple employees at once to reduce the amount of manual work required. Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import employee dependents do the following:

  1. Click (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processingmenu.

  2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Employee Dependents import template option. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

    The layout requirements are:
Field                              Description
Column Number                      The corresponding column number for the imported data.

    Field                               Description
    Category Description                 •      Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.
                                         •      Spouse: Whether the dependent is the employee's spouse.
                                                A spouse must have a Relationship Type of Dependent.
                                         •      First Name (required): The dependent's first name.
                                         •      Last Name (required): The dependent’s last name.
                                         •      Middle Initial: The dependent's middle initial.
                                         •      Gender: The dependent's birth gender. Please note the
                                                below validations for the Gender field:

                                                •   If Gender Non Binary is flagged on the System
                                                    Parameters form, then you must be able to import Non-
                                                    binary as a Gender option. The Gender Non-binary field
                                                    value is defined as X.
                                                •   If Gender Decline To State is flagged on the System
                                                    Parameters form, then you must be able to import
                                                    Declined to state as a Gender option. The Gender
                                                    Declined to state field value is defined as D.
                                         •      Birth Date: The dependent's birth date.
                                         •      Dependent SSN: The dependent's Social Security number.
                                         •      Tobacco Use: Whether the dependent uses tobacco.
                                         •      EE SSN, EE ID, or Clock No. (required): Used to identify

    Field                               Description

    Required?                           Indicates if the field is required.
  1. Optionally, click Clear existing dependents from employee records to replace existing employee dependent records with the information in the import file. Leave this option unchecked to add this information to existing employee dependent records, including duplicates. When this option is checked, the validation logic evaluates any previously identified dependent record not included in the current import file to determine if that dependent record has current coverage or prior coverage history. Additionally, an informational message stating, “Required fields may vary based on client setup for New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides” displays. • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have current coverage or prior coverage history: The record is skipped and the following error message displays: “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID [Dependent ID Number] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with it.” A variation of this same message displays when multiple dependent records with current coverage or prior coverage history must be skipped for the same employee: “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID’s [Dependent ID Numbers separated by a comma] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with them.” • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have no current coverage or prior coverage history associated with it: The record is deleted. This validation works similar to the validation logic used when you attempt to manually delete a dependent with coverage history from the system. In that instance, a message displays indicating that you cannot delete the record but you can mark it Inactive.

Required Fields Validation When fields are configured as required fields on either the New Hire and Dependent Required Fields (Global) form or the New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides form, validations are in place to ensure correct data is passed and required fields are not missing or invalid during the File Upload process.

Valid Data Checks: If the following fields are configured as required and the field values are found to be invalid during the File Upload process of the Employee Dependents Import, an error message displays on the Messages tab of the Data Import Tool for each invalid value.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 327 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

l Birth Date - Must have valid date format. l Gender - Must have valid value (i.e., M, F, X, or D). l Relation - Must have valid value. The system uses the Relation Codes specified here to validate against: Benefit Plan Maintenance > Group Benefit Plans (Global) > Relationships.

Missing Data Checks: If the following fields are configured as required and the field values are missing, an error message displays on the Messages tab of the Data Import tool for each missing value. l Social Security Number l Birth Date l Gender l Relation l Address (Address Line 1, City, State, ZIP Code)

Translation Tables Use translation tables to convert codes found in the data file to standard action codes that PrismHR software uses. External action codes are located in an external data file, and standard action codes correspond to external action codes. Options include: • Action Translations: Enter action codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard action codes in the next column. • Client Translations: Enter company IDs found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard company IDs in the next column. • Plan Translations: Enter benefit plan codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard benefit plan codes in the next column. • Plan Type Translations: Enter plan type (coverage levels) found in the external data file in this column Enter the corresponding standard plan types in the next column. • Network Translations: Enter network codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard network IDs in the next column. 1. In the Translation Tables dialog box, click Actions. The Benefit Import Actions Translation Table form opens. 2. To indicate the action the system should take for each line of data, enter the External Action Codes found in the data file and the corresponding Standard Action Codes from the following table.

Code Name Description ADD Creates a new benefit enrollment. WAIVE Waives coverage for an existing enrollment. CHANGE Changes the plan type/coverage of an existing enrollment. TERM Terminates an existing enrollment.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 332 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

Code Name Description DEPEN+ Adds a covered dependent to an existing enrollment. You can also use this to add covered dependents to a new enrollment, as long as the new enrollment occurs in the file before the line that adds the dependent. BENEF+ Adds a beneficiary to an existing enrollment. You can also use this to add a beneficiary to a new enrollment, as long as the new enrollment occurs in the file before the line that adds the beneficiary. DEPEN- Removes a covered dependent from an existing enrollment. BENEF- Removes a beneficiary from an existing enrollment. ENROLLFSA Creates a new flexible spending account (FSA) enrollment. ENROLLHSA Creates a new health savings account (HSA) enrollment. TERMFSA Terminates an existing flexible spending account (FSA) enrollment. TERMHSA Terminates an existing health savings account (HSA) enrollment. CHANGEFSA Changes the plan type/coverage in an existing flexible spending account (FSA) enrollment. CHANGEHSA Changes the plan type/coverage in an existing health savings account (HSA) enrollment.

Importing Benefit Enrollments Use the Benefit Import process to enroll employees in group benefit plans using the information in an external data file. The process requires you to set up a data file and a benefit import definition. You can set up the data file either before you begin the import or from within the Benefits Import form. You must set up company benefits and benefit rules before using this process. See “Benefit Groups” and “Benefit Rules” in the Benefits Administration User Guide for more information.

To set up the data file: 1. Create an Excel spreadsheet that includes at least the following columns of information in the same order as in the template. The data file must be either tab-delimited or comma-delimited. • Action Code • Company ID • Employee ID, Employee SSN, or Employee Clock Number • Benefit Plan ID • Benefit Plan Type • Effective Date 2. Save the spreadsheet in either CVS or TXT format.

Importing Benefit Adjustments You can import multiple benefit adjustments for multiple employees at once to reduce the amount of manual work required. Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 335 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

To upload and import benefit adjustments, do the following:

  1. Click (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.
  2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Benefit Adjustments import template option. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) The layout requirements are:

Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data. Category Description • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. • Employee ID (required): Unique identifier for the employee whose benefit billing record will receive an adjustment. • Plan ID (required): Unique identifier for the Benefit Plan that requires an adjustment. • Plan Period (required): The benefit plan period in the format YYYYMM. For example, 202310 for October 2023. • Bill Amount (required): The amount to bill to the client per pay cycle as a result of an adjustment. • Employee Contribution: The amount to deduct from the employee’s pay check per cycle. This amount is credited to the client to offset the billing amount. • Cycles (required): The number of future payroll cycles to apply an adjustment. • Start Date (required): The Start Date of the period when the deduction related to an adjustment goes into effect. • Insurance Cost: The premium cost associated with an adjustment. • Adjustment Amount: The B/R adjustment to apply to the benefits reconciliation process of an adjustment. • Retro Enroll: Whether an adjustment applies to a retroactive enrollment. Pre-tax contributions cannot fund any part of the premium for retroactive enrollments. Valid values are Yes or No. • Comments: Descriptive comments about an adjustment.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 336 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

Note: Cycles Billed is not a required field anymore for importing Benefit Adjustments. It will automatically be set to 0 when importing Benefit Adjustments.

  1. Optionally, click Clear existing dependents from employee records to replace existing employee dependent records with the information in the import file. Leave this option unchecked to add this information to existing employee dependent records, including duplicates. When this option is checked, the validation logic evaluates any previously identified dependent record not included in the current import file to determine if that dependent record has current coverage or prior coverage history. Additionally, an informational message stating, “Required fields may vary based on client setup for New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides” displays. • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have current coverage or prior coverage history: The record is skipped and the following error message displays: “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID [Dependent ID Number] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with it.” A variation of this same message displays when multiple dependent records with current coverage or prior coverage history must be skipped for the same employee: “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID’s [Dependent ID Numbers separated by a comma] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with them.” • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have no current coverage or prior coverage history associated with it: The record is deleted. This validation works similar to the validation logic used when you attempt to manually delete a dependent with coverage history from the system. In that instance, a message displays indicating that you cannot delete the record but you can mark it Inactive.

Importing Offer Types You can use this import template to import/update offer types for existing benefit plans. This will save time and effort to manually add/update the Offer Type field on the Group Benefit Plans form. (If you try to modify any other field using this process, you will receive an error.) Note the following: • This import template is only available to service providers. • Client Access Group Security is not enabled on this form.

To import and update offer types:

  1. To access this form, click (Back Office). In the Operations|Import menu, click Data Import Tool.
  2. Select Offer Types in Import Template. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Data File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) The layout requirements are:

Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 350 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

Category Description • Plan ID (required): Unique identifier for the benefit plan. • Plan Description (required): Description of the benefit plan. • Insurance Class (required): Indicates the type of coverage this plan provides. • Offer Type (required): Indicates the offer type that classifies the benefit plan.

Required? Indicates if the field is required.

  1. Click Download Data File to download the sample header file. The header file contains the four columns in the File Format tab. Fill in the necessary data for all the Benefit Plan IDs to update the Offer Type to build your Import file. Note: If you want to update the Offer Type for all Benefit Plan IDs in bulk that do not have an associated offer type, select Prepopulate file (all plans with BLANK Offer Type). The system downloads a .csv file to your system that is pre-populated with data from the Group Benefit Plans for all plans with a BLANK offer type. (If you do not select this field, the system downloads the file with headers only.)
  2. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.
  3. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.
  4. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File displays in the File Upload dialog box.
  5. Click Start Upload to upload the file.
  6. Click Close in the File Upload dialog box.
  7. The uploaded Import File name displays in the File Name field on the form. The content of the file displays in the File Content tab. Errors, if any, display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process.
  8. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR.
  9. Click Report to display the Imported Offer Types Report. The Import Status column indicates whether the offer type for that plan ID was imported. If not, then the Messages tab states the reason why. Once the import is successful, the system updates the Offer Type field on the Group Benefit Plans form with the plans contained in the Import File.

Importing Plan Comparison Data You can import benefit plan comparison information into the Comparison Field tab of the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form (Workflow Setup > Benefits Specific > Benefits Enrollment Plan Details). Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 351 Chapter 6 Importing Benefits

To upload and import plan comparison data, do the following:

  1. Click (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processingmenu.

  2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Plan Comparison Data import template option. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it. The sample file contains the Plan ID and Effective Date columns plus additional columns based on the Category Descriptions found for the selected Offer Type. It also includes additional fields at the end of the sample header file which can be imported into the fields in the Additional Plan Details section on the Benefit Enrollment Plan Details form. For a particular Offer Type, you can view the names of the fields in the Additional Plan Details section of the Benefit Enrollment Plan Details form under the Category Description column on the Data Import Tool form.) The layout requirements are: Field Description Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data. Category Description • Plan ID (required): Unique identifiers for the Benefit Plan IDs being compared. • Effective Date (required): Effective dates for the benefit plans being compared. Note: Additional Category Descriptions may appear in the file layout. These represent optional columns and will vary based on the Category Descriptions found on the Details tab of the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form for the selected Offer Type. Required? Indicates if the field is required.

  3. Before you import, you must complete the following required field. Use this option To define this Offer Type The benefit Offer Type associated with the plans you are comparing. Example: Medical, Vision, or Dental.

Chapter 7 Enrolling Employees in Retirement Plans To enroll employees in retirement plans, use the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. When an employee is enrolled in a retirement plan, PrismHR automatically adds the deduction to the employee’s deduction form. You can access other information and settings using the Actions menu: • Loan Details: View information about the employee’s retirement loans. • Enrollment Audit: View information about the employee’s retirement plan enrollment. • Details Audit: View information about the employee’s retirement plan deductions.

Retirement Plan Enrollment Use the Retirement Plan Enrollment form to enroll employees in retirement plans. Once the employee is enrolled in a retirement plan, PrismHR automatically adds the deduction to the employee’s deduction form. Use the panels to specify the plan information for the employee: • Setting General Retirement Plan Enrollment Information (page 353) • Defining Financial Details for Retirement Plan Enrollment (page 355) • Establishing Election Details (page 355) • Including and Excluding Pay Codes for Retirement Plan Enrollment (page 358) • Defining Extra Contributions for Retirement Plan Enrollment (page 359) • Defining Override and Deferral Limits for Retirement Plan Enrollment (page 360) • Adding or Editing Employee Retirement Loans (page 360) • Creating or Editing Retirement Register Adjustments (page 361) You can access other information and settings using the Actions menu : • Enrollment Audit: View information about the employee’s retirement plan enrollment. • Details Audit: View information about the employee’s retirement plan deductions.

Setting General Retirement Plan Enrollment Information To set up general retirement plan information for an employee, use the Retirement Plan Enrollment panel in the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 353 Chapter 7 Enrolling Employees in Retirement Plans

A Quicklink to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form is on the top right of the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, which will display only after the Employee and the Retirement Plan fields are selected on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. This provides ease of access to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form for the selected employee directly from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. When you click the Quicklink to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. The Employee Retirement Plan Register form opens in a modal where: • The Employee ID field is auto-populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. • The Plan ID drop-down field will have all the retirement plans for the employee selected on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. You can select one of them. • The Employee Retirement Plan Register modal form behaves the same way as the regular Employee Retirement Plan Register form. You can select the other fields as necessary to view the relevant information.

Note: This Quicklink will not be visible if you do not have access to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form.

Adding or Editing Employee Retirement Loans You can use this form to directly access existing employee retirement loan information for the selected Employee. If an employee has been in more than one retirement plan, only those Employee Retirement Loans that were processed for the selected Retirement Plan field will display. This section lists the employee retirement loans for the selected employee in an ascending order by Loan No. by default. This grid has the following columns: • Loan No. • Loan Amount • Loan Date • Deduction Start Date • Payment Amount • Pay Back Amount • Override Payment Amount • Override From Pay Date • Override To Pay Date • Paid Back To Date • Balance Due You can click on any of the column headers in the grid to sort the retirement loans as you choose.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 360 Chapter 7 Enrolling Employees in Retirement Plans

• Click a Loan No. from the list to open the loan details on the Employee Retirement Loans modal form with all corresponding data pre-populated that is tied to the Loan No. selected. • The Loan Number, Employee and the Retirement Plan fields are read only and populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. • You can edit the other fields for this retirement loan. • Click Set up new loan to set up a new retirement loan for the selected employee on the Employee Retirement Loans modal form. • The Loan Number is pre-populated with a system generated number. You cannot edit this. • The Employee and the Retirement Plan fields are read only and auto-populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form You cannot edit this. • Enter the other required fields for this new retirement loan for this employee. • Click Save to save the new retirement loan for the employee. After saving the new retirement loan, it will appear in the list under the Employee Retirement Loans section on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

You can access existing employee retirement register adjustment information for the selected Employee, client, and Retirement Plan. If an employee has been in more than one retirement plan, only those Retirement Register Adjustments that were processed for the selected Retirement Plan field will display. Performing Bulk Changes to Retirement Plans Use the Bulk Change Retirement Plan form to perform a bulk change to retirement plan enrollment records from one plan to another. This operation updates the Plan ID on each employee’s plan enrollment record. Associated retirement plan loan records and standard deduction records are also updated with the new plan ID and deduction codes. You can run this process for all companies or for a single company.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To perform a bulk retirement plan change for a group of employees: 1. On the Back Office menu, select Operations|Action > Bulk Change Retirement Plan. 2. Click From Retirement Plan to select the plan ID you want to change.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 363 Chapter 7 Enrolling Employees in Retirement Plans

  1. Click To Retirement Plan to select the plan ID you want to switch to.
  2. Select a client (optional).
  3. Click Update.
  4. The system displays a pop-up window with a preview of the changes that is to be made by the program, including From code tp To Code for each deduction type, counts of clients, employees, and deduction records impacted, and errors expected from running the process.
  5. Click Yes to complete the update to all indicated records.
  6. Clicking No if you do not want to make update. You will be returned to the original screen without any changes.

Retirement Plan Termination In PrismHR, the process for terminating a retirement plan involves navigating to the Benefit Plan Setup and updating the plan to reflect the desired stop date. You must also make all employee retirement enrollments inactive to ensure that deductions cease. Currently, PrismHR does not offer a bulk method for making employee retirement enrollments inactive, and this task must be performed manually through the Retirement Plan Enrollment section on an individual employee basis.

Step One: Terminate a Retirement Plan To terminate a retirement plan: 1. Open the Benefit Plan Setup form (Benefit Plan Maintenance > Group Benefit Plans (Client) > Benefit Plan Setup) and display the plan you want to terminate by specifying a Plan Class of Retirement and then selecting the Plan.

  1. Enter the desired Stop Date (termination date).
  2. Click Save.

Step Two: Mark Employee Retirement Enrollments Inactive To mark employee retirement enrollments Inactive: 1. Open the Retirement Plan Enrollment form (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Retirement Enrollments > Retirement Plan Enrollment) and display the employee whose retirement enrollments you want to make Inactive by selecting the Employee and the Retirement Plan. 2. Then, change the Status to Inactive Enrollment. (Your setup may vary. If you do not see an Inactive Enrollment option, select an equivalent option for “Inactive”.) 3. Click Save. 4. Repeat the above steps for each employee where you want to mark retirement enrollments Inactive.

Chapter 9 Using Benefit Billing Options This article describes how to use benefit billing and how to set up the necessary bill codes in PrismHR.

Benefit Billing Scenarios There are three common scenarios for benefit billing in PrismHR:

Scenario 1: PEO-sponsored benefit plan, used by the client • Description: The PEO sponsors a benefit plan which the client uses (alternately, the PEO manages the funds for the client’s provider). The PEO pays the full cost of the benefit plan to the plan provider, then bills the client for this payment. The PEO then deducts employee contributions to the benefit plan, and reimburses the client for this contribution. • Requirements: Do the following:

 Action                                     Description
 Set up bill code                           You must set up a bill code on the benefit plan in the Group
                                            Benefit Plans form. The bill code handles both billing the client for
                                            the amount paid to the plan provider as well as reimbursement of
                                            employee contributions to the client.
 Set up standard deduction                  You must set up a standard deduction code in the Deduction
 code                                       Codes form to deduct employee contributions for the benefit plan.
 Set up above deduction code                You must set up the above deduction code with no value in the
 with no value                              Client Bill Rate Code field. A deduction code that includes a value
                                            would reimburse employee deductions twice to the client since
                                            the bill code already handles both billing and reimbursement.

Scenario 2: Client-sponsored benefit plan • Description: The client sponsors its own plan. The client pays the full cost of the benefit plan to the plan provider. Since the client pays for the benefit plan directly, the PEO does not bill the client for the cost of the benefit plan. The PEO deducts employee contributions, then reimburses the client for these contributions. • Requirements: Do the following:

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 380 Chapter 10 Using the Hawaii 1.5% Rule

Chapter 10 Using the Hawaii 1.5% Rule In Hawaii, an employer can elect to pay the entire premium amount or share the cost with the employee. The employer must pay for at least one-half of the (single) premium cost, however, the employee’s contribution cannot exceed 1.5% of the employee’s monthly wages.

Requirements Within a payroll batch, the system processes this calculation for employees who meet the following requirements: • The employee’s resident state is Hawaii • The employee has not waived their right to medical coverage. You can set medical waiver information for employees on the Employee Details form Other tab. For more information, see the Human Resources User Guide. For the purpose of this calculation, a “wage” is defined as any pay code with a pay classification of Earnings.

Note: This assumption is based on the definition of wages found in the Hawaii Revised Statutes from the Hawaii Department of Labor, Chapter 388, which specifically states that wages do not include tips or gratuities of any kind.

Calculation The calculation uses the following information in all reports that cover employee premium contributions:

Field Description Employee Contribution The amount the employee is scheduled to contribute towards the cost of single coverage, based on the defined benefit rule. Employee Premium The pay period amount the employee is scheduled to contribute Contribution towards the cost of single coverage. Employee MTD The month-to-date amount contributed by the employee towards the Contribution cost of the benefit premium.

•    The system processes the deductions for a regular batch, or special batch that is taking the place of a
     regular batch.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 381 Deduction Periods for Vacation Pay Vouchers

•    The system takes the deduction only from regular and vacation vouchers.
•    The system then checks to make sure that the currently scheduled employee contribution for an active
     medical plan does not exceed 1.5% of the employee’s current earnings. In doing this, it also calculates
     month-to-date earnings and employee contributions, and makes adjustments to the employee’s
     contribution either upward or downward throughout the month.

For example, if the employee’s wages are low in the first two pay periods of the month, the system reduces the employee’s scheduled contribution so that the contribution does not exceed 1.5% of earnings. If the employee is given a large bonus in the third pay period of the month, the system increases the scheduled contribution on the current voucher up to the amount that equals 1.5% of month-to-date wages to make up for the shortfall in the first two periods. This adjustment is done on a monthly basis. The system does not carry over any shortfall or overage into the next month.

Note: To determine the scheduled month-to-date contributions at each pay period in the month, this calculation logic relies on the deduction periods. Be sure that the deduction periods defined in the payroll are defined correctly and in a linear fashion.

Deduction Periods for Vacation Pay Vouchers It is critical that if vacation is paid in future pay periods, the deduction periods for those vacation pay vouchers must be defined correctly. You can set deduction periods in the Vacation Pay Override form. For more information, see the Payroll Overrides Guide.

Setting Up Override Rates for Hawaii TDI Tax Use the Hawaii TDI Override Rates form to set up the override rates for Temporary Disability Insurance (TDI) tax for the state of Hawaii that is provided by the TDI insurance carrier. The state of Hawaii requires that employees and employers pay into the state’s temporary disability insurance fund. While this fund is not a tax in its truest form, as this is not a program administered by the state of Hawaii but rather a mandate by the state to use an applicable TDI insurance carrier like we see with Workers Compensation.

Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form.

To access the form, click Back Office. Under System|Change, click Hawaii TDI Override Rates.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 383 Setting Up Deduction Start Dates

Setting Up Deduction Start Dates When an employee enrolls in a benefit plan, the deduction typically starts on the first day of the following month. The system sets the start date in this way so the deduction amount associated with the benefit plan is always for a full month. For example, if an employee enrolls in the month of January, deductions begin on February 1st, and the company creates a benefit billing adjustment for January. The system adjusts the amount for the actual number of days that the employee was covered.

Note: Some plans allow mid-month enrollment, which means coverage may start on any day of the month.

Deduction start dates begin on the first day of the following month with benefit adjustments when either of the following are true: • The coverage start date for the benefit plan is before the current date. For example, if an employee enrolls on 01/11/2017 in a benefit plan that has a coverage start date of 01/01/2017, the system sets the deduction start date for the benefit plan to 02/01/2017. • A payroll batch has been created with a pay date that is after the coverage start date. For example, if an employee enrolls in a benefit plan that has a coverage start date of 01/01/2017, and a payroll batch is already created for the month of January, the system sets the deduction start date for the benefit plan to 02/01/2017. In both of these scenarios, benefit adjustments are created to cover the deductions for the month of January. Benefit adjustments are based on the pay period for benefit billing frequency and payroll deduction frequency, even if the plan has designated a monthly benefit billing frequency.

Changing Deduction Start Dates and Benefit Adjustments The recommended best practice is to enroll the employee in benefits prior to their effective date, and use the system defaults for deduction start date and benefit adjustments. You can, however, modify the deduction start date and/or benefit adjustments as follows:

Chapter 11 Setting Up Composite Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefit Plans This section explains how to set up composite benefit plans for the medical, dental, and vision insurance classes at the system level in PrismHR. Settings in Group Benefit Plans To create and maintain benefit plans, use the Group Benefit Plans form.

General Settings in Group Benefit Plans To establish the basic parameters of the group benefit plan, use the Group Benefit Plans form. The Offer Type is required if your organization uses Benefits Enrollment. 1. Enter the Benefit Plan ID. If you are creating a new plan, use an ID that briefly describes the plan. 2. Enter the Plan Description. 3. Select the Insurance Class (Medical, Dental, or Vision) that indicates the type of coverage this plan provides. This affects which panels display, what fields are available, and the calculation method the system uses in deriving the premium for the benefit plan. 4. Enter the Payee ID of the benefits provider that receives the deducted amounts. If you need to define a new payee for this benefit provider, open the Actions menu and select Payees. 5. Select the Cost Basis associated with any premiums and contribution amounts for this benefit plan. Refer to this field when changing premium rates or assigning employee overrides.

Note: Some companies offer their employees a set amount of life insurance coverage, and the option to buy more at the employee’s expense. The manual premium calculation allows you to manually enter the employee’s individual premium and contribution on the employee enrollment record. Manual premiums can also apply to some medical plans that do not have set premiums.

Setting Up Premium Rates You can access the Premium Rates form in the Actions menu of Group Benefit Plans. The rates you enter here are the actual premium rates charged to your organization by the insurance carrier. The fields that display vary depending on the plan’s Insurance Class and other options selected in Group Benefit Plans. The rates entered correspond to the Cost Basis field in the Group Benefit Plans form. For example, if the Cost Basis field is set to Monthly, the rates represent monthly premium costs.

To set up premium rates: 1. The Benefit Plan ID populates from the Group Benefit Plan form. 2. Select the Plan Type. The drop-down lists only the plan types defined for the group benefit plan. 3. Enter a new Effective Date, or select an existing one on the right (if any). Unless the benefit plan is also set up as age banded by selecting the Age Banded Medical Billing option in Group Benefit Plans, you must enter a one-line “all encompassing” age range in the From Age and To Age fields, for example, 0-99. 4. For each age range: • Enter the From Age for each line, which is the starting age. • Enter the To Age, which is the upper age limit. • Enter the Total Premium amount billed to the client for the benefit rate level. • Enter the Employee Premium cost for the plan type and age group. • If applicable, enter the Dependents Premium cost associated with covering an employee’s dependents for this plan type and age group. The Total Premium field is the sum of the Employee Premium and Dependents Premium. Once you enter two values, the third calculates automatically. For example, if you enter a Total Premium of 500 and an Employee Premium of 300, the system populates Dependents Premium with 200. 5. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type. 6. Repeat these steps for each plan type set up in the Plan Types panel in Group Benefits Plans. 7. Click Close when you are finished.

Optional Settings The following are common optional settings for medical, dental, and vision plans in Group Benefit Plans.

Settings in Group Benefit Plans Panel Use settings described below to establish whether the plan is: • Section 125 Electable if this benefit can be elected for flexible spending plans. If you select this option, you must also enter the prepay benefit account numbers in the 125 Deduction Code field. • COBRA Electable if this benefit plan can be elected for COBRA coverage. • A High Deductible Plan (HDHP) if this health benefit plan has a high deductible which might entitle the employee to participate in a health savings account (HSA).

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 389 Settings in Other Processing Parameters Panel

Settings in Other Processing Parameters Panel Use these settings to establish: • Dependent age limits • Disability coverage eligibility • Mid-month coverage

Dependent Age Limit and Disabled Dependent Eligibility Enter the Dependent’s Age Limit; if the dependent reaches that age limit before the plan effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage. The value selected in the drop-down determines when the dependent age limit actually becomes effective: • On Date of Birth (DOB): The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on the dependent’s birth date when the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 6, 2017. If this date falls before the plan’s effective date, the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage and will not be able to enroll. • End of DOB Year: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on January 1st of the year the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on January 1, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage and will not be able to enroll.

Note: This means that the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage in the benefit plan even though the dependent’s actual age has not yet reached the age limit specified.

• End of DOB month: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective at the end of the month the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 390 PCP Information Setting in the Web Enrollment Parameters Panel

April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017. If this date is before the plan's
effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll.

Note: If the plan effective date falls before the date the dependent’s age limit becomes effective (for example, if the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017 and the plan effective date is April 25, 2017) the dependent will still be considered eligible for coverage and will be able to enroll even if the dependent’s actual age has reached age limit specified.

• Select Disabled Dependent Eligible and specify a Disabled Alt Age Limit to establish benefit eligibility for disabled dependents who are above the age specified in the Dependent’s Age Limit field and who would otherwise be ineligible for coverage.

Mid-Month Coverage Setting • Select Mid-Month Coverage Dates if the benefit plan allows for mid-month coverage start/stop dates. Otherwise, coverage starts on the first day of the month and ends on the last day of the month.

PCP Information Setting in the Web Enrollment Parameters Panel If this is a benefit plan which requires employees to enter primary care physician (PCP) information during enrollments, select Collect PCP Information . Typically these are health maintenance organization (HMO) medical plans, but some dental plans might also require this information. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) If selected, you must also specify a URL where employees can look up their PCP in the PCP Lists field in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form; For more information, refer to Benefits Enrollment Plan Details in the Benefits Enrollment User Guide. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Settings in States Offered In Panel A medical, dental, or vision benefit plan that is state banded is only offered in certain states. In the States Offered column, enter the two-character state codes for each state where this benefit plan is offered. The State Name displays. 2. Enter the Plan Number for each state.

Setting Up Eligible ZIP Codes To enter eligible locations by ZIP code, use the Eligible ZIP Codes form.

Note: This form is accessed by selecting Eligible ZIP Codes in the Actions menu in Group benefit Plans, and is used only for benefit plans that are not set up to collect network information.

Only those employee home locations that match the ZIP codes on the plan will be eligible for enrollment. If no ZIP codes are entered for the benefit plan, employees will be able to enroll regardless of home location. 1. Enter the ZIP Codes you want to attach to the benefit plan. The City and State displays. 2. Click Save.

  1. Select Premium Rates Vary By Network if premium rates are maintained separately for each network.

Select Include in Open Enrollments to use this plan for open enrollments. 2. Enter the Insurance Carrier URL, which is the link to the page that provides detail about the insurance carrier. 3. Enter the Plan Description URL, which is the link to the plan description page. 4. Select Approval Required to automatically set an initial status of Pending in the Status field of the Employee Group Benefits form. 5. Enter the Display Benefit Type, which is the code used for display grouping. 6. The code Description displays.

If ZIP Codes Exist in the system for the network ID, Yes displays.

  1. To deactivate the network at the system level, select Yes from the Inactive drop-down.

Setting Up Benefit Network Locations When you select the Collect Network Information option in the Other Processing Parameters panel, the Benefit Network Locations form becomes available and can be accessed by selecting Network ZIP Codes in Actions menu . This is where you can manually enter network ZIP codes for the benefit plan. You can also use the Network ZIP Codes Import to import multiple ZIP codes to benefit plans that have a network assigned.

Required ZIP Code Validation All ZIP codes must first be entered at the system-level to be attached to a benefit plan. ZIP code records that are in the system will always display City & State information in the table. If city and state information does not display, it means the ZIP code record does not exist at the system-level. Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 402 Network Zip Codes

The import form will allow you to save the imported record without error, but when you view the benefit plan’s networks in the Benefit Network Locations form by selecting the Network ID, the system will display the error message “Warning - Key [ZIP code] is not valid for ZIP codes” for each ZIP code that cannot be validated. It is recommended that you review and update all ZIP code records in the Zip Codes form, either manually or by using the import. Once a ZIP code record is in the system, you can attach it to a benefit plan. For more information, refer to ZIP Codes in the System Administration Guide.

Network Zip Codes To enter locations by ZIP code for benefit plans that have a network assigned, use the Network Zip Codes form, accessed by selecting Network ZIP Codes in the Actions menu from the Group Benefit Plans form. This form only displays in the Actions menu when the Collect Network Information option in the Other Processing Parameters panel is selected. Users can also import multiple locations using the Network ZIP Code Import form.

To set up locations for a benefit plan with an assigned network: 1. The Benefit Plan ID is prepopulated from the Group Benefit Plans form. 2. Select a Network ID from the drop-down. This is required. 3. In the ZIP Codes column, enter the five-digit ZIP code where this benefit plan is offered. The City & State will display if the ZIP code exists in the system. You can enter multiple ZIP Codes as needed: click + to add additional rows. 4. Click Save.

Network ZIP Codes Import To import ZIP codes to benefit plans that have a network assigned, use the Network ZIP Codes Import form. The imported file must be a comma-delimited (.CSV) file and include headers that describe the contents of each column. 1. Enter the Plan ID for the benefit plan. 2. Select the Network to which you want to import the ZIP codes. 3. Click Start Import. The Upload window displays. 4. Click Choose File, and select the file to upload. 5. Click Submit. The imported data displays. If the file contains invalid information, an error report displays in the form. • To view the data in the form, click Done with Errors. • To scroll through the report as needed, click Next Page and Previous Page. • To discard the data, click Cancel at any time. 6. To complete the import, click Post Data. The imported ZIP codes will display in a table.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 403 Setting Up Premium Rates for Network Banded Plans

Setting Up Premium Rates for Network Banded Plans You can access the Premium Rates form in the Actions menu of Group Benefit Plans. The rates you enter here are the actual premium rates charged to your organization by the insurance carrier. The fields that display vary depending on the plan’s Insurance Class and other options selected in Group Benefit Plans. The rates entered correspond to the Cost Basis field in the Group Benefit Plans form. For example, if the Cost Basis field is set to Monthly, the rates represent monthly premium costs.

To set up premium rates for network banded plans: 1. The Benefit Plan ID populates from the Group Benefit Plan form. 2. Select the Network ID. The Network ID field displays when the Premium Rates Vary By Network option in the Other Processing Parameters panel is selected. 3. Select the Plan Type. The drop-down lists only the plan types defined for the group benefit plan.

Note: Saving rates according to the effective date allows you to view previous rates for reference purposes. The system calculates premium costs using the premium rates with the most recent effective date.

  1. Enter a new Effective Date, or select an existing one on the right (if any). Unless the benefit plan is also set up as age banded by selecting the Age Banded Medical Billing option in Group Benefit Plans, you must enter a one-line “all encompassing” age range in the From Age and To Age fields, for example, 0-99.
  2. For each age range: • Enter the From Age for each line, which is the starting age. • Enter the To Age, which is the upper age limit. • Enter the Total Premium amount billed to the client for the benefit rate level. • Enter the Employee Premium cost for the plan type and age group. • If applicable, enter the Dependents Premium cost associated with covering an employee’s dependents for this plan type and age group. The Total Premium field is the sum of the Employee Premium and Dependents Premium. Once you enter two values, the third calculates automatically. For example, if you enter a Total Premium of 500 and an Employee Premium of 300, the system populates Dependents Premium with 200.
  3. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter the premiums for another plan type.
  4. Repeat these steps for each plan type set up in the Plan Types panel in Group Benefit Plans.
  5. Click Close when you are finished.

  1. Select the Network ID.
