Note: Unless the benefit plan is also set up as age banded by selecting the Age Banded Medical Billing option in Group Benefit Plans, you must enter a one-line “all encompassing” age range in the From Age and To Age fields, for example, 0-99.

  1. For each age range:
    1. Enter the From Age for each line, which is the starting age.
    2. Enter the To Age, which is the upper age limit.

Note: The Total Bill Amount field is the sum of the Employee Bill Amount and Dependents Bill Amount. Once you enter two values, the third calculates automatically. c. Enter the Total Bill Amount to bill to the client for the cost of this plan.
d. Enter the Employee Bill Amount for this plan.

  1. Click Save. The form clears so that you can enter billing rates for another plan type.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 405 Settings in Group Benefit Plans Panel

Settings in Group Benefit Plans Panel Use settings described below to establish whether the plan is: • Section 125 Electable if this benefit can be elected for flexible spending plans. If you select this option, you must also enter the prepay benefit account numbers in the 125 Deduction Code field. • COBRA Electable if this benefit plan can be elected for COBRA coverage. • A High Deductible Plan (HDHP) if this health benefit plan has a high deductible which might entitle the employee to participate in a health savings account (HSA).

Settings in Other Processing Parameters Panel Use these settings to establish: • Dependent age limits • Disability coverage eligibility • Mid-month coverage

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 406 PCP Information Setting in the Web Enrollment Parameters Panel

Dependent Age Limit and Disabled Dependent Eligibility Enter the Dependent’s Age Limit; if the dependent reaches that age limit before the plan effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage. The value selected in the drop-down determines when the dependent age limit actually becomes effective: • On Date of Birth (DOB): The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on the dependent’s birth date when the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 6, 2017. If this date falls before the plan’s effective date, the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage and will not be able to enroll. • End of DOB Year: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on January 1st of the year the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on January 1, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage and will not be able to enroll.

Note: This means that the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage in the benefit plan even though the dependent’s actual age has not yet reached the age limit specified.

• End of DOB month: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective at the end of the month the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll.

Note: If the plan effective date falls before the date the dependent’s age limit becomes effective (for example, if the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017 and the plan effective date is April 25, 2017) the dependent will still be considered eligible for coverage and will be able to enroll even if the dependent’s actual age has reached age limit specified.

• Select Disabled Dependent Eligible and specify a Disabled Alt Age Limit to establish benefit eligibility for disabled dependents who are above the age specified in the Dependent’s Age Limit field and who would otherwise be ineligible for coverage.

Mid-Month Coverage Setting • Select Mid-Month Coverage Dates if the benefit plan allows for mid-month coverage start/stop dates. Otherwise, coverage starts on the first day of the month and ends on the last day of the month.

PCP Information Setting in the Web Enrollment Parameters Panel

If this is a benefit plan which requires employees to enter primary care physician (PCP) information during enrollments, select Collect PCP Information . Typically these are health maintenance organization (HMO) medical plans, but some dental plans might also require this information. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 407 Settings in States Offered In Panel

If selected, you must also specify a URL where employees can look up their PCP in the PCP Lists field in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form; refer to “Benefits Enrollment Plan Details” in the Benefits Enrollment User Guide for more information. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Settings in States Offered In Panel A medical, dental, or vision benefit plan that is state banded is only offered in certain states. You can use the States Offered In panel to list the states in which this type of benefit plan is offered. 1. In the States Offered column, enter the two-character state codes for each state where this benefit plan is offered. The State Name displays. 2. Enter the Plan Number for each state.

Enter the Plan Description URL, which is the link to the plan description page. 4. Select Approval Required to automatically set an initial status of Pending in the Status field of the Employee Group Benefits form. 5. Enter the Display Benefit Type, which is the code used for display grouping. 6. If this is a benefit plan which requires employees to enter primary care physician (PCP) information during enrollments, select Collect PCP Information . (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) For more information about other required PCP information settings in Benefits Enrollment, see Optional Settings on page 426. 7. In the table, enter each Process Attribute code that applies to the benefit plan. The code Description displays.

Enter each plan Type Code applicable to this benefit plan. The Plan Type Description displays.

Spouse Gender: The employee spouse’s gender (Male, Female). 5. Enter a new Effective Date, or select an existing one on the right (if any).

Note: Unless the benefit plan is also set up as age banded by selecting the Age Banded Medical Billing option in Group Benefit Plans, you must enter a one-line “all encompassing” age range in the From Age and To Age fields, for example, 0-99.

Optional Settings The following are common optional settings for medical, dental, and vision plans in Group Benefit Plans.

Settings in Group Benefit Plans Panel Use settings described below to establish whether the plan is: • Section 125 Electable if this benefit can be elected for flexible spending plans. If you select this option, you must also enter the prepay benefit account numbers in the 125 Deduction Code field. • COBRA Electable if this benefit plan can be elected for COBRA coverage. • A High Deductible Plan (HDHP) if this health benefit plan has a high deductible which might entitle the employee to participate in a health savings account (HSA).

Settings in Other Processing Parameters Panel Use these settings to establish: • Dependent age limits • Disability coverage eligibility • Mid-month coverage

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 420 Settings in Other Processing Parameters Panel

Dependent Age Limit and Disabled Dependent Eligibility Enter the Dependent’s Age Limit; if the dependent reaches that age limit before the plan effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage. The value selected in the drop-down determines when the dependent age limit actually becomes effective: • On Date of Birth (DOB): The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on the dependent’s birth date when the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 6, 2017. If this date falls before the plan’s effective date, the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage and will not be able to enroll. • End of DOB Year: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective on January 1st of the year the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on January 1, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage and will not be able to enroll.

Note: This means that the dependent will no longer be eligible for coverage in the benefit plan even though the dependent’s actual age has not yet reached the age limit specified.

• End of DOB month: The dependent’s age limit becomes effective at the end of the month the dependent reaches the age limit specified. For example, if the age limit specified is 25, and the dependent turns 25 on April 6, 2017, the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017. If this date is before the plan’s effective date, the dependent is no longer eligible for coverage and cannot enroll.

Note: If the plan effective date falls before the date the dependent’s age limit becomes effective (for example, if the dependent age limit becomes effective on April 30, 2017 and the plan effective date is April 25, 2017) the dependent will still be considered eligible for coverage and will be able to enroll even if the dependent’s actual age has reached age limit specified.

Benefits Administration User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 421 PCP Information Setting in the Web Enrollment Parameters Panel

• Select Disabled Dependent Eligible and specify a Disabled Alt Age Limit to establish benefit eligibility for disabled dependents who are above the age specified in the Dependent’s Age Limit field and who would otherwise be ineligible for coverage.

Mid-Month Coverage Setting • Select Mid-Month Coverage Dates if the benefit plan allows for mid-month coverage start/stop dates. Otherwise, coverage starts on the first day of the month and ends on the last day of the month.

PCP Information Setting in the Web Enrollment Parameters Panel If this is a benefit plan which requires employees to enter primary care physician (PCP) information during enrollments, select Collect PCP Information . Typically these are health maintenance organization (HMO) medical plans, but some dental plans might also require this information. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) If selected, you must also specify a URL where employees can look up their PCP in the PCP Lists field in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form; For more information, refer to Benefits Enrollment Plan Details in the Benefits Enrollment User Guide. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Settings in States Offered In Panel A medical, dental, or vision benefit plan that is state banded is only offered in certain states. To list the states in which this type of benefit plan is offered, you can use the States Offered In panel. 1. In the States Offered column, enter the two-character state codes for each state where this benefit plan is offered. The State Name displays. 2. Enter the Plan Number for each state.

Setting Up Eligible ZIP Codes To enter eligible locations by ZIP code, use the Eligible ZIP Codes form.

Note: This form is accessed by selecting Eligible ZIP Codes in the Actions menu in Group benefit Plans, and is used only for benefit plans that are not set up to collect network information.

Only those employee home locations that match the ZIP codes on the plan will be eligible for enrollment. If no ZIP codes are entered for the benefit plan, employees will be able to enroll regardless of home location. 1. Enter the ZIP Codes you want to attach to the benefit plan. The City and State displays. 2. Click Save.

Required ZIP Code Validation All ZIP codes must first be entered at the system-level to be attached to a benefit plan. If you enter a ZIP code that is not in the system, an error message displays. You can correct this by entering the ZIP code at the system-level in the Zip Codes form. Once the ZIP code record is in the system, you can then attach it to the benefit plan. For more information, refer to ZIP Codes in the System Administration Guide.

Chapter 16 Setting Up Tobacco Banded Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefit Plans This section is a guide to setting up tobacco banded benefit plans for the medical, dental, and vision insurance classes at the system level in PrismHR. Enter the Plan Description. 3. Select the Insurance Class (Medical, Dental, or Vision) that indicates the type of coverage this plan provides. This affects which panels display, what fields are available, and the calculation method the system uses in deriving the premium for the benefit plan. 4. Enter the Payee ID of the benefits provider that receives the deducted amounts. If you need to define a new payee for this benefit provider, open the Actions menu and select Payees. 5. Select the Cost Basis associated with any premiums and contribution amounts for this benefit plan. Refer to this field when changing premium rates or assigning employee overrides.

Note: Some companies offer their employees a set amount of life insurance coverage, and the option to buy more at the employee’s expense. Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 10 Intended Audience The contents are for users who are: • Using Benefits Enrollment • Involved in setting up benefit enrollments • Familiar with the use of an internet browser

Note: Unless you have permission to access System Administration features, you cannot set global benefit plans on the system.

Your organization should already have set up the initial defaults, files, and preferences required for system administration, as well as client information. This user guide assumes that you already have a certain amount of knowledge about benefits administration. Before you can set up benefits and open enrollments, you must set up benefit plans at the system level. You must also set up benefit groups and benefit rules for clients, including eligibility and coverage rules, and employee contributions. The procedures for setting up benefits can be very complex, and it is beyond the scope of this user guide to cover them in detail. These subjects are covered in the Benefit Administration User Guide. Explaining industry-specific topics other than the use of this software product is outside the scope of this document.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 11 Chapter 1 Configuring System Settings

Chapter 1 Configuring System Settings The following sections describe system-level settings that are specific to setting up benefits and open enrollments. You must define these settings for benefit plan information to display correctly during enrollments.

Assigning Offer Types You must assign an offer type to each benefit plan offered to employees during benefit enrollments. The offer type classifies the benefit plan according to type (for example, Medical, Dental, Vision) and assures that the benefit plan displays in the correct form during benefit enrollments. If benefit plans are not assigned offer types, you cannot include them in benefits enrollment.

To assign offer types on group benefit plans: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Group Benefit Plans. The Group Benefit Plans form opens.

To assign offer types on flexible spending account (FSA), health saving account (HSA), and commuter (COM) benefit plans: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Flex Spend Account Types. The Group Benefit Plans form opens. Refer to the Benefit Administration User Guide for more information about settings in the Group Benefit Plans and Flex Spend Account Types forms.

Maintaining Enrollment Details To perform the following functions, use the Plan Enrollment Details form. • Define gap coverage amounts in gap (GAP) benefit plans. • Enable employees to set up beneficiary information in life insurance plans during enrollments. • Set up dependencies in accidental death and dismemberment (ADD) or group term life (GTL) insurance plans that require employees to enroll in a basic life (LIF) insurance plan. • Establish settings in long term disability (LTD) or short term disability (STD) benefit plans that determine when an employee is required to submit an Evidence of Insurability (EOI) form.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 12 Chapter 1 Configuring System Settings

Accessing Plan Enrollment Details The offer type for a benefit plan determines the options that are available in the Plan Enrollment Details form.

To access the Plan Enrollment Details form: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Group Benefit Plans. The Group Benefit Plans form opens. 3. Select a Benefit Plan ID. 4. Click the Actions menu and select Enrollment Details. The Plan Enrollment Details form opens. You cannot search for this form by normal means. 5. Here, the Benefit Plan ID is auto-populated based on the benefit plan you select on the Group Benefit Plans form. It is a read-only form. 6. Make the required updates on the form and click Save.

Defining Gap Coverage in Gap Plans The options that are available when you select a gap (GAP) benefit plan enable you to define the gap coverage amount for the plan. You can also restrict employees who are enrolled in health savings account (HSA) benefit plans from also enrolling in gap benefit plans.

Before you begin: • Set up the gap benefit plan to require a medical dependency at the plan level in the Plan Dependency tab in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form.

To define gap coverage in gap benefit plans: 1. Open the Plan Enrollment Details form.

Required Documentation Rulesets The Required Documentation Rulesets panel displays for some offer types. You can use this panel to assign one or more required documentation rulesets to a benefit plan. Employees who fit the conditions of the ruleset during enrollments must download and submit an additional form. For more information on Required Documentation Rulesets, see Assigning Documentation Rulesets.

Assigning Documentation Rulesets To assign one or more required documentation rulesets to a benefit plan, use the Required Documentation Rulesets panel in the Plan Enrollment Details form. Benefits Enrollment provides the following rulesets: • Domestic Partner • Dependents with Different Last Names • Disabled Dependents • Disabled Over-Age Dependents (Florida residents) • Disabled Over-Age Dependents (New York residents) • Florida Contract Benefit Plans

Evaluating Documentation Rulesets The following sections explain how the system evaluates and applies documentation rulesets.

Evaluating Dependent Eligibility Before evaluating an employee’s dependents for the benefit plan’s rulesets, the system checks the employee’s dependents’ eligibility for the benefit plan. This check runs only if the domain and ruleset are set up for the Dependent Eligibility rule. If the domain and ruleset are not set up for the Dependent Eligibility rule, the benefit plan does not display in the enrollment, and the system does not apply any of the documentation rulesets.

Evaluating Documentation Ruleset Eligibility When the Dependent Eligibility rule determines that the employee’s dependents are eligible for a benefit plan, the benefit plan displays in the employee’s enrollment. The system then evaluates the employee’s dependents to see whether they satisfy the conditions for the required documentation rulesets that are set up in the benefit plan. If a required documentation ruleset applies

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 17 Chapter 1 Configuring System Settings

to the dependent (for example, if the employee includes a domestic partner as a dependent in the enrollment), the system triggers the required document for the employee to complete.

Uploading and Tagging Documents You must upload required documents to the Document Repository and tag them correctly. Documents attached to a benefit plan display in the employee’s Benefit Summary when the enrollment is complete.

Evaluating Dependent Eligibility If the Dependent Eligibility rule is set up, the system evaluates dependent eligibility for the benefit plan before determining whether the employee’s dependents satisfy the conditions for the required documentation rulesets. If the dependent is a domestic partner or has a different last name, the system proceeds to the next step and determines whether the dependent satisfies the required documentation ruleset eligibility conditions. If the dependent does not satisfy these conditions, one of the following sets of conditions must apply for the dependent to be determined to be eligible for the benefit plan.

Condition Set Conditions Condition Set #1 • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent in the Employee Dependents form. • The dependent is a Florida resident, as determined by the dependent’s state (if the dependent has no state entered, the system defaults to the employee’s state). • The benefit plans is either a medical (MED) or gap (GAP) plan, and the dependent’s age is less than 30.

Condition Set #2 • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent in the Employee Dependents form. • The benefit plan is a Florida-contracted national plan, indicated by the National Plan in the Carrier Code Maintenance panel in Group Benefit Plans. • The benefit plan is either a medical (MED) or gap (GAP) plan, and the dependent’s age is less than 30.

Condition Set #3 • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent in the Employee Dependents form, and the dependent is disabled.

Evaluating Documentation Ruleset Eligibility After the system determines dependent eligibility, it evaluates the employee’s dependents to see whether they satisfy the conditions for the required documentation rulesets. If a dependent satisfies the conditions, the

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 18 Chapter 1 Configuring System Settings

system triggers the required document for the employee to complete.

Rule Conditions Domestic Partner • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent (DOCUMENT-PARTNER) and has the Relation set to Domestic Partner in the Employee Dependents form. The Relationship Code Domestic Partner must also be set in the Relationships form with the Domestic Partner Relationship Type. • Your organization must set up the required document with the File Tag DP in the Document Repository.

Dependents with Different Last Names • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent (DOCUMENT-LASTNAME): but does not have the Relation set to Domestic Partner in the Employee Dependents form. • The dependent’s last name is different from the employee’s last name. • Your organization must set up the required document with the File Tag LN in the Document Repository.

Disabled Dependents • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent (DOCUMENT-DIS) and Is Disabled is selected in the Employee Dependents form. • The dependent’s age is greater than the carrier-based age limit, defined in Group Benefit Plans by the Dependent’s Age Limit. The point at which the Dependent’s Age Limit becomes effective is defined in the list. • Your organization must set up the required document with the File Tag DIS in the Document Repository.

Over-Age Dependents (Florida • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent residents) and does not have Is Disabled selected in the Employee (DOCUMENT-FLO) Dependents form. • The dependent is a Florida resident, as determined by the dependent’s state (if the dependent has no state entered, the system defaults to the employee’s state). • The dependent’s age is greater than the carrier-based age limit, defined in Group Benefit Plans by the Dependent’s Age Limit, and less than 30. The point at which the Dependent’s Age Limit becomes effective is defined in the list. • Your organization must set up the required document with the File Tag FLO in the Document Repository.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 19 Chapter 1 Configuring System Settings

Rule Conditions Over-Age Dependents (New York • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent residents) and does not have Is Disabled selected in the Employee (DOCUMENT-NYO) Dependents form. • The dependent in a New York resident, as determined by the dependent’s state (if the dependent has no state entered, the system defaults to the employee’s state). • The dependent’s age is greater than the carrier-based age limit, defined in Group Benefit Plans by the Dependent’s Age Limit, and less than 30. The point at which the Dependent’s Age Limit becomes effective is defined in the list. • Your organization must set up the required document with the File Tag NYO in the Document Repository.

Florida Contract Benefit Plans • The dependent is set up with the Relationship Type Dependent (DOCUMENT-FLCT) and does not have Is Disabled in the Employee Dependents form. • The benefit plan is a Florida-contracted national plan, indicated by the National Plan in Group Benefit Plans. • The dependent’s age is greater than the carrier-based age limit, defined in Group Benefit Plans by the Dependent’s Age Limit, and less than 30. The point at which the Dependent’s Age Limit becomes effective is defined in the list. • Your organization must set up the required document with the File Tag FLC in the Document Repository.

This setting overrides the default waive logic of the system and allows the waive option to always display for the offer type.

Assigning Dependents to Group Plans You must add validation on group benefit plan types by assigning them to the relationship codes that represent employee dependent relationships. You must also define the age limit for dependents and when the dependent’s age limit takes effect. These settings allow the correct cost for the offered benefit plans, based on the employee’s dependent selection, to display during enrollments. You must define the following settings. Refer to the Benefit Administration User Guide for more information about settings in the Group Benefit Plan Types and Group Benefit Plans forms. See the System Administration User Guide for more information about the Relationships form. • In the Group Benefit Plan Types form, set up the Minimum Dependents and Maximum Dependents. If the benefit plan type requires that the employee’s spouse be set as a dependent, select Spouse Required or Domestic Partner Req’d on each Type Code. Indicate whether the plan covers the employee’s regular dependents, the domestic partner’s children, or both using the Dependent Min/Max Type list. • In the Group Benefit Plans form, define the Dependent’s Age Limit and select when the benefit plan imposes an age limit from the list. • In the Relationships form, assign group benefit Plan Types to each Relationship Code.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 23 Chapter 1 Configuring System Settings

Configuring Web Enrollment Use the following settings in the Group Benefit Plans Web Enrollment Parameters panel when setting up enrollments. Some medical and dental benefit plans enable or require employees to enter information about their primary care provider (PCP) during enrollment. • To offer the benefit plan in open enrollments, select Include in Open Enrollments. If you do not select this option, the benefit plan is not included. • To give employees the option to enter PCP information, select Collect PCP Information. When you select this option, PCP Required becomes active. • To require employees to enter PCP information, select PCP Required. You must also specify a URL where employees can look up their PCP in PCP Lists in the Details tab in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form.

Assigning Administrative Roles There are many places in PrismHR that require administrator actions. For more information, see the System Administration Guide, Human Resources User Guide, or Approvals Guide.

Requiring Approvals When setting up workflows for enrollments, you have the option to require that an administrator approve all enrollments. If you choose to do this, you must have at least one user or worksite trusted advisor for each of these roles. • If the user is a service provider, assign the role Benefit Manager in the Users form. • If the user is a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor, assign the role Benefit Approver in the Users form. You must also set up approval policies. Each approval policy specifies who must approve an action before it is finalized. • Use the Global Approval Policies form to define approval policies at the system level. • Use the Approval Policies form to override global approval policies at the client level.

Setting Proxy Enrollments You can set up the following proxy enrollments: • Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors who are set up with the Enrollment Proxy user role can act as an employee and execute the employee’s enrollment selections using the Proxy Login form. • Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors who are set up with the Onboarding Proxy user role can read employees’ full onboarding workflows. (Note: The system bypasses any field-level security when using this role.)

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 24 Chapter 1 Configuring System Settings

Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors who are set up with the Enrollment Proxy user role can act as an employee and execute the employee’s enrollment selections using the Proxy Login form. Editing Metadata The Metadata Editor form is used to edit the metadata for Benefits Enrollment and Onboarding documents. This metadata can be used to optimize document organization and search results.

Chapter 3 Setting Up Benefit Plan Information To set up information about available benefit plans, use the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form. For example, you can set up costs for employee contributions, co-payments, deductibles), attach detailed benefit plan summaries and other supporting documents, and set up benefit plan dependencies. You can enter benefit plan information fields manually in the Comparison Fields tab in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form. You can also use the Plan Offer Type Import form to import multiple benefit plan information fields.

Defining Enrollment Plans To set up information about available benefit plans for new hires and employees to view during their enrollments, upload required documents, and set up benefit plan dependencies, use the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form.

To select what to do: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Benefits Enrollment Plan Details. 3. In What would you like to do today? select an option: • Define Offer Type Level Setup. For more information, see Defining Offer Type Setup (page 30). • Define Plan Level Setup. For more information, see Defining Plan Level Setup (page 33). The system opens the selected tab, but you can switch to another tab as needed. If you do this, the system prompts you to save or discard any unsaved changes.

Defining Offer Type Setup In the Define Offer Type Level Setup panel, use the Comparison Fields and Offer Type Dependency tabs to set up benefit plan details at the offer type level. The system prompts you to select the offer type to set up and opens the selected tab. You can switch to another tab as needed. Before you switch to the other tab, the system prompts you to save or discard any unsaved settings.

Use this tab To do this Comparison Define the benefit plan information options employees can view for the offer type.

The system prompts you to select an Dependency offer type from the list. It applies the settings you define to all benefit plans that have that offer type selected.

Defining Employee Options To define the benefit plan information options employees can view in all plans that have the selected offer type during enrollments, use the Comparison Fields tab. After you set up the options, you can set up the values in each individual benefit plan using the Details tab in the Define Plan Level Setup panel. An employee can review this benefit plan information, including costs for employee and dependents, co-pays, deductibles, and so on. An employee can also compare information for up to three benefit plans within the offer type during enrollment.

Defining Dependencies To set up dependencies at the offer type level, use the Offer Type Dependency tab. For example, if plans with the offer type Domestic Partner Medical (MDP) require the employee to enroll in a dependency plan with the offer type Medical (MED), the employee can select any available plan that has the MED offer type. Tier-based dependencies further limit which benefit plans are available to employees during enrollments. The option to set up additional dependencies is available only in offer types that use tiers. It is not available in life insurance or disability benefit plans, which use coverage levels rather than tiers.

To set up dependencies for offer types: 1. Open the Offer Type Dependency tab. 2. Select the offer type to use as a dependency, and then click Add. The Offer Type Dependency is shown in the table. • You can add as many dependencies as needed. The type being viewed in the form requires enrollment in one of the specified dependencies. • To remove a dependency, click (Delete). 3. If necessary, specify an additional tier-based dependency.

Managing Underwriting Questions In some cases, insurance companies require employees to complete underwriting questions to enroll in benefit plans. Underwriting questions determine whether an employee can enroll in a benefit plan based on the response. For example, when enrolling in a benefit plan, the system could ask an employee, “Does this coverage replace or change any existing insurance?” Based on the response, the system could deny employee enrollment. To configure required questions for enrollment, use the Underwriting Questions option when defining plan level setup. Underwriting Questions are only available for the following offer types:

• LTD - Long Term Disability • ACC - Accident Benefits • STD - Short Term Disability • HOS - Voluntary Hospitalization • LDA - Additional LTD • IDT - Identity Theft • SDA - Additional STD • LGL - Legal • CRI - Critical Illness • TEL - Telehealth • CAN - Cancer Benefits • WLI - Whole Life

The BE benefit plan tiles now have an Underwriting tab where employees can answer any necessary questions. If a benefit plan requires employees to answer underwriting questions, they cannot elect coverage until they answer. After an employee answers underwriting questions for an elected benefit plan and submits their enrollment, the questions and responses display on the Benefit Confirmation Statement. The questions and responses also display on the employee benefits enrollment record in PrismHR. You can view this information on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form.

Importing Benefits The Benefits Import Process enables you to enroll employees in group benefit plans using the information in an external data file. The process requires you to set up a data file and a benefit import definition.

Before you begin: • Set up company benefits and benefit rules. For more information, see the Benefits Administration User Guide.

Setting Up the Data File The data file must be either tab-delimited or comma-delimited. It must include the following columns of information, in any order: • Company ID • Employee ID, Employee SSN, or Employee Clock Number

•    Offer Type
•    Benefit Plan ID
•    Benefit Plan Type
•    Effective Date
•    Action Codes

Translation Tables Use translation tables to convert codes found in the data file to standard action codes that PrismHR software uses. External action codes are located in an external data file, and standard action codes correspond to external action codes. Options include: • Action Translations: Enter action codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard action codes in the next column. • Client Translations: Enter company IDs found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard company IDs in the next column. • Plan Translations: Enter benefit plan codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard benefit plan codes in the next column. • Plan Type Translations: Enter plan type (coverage levels) found in the external data file in this column Enter the corresponding standard plan types in the next column. • Network Translations: Enter network codes found in the external data file in this column. Enter the corresponding standard network IDs in the next column. 1. In the Translation Tables dialog box, click Actions. The Benefit Import Actions Translation Table form opens. 2. To indicate the action the system should take for each line of data, enter the External Action Codes found in the data file and the corresponding Standard Action Codes from the following table.

Code Name Description ADD Creates a new benefit enrollment. WAIVE Waives coverage for an existing enrollment. CHANGE Changes the plan type/coverage of an existing enrollment. TERM Terminates an existing enrollment. DEPEN+ Adds a covered dependent to an existing enrollment. You can also use this to add covered dependents to a new enrollment, as long as the new enrollment occurs in the file before the line that adds the dependent. BENEF+ Adds a beneficiary to an existing enrollment. You can also use this to add a beneficiary to a new enrollment, as long as the new enrollment occurs in the file before the line that adds the beneficiary. DEPEN- Removes a covered dependent from an existing enrollment.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 43 Chapter 3 Setting Up Benefit Plan Information

Code Name Description BENEF- Removes a beneficiary from an existing enrollment. ENROLLFSA Creates a new flexible spending account (FSA) enrollment. ENROLLHSA Creates a new health savings account (HSA) enrollment. TERMFSA Terminates an existing flexible spending account (FSA) enrollment. TERMHSA Terminates an existing health savings account (HSA) enrollment. CHANGEFSA Changes the plan type/coverage in an existing flexible spending account (FSA) enrollment. CHANGEHSA Changes the plan type/coverage in an existing health savings account (HSA) enrollment.

Importing Benefit Enrollments Use the Benefit Import process to enroll employees in group benefit plans using the information in an external data file. The process requires you to set up a data file and a benefit import definition. You can set up the data file either before you begin the import or from within the Benefits Import form. You must set up company benefits and benefit rules before using this process. See “Benefit Groups” and “Benefit Rules” in the Benefits Administration User Guide for more information.

To set up the data file: 1. Create an Excel spreadsheet that includes at least the following columns of information in the same order as in the template. The data file must be either tab-delimited or comma-delimited. • Action Code • Company ID • Employee ID, Employee SSN, or Employee Clock Number • Benefit Plan ID • Benefit Plan Type • Effective Date 2. Save the spreadsheet in either CVS or TXT format.

Chapter 4 Setting Up Forms and Workflows A workflow is essentially a wizard—a script that presents employees with a series of forms to guide them through well-defined and highly customizable steps during onboarding and benefit enrollments. In the Form Library, you can create custom versions of the forms or use the prebuilt versions provided with their default language and settings. Prebuilt forms are shown in bold. If you plan to include any media items (such as documents or images) in forms or workflows, upload them to the Document Repository before you create the forms in the Form Library. After you create the forms, you can use them as components to create workflows in the Workflow Library.

Planning Enrollment Workflow Components A typical enrollment workflow might begin with an optional Welcome form and then present forms for medical, dental, and vision plans; long-term and short-term disability plans; and so on. You can organize forms into categories for easier navigation. The final forms in a workflow include the following required forms:

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 57 Chapter 4 Setting Up Forms and Workflows

•     A Benefits Summary form that summarizes the employee's benefit selections and provides the
      opportunity to make changes.
•     A Confirmation form where the employee submits benefit selections and completes the enrollment
      process.

A Welcome form is recommended for workflows, but optional. The Benefit Summary and Confirmation forms are required for enrollments to process correctly.

Before you begin: • Plan the organization of the information blocks to present during enrollments so that the process flows well and makes sense.

Managing Documents, Forms, and Workflows Use the following libraries to manage documents, forms, and workflows for enrollments.

Library Description Document Repository Upload and maintain documents to use when creating forms (graphic files for logos, PDF files containing benefit information, and so on). Form Library (Enrollments) Build the forms, typically using documents from the Document Repository. PrismHR provides prebuilt forms that you can use as templates to create new forms, as well as templates for the Welcome and Confirmation forms. You can also build your own custom forms. Workflow Library Create workflows using forms from the Forms Library as (Enrollments) components.

Managing Versions and Revisions The Form Library and Workflow Library both maintain multiple versions and revisions for forms and workflows. Revisions are set automatically when you submit a new form or workflow or modify an existing one. • When you create a new form or workflow, the Version automatically sets to 1.0. • If you change a form or workflow and select the option to have the changes go into effect immediately, the system adds a revision number after the decimal point in the version number (1.1, 1.2, and so on). The system also immediately sets the Status to Active, and sets the current date as the Start Date. Since there can be only one active version of the form, the system changes the status of any previous active version to Inactive and sets the current date as its end date. • If you change a form or workflow and select the option to have the changes go into effect at a future date, the version number automatically sets to the next number in the sequence, and the revision number resets to zero (2.0, 3.0, and so on).

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 58 Chapter 4 Setting Up Forms and Workflows

The system sets the new version's status to Active on the start date, which you assign when you submit the
form or workflow. Since there can only be one active version, the system changes the status of any previous
active version to Inactive and sets the current date as its end date.

You can view and compare different versions and revisions in both libraries by clicking the form ID or workflow ID in the table. The Versions form opens, displaying all existing versions and revisions. • To modify a form or workflow version or revision, click the ID. • To compare two versions or revisions of a form or workflow, select the two you want to compare and click Compare. The Comparison panel opens below the main table in the form (you must scroll down to view data) and displays settings for both.

Managing Documents Use the Document Repository to upload and manage documents. You can upload pdf, jpg, jpeg, tif, tiff, png, and gif files. When uploaded, you can use the files to create forms for enrollments in the Form Library. Benefits Enrollment users can attach documents to benefit plan records in the Comparison Fields tab in the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form.

Uploading a Single Document You can upload a single document to the Document Repository. You can also upload a .ZIP file containing multiple documents. You must assign uploaded documents unique names within their selected security level. The system displays an error message if you assign a document the same name and security level as an existing document in the Document Repository.

To upload a document: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Upload a Document. The Document Upload dialog box opens.

                                             PPO.pdf).

Uploading Multiple Documents Using .ZIP file format, you can upload multiple documents to the Document Repository. Documents can include logos and other images, PDF files, spreadsheets, and other types of files.

Creating the .ZIP File For bulk uploads, construct .ZIP files exactly as follows. Any variation causes the upload to fail. • Use PKZIP or the Compressed (zipped) folder option in Windows Explorer to create a .ZIP file that contains the documents for bulk upload. • Do not use any implementation-specific features or the file does not extract correctly. • Encryption, passwords, or other security measures are not supported, and cause the upload to fail. • Arrange the folders and files in the .zip file following the directory structure, with three sub-folders (client, employee, public) contained in the root folder. Files placed in the root directory (that is, outside the sub-folders shown) and files placed in any other sub-folders are not supported and cause the upload to fail. Directory names must be in lowercase.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 60 Chapter 4 Setting Up Forms and Workflows

Sub-folder Description client Files in this folder are restricted by Client ID after upload in the Document Repository. • The folder name and all sub-folder names must be in lowercase (client). • The client folder must contain one sub-folder per client, with the folder name set to match the Client ID (including any leading zeroes). For example, if the Client ID is 1908, the sub-folder for that client must be named 1908. • The client documents should be placed inside the client sub-folder. No additional sub-folders are permitted. employee Files in this folder are restricted by Client ID and Employee ID after upload in the Document Repository. • The folder name and all sub-folder names must be in lowercase, for example (employee). • The employee folder must contain one sub-folder per client, with the folder name set to match the Client ID (including any leading zeroes). For example, if the Client ID is 1908, the sub-folder for that client must be named 1908. • Each client sub-folder must contain one sub-folder per Employee ID, with the folder name set to match the Employee ID. For example, if the Employee ID is 22386, the employee sub-folder must be named 22386. • The files should be placed inside the employee sub-folder. No additional sub-folders are permitted. public Files in this folder are imported with no security restrictions, and are viewable by everyone after upload in the Document Repository. • The folder name must be in lowercase (public). • All files must be placed within the public sub-folder. No additional sub- folders are permitted.

Uploading the .ZIP File

To upload the .ZIP file: 1. Click (Back Office).

  1. From System|Change, select Document Repository.
  2. Click Bulk Upload (Zip). The Upload window opens.
  3. Click Choose File and select the .ZIP file to upload.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 61 Chapter 4 Setting Up Forms and Workflows

  1. Click Submit. After the upload completes, the system automatically extracts the documents, stores them in the Document Repository, and generates a metadata.csv file. You can review for errors and edit as needed, with the following restrictions: • Do not change the value in the first column (uuid).. The system uses this value to locate the files in the document repository. Do not remove the first row containing the column headings. • The columns userClassification, label, description, and version are strings and are always treated as a single value. • Classification labels must match the classifications in the Document Repository. • To avoid processing errors, do not use quotation marks inside any of the column values. • In the userTags column, specify multiple tags by separating them with a comma.
  2. Import the metadata.csv file back into PrismHR using the Metadata Import Entry Form to complete the upload process.

Importing the metadata.csv File To import the metadata.csv file into PrismHR, use the Metadata Import Entry form, located in the Back office menu under System > Action. The metadata.csv file is generated when you upload multiple files to the Document Repository using the bulk upload. This is the final step in uploading multiple files to the Document Repository. You must complete it for the files the files to display correctly.

To import the metadata.csv file into PrismHR: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Action, select Metadata Import Entry. 3. Click Start Import. The Upload window opens. 4. Click Choose File, and select the file to upload. 5. Click Submit. The imported data displays. If the file contains invalid information, the system displays an error. • To view the data, click Done with Errors • To scroll through the report, click Next Page and Previous Page. • To discard the data, click Cancel. 6. Click Post Data to complete the import.

Editing a Document You can modify file settings to maintain and organize your files.

To edit a document: 1. Click Back Office.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 62 Chapter 4 Setting Up Forms and Workflows

  1. From System|Change, select Document Repository.
  2. Click the Name of the file. The Document Settings dialog box opens.
  3. Modify the File Label, Description, File Classification, File Tags, and File Version Number. The Security Level for the document is read-only and you cannot change it. The File Classification and at least one File Tag are required to save changes.
  4. Select one of the following options: • To update the document with a new version, click Upload New Version. The system prompts you to navigate to the location of the file to upload and select the file. • To save changes, click Save. • To delete the file, click Delete. • To view the file, click Preview. • To download the file, click Download. • To return to the Document Repository without saving changes, click Close.

Searching and Filtering Documents PrismHR provides various ways to search and filter files in the Document Repository. The total number of documents displays in the lower left-hand corner of the Document Repository.

Search Option Description Select documents to display Displays a specific set of documents. • Public and Client—The set contains all public and client documents. This is the default. • Employee for Client ID—The set contains all employee documents for the selected client ID. The set does not contain public and client documents. Search Searches for files in the Document Repository. Start typing to search, or narrow the search by Name, Description, Tags, and Label. Classification Filters your view using the list. Only documents assigned the selected classification display. Tags Filters your view by selecting one or more file tags. Only the documents assigned to the selected file tags display. Filters your view based on the columns you select or clear. Columns with the icon display in the table. Columns with the icon do not display. Sort Ascending, Sort Descending Sorts files in ascending or descending order for the column header (Name, Date, Label, Version, Description) that you click. To hide a column from view, select Hide Column.

Managing Forms To create and maintain forms, use the Form Library. These forms include Benefit Summary forms and Confirmation forms, which are required for enrollments to process correctly, as well as optional Welcome forms. PrismHR provides prebuilt forms that can be used with minimal customization and the ability to create custom forms for additional enrollment options.

To open the Form Library: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Form Library. The Form Library displays.

Form Type • Default: This indicates that the form is a prebuilt form. • Custom: This indicates that the form was created manually.

Workflow • Enrollment: This indicates that the form is used in Benefits Enrollment. Type • Onboarding: This indicates that the form is used in Onboarding.

Status • Active: This indicates that the form is available for use in a workflow. • Draft: This indicates that the form has been saved as a draft and can be viewed or edited. • Inactive: This indicates form is not available use.

Creation The date the form was created. Date Start Date The date the form was made available for use.

Working with Substitution Variables Substitution variables are tags you can use as placeholder text when building content in custom forms and notifications in Benefits Enrollment. When generating the output, the system replaces the variable with data pulled from PrismHR. Substitution variables are similar to the mail merge fields used in word processing programs: they give content a more personal impact while also making it easier to customize and reuse content for multiple employees, clients, and workflows. For example, you might set up a form for a workflow that includes text using the substitution variable for the employee’s name:

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 71 Chapter 4 Setting Up Forms and Workflows

Welcome, <>! When the employee views the form, the substitution variable is replaced by the employee’s name and displays as: Welcome, Jane M. Smith! Users can include the following substitution variables in both notifications and custom forms. These variables are case-sensitive. You must type them exactly as shown.

Managing the Workflow Library Use the Workflow Library to create workflows for enrollments. A typical enrollment workflow might begin with an optional Welcome form, then present forms for medical, dental, vision plans, long-term and short-term disability plans, and so on. You can organize forms into categories for easier navigation. The final forms in a workflow include a Benefits Summary form (which summarizes the employee’s benefit selections and allows the opportunity to make changes), and a Confirmation form (where the employee submits benefit selections and completes the enrollment process). These are required.

Before you begin: • Plan the organization of the information to present during enrollments so that the process flows efficiently and makes sense.

To view workflows used for Benefits Enrollment: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change,select Workflow Library. The Workflow Library opens. 3. In Workflow Type, select Enrollment. You can sort the table view by clicking the column headings.

Creating a Workflow To create workflows for enrollments, use the Workflow Library form. You can also use this form to add notifications to send to employees or groups during enrollments. As you create the workflow, you are also building the workflow’s navigation menu structure that the employee views during the enrollment. The forms in the workflow display in the navigation menu in the same order in which you arrange them.

To create a custom workflow for enrollments: 1. Click Back Office. 1. From System|Change, select Workflow Library. The Workflow Library opens. 2. Click Create New Workflow. The Create New Workflow form displays.

Bulk Launch Benefit Workflow This new form is a new bulk creation tool that can create enrollment records simultaneously, so information no longer needs to be added one record at a time. This is especially helpful for take-on clients. Service providers also now have the ability to launch life events in bulk. The form is called Bulk Launch Benefit Workflow and provides these options: • Employee record check boxes where you can select a single or multiple employees. You can also Select All employees with a check box. • Column sorting and filtering. • A record counter at the bottom of the table that displays the total number of items, the number of items displayed that are based on filtering, and the number of items selected or checked. • Data displayed in the table is pulled from the Employee Detail record. • Pre-filtering options for clients, employment type, and employment status. • Two action buttons exist on this form: Launch Life Event and Launch Benefit Enrollment. • View and download reports associated with benefit enrollment changes. • These columns of data are included in the table:

Chapter 5 Setting Up Notifications To set up notifications to send during enrollments, use the Notification Templates and Notification Recipients forms.

Before you begin: • Set up Email Services. See the System Administration Guide for more information.

To access the Notification Templates form: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Notification Templates. The Notification Templates form opens.

To access the Notification Recipients form: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Notification Recipients. The Notification Recipients form opens.

To access the Notification Control Panel: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Operations|Action, select Notification Control Panel. The Notification Control Panel opens.

Setting Up an Enrollment User You must set up an enrollment user in PrismHR with the User ID called Enrollment. See the System Administration Guide for more information. The Enrollment user serves as the administrator and sender for all notifications. The email address set up on the user account displays in From for all notifications sent to employees and new hires. If this user account is not set up, the notifications engine does not send notifications. The User ID must be as follows, spelled correctly, and with no punctuation: Enrollment

To test the Enrollment user: 1. In the Notification Templates form, set up a test notification template recipient. 2. In the Notification Recipients form, set up a test recipient.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 87 Chapter 5 Setting Up Notifications

  1. In the Notification Control Panel, turn on the notification engine using a test client.
  2. Send a test message from the Enrollment user to confirm that it is set up correctly. If the Enrollment user is set up correctly, the test recipient receives the notification.

Setting Up Templates and Recipients After you set up the Enrollment user, you can set up content for notifications in the Notification Templates form. You can designate recipients for notifications in the Notification Recipients form. The notifications that you create are available in the Workflow Library where you can add them to workflows.

Managing Notifications To specify how often the system should send the notifications and to start the notifications engine, use the Notification Control Panel. You can run the Notification Audit Report to review notifications sent to all recipient types (for example, employees, generic recipients, message groups). Messages are also stored in the Messages center in PrismHR. You can also set up your SMTP server to retain a copy of every email sent.

Handling Undelivered Notifications There are two possible circumstances that can result in notifications not reaching their recipient. • The email address is not entered correctly. For example, it is entered as @​example.com​ instead of jsmith@example.com.​ PrismHR logs this error but it is not accessible to the user. Users should contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team. • The email address is entered correctly, but is otherwise not deliverable (for example, the email address is no longer active). In this case, PrismHR simply sends the email. There is no error log, and in most cases there is no way to know that it was not received. Many email servers are configured not to send notifications of undeliverable emails.

Tracking Notifications To track notifications, set up the Notification Recipients form to send copies of all notifications to an administrator in your organization. This also enables you to forward notifications as needed.

Setting Up Notification Templates The Notification Templates form is used to create templates for the notifications that are sent to employees or groups during benefit enrollments, open enrollments, anytime enrollments, or life event enrollments. Each template specifies the content that is included in the notification, such as the subject and message body, as well as the criteria for sending the notification and the communication method used to send the notification.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 88 Chapter 5 Setting Up Notifications

When defining notification content, substitution variables can be used to replace generic information with specific information from PrismHR. Once the template has been created, the Notification Recipients form can be used to define the recipients who receive the notification. In addition, the notifications can be added to a workflow using the Workflow Library.

Note: Notification templates that have been attached to a workflow or a notification recipient record cannot be deleted.

Chapter 6 Maintaining Life Event Codes To set up workflow codes for employee life events such as marriage, divorce, and birth, use the Life Event Maintenance form. Benefits Enrollment provides predefined life event codes that your organization can configure as needed, but you can also create your own as needed. After you set up the life event workflow, administrators can assign the life events to employees in the Life Event form. After you save the life event assignment, the system generates an enrollment workflow and the employee can complete the life event workflow in EP.

Configuring Required System Settings You must set up the following settings before creating a new life event record: • Set up all benefit plans to include in the life event workflow. Assign them the correct Offer Type to include in the offer type forms assigned to the workflow. • In the Client Workflow Grid, assign a benefit enrollment workflow that corresponds to the effective date to use for the life event workflow. The life event workflow is based on this pre-existing benefit enrollment workflow, and the life event code settings serve as overrides. • Set up Benefit Summary and Confirmation forms to use in the life event workflow in the Forms Library. You can also set up an optional Welcome form. You can customize these forms as needed for the life event. • Set up the notifications to send for each life event. The notification templates must have the Workflow Type Life Event selected, and must be set up with recipients for the notifications to be available. • If you want the system to automatically approve every employee enrollment for the life event, set up a global approvals policy. See the System Adminstration Guide or Approvals Guide.

Viewing Life Event Codes and Clients The Life Event Maintenance form is divided into two tabs, Codes and Clients. Existing life event work codes display in the main table in the Codes tab, and client information displays in the main table in the Clients tab. You can: • Sort your view of the tables in the Codes and Clients tabs by clicking the column headers and selecting Sort Ascending, Sort Descending, or Hide Column. • Use the Search box to search for a specific record as needed.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 96 Chapter 6 Maintaining Life Event Codes

• Use the View list to select the number of records to view in either table (25, 50, 100). • Use the navigation arrows to scroll through records. If you edit settings, the settings change for all clients, not just the client you are viewing. If you want to change settings for just one client, create an alternate life event workflow code.

To access the Life Event Maintenance form: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Life Event Maintenance. The Life Event Maintenance form opens. The Codes tab is displayed by default.

Viewing Codes The Codes tab displays information about the event workflow codes. The main table list all codes you created, as well as the pre-defined life event codes provided in Benefits Enrollment.

Changing Predefined Life Event Codes The system provides the following predefined codes. You can modify them as needed. Predefined codes have default settings, but you need to reconfigure them base on the settings your organization requires. Review and modify the settings as needed before you use them for life events.

Selecting Forms To select the Welcome, Summary, and Confirmation forms to use in the life event workflow, use the Process tab in the Add Life Event form. The forms you select in the Welcome, Summary, and Confirmation lists override the forms that are set up in the benefit enrollment workflow that is being used as the basis for the life event workflow. For example, if you do not select a Welcome form, no welcome form displays in the life event workflow, even if one is set up in the original benefit enrollment workflow.

To select the forms to use in the workflow: 1. In the Add Life Event form, select the Process tab. 2. Select the Welcome form to use. This form is optional. 3. Select the benefit Summary form to use. This form works in conjunction with the Confirmation form and is required.

Chapter 7 Assigning Workflows to Enrollments Use the System Workflow Grid and Client Workflow Grid forms to assign the workflows to use for enrollments at the system or client levels.

Assigning Workflows at the System Level To assign workflows to use for enrollments at the system level, use the System Workflow Grid form. You can also assign workflows at the client level. Settings defined at the client level override global settings. For more information, see Assigning Workflows at the Client Level (page 107). The Min # of Overlap days designates the limited amount of time an employee has to complete the open enrollment workflow when the workflow start date plus the Min # of Overlap days extends beyond the open enrollment window. This option is used only in an enrollment workflow overlap scenario. • If the start date is the date the first workflow is submitted, 4/25/19, the system checks the Min # of Overlap days on the grid and adds that number of days to the Start Date Window. It then calculates a date of 4/27/19. The system then checks the End Date Window on the grid. • If the calculated date is greater than the end date on the grid, the system uses the calculated date. • If the end date is in the past, 4/23/19, the system uses the calculated date of 4/27/19 for the workflow end date. • If the dates are equal, 4/27/19, the system uses the calculated date of 4/27/19 for the workflow end date. • If the end date is in the future, 5/3/19, the workflow end date is 5/3/19. • If the Min # of Overlap days is left blank, the system uses the current logic of same length as window dates - the length between start date window and end date window. • Use the Filter Records panel to filter system-level workflows by entering the OE Start Date and OE End Date, then clicking Search. • Use First, Prev, Next, and Last to navigate through the workflow history. • View the total number of records, shown in the lower right-hand corner.

Chapter 8 Setting Up Anytime Enrollment Anytime Enrollment enables employees to enroll in Anytime Benefits at any point during a plan year. A date or event does not trigger the Anytime Enrollment process — you can enroll in Anytime Benefits at any time. One example of an Anytime Benefit plan is pet insurance. If you acquire a pet and want to enroll in a pet insurance benefit plan, you can do so at any time outside of annual enrollment restrictions. To set up Anytime Enrollment, you must: 1. Configure a benefit plan to include in an Anytime Enrollment workflow 2. Set up a notification template 3. Set up notification recipients 4. Create an Anytime Enrollment workflow 5. Add the workflow to the system or client workflow grids To begin, you must configure an Anytime Benefit plan to include in an Anytime Enrollment workflow.

Including a Benefit Plan in an Anytime Enrollment Workflow To include a benefit plan in an Anytime Enrollment workflow, use the Group Benefit Plans form.

To include a benefit plan in an Anytime Enrollment workflow: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Group Benefit Plans. The Group Benefit Plans form opens. 3. Configure a benefit plan for Anytime Enrollment or use the Benefit Plan ID link to select a plan from the list. 4. In the Web Enrollment Parameters panel, enable Include in Anytime Enrollment Workflow. 5. Click Save. After configuring a benefit plan to include in an Anytime Enrollment workflow, you must set up a notification template.

Setting Up an Anytime Enrollment Notification Template To set up a notification template for an Anytime Enrollment workflow, use the Notification Templates form.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 111 Chapter 8 Setting Up Anytime Enrollment

To set up a notification template for an Anytime Enrollment workflow: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Notification Templates. The Notification Templates form opens. 3. Configure a notification template for Anytime Enrollment or use the Template Id link to select a template from the list. 4. In the Workflow Type panel, enable Anytime Enrollment. You can combine with other workflow types except for Onboarding. 5. Click Save. After configuring a notification template for an Anytime Enrollment workflow, you must set up notification recipients.

Setting Up Anytime Enrollment Notification Recipients To set up notification recipients for an Anytime Enrollment workflow, use the Notification Recipients form.

To set up notification recipients for an Anytime Enrollment workflow: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Notification Recipients. The Notification Recipients form opens. 3. To configure notification recipients for Anytime Enrollment, click Setup a new Notification. Or, to select a recipient group from the list, use the Notification Id link. 4. In the Notification Template panel, to assign the recipient group to a template configured for Anytime Enrollment, click Template Id. For more information, see Setting Up an Anytime Enrollment Notification Template (page 111). If you select a notification template configured for Anytime Enrollment, the Workflow Type and Message Delivery Method panels are disabled. 5. Click Save. After configuring notification recipients for an Anytime Enrollment workflow, you must create the workflow.

Creating an Anytime Enrollment Workflow To create an Anytime Enrollment workflow, use the Workflow Library form.

To create an Anytime Enrollment workflow: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Workflow Library. The Workflow Library form opens. 3. In the Type list, select Enrollment.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 112 Chapter 8 Setting Up Anytime Enrollment

  1. To edit an existing workflow for Anytime Enrollment, select a workflow from the list. To create a new workflow, click Create New Workflow.
  2. On the Process tab, enable Anytime Enrollment.
  3. On the Forms tab, select forms to include in the workflow.
  4. On the Notifications tab, enable the notification template configured on the Notification Template form. For more information, see Setting Up an Anytime Enrollment Notification Template (page 111).
  5. Click Save. After creating the workflow, you must add it to the system or client workflow grids.

Adding an Anytime Enrollment Workflow to the System Workflow Grid To add an Anytime Enrollment workflow to the system workflow grid, use the System Workflow Grid form.

To add an Anytime Enrollment workflow to the system workflow grid: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select System Workflow Grid. The System Workflow Grid form opens. 3. In the Anytime Enrollment column, select a workflow from the list to add it to the workflow grid. You can also click Add Row to add another row to the workflow grid. In the Add a New Record section, you can select an Anytime Enrollment workflow from the AE Workflow list. 4. Click Submit Changes. After submitting your changes, the workflow is now available at the system level. You can also assign the workflow at the client level using the Client Workflow Grid form. Client-level settings override system-level settings.

Adding an Anytime Enrollment Workflow to the Client Workflow Grid To add an Anytime Enrollment workflow to the client workflow grid, use the Client Workflow Grid form.

To add an Anytime Enrollment workflow to the client workflow grid: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Client Workflow Grid. The Client Workflow Grid form opens. 3. In the Anytime Enrollment column, select a workflow from the list to add it to the workflow grid. You can also click Add Row to add another row to the workflow grid. In the Add a New Record section, you can select an Anytime Enrollment workflow from the AE Workflow list. 4. In Enable Notifications, you can select the following specific to Anytime Enrollment workflows:

Adding Anytime Benefits to Employee Portal In Employee Portal (EP), you can add a widget displaying available Anytime Benefits enabling employees to enroll directly from EP. A link from EP opens directly to an Anytime Enrollment workflow (through SSO) where they can enroll in any of the available benefit plans. For more information on creating the widget, see Adding Anytime Benefits to Employee Portal (EP) on the Customer Resource Center.

Chapter 9 Maintaining Web Enrollments You maintain web enrollments using the following forms: • To view an employee’s enrollment activity during enrollments, use the Web Enrollments History form. • To extend the end date in an enrollment for an employee who needs more time to enroll, use the Web Enrollment Configuration form. • To create a custom enrollment period for an employee, use the Web Enrollment Configuration form. • To assign a new workflow to active enrollments, use the Web Enrollments Bulk Update form. • To modify the start and end dates on active enrollment workflows, use the Web Enrollments Date Update form. • To create enrollment batches and post benefit enrollments, use the Post Benefit Enrollments form.

Viewing Web Enrollment History To view an employee’s enrollment activity during enrollments, use the Web Enrollments History form. The information you can view includes: • The dates and times the employee viewed a workflow, as well as each form in the workflow. • The effective dates, plan types (tiers), premium rates, and coverage details for each benefit plan viewed by the employee. • The benefit plans the employee selected. • Whether the employee waived benefits individually or for a spouse. • If the employee waived benefits for a spouse, the waive reason the employee selected.

To view an employee’s enrollment activity: 1. Select HR in the menu bar. 2. From HR|View, select Web Enrollments History. The Web Enrollments History form opens. 3. Enter the Employee ID. 4. Click Load. A detailed record of the employee’s enrollment activity displays in the table. You can click Next or Previous to navigate multiple screens of data.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 115 Chapter 9 Maintaining Web Enrollments
