Tracing Benefit Enrollment When an employee logs in and begins the enrollment process, the system determines the benefit plans to display and calculates the employee costs for each benefit plan by applying a series of checks on each form in the workflow. You can view a record of these checks in the Benefits Enrollment Trace form.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 121 Chapter 9 Maintaining Web Enrollments

The Tracing tool is especially useful for troubleshooting and finding errors when you set up benefits and open enrollments. If a user made an error in setting up a workflow or a benefit plan, tracing provides a way to find the error. You can then make any needed corrections to enable employees to access the correct benefit plans and view correct calculations for the costs of the available plans. The Benefit Enrollment Trace form displays data only for a form that is currently open and active in an enrollment. It can display details for only one form at a time.

Note: You must be logged in to an enrollment using the correct employee credentials. Also, the form whose details you want to view must be open and active to use this tool.

Before you begin: • Verify that the correct client record is shown near the top of the form. If it is not, click it and then select the correct client. If the correct client is not selected, the system cannot access system checks for the client’s enrollments. • Log in to the enrollment using the employee’s login credentials, and open the form to view. The form opens in the enrollment.

To trace benefit enrollment: 1. On the HR menu, select HR|View > Benefits Enrollment Trace. 2. Enter the Employee ID and click Reload. 3. The system checks (for the form that is open and active in the enrollment) are shown in the table. You can click Download to save a text file of the trace log.

Suspended Employee Enrollment Process To manually suspend benefit enrollments for new hires if the benefits setup is not yet finalized for the client, use the Suspended Employee Enrollment Process form.

Note: The New Hire Suspension Process runs automatically once a day; this form allows you to run it on demand.

This process updates employee records, removes the suspended status for employees who are now eligible, and displays the results.

Note: On the System Parameters form, your organization must enter the SUSPENDENH custom feature code for this manual process to work. For more information, see Suspending Benefit Enrollments (page 123).

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 122 Chapter 9 Maintaining Web Enrollments

To launch the suspended employee update process: 1. Enter the Client for which you want to launch the New Hire Suspension Process. If you leave this field blank, the system runs the process for all clients. 2. Click Run. When the process is finished, the results display in a form.

Suspending Benefit Enrollments The new hire suspension process lets organizations suspend benefit enrollments for new hires if the benefits setup is not yet finalized for the client. The purpose is to ensure that new hires are not offered benefits based on obsolete settings. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) The new hire suspension process works as follows: • On the System Parameters form, the organization enters the SUSPENDENH custom feature code. This code activates the new hire suspension process at the system level. • On the Client Details form Benefits tab, administrators setting up benefits for a client define the Benefits Rules Good Through Date to indicate the date up to which the current enrollment offerings for new hires is valid. • When the validity date passes, the system initiates the new hire suspension process to prevent benefits from being offered online to new hires. • The system runs the new hire suspension process automatically once a day when the first administrator logs on to a SCORPEO or HRP.ADMIN account and applies the suspension to any new hires. (PrismHR customers must log on to their HRP.ADMIN account every day for this process to run). Administrators can also manually run the process once a day (at any time) using the Suspended Employee Enrollment Process form. • A benefits administrator then reviews and updates the benefits offered, and adjusts the Benefits Rules Good Through Date when the benefit offerings are ready for new enrollments. As long as the enrollment workflow has the notification enabled, employees receive a notification that they can now enroll online. • Users can run the Suspended Enrollment Employee Report to view employees whose benefits enrollments are suspended or on hold. • The Benefits Good Thru Date cannot be blank if the client had a Good Thru Date at any time in their record.

To enable the new hire suspension process at the system level: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select System Parameters. The System Parameters form opens. 3. Click the Custom Feature Codes link. From the list, select SUSPENDENH.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 123 Chapter 9 Maintaining Web Enrollments

  1. Click Save.

To indicate the latest validity date for enrollment offerings for new hires: 1. Click the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select Client Details. The Client Details form opens. 3. On the Benefits tab, enter a date in Benefits Rules Good Through Date. When this date passes, the system initiates the new hire suspension process. If the system finds that an employee’s earliest potential eligibility date exceeds the Benefits Rules Good Through Date, it suspends the employee’s enrollment.

Viewing the Enrollment Suspended Until Date On the Employee Details form Other tab, you can view records for employees whose enrollments are suspended. They display a date in the Enrollment Suspended Until field. This date indicates the next date that the new hire suspension process will review the record again. The date automatically advances by one day each time the process determines that the record should remain suspended. For more information, see the Human Resources User Guide.

Manually Running the Suspended Employee Enrollment Process The system runs the New Hire Suspension Process automatically once a day and applies the suspension to any new hires. If needed, administrators can use the Suspended Employee Enrollment Process form to manually suspend benefit enrollments for new hires at any time.

Viewing the Suspended Enrollment Employee Report You can also run the Suspended Enrollment Employee Report to view employees whose benefits enrollments are suspended. For more information, see Suspended Employee Enrollment (page 179).

Reviewing a Batch Click Review to review a batch when its status is Ready to Review. When the review is complete, the Batch Detail View displays. If the review process finds no errors in an enrollment, it returns the enrollment status Ready to Post. The enrollment can now be posted.

Note: All enrollments included in the batch must have the Ready to Post enrollment status to successfully post.

If the review process finds errors in any of the enrollment records: The system displays the following alert: Would you like to move the enrollments that failed review to a new batch so you can continue to post this batch? and prompts you to click Yes or No. • If No, the system displays the following message Please review the Error Report, fix any errors, and review this batch again before attempting to post. The system returns you to the batch and displays the enrollment status Review Failed. Records that failed to post are not removed from the batch. The Error Report and Change Report options display at the bottom of the batch table: • Click Error Report to run the Benefit Enrollment Review Error Report to review specific enrollment errors in the batch. • Click Change Report to run the Benefit Enrollment Review Change Report to review the changes and fixes made to the enrollments. • If Yes, the system prompts you to enter a batch name and to confirm that you want to proceed. The system displays the following message: Failing enrollments have been moved to a new batch [Batch Name] [Batch Number]. The system moves the Benefit Enrollment Review Error Report and the Benefit Enrollment Review Change Report for these enrollments to the new batch where you can view them without doing another

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 132 Chapter 10 Post Benefit Enrollments

     review. The system allows you to remain in the original batch where you can then post the batch with
     the remaining enrollment records.

You must fix all enrollment errors before the enrollment can be posted with a batch. You can remove an enrollment from the batch at any time by clicking selecting one or more enrollments and clicking Remove. When you remove an enrollment, it returns to the list of available enrollments. After you fix the enrollment errors, review the batch again until the errors are fixed. Each time you review, the Benefit Enrollment Review Error Report and the Benefit Enrollment Review Change Report are updated. You can review the batch as many times as needed before posting.

Reviewing Errors that Can Occur When Posting a Batch Use the Benefit Enrollment Review Error Report to review errors in the enrollment records that can occur when posting a batch in the Post Benefit Enrollments form. You must fix all errors for the system to successfully post the enrollment record. The following information is shown for each error. • Company: The client ID. • Employee: The employee ID. • Employee Name: The employee name. • Offer Type: The offer type for the benefit plan that generated the error message. • Error Message: The error message.

Reviewing Changes Made When Fixing Errors After posting a batch on the Post Benefit Enrollments form and correcting any errors, you can use the Benefit Enrollment Review Change Report to review changes made to the enrollment records during that process.

Change Report Output The following information is displayed on the report: • Company: The client ID. • Employee: The employee ID. • Employee Name: The employee name. • Offer Type: The offer type for the benefit plan that generated the error message. • Plan ID: The plan ID for the benefit plan. • Plan Name: The name of the benefit plan. • Type: The plan type or tier selected for the benefit plan. • Action: A description of the change that was made to the enrollment.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 133 Chapter 10 Post Benefit Enrollments

Posting a Batch When all enrollments in the batch are reviewed and display the Ready to Post enrollment status, you can post the batch by clicking Post. The system runs a final check on the enrollments included in the batch. • If any enrollments contain errors, the posting process stops. You must fix the errors or remove the failed enrollments from the batch before you can post the batch. The system prompts you to specify whether to save the failed enrollments to a new batch. • If posting is successful, the Batch Detail View of the form displays with the Enrollment Status Post Complete.

Posting Enrollments Automatically When your organization selects Auto post BE/OE enrollments when overlap with OE in the Enrollment Options form, the system automatically posts any new enrollment records created for employees during an active open enrollment period. If the enrollment posts successfully, a new enrollment record is automatically created for the employee for the active open enrollment. If posting for this new enrollment record fails, the posting batch that includes the new enrollment does not post but remains in the posting queue in the Post Benefit Enrollments form. The enrollment record displays the status Review Failed. In such a case, you must manually fix all errors in the enrollment before it can post.

Chapter 11 Using the Dashboard The PrismHRDashboard provides quick access to company information and relevant features. The information shown in the Chart and List sections of the Perspective panel reflects the client selected. To view onboarding tasks within Benefits Enrollment, in the Chart section of the Perspective panel, select Benefit Enrollments by Status from the list.

Displaying Tasks and Their Status The chart in the Perspective panel displays enrollment tasks and their statuses. You can use the type list to filter the type of enrollment to view in the Dashboard (All Types, Benefit Enrollment Only, Open Enrollment Only,

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 137 Chapter 11 Using the Dashboard

Life Event Only, Anytime Enrollment Only). When you select an enrollment type, the system displays the number of employee enrollments available.

Status Description In Progress The employee has either not started, or has started but not yet completed the enrollment. Waiting for Approval The employee has submitted the enrollment, and the enrollment is awaiting approval. Ready to Review The employee’s enrollment is approved, and in the posting queue. At this point, the enrollment might be included or not yet included in a batch. Ready to Post The employee’s enrollment is in a batch, has passed review, and is ready to post. Post/Review Failure The employee’s enrollment is in a batch, but has either not passed review or failed to post. OE Eligible Employees included in this status are eligible for open enrollment. OE eligibility is determined as follows: • Benefits Enrollment Enabled must be selected in the Global Configuration form. • If the client restricts eligible benefit plans (by Department, Benefit Group, Division, or Location) using the Eligible Benefits Determinant in Client Details, the system checks list of Eligible Benefits at the restriction level to see if the benefit plans are active and the employee is OE eligible. If no list of Eligible Benefits is entered at the restriction level, the system excludes the employee’s benefit group and the employee is not OE eligible. • If the client lists the employee’s status as eligible in the Benefits Enrollment Eligibility Criteria panel in the Client Details form, the employee is OE eligible. If the client has not listed eligible statuses in this panel, the system excludes terminated employees from being OE eligible. Employees who are not terminated are OE eligible. • If the client lists the employee’s type as eligible in the Benefits Enrollment Eligibility Criteria panel in the Client Details form, the employee is OE eligible. If the client has not listed eligible types in this panel, the employee’s type must have Eligible For On-line Benefit Enrollment selected at the system-level in Employee Types for the employee to be OE eligible.

Displaying Benefit Enrollments by Type The List section displays the individual benefit enrollment records for the type selected. You can further filter benefit enrollment records that display in the list by clicking a status in the pie chart. The list updates, and the colored dot that displays next to each item matches the color in the pie chart section.

Benefits Enrollment User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 138 Chapter 11 Using the Dashboard

The table displays the following columns.

Column Description Employee Name The employee’s name. Employee ID The employee’s ID. Start Date The start date for the enrollment workflow. End Date The end date for the enrollment workflow. Effective Date The enrollment effective date. Workflow The name of the enrollment workflow. Status The status for the enrollment.

Actions An action to perform for a specific enrollment record. The following options are available: • Archive: Archives the enrollment record. The system displays an informative message and prompts you to confirm Yes or No. If you click Yes, the system archives the record and displays a confirmation message when complete. Click OK to close.Click OK to close. • Extend: Changes the enrollment End Date and extends the enrollment period for the employee. The system displays a dialog box where you can enter the new end date and click Extend to save. • Proxy: Performs a proxy enrollment in the Proxy Login form. • View Web Enrollment: Displays the enrollment record in the Web Enrollment Configuration form.

Retirement Auto Enrollment Report Use this form to generate a report to show the list of employees auto enrolled for a retirement plan based on their following auto enrollment statuses: • Active – This report shows retirement enrollments for active employees who were automatically enrolled in the system. Their status on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form is Active Enrolled. • Eligible – This report shows new hire employees who were automatically enrolled into a retirement plan upon hire, but their status on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form is still Eligible Unenrolled. This is the status of all new hire employees retirement enrollment until they are calculated in a payroll. The payroll calculation will automatically apply the Benefit Plan Setup Auto Enrollment Percent, and change the status to Active Enrolled. These employees will appear on this report until the status is changed to Active Enrolled.

Note: If the Auto Enrollment Percent on the Benefit Plan Setup form is not set up, the employee does not change to Active Enrolled upon payroll calculation.

Setting New Hire Questions You can create new hire employee questions using the New Hire Questions form. These questions can be assigned to a specific work location state with the New Hire Wizard.

Note: You can submit a maximum of 30 questions. For more information about assigning new hire questions, see the System Administration Guide.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 22 Chapter 1 Setting Up System-Level Human Resources Codes

To do this Perform these steps Creating a New Hire Question 1. Click Back Office. 2. Select New Hire Questions from the System|Change menu. 3. Click New Question. The Question ID field populates with NEW, and the system generates an ID when you save the new question. 4. Enter the Question Text to display in the New Hire Wizard. 5. Select the Field Type to define the format for the answer to the question. • If you select Dropdown, the system prompts you to enter the values for the drop-down. • If you select Radiobutton, the system prompts you to enter the default value (No = unselected, Yes = selected) as well as the description of the radio button. Only one option can be set to Yes. 6. Select Mandatory if users must answer the question. 7. Click Save. Editing a New Hire Question 1. Enter the Question ID. 2. Change the Question Text and Field Type, if needed. 3. Click Save. Assigning New Hire Questions The PrismHR administrator assigns questions to specific states using the State Rules form. The system then presents the question to new employees on the Additional State Questions page of the New Hire Wizard during the new hire process.

Setting Approval Policies Even if you have global approval policies, you can set approval policies at the client level. Using the Approval Policies form, you can maintain policies for several approval types. See also Global Approval Policies.

Note: You can click View All Policies in this form to view the policies defined for your organization and select one to edit.

Available Approval Types The following approval types are available: • Direct Deposit Change Approval Policy: This approval type uses the Direct Deposit Change option to require approval at the client or global level to store direct deposit information in the employee details record. For example:

Important! There must be a client-level or global-level approval policy in place to use this feature. (Without
an approval policy, the system immediately records any changes and applies them to the employee record.)
In addition, the approval policy only applies when an employee changes, adds, or removes the Transit
Number or Account Number in the direct deposit information.
When an approval policy is defined for a client using the Direct Deposit Change option and an employee,
worksite manager, or worksite trusted advisor submits a new or updated direct deposit or deletes a direct
deposit, the system sets the update to Pending status and an approval is required. (After approval, the direct
deposit follows the regular prenote process, if one is in place.) However, if a service provider makes an
update, the change does not go through an approval process and is immediately applied to the employee
record.
Note: The approval is submitted either from an employee making an update in Employee Portal or from a
worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor making an update in Employee Portal or in the Prism Core
application.
When an approval is pending and a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor tries to make a change,
the following occurs on the Deposit tab in the Employee Details form:
•    "Approval Pending" displays next to the Direct Deposit Information panel header.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 31 Chapter 2 Setting Up Client-Level Human Resources Codes

•    If they select Save or Save & Close a message displays, "A prior direct deposit change is waiting for
     approval. Your updates will discard the previous changes. Do you wish to continue?" Click Yes to discard
     the previous update.

• Late Payroll Posting Approval Policy: This approval type stops payrolls from being posted on or after the Late Payroll Posting date and time during the finalization process, which prevents the payroll from finalizing until it is approved by a user in accordance with the applicable Approval Policy configuration. Each approval policy specifies who must approve an action before it is finalized. There are different levels of approvals:

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 34 Chapter 2 Setting Up Client-Level Human Resources Codes

• Client worksite personnel can approve actions (for example, a pay rate change entered for an employee by a departmental manager). • The internal staff of the service provider can approve actions. • Approval policies can also require approval from both worksite and service provider users.

Note: When service providers enter HR-related changes, those changes go through without requiring approvals. Only payroll-related processes made by service providers are subject to approval policies.

Setting Up Approval Policies To set approval policies at the client level: 1. Go to the Approval Policies form on the HR|Change menu. 2. Select the Approval Type, which is the type of action that requires approval. 3. For each step, set one of the following: • Enter the PrismHR User ID, if the step requires that a specific user approve the action. • Specify the HR Role for worksite approvers. • Specify the A/M Role, which is the service provider account management role. When you include an A/M Role, you should select the A/M Filter from the drop-down as your organization’s security policy requires: • All Users with designated A/M role: Any user with the account management role can see the approvals. • Only A/M Assigned to Client: Only service provider users assigned to the client can see the approvals; the system checks the account assignment in the Client Details Account tab for the specified A/M Role and displays the approval for only that user.

Note: PrismHR automatically assigns a number to each approval step you select. The approvals are processed in that order.

  1. Click Save.

Chapter 3 Understanding Human Resources Roles Human Resource roles determine what the user can do in PrismHR. The user can only perform actions for client companies assigned in Data Security. Note the following: • The Payroll Processor can perform all payroll tasks. • If your organization separates the time sheet entry and check printing tasks, you should assign some worksite users as Time Sheet Entry types and other users as Payroll - Prints Checks and Payroll - Print Garnishment Checks.

Human Resource Role Details Employee’s Manager User can approve employee leave requests. (Leave Request Only) H/R Action Approver User can approve human resource actions for clients assigned in Data Security. Payroll Approver User can approve payroll-related actions for clients assigned in Data Security. Payroll Processor User can process payroll information for clients assigned in Data Security. (Applies to Portal Time Sheet Entry.) Time Sheet Entry (w/ Pay User can enter time sheet data, including pay rates. (Applies to Portal Rates) Time Sheet Entry.) Time Sheet Entry (w/o Pay User can enter time sheet hours, but cannot see or enter pay rate Rates) information. (Applies to PrismHR Core and Portal Time Sheet Entry.) Payroll - Prints Checks User can view and print regular paychecks. Note: If a user’s role is only set to the Payroll - Prints Checks role, they cannot print garnishment paychecks. Payroll - Print User can view and print garnishment paychecks. Garnishment Checks Note: If a user’s role is only set to the Payroll - Print Garnishment Checks role, they cannot print regular paychecks.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 36 Chapter 3 Understanding Human Resources Roles

Human Resource Role Details Enrollment Proxy User can act as an employee and execute the employee’s enrollment selections. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) Onboarding Proxy User can read employees’ full onboarding workflows. (Note: The system bypasses any field-level security when using this role.) Benefits Approver User can approve benefits-related actions for clients assigned in Data Security. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.) PTO Administrator User can see all employees in the Planned Time Off Requests form, regardless of whether they are restricted by Data Security settings, not only direct reports. Client Manager User can be assigned to receive notifications in the Notification Recipients form. I-9 Approver User can approve Form I-9s for employees during the onboarding process. Pay Card Account User can approve pending pay card account approvals. Approver Manager User Setup Worksite managers can set up other worksite managers. Custom HR role (defined If your organization has defined custom human resources roles using by your organization) the Custom HR Approval Roles form, you can add them to the user. These roles are for customizing global or client-specific approval policies.

Defining Positions You can define position-related information for the client using the Positions form.

To access this form: 1. Click Client. 2. From Client|Change, select Positions.

Click the Import button to display the Data Import Tool form, which allows you to import a Position Codes template file that contains the following fields (this file must be in .txt format): • Position Code (Required) • Position Title (Required) • Position Classification (Required): An error displays if the imported code does not exist on the Position Classifications form (accessed from the System|Change menu) • Supervisory: Accepted values are Y (True) or N (False) • Tipped Position: Accepted values are Y (True) or N (False) • G/L Segment Code 1 • G/L Segment Code 2 • G/L Segment Code 3 Note the following: • The Import button displays on the Positions form for all Service Provider user roles except the “Deny” and “Inquiry-only” roles. Imports can be performed for multiple clients at the operations level. • For more information about the Data Import Tool form, see the PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 38 Chapter 4 Defining Employee Positions

Defining Position Information and Requirements You can define basic position information and requirements using the Positions panel.

Note: If the position exists in several departments, use a job code that easily identifies the department in which the position is assigned.

Complete these fields as required.

Field Description Position Code Enter or select a unique code that briefly describes the position. For example, OPER for vehicle operator. (Codes cannot contain spaces or special characters.) If you select this field, a selector form displays where you can search for a specific position code, title, or classification or select a code from the list that displays. When this form opens, the position code, its title, classification, FLSA exempt status, and obsolete status display. To filter the search further by displaying only obsolete codes, select Yes in the Obsolete field (the default is No). To refresh the list, select Reset Search and Filters. Position Title Enter an official title. For example, General Manager. Position Classification Enter the position classification. The system displays the FLSA Exempt settings, EEO position group, and the EEO class, if they apply to this position. FLSA Exempt indicates whether the selected position classification is set to be exempt from both the minimum wage and overtime provisions of the FLSA. You cannot change it here. Remote Position Enter an alternative position classification for remote employees of the Classification same position. The system displays the FLSA Exempt settings, EEO position group, and the EEO class, if they apply to this remote position. FLSA Exempt indicates whether the selected remote position classification is set to be exempt from both the minimum wage and overtime provisions of the FLSA. You cannot change it here. Position Description Enter a description for this position. The second panel defines requirements for the position and the pay. Supervisory Select if this is a supervisory position. The system uses this field for statistical reports. Hierarchy Tier For future development. Does not currently impact the functionality of PrismHR.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 39 Chapter 4 Defining Employee Positions

Field Description Pay Grade Select to use as a default for new hires assigned this job code, if applicable. The Special Requirements option identifies those positions that have physical or mental requirements. The Americans with Disabilities Act prohibits employers from discriminating against qualified individuals with disabilities. Not including a particular person in the applicant pool for a certain job is only nondiscriminatory if that person does not meet any physical or mental requirements identified as essential functions of the position. Applications for these jobs must be closely monitored for ADA compliance. Special Requirements Select if this position requires any special physical or mental requirements. Probation Days Optional: Enter the number of days from hire that a new employee is on probation. Sales Position Select if this is a sales position. Tipped Position Select if this is for a position that receives tips. D.O.T. Requirements Select if this job code has special requirements as set forth by the U.S. Department of Transportation. The G/L Segment Code can be used as an alternative to this position when using G/L Accounting. See the PEO Client Company Accounting Task Sheet on the Customer Resource Center for more information. G/L Segment Code If applicable, enter the G/L Segment Code 1, G/L Segment Code 2, or G/L Segment Code 3 to use as the general ledger account number segment(s) in place of the Position Code. These are defined in PEO client accounting wild cards as EEJB, EEJB2, and EEJB3.

Defining Codes and Other Pay Information You can define codes and other pay information for the position in this panel. Complete these fields as required.

Field Description Union Code Select this override for table-based union calculations. If an override is not Override selected, the system uses a union code in Employee Details, if any.

PR Chauffeur Tax Select if this position is subject to Puerto Rico chauffeur’s tax and the Applies primary work location is Puerto Rico. Indirectly Tipped Select if this a tipped position that receives tips indirectly. For example, a busboy, cook, or service bartender.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 40 Chapter 4 Defining Employee Positions

Field Description Alaska Position Code If applicable, enter the Alaska Position Code sent to MasterTax for quarterly tax reporting to the state of Alaska. SOC Code Enter the Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Code, if appropriate. Enter only numbers, no dashes. This information is included in the MasterTax RTS file and the Employer and Client LA quarterly files in place of the position’s description. If you do not define a SOC code for the position, the files include the description. TTO Code Define which positions are considered eligible tipped positions to comply with the tips requirements of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. You can enter the TTO Code (Tipped Taxable Occupation Code) manually or you can click the TTO Code hyperlink and select it from the TTO Codes dialog box. The TTO Description displays upon entering a valid TTO Code. The system will validate when you enter a TTO Code against the SOC Code during the creation or updation of a Position. • Invalid TTO/SOC combinations result in an error message: TTO code [] and SOC code [] are not related. • Invalid TTO code results in an error message: TTO Code [] does not exist. • Invalid entries cannot be saved. • Valid TTO code entry is allowed when the SOC code is blank. Indiana Seasonal Enter a two-digit code if the position is seasonal and located in Indiana. This Employee Code code is required for SUI electronic filing in Indiana. Prevailing Wage Enter the Prevailing Wage for this position. This can print on pay stubs as a pay detail field. Price Code Select a price code that overrides the Bundled Rate for any employee who has been assigned to this position. Note: Only use Price Code with Bundled Billing if an employee is granted special pricing rather than using the standard bundled rate and with an employee-specific add-on unbundled rule. Per Diem Percent Enter this percentage to allocate to non-taxable per diem when paid using the percentage method. W/C Time Sheet Loc Select to calculate workers’ compensation accruals for each employee’s Based actual work location. This overrides the setting in Client Details. Obsolete Select if this position is no longer used.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 41 Chapter 4 Defining Employee Positions

Field Description Suppress Work State Select if employees in this position are subject to taxes in their state of Tax residence rather than state of work. During calculations, the system will use the employee’s residence for the basis of state taxes. Benefit Group Assign a default benefit group for employees hired in this position. Agricultural Worker Select if the employee is an agricultural worker and the employee’s income will be reported to the IRS on Form 943. (Note: All employees assigned to this position are auto-assigned this designation during the new hire process.)

Tracking Hazardous Materials You can track any hazardous materials associated with this position using the Hazardous Material Exposure panel. Enter each hazardous materials Material Code that people in this position encounter.

Working with Miscellaneous GL Segments Use the Misc GL panel to review Misc GL Counts (predefined wildcards) for this position and enter replacement Misc GL Segments. Note: During payroll processing, the system substitutes the GL segments for wildcards in GL account codes. These wildcards must also be included in the following setups: • GL setup, which is processed into payroll accounting. (You can configure them in the G/L Setup form.) • PEO client accounting setup, which is processed into client accounting. (You can configure them in the PEO Client Accounting form.)

When working with miscellaneous GL segments: 1. The predefined wildcards display in rows in the Misc GL Count column, where the codes are always EEMJB01 through EEMJB99. (The program that evaluates the wildcards only looks for those values.) 2. If appropriate, enter the Misc GL Description. For example, EEMJB01 = Segment 1 and EEMJB02 = Segment 2. (You can apply these misc segments to account codes for other areas besides pay, such as taxes or deductions.) Important! Any changes made to the descriptions affect all positions in the active client. Note: The Misc GL Description column’s values are for reference only. (These descriptions are stored in the client’s record.) The system automatically loads these values each time a position record displays. 3. If appropriate, enter the Misc GL Segment value that replaces the Misc GL Count wildcard. Note: When the system evaluates the Misc GL Segments, they are always based on the “home” job, which is different from the way segments are evaluated for departments (that is, for account codes for payment, the system uses the timesheet “worked-for” department). 4. Click Save.

To establish employee address information, do the following: 1. Go to the Employee Details form on the HR|Change menu. 2. Enter or select the Employee. 3. Click the Address tab and complete the following fields:

 Field                                  Description
 Address                                Enter the employee’s residential Address.
 ZIP Code                               Enter or select the ZIP Code for the employee’s residential city or
                                        town. The employee’s City, State, County, and Geocode populate
                                        automatically. You will be presented with a pop-up of Geocode
                                        options when an entered zip code spans multiple cities, counties,
                                        or localities. Select the correct Geocode to update the address.
                                        You can enter the ZIP+4 extension for the residential address, if it
                                        was not populated by the system.
                                        After you enter or select the ZIP Code, the system checks the
                                        street address to make sure that it is valid. If there are typos,
                                        missing information, or other unrecognized values, the system

                                        existing address, it displays the first address in the master list for
                                        the ZIP code (such as 1 Apple Drive).
 Geocode                                Enter the Vertex GEO Code for the employee’s city or town to use

Overriding Geocode for Employee Residence You can override the employee’s Resident Address Geocode on the Employee Details form, so the system will calculate taxes using a different taxing municipality than the one for their residence. Note: Before beginning this process, refer to the Vertex Calculation Guide in the Customer Resource Center to determine the geocode for the appropriate taxing municipality for the selected employee.

To override the geocode for the employee residence, do the following: 1. Go to the Employee Details form on the HR|Change menu. 2. Enter the Employee ID, then select the Address tab.

  1. In the Override Geocode field, enter the geocode determined in step 1.
  2. Enter the Override End Date on which the Override Geocode should no longer be used. Note: If there is no end date at this time, then leave this field blank. The geocode override remains in effect until it is changed.
  3. Click Save.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 57 Chapter 5 Maintaining Employee Details

Assigning School District GeoCodes You can assign a School District GeoCode in Employee Details in PrismHR to ensure that the system properly calculates the employee’s school district taxes. 1. Refer to the Vertex Calculation Guide in the Customer Resource Center to determine the school district GeoCode for the appropriate state, town and school district for the selected employee. 2. Open Employee Details (found in the HR menu under HR|Change. 3. Enter the Employee ID and then select the Tax tab. 4. Scroll down to the Miscellaneous panel and enter the School District GeoCode determined in step 1.

  1. Click Save.

Maintaining Work-related Employee Information You can maintain work-related information for the employee by using the Work tab on the Employee Details form.

Maintaining Employee Hiring Status Information The Status Dates panel lists the employee’s hiring status information.

To maintain employee hiring status information, do the following: 1. Go to the Employee Details form on the HR|Change menu. 2. Enter or select the Employee. 3. Click the Work tab and complete the following fields as available and needed in the Status Dates panel:

 Field                                  Description
 Last Hire Date                         The Last Hire Date is the date on which the employee was most recently
                                        hired.
 Original Hire Date                     The Original Hire Date is the date on which the employee was originally
                                        hired.
 Leave Return Date                      The Leave Return Date is the date on which the employee returned to work
                                        from leave.
 Employer Start Date                    The Employer Start Date is the date on which the employee started with

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 58 Chapter 5 Maintaining Employee Details

 Field                                  Description
                                        your organization.
 Hire Report Date                       The Hire Report Date is the date on which the hire was reported to the
                                        state.
 Seniority Date                         The Seniority Date is used to calculate the employee's benefits. You can
                                        adjust it to give the employee more seniority than the last hire date; this
                                        can affect benefits, paid time accrual, and so on.
 Benefits Thru Date                     Enter or select the Benefits Thru Date for this employee. This is the date
                                        through which benefit contributions have been deducted from this
                                        employee's pay.
 Last Day Worked                        Enter or select the Last Day Worked to indicate the last day on which
                                        employee actually worked (if the employee left the client).
 Provider Notified On                   The Provider Notified On field indicates the date on which your
                                        organization was notified of the employee’s termination.
 Term Reason                            If appropriate, enter or select the Term Reason, which is the reason the
                                        employee was terminated.
                                        Note the following when using this field:
                                        •    If you select the Term Reason field, the Select Reason form only
                                             displays the reason codes set up in the Reason Codes panel on the
                                             Control tab on the Clients Details form.
                                        •    If you enter a termination reason in the field that is not set up in the
                                             Reason Codes panel on the Control tab on the Clients Details form an
                                             error message displays, "The code entered is not valid for this client."

 Rehire Okay                            Use the Rehire Okay drop-down to indicate whether the employee could
                                        potentially be rehired:
                                        •    Yes: The employee can be rehired.
                                        •    No: The employee should not be rehired.
                                        •    Not Specified: There is no preference specified as to whether the
                                             employee could be rehired.

Maintaining Resident Alien Information The following section maintains resident alien information for the employee.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 67 Chapter 5 Maintaining Employee Details

  1. Complete the following fields:

    Field Description Non-Resident Alien Select Non-Resident Alien if the employee is a non-resident alien. Importing Labor Allocation Data You can access the Labor Allocations import template in the Data Import Tool from this form to import labor

allocation data by clicking Import in the Allocations panel. The Labor Allocations import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Allocations panel on the Pay tab in the Employee Details form.

Note: You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Labor Allocations import template option. Note the following when importing Labor Allocations data: • Allocations must be equal to 100 percent. If not, an error message displays, “Total of allocation percentages must equal 100%.” • If you enter a labor allocation value that is not part of the client the following error message displays, “ is not on the file LOCATIONS.CODES.” • If you import labor allocations for an employee whose allocations already exist, those allocations will be overridden during the import. The following message displays during this situation, “Labor Allocations imported through this process will override any existing records. Updates to existing labor allocations must be done manually.” • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Employee Pay form (accessed by selecting the Pay tab on the Employee Details form) cannot import data using the Labor Allocations import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form. • Users whose user role is set to FULL or INQUIRY for the Employee Pay form (accessed by selecting the Pay tab on the Employee Details form), but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the Employee Details form.

Cumulative Versus Annualized Tax Calculations The difference between the two calculations can be marked, especially when an employee’s payment amounts are erratic.

                        Wages                      Cumulative Method           Annualized Method
     Week 1                              $500.00                     $25.82                       $25.82
     Week 2                               500.00                       25.81                        25.82
     Week 3                               500.00                       25.81                        25.82

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 78 Chapter 5 Maintaining Employee Details

                        Wages                         Cumulative Method           Annualized Method
     Week 4                                  500.00                       25.83                         25.82
     Week 5                                3,000.00                     400.82                         681.01
    Subtotal                                                           $504.09                        $706.83

In the table, a salesperson receives a monthly commission check. If the amount of the commission considerably exceeds the employee’s regular salary payments; • The annualized tax rate calculation returns a tax rate based on a higher tax bracket, resulting in a larger tax deduction amount. • The cumulative method calculates the tax rate based on a cumulative average of the month’s earnings, returning a tax deduction amount that is a more accurate representation of the employee’s overall earnings.

                            •    Designating one account to receive the remaining balance ensures that

Tracking Employee Property You can track any client property assigned to the employee using the Property tab on the Employee Details form.

Listing the Employee’s Property You can list the employee’s property on the Property panel.

To list client property assigned to the employee, do the following: 1. Enter the Property Code that represents the client property assigned to the employee. The Description displays. 2. Enter the Date Issued, which is when the employee received the client property. 3. Enter the Serial No. of the client property. 4. Enter the estimated value of the client property in the Property Value field. 5. When the employee returns the property to the client, enter the Date Returned. 6. Enter any Comments specific to this client property.

Listing the Employee’s Vehicle You can list the employee’s vehicle property on the Vehicle Information panel.

To list the vehicle assigned to the employee, do the following: 7. Enter the Make of the employee’s vehicle. 8. Enter the Model of the employee’s vehicle. 9. Enter the Year of the employee’s vehicle. 10. Enter the Date Added, this is the date that the vehicle is starting use for company business. 11. Enter the Date Removed, this is the date when this vehicle is no longer used for company business. 12. Enter the Registration Number of the vehicle.

Maintaining the Employee’s License Information You can maintain the employee’s driver’s license information on the License Information panel.

To maintain the employee’s driver license information, do the following: 13. Enter the employee’s Driver’s License Number. 14. Enter the Driver’s License Class designation of the license. 15. Enter the License Expiration Date when the driver’s license expires. 16. Enter the State Issuing License, which is the state that issued the driver’s license.

Maintaining Employee’s Auto Insurance Policy Information You can maintain the employee’s auto insurance policy information on the Auto Insurance Policy panel.

To maintain the employee’s auto insurance policy information, do the following: 17. Enter the Carrier Name of the employee’s auto insurance. 18. Enter the Policy Number of the employee’s auto insurance. 19. Enter the Policy Start Date, the date the auto insurance policy started for that employee. 20. Enter the Policy Expire Date, the date the auto insurance policy will expire. 21. Enter the Policyholder Name, this is the person that holds the auto insurance for that employee. 22. Click Save. Note: A save banner, “The current record has been saved,” displays on the tab at the top of the form after you make an update and click Save. (The save banner disappears in a few seconds.)

Viewing Employee Termination Explanation The Termination Explanation panel displays the detailed termination explanation entered when the employee was terminated. (See Terminating an Employee on page 210.) Note the following: • You can add, update, or delete a Termination Explanation after an employee has been terminated. To do this, you must first enable the EDITTERM custom feature code in the System Parameters form. • You can enter a Termination Explanation that exceeds 200 characters when you enable the TERMEXPLAIN custom feature code on the System Parameters form.

Tracking Employee Retirement W2 Status The Retirement W2 Status panel will tell the system to check the Retirement Plan Box on Form W-2 even if the employee did not have any deductions during the tax year. An example would be for a pension plan where the client contributed if the employee did not. This should only be used if the employee is NOT enrolled in a retirement plan but SHOULD have the box checked on their Form W-2.

To track employee retirement W2 status, do the following: 1. Enter the Retirement Year the employee is NOT enrolled in a retirement plan. 2. Select the Retirement Status from one of the following options: • Not Eligible • Eligible 3. Click Save.

Tracking Employee Retirement HPE Status For a Highly Paid Employee (HPE), the Retirement HPE Status panel tracks if the employee met or exceeded the HPE threshold in the prior tax year. For example, for tax year 2024, if the employee met this threshold, then the Retirement Year record would be entered as 2025 with the HPE Prior Year option selected as Yes. Note: This grid has field level security as it contains salary information. This field therefore will be hidden by default. You will need to enable it using the User Roles form. • When enabled, you will have full access to view and modify the record. • When disabled, you will have view only access to the form.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 97 Chapter 5 Maintaining Employee Details

• When hidden, you will not see the field at all.

To track employee retirement HPE status, do the following: 1. Enter the Retirement Year. 2. Select the HPE Prior Year from the drop-down. 3. Click Save.

Using the Employee Details Action Menu Some of the features found in the Action menu of Employee Details are also available in other parts of the system. Those listed below are available primarily through the Action menu .

Changing an Employee’s User Password Use the Change Password form to change an employee’s user password. We recommend that you enter a password that you intend to be temporary, and instruct the employee to change it the next time they log in to Employee Portal (EP).

  1. Verify the Username is the correct user.
  2. Enter the New Password. The system validates the password; if it does not pass the validation, PrismHR informs you what you need to do to create a valid password.
  3. Reenter the password in the Confirm New Password field.
  4. Click Save. The next time the employee logs on, he or she will use the new password. This resets the lockout period, if any, in cases where you are changing the password because the employee was locked out of EP due to too many failed login attempts.

Attaching Files to Employee Records You can attach files to an employee record and open any files attached to it using the Employee Documents form. To access the form, open the Actions menu in Employee Details and select Documents.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 98 Chapter 5 Maintaining Employee Details

To attach files to an employee record, do the following: 1. Click Load a Document. 2. In the Upload a File window, click Choose File. 3. Navigate to the file that you want to upload, and then click Open. 4. Click Submit in the Upload a File window. 5. Click Close in the successful upload message. 6. In the Confirm Document form, the Document Name field populates with file name. 7. You can enter any Document Notes. 8. Click Accept. You return to the Employee Documents form.

Once a document is in the Employee Documents list: • Click the Document Name to download the document. • Click the next to a document to remove it from the company record. • Use the ESS check box to indicate whether the document is visible in Employee Self-Service (ESS).

Reviewing Employee Events You can review existing and add new qualifying events for the employee using the Employee Events form. These are typically training classes, certifications, and so on.

To add a new qualifying event, do the following: 1. Enter the Event Date. 2. Enter the Event Code. The Event Description displays. 3. Enter the Action Date, which is the renewal date or date when further action should be taken. 4. Enter a Comment that applies to the event. 5. Click Save.

Viewing an Organization Chart You can view organization structure information relevant to the employee using the Organization Chart. The system builds the chart based on the values in the Manager field in the Work tab on the Employee Details form.

Note: Because they are not employees, service providers are not included in organization charts.

Note that: • You can view the organization chart for any employee from HR|Change|Employee Details. Enter or select an employee, then select Organizational Chart on the Actions menu. • Managers and employees (but not Service Providers and Trusted Advisors) can view their own organization charts from HR|View|Organization Chart. • Worksite trusted advisors selected as an employee’s manager in the Manager field in the Work tab on the Employee Details form display at the top of the organization chart with the job title “Worksite Trusted Advisor.” (Worksite trusted advisors always display at the top of the chart because they are not assigned a manager.) This organization chart shows the worksite manager (Jason Argonis) and his direct reports. For each of these direct reports, Jason’s ID is in the Manager field in the Work tab on the Employee Details form.

Reporting Qualified Overtime and Tips Use the Qualified Tips and Overtime form to update the annual data for qualified overtime and qualified tips to report them in the employee Form W-2 for the tax year This option is provided to support federal reporting and compliance requirements supporting the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). For more information, please visit the article named OBBBA No Tax Setup Guide on the Customer Resource Center. If an employee works for multiple clients in a tax year, this form will report information for the active client only. If an employee works for multiple clients in the same employer, then Box 14 will have combined amounts when built on the employer. W2 data will be aggregated by employer if applicable. If an employee works between multiple positions, you should determine a single TTO Code for reporting purposes. Box 14 of the employee Form W-2 reports the qualified tips and overtime dollar amounts against the following applicable designations for SBEA and employer builds: • Approx Qualified OT • TTOC ; Cash Tips

Note: You cannot access this form using the search bar.

To access this form for an employee, select the employee in the Employee Details form. From the Actions menu, select the Qualified Tips and Overtime form for the employee for the client. Note: This information can also be added via the Data Import Tool.

Chapter 6 Performing Employee Fields Import The Employee Fields Import utility imports and updates employee information using a tab-delimited text file or a CSV file into the various tabs and fields of the Employee Details record. There are two sections to this form: Generate Import Spreadsheet and Import Employee Data. Important! This form enforces Client Access Group (CAG) Security. Therefore, the system skips any employees in the import file who are associated with clients not permitted by the user’s CAG.

To access this form:

  1. Click Back Office .
  2. On the Operations|Action menu, select Employee Fields Import to access the fields import utility. The Employee Fields Import form appears. This form includes these features: • Generate Import Spreadsheet: Create an import spreadsheet for later use by saving existing settings and then downloading the spreadsheet. This aids in performing subsequent field updates for your employees. (See Understanding Employee Fields Import Workflow on page 107.) • Import Employee Data: Import a tab-delimited text or CSV file with updated field information for employees. (See Importing Employee Data on page 109.)

Understanding Employee Fields Import Workflow This section describes how Employee Fields Import operates.

The workflow is: 1. In the Generate Import Spreadsheet section, select the employee fields to be updated. This will assist in selecting employees and will provide greater transparency in identifying the fields that can be edited during the import process. For example, you can select the Federal Filing Status field code to update employees’ Federal filing status in bulk. (This may be necessary at least once a year or you might need to perform this update more frequently.) If you use this field code, note the following: • You must select the Include Current Data checkbox to include a column in the spreadsheet that contains the selected employees’ existing data.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 107 Chapter 6 Performing Employee Fields Import

•    You must select the Include Filter checkbox to view and use Federal Filing Status as a filter in the Select
     Employees list. (To do this, select a client in the Select Employees by Client panel and then select Select
     employees, which opens the Select Employees list where the Federal Filing Status column displays.)
•    If you import "NONE" for the Federal Filing Status, the system updates the employees' Federal Filing
     Status field on the Tax tab on the Employee Details form to Select (null).
•    If you import a blank Federal Filing Status and select Keep Existing Employee Data in the Import
     Employee Data section, the system does not change the employees' Federal Filing Status and displays
     the following text in the transaction report, Prior Value Retained.
•    If you import a blank Federal Filing Status and select Remove Existing Employee Data in the Import
     Employee Data section, the system does not change the employees' Federal Filing Status and displays
     the following text in the transaction report, No Values Imported, and the Error Message column
     displays, Unable to complete row update for Employee ':<EMPLOYEE.ID>:'. Enter "NONE" as the federal
     filing status if you would like to remove the existing status.
You can use the following filters in the Fields to Update panel:
•    Select the Include Current Data checkbox to include a column in the spreadsheet that contains the
     selected employees' existing data.
•    Select the Include Filter checkbox to view and use filters in the Select Employees list. (To do this, select a
     client in the Select Employees by Client panel and then select Select employees, which opens the Select
     Employees list.)
To delete an existing template:
1. Select the template you want to delete in the Use template field. The template displays in the Save
   Selected Fields as a Template (optional) section.
2. Click Delete Template.
3. A message displays, "Are you sure you want to delete this template?" Select Yes to remove the template
   from the list of available templates.
Note: After you delete a template, you can reuse the template name and ID to create a new template.
  1. Once fields are selected, you can select employees using the Employees to Update multi-value grid. (This step is optional.)
  2. Click an Employee ID to use the Select Employees selector. Attributes that were selected on the MVG are used as filters on the multi-selector.
  3. You can now download a spreadsheet in the correct format for entering in new data.
  4. Save the selected fields into a template. This provides faster processing when you need to import subsequent changes. Only the selected fields are saved in the template.
  5. Import the file into the system as a CSV file.
  6. Decide how to handle blank fields in the file. You can either write in blanks in Employee Details, or skip over blank fields and leave in current data for these fields.
  7. Optional: Upload a previous file with updated data instead of downloading a spreadsheet.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 108 Chapter 6 Performing Employee Fields Import

  1. After the file is imported, you will receive a transaction report that includes both the errors and the values that were successfully imported.

Importing Employee Data You can import a tab-delimited text or CSV file with updated field information for employees. This updates fields on the Employee Details form.

To upload a file that updates employee records: 1. Enter an Import Name. This is a required field; you cannot import a file without this information. 2. Select whether to keep or remove existing employee data (provided the uploaded file contains blank fields).

Note: If a data attribute in the import file has a null value and Keep Existing Employee Data is selected, then the current attribute in the system is not replaced with a null value.

  1. Click Upload File.
  2. Navigate to a locally stored field import file, then click Submit.
  3. Click Import. An Employee Fields Import screen appears. Processing steps describe the information saved to employee records and include a date and time stamp. You can view this as a report or download in PDF or XLS format by clicking Report.
  4. Click Close.

Fields Import Format Changes The PrismHR field import format has changed. Field names are now the same as a field description. For example, is now Position. Field values also include a field description that precedes the field value. As seen here, Promo is preceded by New Position Reason Code. This corresponds to a field on Employee Details. This example compares the old way of specifying fields against the updated way.

For grouped fields , this new format also can handle changes with multiple records per field.

Updating Employee Fields from an Import File You can use the Expanded Employee Import file to bulk load employees into PrismHR. When you use the Expanded Employee Import method to import employee information, enter the information in the Template_for_Expanded_Employee_Import_TXT.xls file. The contents of this file are listed in the following table. The file template is also available on the Customer Resource Center.

Important Notes About the 2020 Form W-4 Beginning December 2019, this import supports the new 2020 Form W-4 filing statuses and fields. Please note the following updates: • In column AV, you can enter the new filing statuses (SS, MJ, and H). • If your state is using the new Form W-4 (Colorado, Delaware, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, South Carolina, and Utah), you must enter the new filing statuses in this field to avoid calculation errors. • Federal, work state, and home state values are now supported for the new Form W-4 fields, beginning in column GX. Note that there are no validations on these fields. • You must enter dollar amounts in the Other Income, Dependents, and Deductions fields. See the Form W-4 instructions for more information.

Information about this import file • File Type: ASCII, Tab Delimited • File Use: Stores employee data imported from foreign system • Key Format: Sequential Integer

Multi-Selectors and Dynamic Filtering A multi-selector lets you make multiple selections for fields you want to update for employees. Up to six of the selected fields can be designated as filters to be used in the Employee Selector.

Fields to Update (Select Field Selector) This selector lets you add field codes for use in an import spreadsheet.

To select fields: 1. Add fields to the Fields to Update table by clicking the Field Code link in the column header. This launches the Select Field selector.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 128 Chapter 6 Performing Employee Fields Import

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 129 Chapter 6 Performing Employee Fields Import

  1. Enter a field description or name, or select fields from the pick list on top of the selector by double-clicking them. The Records Selected table is populated with your selections. You can remove a selection by clicking the x icon on the right side of the table.

  2. Optional: Filter results further by selecting a Field Set. For example, Labor Union Affiliation.

  3. When you are finished making selections, click Done. You are returned to the Fields to Update table with your selections displayed.

  4. Select fields you want to filter on for employees by clicking Include Filter next to each field. You can only select six fields to use as filters. If you select more than six fields, the system warns you that only 6 filters can be added to the Employee Selector.

Note: Any field data that is changed in Fields Import will appear in the audit log on the Employee Details form.

Employees to Update (Select Employee Selector) Use the Select Employee Selector to specify a group of employees to include in a spreadsheet you can download for later use. Up to six attributes can be specified on the Select Field Selector for use as dynamic filters on Select Employee. For example, Pay Method and Location can be pre-selected as filters. This allows you to narrow down your search for specific employees who have these attributes applied to them.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 130 Chapter 6 Performing Employee Fields Import

To launch this selector and make employee selections: 1. Click Employee ID in the Employees to Update table. This opens the Select Employees Selector. 2. Enter Employee ID or Employee Name, or select employees from the pick list on top of the selector by double-clicking them. The Selected Employees table is populated with your selections. 3. Filter results further by selecting one of the dynamic filters you previously specified. For example, Pay Method. 4. When you are finished making selections, click Done. You are returned to the Employees to Update multi- value grid with your selections displayed . This specifies the employees that will appear on the spreadsheet you will download.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 131 Chapter 6 Performing Employee Fields Import

  1. Download your settings as a spreadsheet. (See Generating and Downloading an Import Spreadsheet on page 109.)
  2. Save your settings as a template. (See Saving the Spreadsheet as a Template on page 132.)

Saving the Spreadsheet as a Template You can save specified fields into a template to provide faster selection when you need to import future field updates. Only selected fields are saved as a template.

To save selected fields as a template (assuming Generate Import Spreadsheet panel is expanded): 1. Enter fields in the Fields to Update section. 2. Enter a Template ID. 3. Enter a descriptive name in the Template Description field. 4. Click Save Template. If you make changes to an existing template and try to save it, the system asks if you want to write over the existing template.

Note: Saved templates will appear as selections in the Use Template drop-down under Generate Import Spreadsheet.

Employee Fields Transaction Report Click View Transaction Report to display both error values and values that were successfully imported into the system in a single report. The default report name is - fields-import-transactions.csv. Rows with errors display at the top of the report. Columns in the report are:

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 132 Chapter 6 Performing Employee Fields Import

•    Status: The status is Error if an error was generated, or Saved if no error was generated.
•    Company ID: Company ID of the imported data.
•    Employee ID: Employee ID of the imported data.
•    Employee Name: Employee Name of the imported data.
•    Field Name: Description of the field that was updated.
•    Prior Value: If the prior value is blank, this cell will also be blank. If there was a previous value, this cell
     will contain that value.
•    Imported Value: If the status is Error, and no attribute was updated, this cell will populate with *No
     Values Imported. If the import ran with the remove existing employee data flag set, this cell value is
     *Value Removed. If the import ran with the keep employee data flag set, populate with the updated
     data. If there is a null value on the import file, and a value exists for this field in Employee Details and
     Keep Existing Employee Data is selected, this field will display in the transaction report.
•    Error Message: Displays the default error message generated by the job progress report. The column is
     left blank if no errors occurred.

When importing values that require multiple attributes, each attribute is added as a separate row in the Fields Import Transaction Report.

Downloading the eFlex by Pay Date File This form exports and downloads a file that lists employees in one or more selected Section 125 plans within a specified range of pay dates. Only employees who are available to the user are contained on the exported file.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form and download the file:

  1. From (Back Office) > Operations|Action, select Eflex Export by Pay Date.

  2. Complete these fields as required.

    Field Description Starting Pay Date Starting date in the range of pay dates. Ending Pay Date Ending date in the range of pay dates. Section 125 Plan Click the link to limit the report to a selected plan. If left blank, the process runs for all 125 plans.

  3. Click Build. If errors occur, fix them and then rebuild the download.

  4. Click Close to save the file to your local drive.

Chapter 7 Managing Employees’ Dependents and FMLA Events Use PrismHR to manage employees’ dependents and FMLA (Family Medical Leave Act) events.

Maintaining Employee Dependents To add new or edit existing employee dependent information, use the Employee Dependents form. (You can access this form by selecting Dependents in the Actions menu on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form.) If you have selected an employee on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form before opening the Employee Dependents form, the system pre-populates on the Employee Dependents form. Note: To quickly access the Employee Dependents import template in the Data Import Tool, select Import Employee Dependents. You can use the Employee Dependents import template to import multiple employee dependents for multiple employees at once to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Updating or Creating Employee Dependent To select an existing dependent record or create a new one, use the Employee Dependent panel. 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 2. To create a new dependent record for the employee, click New. Or, select an existing dependent record from the Dependent ID list. The list shows the dependent ID, name, and type.

FMLA Events Use the FMLA Events form (Figure 1) to maintain the information for an employee’s Family and Medical Leave Act event. Figure 1: FMLA Events

  1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window.
  2. Select the Event Number to edit an existing event, or select NEW to create a new one. PrismHR automatically generates the FMLA event numbers.
  3. Enter a brief Event Description of this event. The event description should uniquely identify this event from other FMLA events for the same employee.
  4. Enter the date the employee communicated the need for the leave event in the Date Notified field.
  5. Select the Reason Code that best describes the reason for the event.
  6. Select Intermittent/Reduced Schedule Leave if employee will take the leave as an intermittent or reduced schedule rather than full-time leave.
  7. Select Medical Certification Required if this event requires medical certification to verify the health condition of the employee or an immediate family member.
  8. Enter the Date Medical Certification Requested.
  9. Enter the Expiration Date for the event.
  10. Select the FMLA Year Basis type.
  11. If FMLA Years Basis is set to Fiscal, select the Fiscal End Month in which the year ends.
  12. If FMLA Years Basis is set to Fiscal, select the Fiscal End Day of the month in which the year ends.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 140 Chapter 7 Managing Employees’ Dependents and FMLA Events

Hours Adjustment Use the Hours Adjustment panel (Figure 2) to adjust the total hours for this FMLA Event. Figure 2: Hours Adjustment

  1. Enter the Effective Date of the leave.
  2. Enter the Pay Code to use for the leave hours.
  3. Enter the Leave Hours to adjust. Enter a negative amount to decrease the total number of leave hours.
  4. Click Post Adjustment to apply the hours.
  5. Click Yes to confirm that you want to create the adjustment.
  6. Click Save.

Event History The Event History panel displays the time the employee has already used for this FMLA event. Figure 3: Event History

Job Candidate Status Codes Use the Job Candidates Status Codes form to maintain the statuses used in the Job Candidates form.

To set up a job candidate status code: 1. Enter the Status Code. If you are creating a new status, use something brief but descriptive, for example, APL. 2. Enter the status Description, for example, Applied. 3. Click Save.

Maintaining Job Candidates Information You can maintain information about candidates for positions at the client using the Job Candidates form.

Establishing Information About a Candidate The Job Candidates panel establishes information about a candidate.

If you try to enter this information without indicating an existing candidate or new candidate the system displays an error message, “Select New Candidate or select an existing candidate to continue.” In addition, note the following: • If you select Hire in the Job Candidates panel in a blank record an error message displays, “Candidate not found.” • If you click Save in a blank record an error message displays, “[Last Name] [First Name] [Sort Name] is mandatory.”

Setting Up New Hire Information You can enter a newly hired employee’s information into PrismHR using the New Hire form.

Note: Depending on the system parameters and the company’s settings, different fields might be required.

You can access job candidate information by selecting Candidates from the Actions menu . Use the search dialog to select the job candidate you want; the candidate’s information populates the form. • Candidates: See Maintaining Job Candidates Information on page 142 • New Hire Notes: See Entering New Hire Notes on page 164 Once you save the New Hire form, you can select Employee Details from the Actions menu .

To set up new hire information, do the following:
