Identifying Employee Type You can identify the type of employee being hired using the New Hire panel.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 148 Chapter 8 Defining Job Applicants and New Hires

To identify the employee type, complete the following fields:

Field Description Work Location Enter or select the primary Work Location ID where the employee works. When there are mandatory new hire questions, a new form opens. Complete the form and click Submit Answers, then continue completing the New Hire form. Employer ID Select the Employer ID. Social Security Number Enter the new employee’s Social Security number. The Social Security Number field does not accept any values that begin with the numeral 9, but you can enter the ITIN for a 1099 Contractor which begins with the numeral 9. (All valid Individual Taxpayer Identification Numbers (ITINs) are a nine-digit number in the same format as the SSN (9XX–XX-XXXX), begins with a 9 and the 4th and 5th digits range from 50-65, 70-88, 90-92 and 94-99.) If you enter the ITIN of a 1099 contractor, you will receive a message stating The number you have entered is not a valid Social Security number. The new hire cannot be onboarded as an employee with this number. You should proceed only if you wish to enter this new hire as a contractor, and the new hire meets IRS requirements for using an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number in place of a social security number. Click OK to continue. The Hire Type Field will automatically change to Contractor (1099) on the New Hire form.

                              Note: Custom Feature Code ALLOW999SSNS should not be enabled for the
                              client.

                              Note: On the Client Details form, on the Other tab, under Other Options the
                              field named Contractors (1099) Allowed should be selected.

Hire Type Select the employee Hire Type. The Use Onboarding field displays only if the company is set up to prompt for electronic onboarding. Use Onboarding From the Use Onboarding drop-down, indicate whether you are entering all of the employee’s information or if the employee will enter it in Employee Portal (EP). This affects which fields are required. Employee IDs are generated automatically at the creation of the employee record and they cannot be edited. Each ID consists of a letter followed by five digits.

Employment Status Enter or select the employee’s Employment Status. Employment Type Enter or select the employee’s Employment Type. Benefit Group Enter or select the employee’s Benefit Group. Field Description Project Enter or select the employee’s Project. Work Group Enter or select the employee’s Work Group. Union Code Enter or select the Union Code for the union to which the employee belongs. PTO Approver Enter or select the employee ID or enter the worksite trusted advisor’s user ID of the PTO Approver who would approve the new hire’s PTO requests. Worksite managers, as the logged-in user, can automatically assign themselves as the person who approves the employee’s PTO requests by selecting Assign To Me. This option is useful for WSMs who do not have access to view themselves in the PTO Approver Employee Search Results list because of data security. However, they can still enter or paste their employee ID in the PTO Approver field as long as they are an employee in that company. Note the following: • This option is only available for worksite managers. If you log in as a service provider or worksite trusted advisor, Assign To Me does not display. • When worksite managers select Assign To Me, the system automatically populates their employee ID in the PTO Approver field when they are also an employee in the active company. (Worksite managers can be an employee in more than one company.) If they are not an employee in the active company, an error message displays, “The Employee ID you entered is not valid for this company.” • Worksite managers cannot enter or paste their employee ID in the PTO Approver field for an employee outside of the company where that WSM works. (An error displays if they try to perform this action.) However, service providers can enter or paste a worksite manager’s employee ID for an employee outside of the company where the WSM works.

Manager Enter or select the employee ID or enter the worksite trusted advisor’s user ID of the person who the employee reports to upon employment. Worksite managers, as the logged-in user, can automatically assign themselves as the person who supervises the employee by selecting Assign To Me. This option is useful for WSMs who do not have access to view themselves in the Manager Employee Search Results list because of data security. However, they can still enter or paste their employee ID in the Manager field as long as they are an employee in that company. Note the following: • This option is only available for worksite managers. If you log in as a service provider or worksite trusted advisor, Assign To Me does not display.

To establish compensation details about the new employee, complete the following fields:

Field Description Pay Group Enter or select the Pay Group to which the new employee belongs. Pay Method Select the Pay Method by which the employee will be paid. Note: The Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. Pay Rate Enter the Pay Rate that corresponds with the selected Pay Rate Basis. This is a warning only. Continue? • Click Yes to save the change. • Click No to return to the Pay Rate field. Pay Rate Basis Select the Pay Rate Basis that determines the employee’s pay period. Standard Hours Enter the Standard Hours worked by the employee during the pay period. The system uses this to calculate the employee’s annualized pay. Auto Time Sheet Select Auto Time Sheet if this is a salaried employee and PrismHR should automatically create and accept time sheets for the employee. Default Time Sheet Hours Enter the Default Time Sheet Hours to use in conjunction with the Auto Time Sheet option. The employee’s time sheet defaults to that number of hours. First Pay Period Hours If available, you can enter the First Pay Period Hours. This is typically used for employees with auto time sheet hours when their hire date falls in the middle of a payroll period. Entering New Hire Notes You can enter notes or reminders about a newly hired employee using the New Hire Notes form.

To enter notes or reminders about the new hire, access the form using one of these methods: • Enter New Hire Notes in the search box. • Select New Hire Notes from the Actions menu in the New Hire form on the HR|Action menu.

Use the Suppress option to restrict the display of notes by user or user role. To suppress a note immediately, click the Stop Showing button.

New Hire Download Processing Note that the New Hire Reporting form (Process ID: HRPY.WORK*NEW.HIRE.REPORTING.ENTRY) can include information on employees from restricted clients. The system produces a complete file which includes annual salary without exceptions based on the Client Access Group and the restricted clients listed in it. For this reason, it is recommended that access to this form be limited to users with unrestricted access to all clients in the database. The New Hire Reporting feature builds a file that includes all required criteria and meets specifications for all states. The utilities for new hire report processing are: • New Hire Reporting - Creates a New Hire Report that you can review for accuracy before building the download file to send to the state. • Clear New Hire Reporting Dates - Clears the previously assigned Hire Report Dates so you can run New Hire Reporting again. Currently this process is performed in the backend system for PrismHR. • Set New Hire Reporting Dates - Sets the date for previously reported employees so they will not be included in the New Hire Reporting file. This process is also performed in the backend system for PrismHR.

New Hire and Termination Reporting Center The New Hire and Termination Reporting Center provides convenient access to the forms required to process new hire and termination reporting. The New Hire and Termination Reporting form can include information on employees from restricted clients. The system produces a complete file which includes annual salary without exceptions based on the Client Access Group and the restricted clients listed in it. For this reason, it is recommended that access to this form be limited to users with unrestricted access to all clients in the database.

To open a New Hire and Termination Reporting page: On the Work Centers panel, under Compliance, click New Hire and Termination Reporting and then select the relevant form. Under Reporting Date Overrides, select from the following options: • See Clearing Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates on page 167 • See Clearing New Hire Reporting Dates on page 166 • See Setting a New Hire Reporting Date on page 167 Under Downloads, select the following option: • See Termination Reporting on page 170 • Previewing New Hire Reporting

To get detailed instructions for using the open form:

• Click Online Help in the header area.

To return to the previous page:

• Click in the header area of the form.

Clearing New Hire Reporting Dates If you enter a new hire reporting date in an employee record, the employee does not display on the New Hire Reporting download. The Clear New Hire Reporting Dates process clears the new hire reporting dates, so the employees display on the subsequent New Hire Reporting download. For example, if you are supporting international employees, they initially use a temporary SSN during the application period. When the permanent SSN is issued, you might need to clear the New Hire Reporting Date so those employees are included in the next reporting cycle. Use the Clear New Hire Reporting Dates form to clear the New Hire Reporting Date for a specified date range for one or all clients. You can also use this form to clear the New Hire Reporting Date for a specified date range for one or more employees for a selected client.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under the heading Compliance, click New Hire and Termination Reporting. Then under the heading Reporting Date Overrides, click Clear New Hire Reporting Dates.

To clear new hire reporting dates: 1. Complete the following

Field Name Description Starting New Hire Report Enter the starting date of the reporting date range from when you want to clear Date New Hire Reporting Date.

Ending New Hire Report Enter the ending date of the reporting date range till when you want to clear New Date Hire Reporting Date. Client ID This field is optional. Leave it blank to select all clients. If you want to clear the New Hire Reporting Date for employees for a particular client, enter it here or click the Client ID hyperlink to select it from the Select Client dialog.

                              Note: Once you enter a Client ID here, the following field becomes visible.

Employee This field is optional. Leave it blank to select all employees for the selected client. Here you can enter one or more employees for whom you want to clear the New Hire Reporting Date for the selected date range, or click the Employee hyperlink and select one or more employees from the Select Employee dialog.

Clearing Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates Use this process to reset the Employment Verification Service (EVS) reporting dates. These Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates are used when processing the EVS download file that is generated from the W-2 work center (W-2 Processing > W-2 Processes > Create Employee SSN Verification Download). If a reporting date is entered in the Employment Verification Service (EVS) reporting date, the employee is not shown on the EVS download. This process resets the EVS reporting dates so that the employees will be shown on the EVS download file.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under the heading Complianceclick on New Hire and Termination Reporting. Then under the heading Reporting Date Overrides click on Clear Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates.

To clear employee SSN verification reporting dates: 1. Enter Starting EVS Report Date which is a mandatory date field. Please enter the date from which you want to clear the employee SSN Verification reporting. 2. Enter Ending EVS Report Date which is a mandatory date field. Please enter the date upto which you want to clear the employee SSN Verification reporting. 3. Company ID is an optional free text field. Leave it blank to select all clients. 4. Click Process. A progress window opens that shows the number of records read and the number of records cleared and notifies you when the process is complete. The Close and Report buttons remain disabled while the report is being generated. 5. Click Close to close the window. 6. Click Report to display the Job Control Status Report window. 7. In the Job Control Status Report window, click the XLS link to download the report.

Setting a New Hire Reporting Date Use the Set New Hire Reporting Dates process to enter new values for the new hire reporting dates. When a new employee is hired, the employer is required to report that new hire to the state they are hired in via an electronic file (Back Office) > Operations|Action > New Hire Reporting. The final step of this reporting download process is to add the new hire reporting date on the employee record so that the employee is not reported multiple times.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 167 Chapter 8 Defining Job Applicants and New Hires

The Set New Hire Reporting Date option enables you to manually add the new hire reporting date on the employee record in either of the following situations: • The employee record was locked, therefore not included in the New Hire Reporting Download file, but was manually added to the States Download. • The employer does not want to report the new hire to the state using the New Hire Reporting Download file.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To set new hire reporting dates: 1. In the Work Centers panel, under Compliance click New Hire and Termination Reporting. Under Reporting Date Overrides select Set New Hire Reporting Date. 2. Starting New Hire Report Date is a required date field — select the start date of reporting date range. 3. Ending New Hire Report Date is a required date field — select the end date of reporting date range. 4. Click the Client ID link to select a specific client for the report or leave blank to select all clients. 5. Click the Employee ID link to select a specific employee for the report or leave blank to select all employees. 6. Click Process. A progress window opens that shows the number of records read and the number of records updated and notifies you when the process is complete. The Close and Report buttons remain disabled while the report is being generated. 7. Click Report to display the Job Control Status Report window. 8. In the Job Control Status Report window, click the XLS link to download the report.

Chapter 9 Defining OSHA and Workers’ Compensation Case Files Use PrismHR to define and work with OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration) and workers’ compensation case file information.

Note: Before entering case files, your organization must define events; see Establishing OSHA Event Codes on page 21.

Creating and Updating OSHA Case Files Use the OSHA Cases form to create and update Occupational Safety & Health Administration (OSHA) case files for work-related injuries or illnesses.

OSHA Case The first panel establishes basic information for the OSHA case file.

To set up or modify an OSHA case: 1. Click New Case to create a new OSHA case file, or enter the Case Number of an existing case file. 2. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 3. If this case involves privacy concerns, select the Privacy Case? option. If this field is selected, the OSHA 300 Log will display the employee name as “Privacy Case”. 4. Enter the employee’s Position. The default comes from the Employee Details; do not enter the activity in which the employee was engaged. 5. Enter the code for home Department code in which the employee worked when the injury occurred or at the onset of the illness. The default comes from the Employee Details. 6. Enter the Location code where the injury or illness occurred. The description displays. 7. Modify the fields in the panels listed below, as necessary. 8. Click Save.

Note: PrismHR uses the Benefit Start Date to calculate the number of months the employee has worked for the client.   3. Enter the YTD Hours Calculated (+), which is the starting balance of Time Off hours accrued in the current year. About Benefit Start Dates The Benefit Start Date field dictates the calculation that the system uses. • You can only adjust the Benefit Start Date for employees enrolled in fiscal year registers. You cannot change it for anniversary-based registers. • When the eligibility for Time Off benefits is based on seniority level (the number of months worked), the system uses its calculation based on this date to determine the employee’s seniority level. • If the client’s Time Off register uses Anniversary Year End as the accrual schedule’s accrual calculation method, the system uses the date to calculate the Time Off register year-end date.

Understanding the Calculated Thru Date Field If the employee has accumulated Time Off hours prior to the initialization of this Time Off Register, you must enter the number of Time Off hours, any carryover hours available, and the date through which the hours were accrued.

WARNING: If you do not enter the correct date in the Calculated Thru Date field, PrismHR may accrue
excess hours for this employee.

It is critical that you enter the correct “accrued through” date in the Calculated Thru Date field. The system accrues any Time Off hours from this date forward, according to the terms of the absence Time Off plan and accrual schedule. To determine the date correctly, it is important to understand the client’s Time Off plan; that is, does it accrue increments of Time Off hours throughout the year, or perhaps deposit the whole amount at one time? For example, an employee has three vacation days available to her at the time you take on a particular client. The employee is not scheduled to accrue any more until January 1 of the following year. You must ensure the date you enter in the Calculated Thru Date field is December 31. The next time the register is triggered, whether the it is the next pay period, end of month, or another time, PrismHR will calculate the number of days between December 31 and the trigger date. During payroll processing, PrismHR automatically updates the employee’s Time Off register with any due accruals.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 190 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

If you are going to update Time Off hours more frequently, such as when increments of time are deposited each payroll period, ensure you understand exactly what “accrued through” date the client used when they submitted the employee’s Time Off hours to you. Was it through the last day of the payroll period or through the pay date? You must determine the “accrued through” date with the client to ensure the employee’s Time Off register accrues correctly.

Processing Time Off Auto Register Enrollment The Time Off automatic enrollment process tests every employee against the eligibility rules (set up for the client in Time Off Auto Enroll Rules, found in the Client menu) and enrolls employees into absence benefits if they meet the eligibility criteria. Use the Time Off Auto Register Enrollment form as a quick way to build up a list of employees in a plan and assign them their first Accrued Thru Date. You would typically use this feature when you need to enroll existing employees in a new Time Off plan.

To build up a list of employees in a plan and assign them: 1. If appropriate, enter the Benefit Start Date to override the default. The system uses this date to calculate the number of months that the employee has worked for the client. If you do not enter a date in the field, the system automatically calculates the date on which it would have begun for each employee. Note: The Benefit Start Date field will not override on registers where the Time Off Auto-Enroll Rule has either Seniority Date or Hire Date selected on the Use Seniority Date or Hire/Rehire Date? field. 2. In the Accrued Thru Date field, you should enter the date through which time off benefits would have previously been accrued. • When you enter a date, the system calculates each employee’s Time Off benefits from that date forward.

How PrismHR Uses the Accrued Thru Date for Time Off Benefits When it is time for payroll to send out paychecks, the system calculates Time Off benefits from the day after the last date through which the employee accrued benefits (the “accrued through” date) up through the period end date. For example, employees in the ABC Company are paid semi-monthly and were last paid on May 15. When they are paid on June 1, the system knows the accrued through date is May 15, so it calculates the Time Off benefits from May 16 through June 1. If your organization added ABC Company to PrismHR on May 20, you would want to automatically enroll the ABC employees in Time Off benefits. The system has never calculated payroll for these employees before, but its calculations require an “accrued through” date. You define the accrued through date as May 15, so the calculations result in a normal accrual cycle on June 1. Therefore, you use the Time Off Auto Register Enrollment form to not only automatically enroll the employees, you also define an Accrued Thru Date date for the system. When payroll processes the paychecks, the system determines the employees’ Time Off benefits from the day after the date you entered.

Working with Planned Time Off Requests You can review and make changes to employees’ time off (PTO) requests in the Planned Time Off Requests form. The form is found in the HR menu under HR|Action. Important! The system circumvents leave approval security configurations and workflows for users with access to this form, which can result in unexpected behavior. Please note the following security used by this form: • Users with the PTO Administrator H/R Role and access to Manage Planned Time Off Requests can update leave for all employees in the client regardless of their Data Security access or the assigned PTO Approver. • Users without the PTO Administrator H/R Role and with access to Manage Planned Time Off Requests can update leave only for employees where the user has access via Data Security, regardless of the assigned PTO Approver.

Viewing Planned Time Off Requests The requests in the list are for employees at the active client who submitted them through Employee Portal (EP).

When the form opens, the following message displays, “Please wait while we get the leave requests.” (Note: This form defaults to the Display Pending and Display Approved options, so the system will display those entries.) 2. Use the filters at the top of the form to specify which requests to display. 3. If there is more than one page of results, the total number of pages displays above the results, and the Next Page and Previous Page buttons display at the bottom of the page. Making Changes to an Employee’s Time Off To make changes to an employee’s time off, you can: • Set an Approved request to Cancelled. • Set an Approved request to Paid. If you select Paid, then it is removed from this list and from any payrolls. • A yellow indicator displays next to the start date if it is before the period end date of the last completed scheduled payroll batch for the employee’s pay group. Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 195 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

The different statuses affect the system as follows:

Status Description Pending The Time Off request has not yet been approved, cancelled, or paid by the employee’s manager. Note: The request does not display on the timesheet in this status. Approved The Time Off request is approved and scheduled to be paid. Note the following: • If a manager cancels a Time Off request on this form and then the request is approved later on this form, the leave request indicator in the Summary Time Sheet Entry form is restored and the employee’s EP Time Off landing page displays the approved request. • The system does not record the user who approves a Time Off request as the leave approver in the Planned Time Off Requests form. Instead, the system displays the approver from the approval policy.

Cancelled The Time Off request is cancelled. This cancels an employee’s approved Time Off in the EP that occurs in the future. Note the following: • Canceling approved Time Off that occurs in the future stops the Time Off from being applied to the timesheet when it is created. • Canceling approved and applied Time Off on the current timesheet does not remove the indicator and the hours should be manually adjusted in the timesheet.

Paid The Time Off request was previously paid and the employee’s Time Off register was updated. Only service providers can select this option. Note: This status removes the leave request indicator from the timesheet and removes the request from the employee’s EP or Employee Portal (EP) Time Off landing page. It also hides the request from the Planned Time Off Requests form unless you choose to Display Paid.

Note: By default, worksite manager and trusted advisor users can only access employees who report to them, as indicated in the Employee Details Work tab. Note that if you want a user to be able to view requests but not approve them, the user role must have Inquiry permission for Planned Time Off Requests.

Correcting a Duplicate Employee Record WARNING: PrismHR strongly advises you to test this in your Demo account before performing these tasks in your Live account.

If an employee is entered twice with two different Social Security numbers (SSNs), two different sets of records for that employee exist in the system. If the system pays the employee under both SSNs, you must transfer the information from the incorrect record to the correct record to ensure that only one Form W-2 generates.

Terminating Employee Record with Incorrect SSN First, you must terminate the incorrect employee on the Employee Termination form.

To terminate the incorrect employee, do the following: 1. Click the HR menu. 2. From HR|Action, select Employee Termination. The Employee Termination form opens. 3. Complete the following:

 Use this option                        To do this
 Employee ID                            Enter the employee ID with the incorrect SSN (required).
 Termination Status Code                Select a termination status code.
 Reason Code                            Select a reason code (required).
 Termination Date                       Select the termination date (required).
 Termination Explanation                Enter an explanation for the termination. For example, Incorrect
                                        SSN.
  1. Click Save.

Editing the Terminated Employee Record After terminating the employee record with the incorrect SSN, you can edit the terminated employee SSN on the Employee Details form.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 197 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

To edit the employee SSN, do the following: 1. Click the HR menu. 2. From HR|Change, select Employee Details. The Employee Details form opens. 3. Click the Personal tab. 4. In the Personal panel, click Edit SSN. Enter a unique SSN that differs from the correct employee record. For example, 777-88-9999.

  1. Click the Name tab.

  2. To prevent anyone from using the employee record, edit the employee name so users know it is not a valid employee record. For example, John Doe - DO NOT USE.

  3. Click Save. If the employee was paid under the incorrect SSN, you must transfer the tax amounts to the correct employee record. To transfer the tax amounts, subtract the taxes from the incorrect tax register and add them to the correct tax register. First, you must obtain the employee and employer tax totals for the employee paid under the incorrect SSN.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 198 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

Obtaining Tax Totals for Tax Adjustments You can find the employee and employer tax totals for the employee paid under the incorrect SSN on the Payroll Voucher form.

To obtain tax totals for tax adjustments, do the following: 1. Click the Payroll menu. 2. From Payroll|View, select Payroll Voucher. The Payroll Voucher form opens. 3. Select the correct Voucher Number, then click the Tax tab. Make note of the information in the Employee Tax and Employer Tax panels. After obtaining the employee and employer tax totals, you can adjust the taxes.

Adjusting Taxes With the employee and employer tax totals for the employee paid under the incorrect SSN, you can make a tax adjustment on the Tax Adjustment form.

To make tax adjustments for the employee paid with the incorrect SSN, do the following: 1. Click the Payroll menu. 2. From Payroll|Change, select Tax Adjustment. The Tax Adjustment form opens. 3. Enter the Employee ID, Adjustment Date, Employer, and negative amount for taxes. If you do not want to bill the client for the tax adjustment, enable Suppress Billing. If disabled, the system bills the client for the adjustment and updates the billing registers. Then, you must enter both the employee and employer tax withholdings. 4. Click Save.

To make tax adjustments for the employee with the correct SSN, do the following: 1. Click the Payroll menu. 2. From Payroll|Change, select Tax Adjustment. The Tax Adjustment form opens. 3. Click New adjustment. 4. Enter the Employee ID, Adjustment Date, Employer, and a positive amount for taxes. If you do not want to bill the client for the tax adjustment, enable Suppress Billing. If disabled, the system bills the client for the adjustment and updates the billing registers. Then, you must enter both the employee and employer tax withholdings. 5. Click Save. The system displays a dialog box asking if you want to print a refund check now, of if you want to update scheduled payments and reimburse next pay period. Click No. After clicking No, you can go to the Scheduled Payments form to delete the tax refund for both the incorrect and correct employee record.

Verifying Taxes Adjusted Correctly To verify the taxable earnings and tax amounts for the incorrect and correct employee, use the Employee Tax Summary form.

To verify the tax information, do the following:

  1. Click (Back Office).

  4. Enter the correct Employee ID and Year. The amounts should reflect the tax adjustment and any wages paid under the correct employee ID. Both employees have adjustment vouchers in their history explaining the pay and tax adjustments. If you do not want to perform a tax adjustment to correct the paid wages and taxes, you can void payroll vouchers for the incorrect SSN and then calculate and post the pay for the correct SSN. Things to consider: • You can post pay by pay date or by quarter. • Do not to enter pay that crosses from one quarter to the next. • Before processing your ACH file, remove any ACH entries for crediting and debiting the employee and client.

Entering Employee Absences Use the Employee Absence Entry form to enter employee absences from work. This is time off that will affect the employee’s Time Off register. This is found in the HR menu under HR|Change. You can: • Enter a paid absence: Sometimes salaried employees’ absences are not paid out on a time sheet, but they need to be subtracted from the Time Off register. When you use an absence code associated with a Time Off register, the system applies the hours as well as any comments you enter. • Enter an unpaid absence: Track absences for record-keeping purposes. There are reports that list unpaid absences. • Adjust “hours taken”: Adjust the total number of hours taken on the employee’s Time Off register. (To adjust the number of hours accrued or carried over, see Adjusting Accrued or Carryover Hours for Employees on page 249.)

Note: Absence Codes must exist before you can use the Employee Absence form.

To enter employee absences: 1. Enter the Employee ID by either typing the name or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records, or by clicking the field label to open the search window. 2. Select the Absence Code for this absence. 3. Enter the Date Absent, which is the day the employee was absent or the start date of the absence period if the absence spans multiple days. 4. Enter the total number of Hours Absent. 5. Enter a Comment for this absence, if applicable. For example, you can use this reference a specific voucher or event. 6. Click Save. The system generates the Journal ID when you save the absence entry.

Tracking Employee Leaves of Absence Use the Leave of Absence form to track an employee’s leave of absence while maintaining the employee’s status of employment at your company. This is used for absences that are not covered by PTO registers.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 201 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

Note: The PTO Accruals panel only displays when the following conditions are met: • The entered or selected employee is enrolled in one or more PTO registers. • You enter a Leave Effective Date that is either the current day or a date before that day.

To track an employee’s leave of absence, do the following: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. The employee’s current status and type display. 2. Select the Leave Employment Status for the employee. Note: This field displays the full description of the status code, separated by a dash (-) in front of the status code. 3. Enter the Leave Effective Date. 4. Select the Reason Code for the leave of absence. 5. Enter the Planned Return from Leave date when the employee plans to return to work. 6. To stop PTO accruals for the employee, select the Stop PTO Accruals field for the PTO Register Type. (The PTO Register Type and PTO Benefit Plan columns display the PTO Register and Plan where the employee is enrolled.) Note: After you save this selection and there is a leave of absence approval policy in place, when the leave of absence is approved this setting registers in the Stop Time Off Accruals field on the Employee Time Off Register form. 7. Click Save.

Note: Use Reactivation to return an employee to regular employment status.

For example, if your client employs seasonal employees whom they terminate at the end of the season, you can select the Termination option to terminate those employees in a single process. Reassigning Pending Approvals for Terminated Employees During the termination process, the system detects if any employees being terminated have pending approvals. If the terminated employees do have pending approvals a prompt displays after the termination is complete, “There are pending approvals assigned to terminated employees. Do you want to reassign the pending approvals to other client users?”

To reassign pending approvals for terminated employees, do the following: 1. Click Yes. 2. The Manage Pending Approvals form displays, where you can reassign pending approvals to other users. Note: For more information, see Managing Pending Approvals.

Inactivating Mass Employee Direct Deposit Records Use this feature to locate all employees who have not been paid as of a certain date and inactivate their direct deposit records at once.

Performing Mass Employee Direct Deposit Inactivation You can locate and inactivate direct deposit records for multiple employees using the Mass Inactivate Employee ACH Record form.

To use this feature, do the following: 1. Go to the Mass Inactivate Employee ACH Record form on the HR|Action menu. 2. Select or enter a date in the Employee Not Paid As Of field. A list of employees associated with that date displays. 3. If necessary, select an appropriate option in the Employment Status field to filter employee records for the client (the default is ALL). 4. To inactivate the direct deposit records for all employees in the list, click Select All. Otherwise, select each employee as a recipient of this action. 5. Click Inactivate ACH. A confirmation dialog displays. 6. Click Yes to continue. A message displays confirming that the records for the selected employees were updated.

Working with Backdated Leave Requests You can process approved, backdated leave requests for salaried employees by creating a manual check adjustment using the Backdated Leave Request Processing form.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 207 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

To display on this form, an employee must be in a payroll batch with the Time Sheet Entry status. Also, the batch pay period dates must be later than the backdated leave request dates to be processed using Backdated Leave Request Processing functionality. The manual check created from this process backs out the hours and associated dollars from the Offset Pay Code and assigns them to the Leave Pay Code using the appropriate codes on the Time Off Pay form. It also updates the employee’s Time Off register with the appropriate hours taken and includes other details from the Leave Request.

To process a backdated leave request: 1. Check the Select All checkbox to process all the requests or check individual requests. 2. Click Save. 3. A dialog displays stating that clicking Yes will process the approved, backdated leave request(s), then a manual check adjustment for each selected request will be created to reduce the offset pay code hours by the absence code hours. Clicking No cancels the process. 4. A confirmation dialog displays stating that the request(s) was successfully processed, and changes will be reflected in the next payroll. Click OK. 5. Click View Report to view the Backdated Leave Request Report. 6. After closing the report, successfully processed records no longer display in the form.

Note: To enable Backdated Leave Request Processing for Worksite Managers and Trusted Advisors, set the ALLOWWSMWTABDLR custom feature code at the system level.

Viewing Pending Actions To display the number of employees in a regular payroll with pending backdated leave requests, click the yellow indicator in the Pending Actions column on the Time Sheet Entry, Process Payroll, and SuperBatch forms. (A form displays that provides more details.) Note that backdated leave requests only display on the Backdated Leave Request Processing form in the following conditions: • Only salaried employees display.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 208 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

• The backdated leave request must be approved. • The date of the backdated leave request must occur before the current timesheet pay period. • The employee must be part of the current timesheet. • The payroll for that timesheet must be in Time Entry status. • The payroll is a regular batch. • The backdated leave request pending actions do not display on the SuperBatch form when there are no pending approvals.

You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. The employee’s current status and type display. 2. Select the Reactivated Employment Status. Note: This field displays the full description of the status code, separated by a dash (-) in front of the status code. 3. Select the Reactivated Employment Type.

Terminating an Employee Use the Employee Termination form to terminate an employee.

Note: To terminate multiple employees at once, see Processing Mass Employee Changes.

When you terminate an employee, PrismHR performs the following based on your system’s global settings: • Terminates the employee’s benefits • Removes the employee’s web access login • Disables the employee’s ACH • Refunds the client for the new hire fee, if the PEO has a policy when new hires are terminated within 30 days of being hired • Displays a warning flag if the employee has an outstanding loan balance

Rehiring a Terminated Employee You can rehire an employee who was previously terminated using the Rehire form. When the Rehire form opens, four panels display the following information after you enter or select a terminated employee: • Rehire: Displays the employee’s employment status information. • Personal Information: Displays the employee’s contact information. • Employment Details: Displays the employee’s work details. • Pay Details: Displays the employee’s pay information. Note: Any changes you make in the Employment Details panel and the Pay Details panel take effect immediately and do not abide by the date entered in the Rehire Date field in the Rehire panel. (Future dated changes are not supported. If you enter a future date, the system uses the current date.) After you enter or select an employee, the following panels display depending on the client’s settings on the Client Details form: • E-Verification Options: Select whether to launch E-Verification for this employee. (This panel only displays if the Enable E-Verification? field in the Control tab on the Client Details form is enabled and the employee’s worksite location is not selected to exclude E-Verify.) • Onboarding Options: Select whether to launch Onboarding for this employee. (This panel only displays if the Electronic On-Boarding for Rehires field in the Control tab on the Client Details form is set to Prompt.) • Benefits Enrollment Options: Select whether to launch Benefits Enrollment for this employee. (This panel only displays if the Electronic Enrollment field in the Control tab on the Client Details form is set to NextGen.)

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 223 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

Note: To rehire multiple employees at once, see Processing Mass Employee Changes.

For example, after you enter or select a terminated employee’s information, the following panels might display:

In addition, required field settings in the Control tab on the Client Details form that have associated settings in the Controls panel on the New Hire form and the Employee Details form for Department, Shift, Work Group, or Division fields are conditionally required on the Rehire form.

Reviewing Status Type History You can access the employee’s status history by opening the Actions menu and selecting Status Type History.

Performing Status Type Changes Use the Status Type Change form to change: • Employment status to one of the same class, such as Active PT to Active FT • Employment type, such as seasonal to part-time • Employment hours

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 229 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

Note: To perform a status change for multiple employees at once, see Processing Mass Employee Changes.

To change an employee status, do the following: 1. Enter or select the Employee ID. The employee’s name, current employment status and type display. Note: A warning message displays when there is an existing future dated pay history record for the same effective date and an entry exists in the New Standard Hours field, “A Pay Rate Change has already been entered with that effective date. If you continue, that change will be discarded. Do you wish to continue?” If you select Yes, the system saves the record and clears the form. (Selecting No returns you to the form where the entries still display.) 2. Select the New Employment Status. This must be a status of the same class as the current status: either active, leave, or terminated. If you need to change the status from an on leave status to an active status, for example, you need to use the Reactivation feature. Note: When you perform a status type change for an employee who has an on leave status classification or a terminated status classification, the following items do not update: • Auto enrollment of benefits • Auto enrollment of PTO • Auto enrollment of retirement • Standard hours or default time sheet hours updates 3. Select the New Employment Type associated with an updated employment status. 4. Enter the New Standard Hours associated with an updated employment status. The Current column displays the employee’s current Standard Hours and Default T/S Hours (if any). 5. Enter the New Default T/S Hours associated with an updated employment status. Note: The New Standard Hours and New Default T/S Hours field values are not required, so only enter these hours if they are applicable. Also, to hide these fields so Worksite Managers and Worksite Trusted Advisors cannot access them (recommended method), set the field security to Hidden for the form. (Setting the field security to Disable disables the fields.)

Setting up Changes to an Employee’s Benefit Group You can set up a change to an employee’s benefit group using the Benefit Group Maintenance form.

To set up a proposed change to an employee’s benefit group, do the following: 1. Go to the Benefit Group Maintenance form on the HR|Action menu. 2. Enter the Employee name or click this field and select it from the Employee Search Results for Active Employees list. 3. Click New Benefit Group and select a benefit group from the Benefit Group list. The benefit group number displays in the field, along with its description. 4. The Benefit Group History panel also displays where you can view the effective dates and codes for changes to that employee’s benefit group. 5. Enter the effective date in the Benefit Group Start Date field or select a date. 6. Click Save to save the changes to the record. 7. Click Cancel to clear the form.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 231 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

Updating or Deleting the Future Effective Date of an Employee’s Benefit Group Change You can update the effective date of a change to an employee’s benefit group or delete the change using the Benefit Group History panel.

To update or delete the effective date for a proposed change to an employee’s benefit group, do the following: 1. In the Benefit Group History panel, click the future date you want to change or delete in the Date Effective column. 2. To change the effective date, click the future date hyperlink. The New Effective Date dialog box displays. a. Enter or select the new effective date in the New Effective Date field. b. Click Save. The list updates with the new effective date. c. Click Cancel to clear the New Effective Date field. d. Click Close to close the dialog box without making any updates. 3. To remove the effective date, select the checkbox against the future date that you want to delete and click Delete. A confirmation message stating Benefit Group change will be deleted. Are you sure? displays. a. Click Yes to delete the record. b. Click No to close the confirmation message and remain on the form.

Note: For entering a past date in theBenefit Group Start Date field: • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the past date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? On the warning message, when you click: • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data. • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written. • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the past date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

Resetting Blocked Filing Status This process resets the employee tax filing status of blocked to single with zero exemptions. The filing year for the Form W-4 must be prior to or equal to the applicable tax year.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To reset the employee tax filing status:

  1. On the (Back Office) menu, select Operations|Action > Reset Federal Withholding Blocked Override.
  2. In Year, enter the tax year applicable to the most current federal Form W-4 on file for this employee.
  3. Click Process.
  4. Click Yes when prompted to continue. A progress window opens and notifies you when the Federal Withholding Blocked Initialization has completed along with the number of employees updated. The Close and Report buttons remain disabled number of employees while the report is being generated.
  5. Click Close to close the window.
  6. Click Report to display the Job Control Status Report window.
  7. In the Job Control Status Report window, click the XLS link to download the report.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 235 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

Using the Approval Process When events take place that could potentially require an approval, such as a new hire or a payroll, PrismHR determines if there is a policy in place for the particular approval type. • If there is no policy definition, then the system immediately updates the database with the new hire or other information. • If there is an approval policy, then the system generates an approval event. If the first step for the approval is assigned to a particular user, then an e-mail is sent to that user. In addition, when the user logs in, the dashboard alerts the user of any pending approvals. Approvals Pending is found in the Client menu under Client|Action.

Working with Pending Approvals The Approvals Pending form lists any pending approvals that are assigned or available to you. • An approval that is assigned to a particular user can only be acted upon by that user. • Approvals are available to a user if one of the user’s roles matches the role applicable to the current approval step. Note: Click the Refresh button to remain on the same form or report while refreshing the window to display new entries. Note the following when working with pending approvals: • Existing employees and newly-entered new hires who have a preferred name display that name on the Approvals Pending form and associated approval forms. In this situation, the system uses the employee’s assigned preferred name instead of their legal first name. • If the employee does not have a preferred name, the system uses their first name, last name. • I-9 Section 2 and Pay Card approvals, or any approval associated with a pre-hire, display the employee’s legal first and last name even if a preferred name is available. • For Late Payroll Posting Approval Policies (see Setting Approval Policies and Setting Global Approval Policies for information about this policy): • When a Late Payroll Posting pending approval is approved: • The associated payroll batch status updates from POSTPEND > INITCOMP. • The Approval status is Approved. • Starting Payroll Finalization again after receiving the approval completes the finalization process without disruption, assuming there are no changes to the timesheet or recalculations have occurred in the payroll. • If you update the timesheet or recalculate the payroll, the approval must be resubmitted. • When a Late Payroll Posting pending approval is denied: • The associated payroll batch status updates from POSTPEND > INITCOMP. • The Approval status is Denied.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 236 Chapter 10 Updating Employee Records

     •   When you attempt Payroll Finalization again after the approval is denied, the system generates a
         new Late Payroll Posting Approval for the payroll.

• For ACH Maximum Approval Policies (see Setting Approval Policies for information about this policy): • When the pending approval is approved and the client is set to Disabled in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the associated payroll status updates from INITPEND to INITCOMP and the Approval status changes to Approved. • When the pending approval is denied, regardless of the client’s setting in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the associated payroll status updates from INITPEND to TSOKCOMP and the Approval status changes to Denied. • When the pending approval is approved and the client is set to Standard or Multistep in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the associated payroll status updates from INITPEND to AP.PEND and the Approval status changes to Approved.

Approvals Pending (Available to You) To act on an approval that is available to you, “grab” the approval. The system assigns the approval to you. 1. Within the Approvals Pending (Available to You) panel, click the desired Approval Type. The Approval form opens. You can click Show Audit History to display the history of users involved in processing the action. 2. Click Grab. The selected approval type now appears in the Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel. There are two methods available to process an approval: • Click the Approve icon (blue checkmark) for the Approval Type you want to approve. Click Yes in the confirmation message that displays to continue with the approval. An approval confirmation displays at the top of the form. • “Grab” the approval: 1. Within the Approvals Pending (Available to You) panel, click the desired Approval Type. The Approval form opens. You can click Show Audit History to display the history of users involved in processing the action. 2. Click Grab. The selected approval type now appears in the Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel.

Note: You can open the pending approval in Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel and click Return to Queue. The approval pending item is then returned to the Available to You queue for you or another user to access later.

Managing Pending Approvals Service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted providers can use the Manage Pending Approvals form to perform the following tasks: • Reassign pending approvals to other users. • Return a pending approval to the queue when the approval policy is based on a role, which allows any user with that role to approve it. (This is useful since you do not need to select a person to perform the pending approval.) • Reassign a pending approval to a specific user or return the approval to the Approvals Pending queue. (See the step on using the Assignment Options panel, which is described below.) Important! Worksite managers can manage approvals for any users who have access to the client using the Manage Pending Approvals form. In addition, Worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors are required to limit user access to approvals for only those employees/payrolls where they are granted appropriate security access.

Note: This form replaces the Reassign Pending Approvals form. If you enter the old form name in the search box and press Enter, the Manage Pending Approvals form automatically displays. You can reassign the following types of approvals: • Pending approvals of service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors assignees • All approval types, including I-9 Section 2 • Allows reassignment to client users whose access is identified in the Customer Users with Access panel on the Security tab of the Client Details form • Multi-step approvals: Retains approval for previous steps and allows reassignment of the next available step

Division History Adjustment Use the Division History Adjustment form to change the effective date of a division change for an employee, or delete the division change entirely.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 244 Chapter 11 Updating Employees’ Historical Information

  1. Click the Date Effective to change or delete. This is the date the division went into effect for the employee.

    1. Enter the New Effective Date.

Adjusting Accrued or Carryover Hours for Employees You can use the Employee Time Off Register Adjustment form to adjust an employee’s number of accrued hours or carryover hours from a previous year. You can also adjust the accrued through date. This is found in the HR menu under HR|Change. Note the following when using the Employee Time Off Register Adjustment form: • Absence Codes must exist before you can use the Employee Time Off Register Adjustment form. • When you archive a register, you cannot adjust it. Therefore, to prevent you from making an adjustment to an archived register, these accrual schedules do not display as an option in the Accrual Schedule field.

Note: The system automatically assigns the Journal ID.

In addition, you can access the Time Off Register Adjustment Import form by clicking the Import icon ( ) that displays in this form. See Importing Time Off Adjustment Information on page 255 for more information.

To adjust an employee’s number of hours, do the following: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 2. Select the Time Off Accrual Schedule for this adjustment. 3. Enter the Effective Date, which is the day of the adjustment or the start date of the adjustment period if the adjustment spans multiple days. 4. Enter the Calculated Hours to add to the employee’s Time Off register.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 249 Chapter 11 Updating Employees’ Historical Information

  1. Enter the Carry-Over Hours to add to the employee’s Time Off register.
  2. Enter the Calculated Thru Date, which is the date through which you want to update the employee’s accrued through for the accrual schedule. Further accruals occur for payrolls with a pay date after this date. If you want to adjust only the date, enter zeroes in the hours fields.
  3. Enter a Comment about the adjustment, if applicable. For example, you can use this reference a specific voucher or event.
  4. Click Save.

Importing 401(k) Adjustment Information Use the Retirement Adjustments Import process to import 401(k) adjustment information and to generate an error report and a transaction report. The 401(k) adjustment information is imported using a comma-delimited, tab-delimited, or pipe-delimited text file that is created in Excel.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group security.

Before you begin: 1. In Excel, create a comma-delimited, tab-delimited, or pipe-delimited text file that contains at least the following adjustment information in the order shown: • Column 1 - Client ID • Column 2 - Employee • Column 3 - Employer ID • Column 4 - Plan • Column 5 - Adjustment Date (MM/DD/YYYY) • Column 6 - Annotation (Optional) • Column 7 - Retirement Earnings (Optional) • Column 8 - Employee Contribution (Optional) • Column 9 - Catch-up Contribution (Optional) • Column 10 - Post Tax Contribution (Optional) • Column 11 - ROTH Contribution (Optional) • Column 12 - ROTH Catch-up Contribution (Optional) • Column 13 - Employer Contribution (Optional) • Column 14 - Non-Elect Contribution (Optional) • Column 15 - Safe Harbor Type 1 Contribution (Optional) • Column 16 - Safe Harbor Type 2 Contribution (Optional) • Column 17 - Successor Retirement Deferral (Optional) • Column 18 - Successor Catch-up Deferral (Optional) • Column 19 - Successor ROTH Deferral (Optional)

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 254 Chapter 11 Updating Employees’ Historical Information

•    Column 20 - Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral (Optional)
•    Column 21 - Loan (Optional)
•    Column 22 - Loan Payment (Optional)
  1. Save the Excel file as a comma-delimited, tab-delimited, or pipe-delimited text file.
  2. Record the file name and where it was saved. Note: You can use the sample downloadable header file instead of creating your own Excel file.

To import 401(k) adjustment information:

  1. Click (Back Office).

  2. From Operations|Import Processing, select Retirement Adjustments Import. The Retirement Adjustments Import page opens.

  3. Fill in the form.

Importing Time Off Adjustment Information You can use the Time Off Register Adjustment Import process to import time off adjustment information and to generate an error report and a transaction report. The time off adjustment information is imported using a comma-delimited, tab-delimited, or pipe-delimited text file that is created in Excel.

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 255 Chapter 11 Updating Employees’ Historical Information

Note: You can access the related report, Employee Time Off Detail Report. This report provides information about employees’ time off.

Before you begin: 1. In Excel, create a comma-delimited, tab-delimited, or pipe-delimited text file that contains at least the following adjustment information in the order shown: • Column 1 - Client ID. • Column 2 - Employee ID. • Column 3 - Adjustment Type: T-Taken, A-Accrued, and C-Carryover. • Column 4 - Accrual Schedule. • Column 5 - Time Off Plan. (Note: Only required if Employee should be enrolled in plan.) • Column 6 - Time Off Pay Code. (Note: Only required if Adjustment Type ‘T’ is selected.) • Column 7 - Effective Date (MM/DD/YYYY). • Column 8 - Adjustment Hours. • Column 9 - Accrued Through (Optional). • Column 10 - Comment/Annotation (Optional). (Note: If you do not provide a comment, the default comment ‘Imported Adjustment’ displays in the Annotation column in the Employee Time Off Register form.) 2. Save the Excel file as a comma-separated values (CSV) file or plain text file. 3. Record the file name and where it was saved.

To import time off adjustment information, do the following:

  1. Click (Back Office).

  2. From Operations|Import Processing, select Time Off Register Adjustment Import. The Time Off Register Adjustment Import form opens.

  3. Complete the form.

    Option Description Upload File Click the link, click Choose File, select the file you created, and then click submit. When you are notified that the file was uploaded, click Close. Delimiter Select Auto, Comma, Tab, or Pipe. If you select Auto, the system selects the delimiter based on the file content. Qualifier Select None.

  1. Click Import. A progress box displays the status. Note: Although only a maximum of 100 records display, all records are actually imported.
  2. When the progress box shows that the process is complete, click Close to return to the Time Off Register Adjustment Import form or Report to open the Job Control Status Report.

Auto-Enrolling Employees While Importing You can use the Time Off Plan column (column 5) in your Excel file to automatically enroll employees while importing their time off adjustments. Note: If you specify a Time Off plan and that employee is not currently enrolled in a Time Off plan, the system automatically enrolls them during the import process. A Time Off Pay Code is only required if the adjustment is T (Taken). When using this feature, observe the following guidelines:

Scenario Description Employee that is not • If you have an employee who has a seniority date that is not already enrolled in a Time equal to the hire date and you add a valid Time Off Plan to Off Plan column E on the import, the system enrolls the employee in the Time Off Plan/Register on the file with a Benefit Start Date that equals the Seniority date, and a Calculated Thru Date equal to the Benefit Start Date and the Year End Date, which defaults to the appropriate date based on the Time Off setup. • If you have an employee that has a seniority date equal to the hire date, and you add a valid Time Off Plan to column E on the import, the system enrolls the employee in the Time Off Plan/Register on the file with a Benefit Start Date that equals the Original Hire Date, and a Calculated Thru Date equal to the Benefit Start Date and the Year End Date, which defaults to the appropriate date based on the Time off setup. • If you enter a Time Off Plan on the file, but it does not match any existing client Time Off Plan codes, the Employee ID displays the

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 257 Chapter 11 Updating Employees’ Historical Information

Scenario Description following message, “Time Off Plan does not exist for this client. Adjustment and enrollment skipped.” • If an employee is not already enrolled in the Time Off Register/Plan combination on the file and the file contains a Time Off Plan, but the employee is already enrolled in a plan/register with the same Time Off Type/Employee ID, you cannot setup in more than one Time Off Register of the same type. (Adjustment and enrollment are skipped.) • When employees are successfully enrolled along with their adjustments, a message displays regarding the job progress, “Time Off Register Enrollments completed: .” • When employees are not successfully enrolled and the file contains the Time Off Plan field, a message displays regarding the job progress, “Time Off Register Enrollments skipped: .” • The process assumes zero (0) hours for the enrollment in the following situations: Accrued and Taken (adjustment for Carryover), Carryover and Taken (adjustment for Accrued), Carryover and Accrued (adjustment for Taken), and when the employee has multiple adjustment types while any type is not represented on the file.

Employee that is already • When an employee in the adjustment import includes a Time Off enrolled in a Time Off Plan Plan in Column E and the employee is already enrolled in that Time Off Plan/Register combination, the import process performs as normal and makes the adjustments while completely ignoring the enrollment. • The system does not display a message regarding enrollments when a Time Off Plan is included in column E and the employee is already enrolled in the same Time Off Plan/Register combination.

Employee that is already • If an employee is not already enrolled in the Time Off enrolled in a different Register/Plan combination in the file and the file contains a Time Time off Register that has Off Plan, but that employee is already enrolled in a plan/register the same Time Off type with the same Time Off Type, the following message displays, “Employee ID - An employee may not be set up in more than one Time Off Register of the same class. Adjustment and enrollment skipped.” • A job progress window displays this employee scenario failure in the number count of Time Off Register Enrollments and Adjustments skipped.

Performing an Employee Time Off Register Inquiry The Employee Time Off Register form displays paid time off for an employee, including the details of time accrued and taken. This form is found in the HR menu under HR|Change. You can also delete or archive a Time Off register for an employee using this form. The Time Off plan determines how much time off an employee will accrue, and the Time Off accrual schedule determines when the employee accrues time off. The employee’s Time Off register is where the system keeps track of the time off. It is a record of “credit” and “debit” transactions, and shows a running balance. Each time time off accrues, it is posted (credited) to the employee’s register; each absence is subtracted (debited) from the register. For example:

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 264 Chapter 12 Accessing Employee Information

To perform an employee Time Off register inquiry: 1. Enter the Employee by either entering the name, Social Security Number, or ID to display a pop-up list of matching employee records. You can also click the field label or press Ctrl+Enter with your cursor in this field to open the search window. 2. Select the time off Accrual Schedule. The drop-down lists only the plans in which the employee is currently enrolled. Note: If an employee is auto-enrolled in a Time Off plan, “Employee Auto Enrolled” displays. 3. Enter the Time Off Plan. Existing information for this employee displays in the form. • The rest of the top panel summarizes the Time Off plan information. • The Paid Hours Absent Details panel displays each absence taken. • The Hours Accrued/Carry-over Details panel displays each accrual earned by the employee. Note: If you change the Time Off Plan during the plan year ending pay period, you may need to make adjustments. 4. The Benefit Start Date displays the date that was selected when the employee was enrolled. The system uses this date to calculate the employee’s time off for this plan. Note: If you need to change this date, you can only change it for employees enrolled in time off with an Anniversary Year year-end basis plan in the following instances: • When there are no payroll-generated accruals (calculated hours). • When there are manually-entered accruals (calculated hours) or any other manual adjustments in the Employee PTO Register Adjustment form, the PTO Register Adjustment Import form, or the Employee

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 265 Chapter 12 Accessing Employee Information

     Absence form, even if the comment is identical to the format from payroll-generated accruals. For
     example, "CALCULATED THRU 8-14-21."
•    When there are no manual adjustments on the employee’s register.
Note: Currently, if the employee is in a register that has a Fiscal Year End Basis, you are allowed to update
the Benefit Start Date at any time.
You can correct errors made in the Time Off Plan Setup. (Originally, you had to delete the Time Off register
and re-enroll the employees, if they were in an Anniversary Year End Register.)
Note: If you change the Benefit Start Date during the plan year ending pay period, you may need to make
manual adjustments.

  1. To prevent an employee from receiving any time off accruals for this plan, select the Stop Time Off Accruals field. A confirmation message displays, “Are you sure you want to stop the employee from receiving accrued Time Off hours?” Click Yes to proceed. (Note: This setting does not impact the employee’s Benefit Start Date and Accrued Thru Date and the employee remains enrolled in the plan.) To restart an employee’s time off accruals for the plan, deselect this field. (Time Off accruals for the employee immediately begin again.) Note the following when using this setting:

Human Resources User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 266 Chapter 12 Accessing Employee Information

•    If an employee exists in more than one Time Off register, enabling this setting only applies to each
     register separately.
•    When this setting is enabled, an employee in any plan or accrual schedule immediately stops accruing
     hours on the payroll.

     an accrual, the employee's voucher still displays the Paid Time Off Accrued panel on the PTO tab with
     zero (0) hours accrued.

leave of absence or reactivation is approved that setting automatically registers here on the Employee Time
Off Register form in the Stop Time Off Accruals field. (See Tracking Employee Leaves of Absence (page 201)
and Reactivating an Employee.)
  1. If you want to perform time off adjustments for the selected employee, select one of the following shortcuts: • Add an Employee Absence: Opens the Employee Absence form, where you can enter the employee’s absences from work. This is time off that affects the employee’s Time Off register. (See Entering Employee Absences on page 201.) • Make Employee Time Off Adjustments: Opens the Employee PTO Register Adjustment form to adjust the employee’s number of accrued hours or carryover hours from a previous year. You can also adjust the accrued through date. (See Working with Planned Time Off Requests on page 194.) Note the following about these shortcuts: • Only the forms you can access will display as shortcut links. For example, if you do not have access to the Employee Absence form, the Add an Employee Absence shortcut will not display. If you have no access or are denied access to both forms, the header and shortcuts do not display. • When you select a shortcut, the system automatically populates the selected employee in the form that opens. • After you make changes or adjustments in a form and click Save, when you close that form the adjustments immediately display in the Employee Time Off Register if the form is open to the same plan and register for those adjustments.
  2. If you want to terminate a Time Off register for an employee click Archive, which keeps an historical record of that register so you can refer to this information when seeking answers about what was done in the past. Note: You must select an Employee and Accrual Schedule to enable the Archive button. When you click Archive a warning displays stating that any pending Time Off request that have not been approved need to be manually removed using the Planned Time Off Requests form. Confirm this warning by clicking OK. Note: Archiving a Time Off register deletes the register’s Audit Log, so it is no longer available.

Deleting Mass Employee Time Off Registers Use this feature to delete Time Off registers for multiple employees at once. For example, you can use this process if your client restructures their time off (including the register) and wants to remove all terminated employees’ bank records.

Note the following when using the Mass Delete Employee Time Off Registers form: • This form is only available for service providers. • After you delete an employee Time Off register, the system permanently deletes a posted record of all accrued, used, and carryover time off for the employees in the Time Off accrual schedule, so those affected employees will no longer be enrolled for this type of time off.

Creating the 1094-C Report Download The Form 1094-C Report creates a PDF version of Form 1094-C and populates it with information from the current client, for the given year.

To run this report: 1. Open the Work Centers menu. 2. Under Work Centers|Compliance, select ACA Processing. 3. Under ACA Reporting, select 1094C Report Download.

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 8 Chapter 1 Reports

  1. Enter the Year for the 1094-C report.
  2. By selecting the Generate All Clients option, you will only receive a PDF for all the clients you have access to. Now, you do not have to print client by client the ACA Form 1094-Cs.
  3. Once you click Run, a Job Control window displays the progress and the number of selected clients. In case of any errors, redo the process. The system downloads a zip file to your computer, containing a Form 1094-C PDF for each client to which you have access.

Creating the 1095-C Report Download Use the 1095-C Report Download form to generate a PDF of Form 1095-C for employees within a specific client or for employees for all clients that you can access.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To access this form, on the Work Centers under Compliance, click ACA Processing. Under ACA Reporting, click 1095-C Report Download.

To download the ACA 1095-C Report: 1. Complete the following fields:

Field Name Description Tax Year Select the appropriate tax year.

From Employee ID This field is optional. If you want to run this report for a set of employees, enter the first Employee ID here. To Employee ID This field is optional. If you want to run this report for a set of employees, enter the last Employee ID here. Mask SSN This field is optional. Select this option if you want to mask the Social Security number of the employees in the output.

  1. Click Run to generate the report for the selected tax year. • You can generate Form 1095-C PDFs for a maximum of 50,000 employees for a client. • When the job completes, you receive a confirmation email. You need to use the Transfer Downloads File to PC form to download the zip file. • The zip file will contain the PDF files in the format COMPANYID.YEAR.EMPLOYEEID.f1095c.pdf. • The zip file will be downloaded to your system from the main form. Depending on the number of employee records, this can take a while. However, you can continue with your work while this process runs in the background. For example, it can take about two hours to process records for 40,000 employees.
