Benefits Billing Detail Report Use the Benefits Billing Detail Report form to determine what information prints on the Benefits Billing Detail Report and in what order.

  1. In the Selection Parameters section choose from the Defined Ranges drop-down to determine what displays on the report. The drop-down contains the following options: • Current Month (default)- The date range is displayed as the first day of current month and the last day of current month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 6/1/2024-6/30/2024. • Year-to-date- The date range is displayed as the first day of the current year till the current system date. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition displayed on this selection will be 1/1/2024-6/15/2024. • Last Batch- The value displayed will be the date on which last batch was processed. • Prior Month- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous month and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 5/1/2024-5/31/2024.

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 11 Chapter 1 Reports

•    Prior 2 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous two months and the last day
     of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition
     for this selection will be 4/1/2024-5/31/2024.
•    Prior 3 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous three months and the last
     day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range
     definition for this selection will be 3/1/2024-5/31/2024.
•    Prior Year- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous year and the last day of the
     previous year. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this
     selection will be 1/1/2023-12/31/2023.
•    Custom Date Range- You can choose dates in the Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before
     fields.
     •   Enter the Pay Date On or After and the Pay Date On or Before to run this report for a date range.
•    Select Batch ID- You can select the Payroll Number.
  1. Select options under the Sort Criteria section for how the report displays. This section has the following fields: • Primary Sort- This selector indicates the top-level of sort organization for the report results. • Secondary Sort- This selector indicates the order of sort organization within the Primary Sort and the order of the column(s) following the Primary Sort column. For example, if you select Benefit Plan as the Primary Sort option and Employee as the Secondary Sort option, then the results displayed will be first by Plan ID and then by Employee ID within the respective Plan ID result segments. • Report Type- This indicates whether you want a detailed or a summarized report. • Use ‘XLS’ Format- Select this checkbox if you want the report in an XLS format.
  2. Enter the report filters to display on the report. Enter the field type. The field label displays. For example, if you enter a Location, the Location Name displays. The report displays records for that Location.
  3. Click Run.

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 12 Chapter 1 Reports

Depending on the Sort Criteria option selected, the possible report columns that display are: • Location: The benefits plan location. • Department: The benefits plan department. • Benefit Plan ID: The benefit plan ID. • Insurance Class: The Insurance Class to which the Benefit Plan is associated with. • Division: The benefits plan division. • Emp. ID: The employee ID. • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first. • Plan Description: The benefits plan description. • Plan Id: The benefits plan ID. • Voucher#: The plan voucher of the benefit plan. • Pay Date: The date paid. • From Arrears: The amount from arrears, if any. • Amount Billed: The amount billed to the client. • Employee Deduction: The amount deducted from the employee during that date range. • Employee Contribution: The amount the employee contributed during that date range. • Net-Amount Billed: The amount billed to the client minus the employee contribution and arrears.

Using the COVID-19 Leave Estimate Report This report retrieves employee hours and payment information to help you set up emergency paid leave that complies with the Families First Coronavirus Response Act.

To run this report: 1. If you want to filter by Employee Type or Pay Method, select the appropriate option(s). 2. If you want to filter by employee, select the appropriate Employee(s). 3. Click Run. The report generates.

Analyzing the Report For each employee, the report returns: • General employee information (employee number, name, type, pay method, and hire date). • Hours Worked (total and two-week average). Does not include sick time hours.

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 13 Chapter 1 Reports

•    Standard Hours (2 weeks). Uses the Standard Hours value on Employee Details > Pay, adjusted based
     on the employee's pay method. For example, the value for employees on a monthly pay cycle is:

•    Sick Leave Hours (Suggested, Actual, Taken, and Remaining). Suggested hours default to 80 for full-
     time employees. For part-time employees, the value is their two-week average unless the employee was
     hired within the last 6 months. In that case, the value is just the employee's Standard Hours on
     Employee Details > Pay. You can override the Actual Sick Leave Hours value using a new field on
     Employee Details > Other, called COVID-19 Paid Sick Max Hours.
•    Rates of Pay and 2/3 these values, in compliance with the legislation. The Standard value pulls from
     Employee Details. The Average (Last Pay Period) value is calculated using data from the last pay period.
     The system divides wages by hours, adjusted according to any FLSA settings on the employee's pay
     codes. If no FLSA settings exist, the system simply divides all gross payments to the employee by the
     number of hours.

COVID-19 Credit Tracking Report Use the COVID-19 Credit Tracking Report to view accrued tax credits, refunds or deferrals associated with COVID-19 paid leave. To access this form, click Reports. Under Operations|Report, click COVID-19 Credit Tracking Report.

To generate the COVID-19 Credit Tracking Report: 1. Complete the following fields:

Field Description Name Start Pay This field is optional. If you want to limit your report to a specific pay date range, enter the Date starting pay date here. End Pay This field is optional. However, if you have entered the starting pay date above, then enter the Date ending pay date here. Report Select the type of report you want to generate from the following options: Type • Employee Report • Client Summary (Client Totals Only)

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 14 Chapter 1 Reports

Field Description Name Break Out This field is optional. Select this option if you want to include the break out of the 941 Liability 941 Total in your report. Liability Total Breakout This field is optional. Select this option if you want to include the break out of the total for the Tax Tax Credits Accrued under tax deduction codes 00-80 to 00-85 in your report. In the report Credits parameters, this column is further divided into totals for each tax deduction code, as well as the Accrued FMLA Medicare, FMLA Healthcare, Sick Leave Medicare, and Sick Leave Healthcare components. Total Include This field is optional. Select this option if you want to only include clients with credits of deferrals Only in your report, which is the employer-side Social Security Tax Deferred plus Tax Credits Accrued. Clients with Credits or Deferrals Include This field is optional. You can only select this option for the Client Summary (Client Totals Only) Refunds Report. Select this option if you want to only include those clients with refunds in your report. Client Ids This field is optional. If you want to limit your report to specific clients only, you can enter the Client IDs here or click the Client Ids hyperlink and select them from the Client Master Search selector.

  1. Click Run to generate the selected report with the selected parameters on screen. If you are running this report for all employees, it might take a while for the system to complete.
  2. Click Close to close this form at any time.

Report Columns This report is organized by clients, then by employers, then by employees. For each employee, the report displays:

Report Description Column Total 941 Liability associated with tax deduction codes 00-10, 00-11, 00-12, 00-15, and 00-16. Liability If you select Break Out 941 Liability Total in the report parameters, this column is further divided into totals for the above tax deduction codes (income tax, employer-side Medicare tax, employee-side Medicare tax, employer-side Social Security tax, and employee-side Social Security tax).

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 15 Chapter 1 Reports

Report Description Column Employer The employer-side Social Security tax liability that accrued between the dates specified in the Social Cares Act Employer Social Security Deferral table and between the dates specified in the report Security setup parameters. Tax Deferred Tax Credits Tax credits accrued under tax deduction codes 00-80 to 00-85. Accrued If you select Break Out Tax Credits Accrued Total in the report parameters, this column is further divided into totals for each tax deduction code, as well as the FMLA Medicare, FMLA Healthcare, Sick Leave Medicare, and Sick Leave Healthcare components. Total Tax Employer-side Social Security Tax Deferred plus Tax Credits Accrued. Credits and Deferrals Net Current Total 941 Liability minus Total Tax Credits and Deferrals. 941 Liability

The report also displays client totals for each of these values.

Refund columns If you select Include Refund, the report includes these columns:

Rebate Column Description Credit Refund Total credit rebates. Form 7200 COVID credits rebated under Form 7200. Defer Refund Refunded employer-side Social Security taxes. UnRefund SS Intended Social Security tax deferrals MINUS the actual rebate. UnRefund CR Total credits minus Credit Refunds and Form 7200 Refunds. Pending Future-dated bill pending items. This total displays at the top of the COVID-19 Refunds form.

                 Please see Viewing and Updating COVID-19-Related Client Bill Pending Entries.

EDI History Report more of an audit report to compare the employee bill rate to the actual premium rate being paid to the carrier and see the variance if any. Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the form, click Reports. Under Operations|Report, click EDI History Report.

Original Client ID This field is optional. This is the original billed Client ID. This would normally be blank for a test download. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all clients. If you want to restrict this report to run for a selected client, enter the Client ID here or click the Original Client ID link and select it from the Select Client dialog box. Process Date On or After This is the date the invoice was processed. This field is optional. Leave this field blank for the report to run for all EDI process dates. Invoice Date On or After This is the invoice date for the item being submitted through EDI. This field is optional. Leave this field blank for the report to run for all invoice dates. If you want to restrict this report to run from a particular invoice date, enter it here. Invoice Date On or Before This is the invoice date for the item being submitted through EDI. This field is optional. Leave this field blank for the report to run for all invoice dates. If you want to restrict this report to run up to a particular invoice date, enter it here. EDI Agent ID Enter the EDI Agent ID here.

  1. Click Run to generate the report. The report shows up on screen.

Creating the EEO-1 Download Report This form produces a report in .csv format, summarizing EEO-1 and, if applicable, Component 2 data.

To run the report: 1. In the Work Centers menu, navigate to Work Centers|Compliance > EEO-1 Processing. 2. Under the EEO-1 Report Processing category, under Reports, select EEO-1 Download Report. 3. Select the report Year. 4. To generate a report that contains Component 2 reporting data, select Build Component 2 Format. 5. Click Generate Report: the Job Control form displays the progress of the report generation. 6. Review the Job Control details and the click Close. 7. Click Download Report to obtain the report download through your web browser.

The generated .csv file will contain labeled counts for each EEO-1 reporting category. Note: Client and Worksite Location level federal contractor settings are now applied to the EEO-1 Download Report. If in the Client EEO-1 & Pay Data Files form Additional Companies are included, and: • If the headquarters client is a federal contractor and any listed additional clients are not, then the specific additional clients who are not federal contractors are not reported as a federal contractor on the EEO-1 Download Report. • However, if those additional clients who are not federal contractors are flagged as federal contractors on their Worksite Locations form, then those specific those worksite locations will be reported as federal contractors. • If the headquarters client is a federal contractor and one or more of the listed additional clients are also federal contractors, then the additional client or clients will be reported as federal contractors using the client specific Unique Entity Identity (UEI).

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 1 Reports

Running the Electronic 1095-C Report The Electronic 1095-C Report lists employees for a specified year, along with their Form 1095-C register status and the identity of the individual designated to receive an electronic Form 1095-C.

Procedure To run this report: 1. Open the Work Centers menu. 2. Under Work Centers|Compliance, select ACA Processing. 3. Under ACA Reporting, select Electronic 1095-C Report. 4. Enter the reporting Year. 5. If you want to include employees who have a Form 1095-C for the selected year, select Yes for Employees with 1095C. 6. If you want to include employees who elected early access to Form 1095-C, select Yes for Employees with Electronic 1095C Form. The report will include employees if Electronic 1095C Form is selected in the Tax section of their Employee Details record. 7. Click Run to generate the report.

Report The report includes the following columns: • Employee Name: Employee name displays as last name first. • Employee ID • 1095C Register: Y (yes) if the employee is listed on the 1095-C Register, or N (no) if they are not listed on the 1095-C Register. • Electronic 1095C: Y (yes) if the employee receives a electronic 1095-C or N (no) if they receive a paper 1095-C.

Analyzing the Employee Count This utility provides a count of employees, either by the number of paid employees or by the classification status of employees in the system.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click (Back Office). Under Operations|Report, click Employee Count Analysis.

To generate an employee count analysis: 1. In the Employer ID field enter the Employer ID, or click the Employer ID link and select the employer to generate the employee count for that Employer. If left blank, and the Client ID is also blank, it will generate employee count of all employees in the system. 2. In the Client ID field enter the Client ID, or click the Client ID link and select the client to generate the employee count for that Client. 3. In the As of Date field, enter the date for which you want the Employee Count Analysis. 4. For Count Type, select any one of the following two options: • Count Paid Employees - gives you a count of employees who were paid using the system as per Employee Type selected. • Employee Status Classification - gives you a breakup of the count of employees as per various classification in the system as per Employee Type selected. 5. If Employee Status Classification is selected, then select any one of the following options: • All • Active • Terminated • Leave of Absence 6. For the Employee Type, select any one of the following options: • All • Full Time • Part Time • Independent Contractor 7. Click Count Employees - a new window Calculating Employee Count appears.

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 42 Chapter 1 Reports

  1. Scroll down the window to view the number of employees counted.
  2. Click Close to close the Calculating Employee Count window.

ID: Employee ID • Age: Employee Age • Pre-Tax Percent / Amount Extra: The pre-tax percentage and dollar amount elected. • Catch-up Percent / Amount: The catch-up percentage and dollar amount elected. • ROTH Percent / Amount Extra: The ROTH percentage and dollar amount elected. • ROTH Catch-up Percent / Amount: The ROTH catch-up percentage and dollar amount elected. • Post-Tax Percent / Amount: The post-tax percentage and dollar amount elected. • Key EE: Indicates whether this employee a key employee. • High Comp: Indicates whether this employee highly compensated. • Effective Date: The date this election went into effect. • Enrollment Date: The date the employee enrolled in this election. • Match Date: The date the employer started matching the employee contribution.

Click Run to generate the report.

OSHA Report This form pulls data from the OSHA Cases records to complete the OSHA 300 and 300A Reports. To ensure data populates correctly, it is recommended to select the Report Incident on the 300A Log field on the OSHA Cases form (found under HR>HR|Change). This report is required by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) agency of the United States Department of Labor to maintain records of all work-related injuries and illnesses.

Note:

• Client Access Group security and Data Entity security is enabled on this form. • Worksite Managers, Worksite Trusted Advisors and Service Providers can access the form.

To access the form, click the Reports menu. Under HR|Report, click OSHA Report.

To generate the OSHA Report: 1. Complete the following: Table 1: OSHA Report form - Fields Field Name Description Year Select the report year from the drop-down. By default the current year displays. You have the option of a 10 year look back.

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 81 Chapter 1 Reports

Field Name Description Location Select the client’s location for which you want to run the report from the following drop-down: • All Locations • MAIN • CALLLL • CA2 LOCAL GLOBAL • FL 2 • FL 3 • MA Report Type Select the report type from the following drop-down: • OSHA 300 • OSHA 300A

  1. Click Run to generate the report. The report shows up on the screen. When you run the OSHA 300A report, then in addition to the PDF report, the following two reports will appear via hyperlink for download here: • OSHA 300A Detail Report: This report in a .csv format provides all the details that appear on the current PDF with a few additional details. • OSHA 300A Employee Count Analysis: This report provides an output of regular processed payrolls - employees - and a total of employees paid for the year / number of pay periods - and how the average on the pdf is calculated. The columns in this report are Pay Date, Employee Count, Employee ID and Employee Name.
  2. Click Close to close the form.

The OSHA 300 Report (Log of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses) classifies work-related injuries and illnesses. The report also records the extent and severity of each case. If the client has more than one establishment or site, you must keep separate records for each physical location that is expected to remain in operation for one year or longer.

Note: If the Description of where accident occurred field on the OSHA Cases form is populated, Column E on the OSHA 300 Report will output this information.

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 82 Chapter 1 Reports

The OSHA 300A Report (Summary of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses) displays the work-related injury and illness totals for the year in each category. In the OSHA 300A Report, the calculation of the Annual average number of employees has been enhanced to better support clients who have multiple pay groups for their employees. • The enhanced calculation will now create an average number of employees paid on regularly scheduled pay periods by pay group. • The pay periods are calculated on an annual basis based on the expected number of pay periods for each pay group. • These averages are then totaled for the total average amount for the OSHA 300A reporting period.

Veterans Employment Report Use this form to generate the Veterans Employment Download which will assist with federal government reporting. Federal Contractor Veterans’ Employment Report (VETS-4212) WHO MUST FILE: This VETS-4212 Report is to be completed by all nonexempt Federal contractors and subcontractors with a contract or subcontract in the amount of $100,000 or more with any department or agency of the United States for the procurement of personal property or non-personal services.

Human Resources Reports Guide © 2026 PrismHR 95 Chapter 1 Reports

     Services include but are not limited to the following services: utility, construction, transportation,
     research, insurance, and fund depository, irrespective of whether the government is the purchaser or
     seller. Entering into a covered Federal contract or subcontract during a given calendar year establishes
     the requirement to file a VETS-4212 Report during the following calendar year.
     WHEN TO FILE: This annual report must be filed no later than September 30.
     HOW TO FILE THE VETS-4212 REPORT: The preferred method for filing VETS-4212 Report is
     electronically through the VETS web-based filing system. Instructions for electronically filing can be
     found on the VETS website at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu. Under System|Change, click Direct Deposit Form Settings.

Field Description Federal Client ID If a Federal Contractor Report has been filed in the past, utilize the number as signed in previously submitted reports, otherwise leave blank. Parent Client Headquarters Enter the ID of the company you want to designate as your headquarters. Parent Client Headquarters Enter the location you want to designate as headquarters. Location Duns Number Enter the Dun and Bradstreet ID applicable to the hiring location or enter the ID applicable to the parent company. Else leave blank. Type Of Reporting Indicate the type of contractual relationship from the following options: Organization • Prime Contractor • Subcontractor • Both Type of Form Indicate the type of form from the following options: • Single Establishment • Multiple Establishment Name Of Contact Enter the name of the contact for the headquarters company. Telephone Enter the contact’s telephone number. Email Enter the contact’s email address. Twelve Month Period Enter the beginning date for the twelve month reporting period used as the Beginning Date basis for filing the VETS-4212 Report.

Field Description Twelve Month Period Ending Enter the end date for the twelve month reporting period used as the basis for Date filing the VETS-4212 Report.   1. Click Generate Report to generate the report. A job progress window opens up showing the processing of records. Click Close to close the job progress window.

 •   is also restricted from clients via client access group security.
 The message states:
 The user role <new user role> has access to the Transfer Downloads File to PC menu. This form does not
 utilize client access group security so it is possible that <user id> maybe be able to download files that

To transfer a Download File to a user’s PC: 1. Click the Filename link. A separate Select File window opens. 2. Scroll and select the Download File that you want to download from the list. Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 18 Client Administration Guide

Intended Audience The contents of this guide are for users who are involved in company or client administration. Unless you have permission to access system-level features, you cannot set global codes. Before using this guide, you must set up all defaults, files and preferences required for system administration, as well as employer information. To effectively use this guide, you must also have background knowledge of workers’ compensation, employee benefits, billing practices, payroll practices, and taxes.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 19 Chapter 1 Introduction

Chapter 1 Introduction The Client Administration User Guide explains the tasks and features used to create and maintain your clients. • Setup - The tasks and steps involved in creating and maintaining clients, as well as the codes, values, and definitions used in client administration. Authorized users set up these values and definitions at the client level, and may perform these tasks periodically when new values or definitions are required. • Administration - The tasks and steps involved in the day-to-day maintenance and administration of clients.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 2 Setting Up a New Client

Chapter 2 Setting Up a New Client Perform the following procedures to successfully set up your client: • Create a new client company. Use the New Client form to create a client • Complete the new client setup in the Client Details form

Creating a New Client Company Create a new client company with the New Client form.

To create a client company:

  1. Click (Back Office).
  2. Select New Client from the Operations|Action menu.
  3. Fill out these fields as required.

Field Description Client ID The system generates the Client ID when you save the new record. This field defaults to NEW when you open the form. Legal Name Enter the Legal Name of the new client company. Client D/B/A Enter the legal doing business as client name in the Client D/B/A field. Address Enter the client’s main mailing address in the Address fields. After saving the new client record, you can enter other addresses (if required). ZIP Code Enter the ZIP Code and press Tab. The system automatically displays the GeoCode, City, and State. If multiple GeoCodes are associated with the ZIP Code, the system prompts you to select the correct one. GeoCode, City, and State After entering the client’s address and ZIP Code, the GeoCode, city, and state display.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 21 Chapter 2 Setting Up a New Client

Field Description Telephone Enter the client’s main Telephone number. Ext Enter the telephone Ext (optional). Fax Enter the client’s Fax number. Website Enter the URL of the client’s Website. Service Type Select the Service Type provided to this client. You must select the appropriate Service Type to ensure accurate billing. • Administrative Services Only (ASO): When you save the new client record, the system automatically creates both a new client record and a new employer record with the same information as the new client. The system immediately links the new employer record to the client. The system assumes cost equals billed for taxes and workers’ compensation. • Corporate: Indicates that the new record is a corporate client, typically used for tracking the service provider’s internal employees. No billing occurs for a corporate client. If the new client needs to be billed, select a different service type. • Professional Employer (PEO): Indicates that the service provider manages human resources, employee benefits, payroll, workers’ compensation, accounts receivable, and COBRA administration for the new client. Cost is considered the PEO cost for taxes and workers’ compensation rates, which are entered at the system/employer levels. Billed rates can be higher (for profit centers) or lower than cost, if appropriate, and rates are specified at the client level. • HR Services Only: The service provider only manages human resources for the client’s employees, which includes hiring, termination, performance, compensation, training, policy, and OSHA-related services. (There is no payroll.) • Payroll Services Only: The service provider only provides payroll and payroll tax services for the client. (The employer does not provide human resources services.) • Admin. Service/Alt. Billing: This is similar to an ASO in that the system creates an employer record automatically. The system treats the new client as it would a PEO client for billing purposes. The service provider can open profit centers on taxes and workers’ compensation. The system does not assume cost equals billed.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 22 Chapter 2 Setting Up a New Client

Field Description Federal ID Number Enter the client’s nine-digit Federal ID Number, also known as the Employer Identification Number (EIN or FEIN). Note: An error message displays if you enter an EIN or a FEIN that is more than nine digits. Status Select the Status of this client. Status Date Enter the Status Date when the selected Status goes into effect. For example, if the client is active, this is the starting date for the client. Employer ID Enter or select the Employer ID to assign for this client. If this is an ASO client, enter NEWASO to create an employer record with the same ID as the client. If this employer is a PEO and certified by the IRS under the Small Business Efficiency Act (SBEA), the system automatically creates a client federal entity and assigns the ID to the client when you save this new client record. If the client needs a different federal entity, edit it in the client record. (See the SBEA User Guide.) Location Code Enter the Location Code, which is the primary location for this client (the default is 1). PrismHR uses this to create the first location record for the client. Client Category Enter or select the Client Category code; for example, PEO. Cost Center Select the Cost Center used to process accounting transactions for this client, if any. Sub-Cost Center Select the Sub-Cost Center to assign to this client, if any. Contract Date Enter the Contract Date on which the contract was signed with the client. (The default is the Status Date.) Deliver Checks Select the Deliver Checks location where your organization should deliver employees’ payroll checks. Corporation Type Select the Corporation Type for this client. The system uses this for tax reporting. Business Enter a brief Business description. NAICS Code Enter or select the NAICS Code (North American Industrial Classification System Code) for the client’s primary business activity. Contact Name Enter a clientContact Name and related information. Title Enter the contact’s Title. Telephone Enter the contact’s work Telephone number. Ext Enter the contact’s telephone Ext. Email Address Enter the contact’s Email Address.

Deleting a Pending Client Use this form to remove a client entered into the system that never actually ran payroll and is no longer expected to be a client.

Prerequisites The following prerequisites must be met before you can perform this action: • A ‘Pending’ Client Status must exist at the system level, with a Status Class of ‘Pending’ (System|Change|Client Statuses) • The client must first be terminated (Client|Action|Client Status Change process). • The client must then be changed to a ‘Pending’ status (Client|Action|Client Status Change process). • The client cannot have any employees or payroll history.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To delete a pending client: 1. Click Client. 2. From Client|Action, click Delete Pending Client. 3. Click the Client link to select a client. The status must be Pending. 4. Click Delete Client to complete this process.

Using the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool You can use the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool to quickly import a list of employees to transfer to new clients. Note the following: • This tool is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Mass Employee Transfer Import form. • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Mass Employee Transfer Import form displays the form in read- only format. • Users who do not have access to a particular client as configured in Client Access Groups cannot transfer employees into or out of the client using the Mass Employee Transfer Import form. • This process accomplishes the same results as executing the standard employee transfer process using the Transfer Employee to New Client form. (See Transferring Employees to New Clients.) The Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool is available from the Operations|Import Processing menu in the Back

Office . For example, the following form displays after you access the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool:

Before you can upload and import data, your source file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. When you open the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool form, the required file layout displays. The layout must match the requirements for number and order of columns, category descriptions, and the required fields.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 33 Chapter 2 Setting Up a New Client

In addition, you can use the sample header file before importing to avoid manually creating an import file that matches the import template type. Note the following when using a comma (,) in a description in your import file: • If you include a comma in a description field using the .csv file format, you must enclose the item in double quotes. For example, “Manager, Admin.” • If you include a comma in a description field using the .txt file format, no extra formatting is necessary.

Using the Sample Header File Before starting the import process, you can first download a sample header file by clicking that link on the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool form. For example:

Note: The header file is in .csv format. You can save the file in .csv or .txt format. After you click the Download Sample Header File link, the system downloads or prompts for download a sample header file that displays columns and headers that match each column and description for the import template option. Also, the file displays a title that matches the selected option.

  6. The uploaded Import File name will display under the File Name field on the form. The content of the file will display under File Content tab. Errors, if any, will display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process. While processing the uploaded file, the following validation occurs: • If any mandatory field is missing from the file, the system displays an error message, “ is a required field.” • If the system does not associate the Employee ID with the From Client field, it displays an error message, “Employee not located in client .” • If the values in the Pay Group, To Retire Plan, To Position, and To Location fields are not valid for the To Client record, then the system displays an error message, “Record . is not on file in <field’s filename>.” • In the Termination Reason field, the system identifies a valid value only if the REASON.CODES contain “Termination.” If you provide any other value, the system displays an error message, “ is not a valid Term Reason Code.”
  7. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR. After the import finishes, the following occurs: • If Transfer YTD Check Stubs is enabled, the program transfers the YTD check stubs. • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is enabled, the program terminates the employee on the original client using the corresponding Termination Date and Termination Reason from the upload file. • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is disabled, the program does not terminate the employee on the original client. • If Terminate Benefit Coverage Today is enabled, the program terminates the employee’s benefit coverage. • If the uploaded file contains a mix of employees who are successfully validated and employees that fail the validations, those employees that are successfully validated are transferred appropriately and the employees that fail validation are documented in the error log and are not transferred or terminated.
  8. Click Report to view the transaction report. This report contains the following information: • Successfully transferred employees display “Success” in the Import Status column. • Employees that failed validation and could not be transferred display “Skipped” in the Import Status column. The “Comments” column for the failed transfer employees displays the error message for whichever failed validation event prevented the transfer.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 36 Chapter 3 Defining Client Billing Information

Chapter 3 Defining Client Billing Information Define the client’s billing information. (This information does not apply to Corporate service types.)

Defining Billing Rules Client billing can be bundled or unbundled: • Bundled billing charges a lump sum percentage of gross payroll per pay period. It includes FUTA, SUTA, FICA, and workers’ compensation. • Unbundled billing breaks out each line item charge for payroll taxes, workers’ comp premiums, and administrative fees.

Note: The billing method (bundled or unbundled) does not affect the invoice format. Both the bill format and the billing template are set on the Billing tab in the Client Details form.

After defining billing rules, you can begin to enter other billing settings on the Billing tab on the Client Details form.

Using Bundled Billing Rules Use the Bundled Billing Rules form to establish information for charging one fee per workers’ compensation class for FUTA, SUTA, FICA, and workers’ compensation. You can “bundle” benefit billing based on the workers’ compensation code. You can use the Bundled Billings Comp Class workers’ compensation code to reflect actual costs that are based on workers’ compensation classifications. You can also set up bundled billing so that each Comp Class has the same billing rate, such as when a client has a flat rate for all classes of employees.

Using Unbundled Bill Rules Based On Options You can use these options as the basis for calculating unbundled billing rules. Based On Calculation Units Enter the flat amount to calculate per unit paid. For example, one unit of bonus pay with a Rate amount of 10 ($10.00) generates a $10.00 admin fee. Hours Worked Enter the flat amount to calculate per hour worked. For example, 40 hours worked with a Rate amount of 10 ($10.00) generates a $400.00 admin fee. Percent of Wages Enter the percent of wages to charge. For example, $1270.00 of gross wages with a Rate amount of 10 (10%) generates a $127.00 admin fee. Amt per Check (One Per Enter the flat amount to bill per check. For example, 100 vouchers Voucher will Fire) with a Rate amount of 1 ($1.00) generates a $100.00 admin fee. Flat Amount Bills the client this amount for each employee and each check. For example, two employees and three total checks (one employee receives two checks) with a Rate amount of 10 ($10.00) generates a $30.00 Admin fee. Flat Amount / Invoice Bills the client this amount per invoice generated. For example, two invoices and a Rate amount of 50 ($50.00) generates a $100.00 Admin fee. Flat Amount / Paid EE (only Triggers the flat amount only once per employee in the payroll once per EE) batch. For example, if an employee receives a regular, supplemental, and vacation voucher on the same payroll, the billing rule triggers only once. If there were two employees and four total vouchers with a Rate amount of 10 ($10.00), the system generates a $20.00 Admin fee.

For example, if the Rate amount is 7.5, then two employees, one (Must also have 0 IMIN) with $7.00 admin fee and another with $10.00 admin fee would not trip the value of $15.00. (If you selected Based On Employee Minimum, the first employee would generate a $0.50 fee, and there would be no fee for the second employee.) Note the following: • If you define one rule with Monthly Rate/52 weeks, and another with Monthly Rate/48 weeks, the system uses only one per voucher. • The Flat Amount / Paid EE sets IMIN basis. (Must also have 0 IMIN) and Invoice Minimum = Only One of these options must be the last billing rules that the system calculates. If either exists as a Billing Rule, the system will resort the rules so they calculate last.

Flat Amount / Benefit Plan Triggers the flat amount based on the classification selected from Class the Benefit Plan Class drop-down. Monthly Rate / 52 Weeks Enter the monthly rate to charge; the system divides it by pay period based on 52 weeks a year per employee. For example, if the Rate amount is 65, the system bills the client $15.00 per employee for a weekly payroll. This does not limit the billing to $65.00 per month. If an employee receives multiple vouchers and the voucher type is not limited, more than $65.00 can be charged in a month. Monthly Rate / 48 Weeks Enter the monthly rate to charge; the system divides it by pay period based on 48 weeks a year per employee. For example, if the Rate amount is 65, the system bills the client $16.25 per employee for a weekly payroll. Employee Minimum Bills the minimum amount on each voucher for each employee. For example, if the rule has a Rate amount of 25 and an employee receives three vouchers (regular, supplemental, and vacation), the system bills the client $75 for that employee. Employee Minimum, NO For example, if the employee minimum is $10.00, but a client pays Credit On Overbills only $7.50 because they had $2.50 in overlimit credits, the system assesses a $2.50 charge. (Employee Minimum would not assess a fee.)

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 49 Chapter 3 Defining Client Billing Information

Based On Calculation Employee Maximum The maximum per voucher per employee that will be billed. For example; a user could set up one rule as a percent of wages and a second rule with an employee maximum, and the system would limit the calculation to the employee maximum. If rule #1 is set up as 20% of wages, and the wages are $2000, then rule #1 calculates at $400. If rule #2 is set up with an employee maximum of $25, then the system limits the admin fee to $25 even though rule #1 was calculated at $400. Invoice Minimum Any admin fee below this amount increases to this amount. Invoice Maximum Any admin fee above this amount reduces to this amount. Invoice Minimum (incl Zero Can be used in conjunction with Invoice Minimum. Invoice) Per Employee Per Month Bills automatically the first payroll after the billing rule is set up and automatically bills on the first payroll of each month following. It only bills for employees that are paid within that pay period. • If there is a new hire on the next payroll, the system will bill for just that employee. • If an employee was not paid on the first payroll of the month but gets paid on the next payroll, the system will bill for just that employee. Percent of Listed Benefit Takes the benefit entered in Benefit Plan and charges this percent against the total amount. For example, 10% of a $1000 benefit (with employee paying $500) would be $100. Percent of Listed Benefit Net Takes the benefit listed and charges this percent against the net Billed to Client amount. For example, 10% of a $1000 benefit (with employee paying $500) would be $50. Percent of Retirement Match Charges a percentage of the Match Fees. Amount Percent to Not Shelter Percentage that will not be sheltered as a benefit from FICA. A Benefit Plan from FICA sheltered amount shelters the whole amount from FICA for billing purposes, so use this option when you want to pass some of the savings through, but not all of them. Flat Amount Based on Charges a flat amount once per Benefit Plan. Benefit Rule

Based On Calculation Tiered Per Employee Per Pay Use this method to bill the same administrative fees for all Period employees based on the total number of employees. Note: Pay Group is the only filter criteria available for the Tiered Per Employee Per Pay Period option. (The system does not recognize any other filters when using this option.) This feature uses a special tier table with three columns: • Tiered From: Smallest number of employees in this tier • Tiered To: Largest number of employees in this tier • Tiered Rate: Admin fee to charge per employee in this tier Add a row to the table for each calculation tier. Flat Amt based on Count Use this method to charge a flat amount per voucher. Specify the rule limiters in the Additional Conditions form’s Rule Minimum and Rule Maximum fields. For example, you need to bill the client at two different rates, based on the number of employees. You would establish two rules using Flat Amt based on Count. Set up the first rule with a Rate of $35, the Rule Minimum set to 0, and the Rule Maximum set to 5. Set up the second rule with a Rate of $100, a Rule Minimum of 6, and a Rule Maximum of 99. When there are five employees or fewer in the batch control record, PrismHR uses the first rule: four employee result in a bill for $140. For a batch with 6-99 employees, the system uses the second rule: six employees result in a bill for $600. Flat Amt based on Count Per Use this method to charge the client a certain amount for the first X Tier number of vouchers and then a different amount for the next X number of vouchers. Specify the tiers for the rule in the Additional Conditions form’s Rule Minimum and Rule Maximum fields. For example, you need to bill one rate for the first five employees, and then at another rate for every employee after that. You would establish two rules using Flat Amt based on Count Per Tier. Set up the first rule with the Rate of $35, the Rule Minimum set to 0, and the Rule Maximum set to 5. Set up the second rule with a Rate of $100, with a Rule Minimum of 6, and a Rule Maximum of 99. The system calculates the first five employees using the first rule, and the sixth employee using the second rule, resulting in a bill for $275 ((5$35)+(1$100)).

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 52 Chapter 3 Defining Client Billing Information

Based On Calculation Annual W-2 Production Fee Use this method to generate a one-time yearly charge for Forms W- 2 (W-2s) as a production fee. This is a one-time flat fee that the system will bill for the current year the first time the rule applies. If your organization would prefer that it run in January, set the Rule Start Date to a date in January of the next year. This rule generates a miscellaneous billing charge. Annual Fee per W-2 Use this method to generate a one-time yearly charge for W-2s as a per-employee fee. This billing rule is based on a count of generated W-2s. W-2s are generated in the first quarter of the following year (for example, your organization will generate 2024 W-2s in Q1 2025). If W-2s have not been generated yet (such as in early January), then the system processes the rule during each payroll until your organization generates the W-2s. This rule generates a miscellaneous billing charge. Minimum Bill for Code 005 Any amount below this value increases to this value.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 53 Chapter 3 Defining Client Billing Information

Based On Calculation Per Active Employee Per This option calculates the admin fee based on the client’s employee Month count on the first regular payroll of the month, using a tiered charge format. (The second payroll captures any new employees.) The fee is based on the total number of active employees in the client associated with the first payroll of the month. This feature uses a special tier table with three columns: • Tiered From (smallest number of employees in this tier) • Tiered To (largest number of employees in this tier) • Tiered Rate (admin fee to charge per employee in this tier) Add a row to the table for each calculation tier. Enabling the Per Active Employee Per Month option bills active employees for the month. For example, if the first payroll of the month has 100 active employees, they will be billed for 100 employees. On the second payroll if there is a new hire and a termination, they will still be billed for one employee on that payroll, since the new hire needs to be billed and the termination was active for part of the month. Note: An edge case could occur that is currently not supported. When you calculate a payroll, the system determines the number of employees that are active at that time and once the payroll is posted, it commits counts to the employee records. If you calculate the payroll and add several employees or terminate employees and then post without recalculating, the system misses the new employees added/removed in the billing cycle. Note the following: • The billing rate calculates the tier rate for the employee count. • The admin fee bills the entire month at the same rate.

Chapter 4 Setting Up Time Off Plans Absence plans are unique to each client and can differ from the simple to the extremely complex. Once you set up the absence accrual files in PrismHR, the system automatically accrues paid time off benefits for each employee according to the parameters you establish. Although it is important to understand how to establish these files, the real key to setting up the files correctly is understanding exactly how the client’s absence benefit plan works. Use these instructions to learn how to: • Establish the absence benefit plan, including carryover rules and accrual rates • Determine how and when accrual calculations should occur • Set up codes to identify Time Off types, accrual schedules, and absences

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 67 Chapter 4 Setting Up Time Off Plans

Tracking Absences PrismHR tracks paid absences automatically during regular payroll processing. Users can manually enter unpaid absences and review them at any time on a number of different absence reports. 1. During Payroll calculation the system reviews the Pay Code record for each Pay Code entered on an employee’s timesheet. 2. If the Pay Code on the timesheet is associated with a Paid Absence Code and Updates Time Off Register is checked, the system updates the employee’s Time Off Register with the hours from the timesheet, deducting from the employee’s available Time Off balance. 3. If the number of Time Off hours exceeds the employee’s available Time Off balance, the system alerts the payroll processor with a warning, but allows processing to continue. 4. You can manually enter absences that are unpaid and other adjustments to the employee’s Time Off Register in the Time Off Adjustments form. Note: Unpaid absences do not affect the Employee’s Time Off register totals, but they might be referenced in various reports and inquiries.

Defining Time Off Types Restrict the number of register types that can be assigned to an employee to avoid employee Time Off register duplication with the Time Off Types form. You need to create only one of each time off type (such as vacation or illness).

To set a Time Off type: 1. Select the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select Time Off Types. The Time Off Types form opens. 3. Complete the required information in these fields:

                               Code link. For example, SICK for sick leave.

 Linked Accrual                Enable this field to mark the selected Time Off Type Code as a linked
                               accrual (default is disabled).
 Transfer To                   Select a Time Off Type Code to transfer to another Time Off type. (This field
                               only displays if Linked Accrual is enabled.)
                               For example, if type A is linked/transferred to type B, type A does not
                               display on the Transfer To list for other types to transfer to (effectively
                               preventing anything from transferring to it).

Note the following: • The system will transfer the prior year accrued hours from the accrual register to the balance register for employees enrolled in a Linked Accrual Time Off Register when the plan year is triggered. • If you set up a transfer to another Time Off type code more than once an error message displays, “Transfer to is already in use.” (You cannot have two Time Off types transferred to the same Time Off type because this is a 1:1 relationship.) • If you enable Linked Accrual but do not select the Transfer To Time Off type an error message displays when you click Save, “Transfer To Time Off Type is required.” • The system tracks changes made to Time Off types in the audit log.

Creating Time Off Accrual Schedules Use the Time Off Accrual Schedules form to create or update a Time Off accrual schedule. Time Off accrual schedules track the usable hours of Time Off that employees accrue over the course of the year. The events trigger Time Off accrual, and the strict definition of “year,” are defined on this form.

Note: The Time Off accrual schedule indicates when employees accrue paid time off. The Time Off Plan indicates how much paid time off employees accrue.

Using Customized Accrual Subroutines If the client uses an accrual method that differs from methods previously described, use a customized accrual subroutine.

Note: Contact a systems professional to design a subroutine using the parameters described here.

To design a subroutine: 1. Click the Client menu. 2. From Client|Change, select Time Off Accrual Schedules. 3. In Accrual Frequency, select Custom Basic Routine. The Custom Basic Subroutines panel displays.

  1. In Trigger Subroutine, enter a custom accrual frequency subroutine to determine whether hours should accrue for each employee. The format is:

             SUBROUTINE
         SUBR.NAME(ABSENCE.REGISTER.REC,EMPLOYEE.SSN,ACCRUAL.TRIGGERED)

    The variable ACCRUAL.TRIGGERED should return either a 0 (zero) or 1 (one). If the value returned is 1, the system calculates an accrual.

  2. In Calculation Subroutine, enter a customized subroutine to replace the standard daily accrual calculation. The subroutine must have the following parameter list:

             SUBROUTINE
         SUBR.NAME(COMPANY.NO,EMP.SSN,REG.TYPE,ABSENCE.REGISTER.REC,
         BENEFIT.PLAN.REC,VOUCHER.REC,HOURS.ACCRUED)

    The hours accrued should be returned in the variable HOURS.ACCRUED. The calling program does not accept the return of a negative number. If the system returns a negative number, it is set to zero instead. Do not return a number with an embedded decimal point because it will be truncated.

  3. Click Save.

Learning About Time Off Plans A Time Off plan, or absence plan, determines how much paid time off an employee can accrue. The employee Time Off register is the place where the system keeps track of how much has been accrued and taken by the employee. The Time Off plan establishes limits on the amount of paid time off that may be earned. This is the number of hours that can be carried over from one plan period to the next, or the number of hours the employee can earn. Clients often have more than one Time Off plan, for example:

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 76 Chapter 4 Setting Up Time Off Plans

•      Vacation
•      Sick
•      Personal
•      Other plan types that represent time accrued and taken according to the client’s policy

You can also have more than one type of benefit plan, such as multiple vacation plans. The Benefit Plan is assigned to an employee at enrollment.

Note: The Time Off accrual schedule indicates when employees accrue paid time off. The Time Off Plan indicates how much paid time off employees accrue.

Defining Time Off Plans To define Time Off plans that determine employee time off accruals, use the Time Off Plans form.

Note: The Time Off Register is where the system tracks how much paid time off the employees have accrued and taken.

Each Time Off plan establishes limits on the amount of paid time off that employees can earn and how many hours they can carry over from one plan period to the next. Clients often have more than one Time Off plan. For example: • Vacation • Sick • Personal • Other plan types taken according to client policy that can represent time accrued

Understanding Unlimited Time Off Plans The Employee Time Off Register and Employee Time Off Register Inquiry forms contain fields that do not apply. They also do not include the Hours Calculated/Carry-over Details panel because that information does not apply to unlimited Time Off plans. After the first payroll of the new year, the date fields in the registers might not update because there are no accruals. They update only after the employee uses time off hours in a posted payroll. Note the following: • The Employee Time Off Register Adjustment form does not allow users to make adjustments to unlimited time off plans. • During payroll initialization, there are no warnings about time off balances for employees enrolled in an unlimited Time Off plan. • Payroll vouchers for employees with unlimited Time Off plans show the hours used but not any calculated (accrued) hours. • The Employee Time Off Detail Report shows no information for carryover, accrued, or available time.

Linking PTO Accrual Plans . You can use the Linked Accrual Plans feature to accrue employee PTO hours for transfer once the plan year ends. This feature consists of two PTO plans that you must set up so employees can accrue time for a plan year in one register that they cannot use until the plan year ends. After the plan year ends, the accrued hours move to a new register where employees can use their PTO hours. (Employees can have several different linked accrual plans, one for sick time, one for vacation time, and so on.) Note the following: • Employees must be enrolled in two PTO registers (one for accrual and one for balance) to use this feature. If there is no Balance PTO register associated with the linked class for the employee, then the system does not move anything will from the Accrual register to the Balance register. (The hours remain in the Accrual register.) • If the Balance PTO Register has a yearly maximum set, the system moves prior year balances from the Accrual register to the Balance register up to the maximum amount. (The remaining amount in the accrual register is lost.) • When the system transfers accrued hours from the Accrual register to the Balance register, it places the hours in the Balance register in the YTD Calculated column. • Accrual plans accrue for the pay period and then transfer to the Balance plan.

Using Linked Accrual Plans Feature To use the Linked Accrual Plans feature, you must set up two PTO plans in the PTO Benefit Plans form:

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 91 Chapter 4 Setting Up Time Off Plans

• Accrual plan: Accrues employee PTO time during the year. At the end of the plan year, the system transfers the hours in the accrual plan to the linked balance plan. (The Accrual plan resets to zero.) Employees can now use the accrued hours in the Balance plan. • Balance plan: Contains the transferred PTO accrual time. The following diagram demonstrates the setup for Linked Accrual Plans:

Note the following: • The employee’s accrual balance for the current year is the year-to-date PTO hours accrued from the previous year. • Employees carry over some hours in some cases, but most plans expire the hours at the end of the plan year. • Most of these plans are set up as anniversary plans, not by the plan year.

Setting Up the Linked Accrual Plans Feature

Set up the following: 1. PTO Class: Use the PTO Classes form to define which PTO classes will be used in conjunction with each other, consisting of a PTO class for the accrual and a PTO class for the balance. (See the Client Administration

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 92 Chapter 4 Setting Up Time Off Plans

Guide for details on defining PTO classes.)
For example:
a. Create a PTO Class Code for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL.
     Note: Do not enable Linked Accrual.
b. Create a PTO Class Code for the Accrual plan. For example, VACACCR.
c.    Enable Linked Accrual.
d. In the Transfer To field, select VACBAL.
Note: These PTO classes are now linked and cannot be linked to other classes.
  1. PTO Register: Enable the Prior Year Accrual trigger method on the PTO Register Types form to trigger the balance register to move the accrued PTO hours from the accrual plan to the balance plan. (See the Client Administration Guide for details on working with PTO registers.) For example:
    1. Create a PTO Type Code register for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL. • PTO Class: VACBAL. • Year End Basis: Set Anniversary or Fiscal, but should match the Accrual register. • Trigger Method: Prior Year Accrual. • Trigger Date: Do not use. • Print on Check, Pay Stub Name, Paid Absence, Absence Code: Set these fields for the Balance register.
    2. Create a PTO Type Code register for the Accrual plan. For example, VACACCR. • PTO Class: VACACCR. • Year End Basis: Set Anniversary or Fiscal, but should match the Balance register. • Trigger Method: Select any trigger method. • Trigger Date: Select any trigger date. • Absence Code: Set this field for the accrual register. (It is not currently used, but it should be populated.) • Print on Check, Pay Stub Name, Inactive Register, and Paid Absence: Do not use.
  2. PTO Benefit Plan: Enroll employees in an Accrual plan and a Balance plan on the PTO Benefit Plans form. The Accrual plan determines the PTO time accrued. The system does not use the Balance plan to determine the accruals, but employees must be enrolled in both plans for the transfer to work correctly.
    1. Create a PTO Benefit Plan for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL. (You must select a calculation basis, but the system does not use it to calculate accruals.)
    2. Create a PTO Benefit Plan for the Accrual plan. For example, VACACCR. (This will hold the settings for the accruals.)

Understanding the Transfer Process When the system transfers accrued PTO hours, the employee register displays the accrued amount in the calculated column in the Balance register and displays an annotation, “Accrual Transfer MM/DD/YY,” in the details. The system then zeroes out the year-to-date accrual amounts in the employee Accrual register and displays an annotation, “XX number of hours moved to linked plan.”

Specifying Time Off Auto-enroll Rules Specify plans that automatically enroll new employees with the Time Off Auto Enroll Rules form. Companies with existing rules display information similar to this:

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 97 Chapter 4 Setting Up Time Off Plans

Note the following: • If there are Time Off Auto Enroll Rules available for the active client and you delete all existing rules, the form refreshes and the Save and Delete buttons no longer display. • When an approval is approved for an applicable change, the system re-evaluates Time Off auto-enroll rules and executes enrollments in the Time Off Auto Enroll Rules form for current or past-dated Status/Type and Position changes. If the change date matches the system date or a prior date the following occurs: • If an employee meets the criteria for a rule and the rule is set to archive in the prior Time Off Register, the system archives existing Time Off Registers that share the same class as the Time Off Register assigned to the affected rule. Note: In this scenario a message displays, “A type change has taken place that will archive this employee’s Time Off plan.” • If an employee meets the criteria for a rule and the rule is not set to archive the prior Time Off Register and no Time Off Type conflicts exist with the employee’s existing register, the system creates a new enrollment/register for the employee’s new plan. • If an employee meets the criteria for a rule and the rule is not set to archive the prior Time Off Register and a Time Off Type conflict exists, the system does not update the Time Off Register. • If an employee does not meet the criteria for any rule, the system does not update the Time Off Register.

Chapter 5 Setting Up Global PTO Plans You can use PrismHR to set up PTO plans on the system level and automatically assign those plans to employees based on work location.

Background As described in the Time Off User Guide (previously titled PTO User Guide), the PrismHR PTO features originally applied only to clients. This presented difficulties for organizations that needed to track paid time off for employees who regularly change location — such as those in the staffing industry. In response to this challenge, PrismHR introduced support for Global PTO plans that can track the accrual of employee paid time based on the employee’s worksite location. These new features enable you to set up discrete Global PTO plans and assign those to a state or even a specific GeoCode range. This setup structure provides significant flexibility in defining how and when employee paid time off accrues.

Activating Global PTO Features Note: Refresh your browser to see the changes from this feature code.

If you want to enable the new global PTO features, you must first apply the associated feature code.

To activate global PTO features: 1. Click Back Office and select System|Change > System Parameters. 2. In the upper right corner of the form, in the Custom Feature Codes table, create a new row. 3. Enter GLOBAL.PTO in this new row (be sure to include the period between GLOBAL and PTO). 4. Click Save. 5. Refresh your browser and then log in again, if necessary. The Global PTO forms and fields are now accessible.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 106 Chapter 5 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

About the Features With these features enabled: • You can establish system-level PTO codes and plans, and then assign those at the state and local levels using new fields on the State Rules form. • Next time you run a payroll, PrismHR will detect any employees who work within the specified state and GeoCode ranges. The system will automatically perform the PTO accrual calculations associated with the specific PTO plans assigned to those locations. Those calculated accruals will be stored in a separate database record created for this purpose. • To fine-tune the global PTO auto-enrollment and hour accrual, you can use client-level opt-in settings and employee-level opt-out settings (described below). • If you want to review PTO accruals to ensure that they are set up accurately, you can use a new view option on the Employee PTO Register Inquiry form. • New in June 2022: For staffing customers, we now support global PTO plans for federal contractors. The FG state code provides a grid for Global PTO plans but not GeoCodes, as they are not necessary. If an employee PLACEMENT record indicates that they are a federal contractor, the auto-enrollment and accrual logic will assign them a PTO plan associated with FG. • New in June 2022: The PTO “auto-enroll and accrue” logic also takes effect whenever you perform a global PTO data import using the PTO Register Import form. • New in June 2022: A new payroll report is available. This report displays a list of employees who were auto-enrolled in global PTO plans within the current payroll batch. You can run this report during payroll processing or separately. See Reviewing Global PTO Auto-Enrollments for a Payroll Batch (page 113). • New in June 2022: Several options are now available for printing Global PTO register data on employee checks. Instead of a binary yes/no option, you can select Always, Never (default), or If Used/Accrued Only for any global PTO register. • New in March 2024: Leave requests made in the Employee Portal that the system pulls into timesheets using the red dot can be accepted there. • New in September 2024: Previously, all Global PTO functionality for the following forms were hidden unless the custom feature code GLOBAL.PTO was enabled. All Global PTO functionality are now available on the following forms without using the custom feature code GLOBAL.PTO. • System / Change / Global PTO Benefit Plans • System / Change / Global PTO Register Types

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 107 Chapter 5 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

     •    PTO Reporting / Reporting / Global PTO Auto Enrollment Report
     •    System / Change / State Rules (Global PTO Plans)
     •    Client / Change / Client Other (Enable Global PTO)
     •    PTO Plan Setup and Enrollment / Plan Setup / PTO Absence Codes (Global PTO Checkbox)
•    New in March 2026: The legacy PTO terminology is being updated to match the terminology used in the

Note: The GLOBAL.PTO custom feature code is still required to calculate Global PTO accruals. This requirement will be removed in an upcoming release.

Creating Global PTO Register Types Use the Global PTO Register Types form to set up PTO register types for plans that are not client-specific. PTO registers track the usable hours of PTO that employees accrue over the course of the year. The events the trigger PTO accrual, and the strict definition of “year”, are defined on this form. After setting up these rules, you can assign these codes using a specialized Register Types table on the PTO Absence Codes form. See Reviewing Accrual Histories.

To set up a global PTO register type: 1. Go to Back Office > System|Change > Global PTO Register Types. 2. Enter or select a Global PTO Type Code. 3. Enter a Description of the global PTO register type. 4. Select the Year End Basis – the means by which the system measures the end of a year (Anniversary or Fiscal). If you selected Fiscal, specify a Fiscal End Month and Day. 5. In the Trigger Method field, select Pay Period Accrual. 6. Set the other optional parameters, as needed. You can find descriptions of these fields in the online help for either the Global PTO Register Types form or the client-level PTO Register Types form. Both forms use the same logic for these fields. See Reviewing Accrual Histories. 7. Click Save.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 108 Chapter 5 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

Creating Global Absence Codes In PrismHR, client-defined PTO absence codes track the accumulation of PTO hours defined under a particular category. PTO absence codes are associated with both pay codes (Back Office > System > Change > Pay Codes) and PTO register types (Client > Change > PTO Register Types).

To create a global PTO absence code: 1. Go to Client > Change > PTO Absence Codes. 2. Enter an Absence Code identifier and a Reason. 3. Enable the Updates PTO Register option. 4. Select Global PTO. The Register Types table on the right-hand side of the form is replaced by a Global Register Types table. 5. Assign the appropriate Pay Codes and Global Register Types in those tables. 6. Fill out the Leave Request Processing section as desired. For details about these fields, see “Creating PTO Absence Codes” in Chapter 1 of the Time Off User Guide. 7. Click Save.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 109 Chapter 5 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

Creating Global PTO Benefit Plans Use the Global PTO Benefit Plans form to set up and maintain the hour carryover and accrual rules related to system-level PTO plans.

Note: In contrast to the client-level PTO Benefit Plans form, there is no Calculation Basis option. Global PTO plans are designed to automatically use the “Flat Amount By Hours Worked” calculation basis.

To configure a global PTO benefit plan: 1. Go to Back Office > System|Change > Global PTO Benefit Plans. 2. Enter or select a Global PTO Benefit Plan ID. Use the Copy from another plan option if you want to use an existing plan as your template. 3. Enter a brief Plan Description. 4. Specify the Global PTO Register Type, configured above, that you will use to track accumulations and PTO usage under this benefit plan. 5. Fill out the remaining fields as needed. For details about these fields, review the online help documentation for Maintaining Global PTO Benefit Plans. 6. Click Save.

Opt-ins and Opt-outs Opting Clients into Auto-enrollment and Accrual You can use a setting on the Client Details form to enable global PTO plans for that client. On the Client Details > Other tab, select Global PTO Plan Auto Enroll & Accrue.

Opting Employees out of Auto-enrollment and Accrual You can use a setting on the Employee Details form to opt employees out of global PTO plan calculations. On the Employee Details > Other tab, select Disable PTO Auto Enroll & Accrue.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 110 Chapter 5 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

Assigning PTO Plans on the State and Local Level Note: You cannot set up GeoCode ranges for plans assigned to the FG state code (Federal Government — use this code for the PTO plans of employees who are federal contractors).

On the System > Change > State Rules form, you can use the Global PTO panel to specify the PTO plans to offer on both the state and local level. • In the State Plan Id panel, enter the IDs of any global PTO plans you want to offer to employees who work in that state. • Use the other panel to offer local PTO plans to employees who work within certain GeoCode ranges. You can use this to refine PTO accrual down to worksite locations within a specific locality. Enter the Starting GeoCode and Ending GeoCode to specify the range. Then, enter a Local Plan Id that you want to offer within that range.

Note: Currently, local PTO benefit plans accrue hours in addition to those of the state-level PTO plans.

Deduction Logic PrismHR uses the following process to select PTO registers for time off deductions. Note that a local PTO plan is any plan assigned to a GeoCode range on the State Rules form. The specific GeoCode is determined by the worksite location associated with the PTO hour payout.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 111 Chapter 5 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

The basic PTO deduction logic takes this form: 1. Deduct from the local PTO plan that matches the worksite location GeoCode on State Rules (if one exists). Repeat until hours run out in the register. If this occurs, move on to the next step. 2. Continue deducting from any other local PTO plans that match the GeoCode and are associated with the employee. If none meet these criteria, proceed to the next step. 3. Look for state-level global PTO registers (no GeoCode range) assigned on the State Rules form. Deduct from any qualifying state PTO plans in order. If PTO hours are still required after all these deductions, the system generates a payroll failure or warning depending on the following settings: • Max Usage Limit Per Plan Year (Global PTO Benefit Plans form) • Stop Init If Exceed Limit (Global PTO Benefit Plans form) • Display a Warning If Employee Uses More Hours Than Available (Global PTO Register Types form)

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 112 Chapter 5 Setting Up Global PTO Plans

Reviewing Accrual Histories There is a new Report View option on the HR > View > Employee PTO Register Inquiry form, called Global PTO. Select this option to review the Charge Date, Hours Worked, and Pay Rate associated with an employee’s global PTO accruals, along with their associated Pay Codes and Project assignments.

Reviewing Global PTO Auto-Enrollments for a Payroll Batch You can use a new on-demand payroll batch report to review a list of employees who were auto-enrolled in global PTO plans during batch processing.

To run the Employee PTO Auto Enrollment Report: 1. Click Work Centers and then select Work Centers|PTO > Reporting > Global PTO Auto Enrollment Report. Otherwise, select this report during payroll batch processing. 2. Enter the batch number in the Batch ID field. 3. Click Run and review the report output.

Configuring “Print On Check” Functionality You can adjust which global PTO register hours display on employee checks, based on register activity.

To update PTO register check printing settings: 1. Click Back Office and then select System|Change > Global PTO Register Types. 2. Locate the Print On Check option. 3. Select one of the following. Note that –Select– is equivalent to “Never”. • Always – always print employee global PTO register data on the check, no matter what • Never – default option. Never print data from this register on the check. • If Used/Accrued Only – only print on check if the employee used or accrued hours under this register within the payroll batch
