Chapter 6 Setting Up PEO Client Accounting PrismHR lets you create an accounting download file and report for your client that breaks out invoice numbers and uses the client’s own account numbers. You must perform four major tasks to create a report and download file: l Define the global or client accounting templates. l Create the accounting download directory. (Note: These instructions are for On-Premise customers only.) l Enable the client accounting for a client company. l Create the download file.

Understanding Accounting Templates Using General Ledger Account Numbers The client accounting templates associate your company’s payroll and billing codes with the client’s general ledger account numbers. These associations enable PrismHR to build an accounting download file and a report with data created during payroll processing. A client company may account for different types of earnings, deductions that have the Rebate bill code, and employer-paid taxes—or other items that are not included in payroll checks, such as delivery fees or report fees. PrismHR allows you to create an accounting entry per bill code. PrismHR also allows you to use “wildcards” that will be swapped out for the appropriate number at the time of payroll initialization; for example, your client charges REG (Regular) pay to account 5101.EEDP and OT (Overtime) pay to account 5105.EEDP. (The wildcard EEDP stands for Employee’s Department.) Wildcards and their usage are explained in “Defining Accounting Templates.” The format of the client account codes usually depends on the company’s accounting system. PrismHR can create an accounting download file in one of the following formats: • A generic comma-delimited file • A file that can be easily imported directly into PeachTree, QuickBooks, or Great Plains

Note: If you want to create a QuickBooks Billing template, contact PrismHR HR Support to submit a Professional Service engagement/request.

• A custom layout There are a few ways to enter client account numbers so that client accounting is generated:

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 123 Chapter 6 Setting Up PEO Client Accounting

• Global Accounting Template alone. • Global Accounting Template with client-level overrides. • Global Accounting Template with invoice-format overrides (Note: If you want to use an account at the billing format, that number is referenced from the Bill Codes in the Company Account field on the Billing Formats form.) • Client Accounting Template alone.

Using Client Bill Format Account Number Overrides One feature in PrismHR that is available—but not likely to be used—is replacing account numbers on the global or client account template with account numbers on the invoice format. If the invoice format contains summarized items, you can replace the account number on the invoice format with the client accounting template account numbers. You can use this feature to make sure the client’s accounting detail is no more than the detail provided on the invoice. This same control is achieved on the client accounting setup by making sure items grouped together for invoicing all go to the same client account number. For example, the client company uses a bundled accounting format. You do not want your 005 (Comp), 004 (Taxes), and 006 (Admin Fee) billing codes to charge different client accounting codes. If you did, the client would essentially receive a breakdown of their bundled rate. Because it is common for many different clients to share a bill format, this option is usually not the best choice. It offers little more than what you could accomplish by carefully designing the client-level and/or global templates. It also makes the template impossible to share.

Defining Accounting Templates and Using Wildcards Defining the Global Client Accounting Template PEOs can set up client accounting in the following ways: • By Client Template (PEO Client Account form): Usually, PEOs produce client accounting reports and download files using account numbers and formats specific to each client company. • By Global Account Template: In a few cases, a PEO might create global account numbers; for example, the PEO might have a group of clients that are defined separately but feed a common accounting system (for example, a franchise operation). The global template allows different clients to share the same accounting setup, where only varying accounts would be set up on the individual clients.

WARNING: The client accounting templates that prepare downloads must work correctly. Make sure you
understand the format requirements before making changes.

To define the global PEO client accounting template: 1. Access the Global PEO Client Accounting Templates form in the System|Change menu. 2. Complete the following:

Defining a PEO Client Accounting Template The PEO Client Accounting Maintenance file defines the client accounts the system builds into the client accounting download file and report.

Chapter 7 Setting Up New York SDI Tax The New York State Disability Insurance (NY SDI) Tax pays for temporary disability insurance for employees within the State of New York. The system calculates the NY SDI tax directly for employees and optionally for client. The system bypasses Vertex tax calculation engine for this tax. Therefore, your organization must set up the tax rates in PrismHR. See Calculating NY SDI Tax for more information on how PrismHR calculates the NY SDI tax.

Note: As of January 1, 2011, the rate for calculating employee NY SDI is 0.50% of wages per week up to a maximum of $0.60.

Establishing Tax Rates and Limits Set various tax rates and limits in the Tax Rates form.

To establish tax rates and limits:

  1. Click (Back Office).
  2. From System|Change select System Parameters.
  3. Select Tax Rate Maintenance from the Actions menu. The Tax Rates form opens.

employer (client) tax, enter the monthly tax rate per employee.

New York SDI Employer Rate Enter the employer rate that is calculated monthly for each (EE/Month) employee who lives in New York. Allow Override By Client Select to permit overrides of the NY SDI tax.

New York MCT Override Enter the rate based on the total company payroll expense. If left Rate blank, the system uses the default rate of 0.34% to calculate the tax.

Performing Pre-ACH Maintenance Use the Pre-ACH Maintenance panel to test ACH files a specified number of days before running payroll to ensure that all transactions can be completed.

Note: See the ACH User Guide for more information.

To set up or maintain Pre-ACH settings for a pay group: 1. Make sure to specify the appropriate pay group. Its information populates on the form. 2. If appropriate, select the number of Pre-ACH Days. The system sends a pre-ACH file ahead of the regular ACH file by the number of days selected. This number must be less than the cycle length for the feature to work correctly. If your organization is not using pre-ACH processing for this pay group, you must set this field to –Select–.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 149 Chapter 8 Establishing Other Client Setup Features

  1. The system can use either an average or a flat amount for the pre-ACH:

Pre-ACH Amount Details Type Average Use the pre-ACH invoice fields to specify an average for up to five invoices. You can enter any information in the Pre-ACH Invoice Number and Pre-ACH Invoice Amount columns, because the system does not verify it. For example, if you are setting up a pre-ACH prenote on the client for the first time and plan to use five invoices for the average that will typically be around $10,000, you can enter five “starter” invoices using any invoice number (for example, START1, START2, START3, and so on) and enter $10,000 for each. When the system processes a real payroll, it drops the first starter invoice from the list and inserts a real invoice at the end. After the first five payrolls, all the starter invoices are no longer on the list. The system sends pre-ACH prenotes using the average of the invoices in the list. After five payrolls, the average will be based on actual data. • The system lists each Pre-ACH Invoice Number in the chain for seeking the current average to pre-ACH. You can enter different invoice numbers. • The Pre-ACH Invoice Amount is each invoice’s contribution amount. You can enter a different amount to force a new average. The Current Average displays below the table. Flat Enter the Pre-ACH Override to use a flat amount rather than the Current Average of invoices and amounts. If you use the flat method, the system always uses that amount for pre-ACH for the client and this pay group. The system never checks nor averages the invoice amounts.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 150 Chapter 8 Establishing Other Client Setup Features

  1. If setting up Pre-ACH for the first time, enter the batch number of any completed batch in the Pre-ACH Batch Number field. For each pay group, the daily Pre-ACH program compares the in-progress batch number with the batch number entered in this field. If these are identical, the system skips the in-progress batch for Pre-ACH processing. When you enter the ID of a previously completed batch, you indicate that PrismHR needs to process the in-progress batch for Pre-ACH. The system will evaluate the in-progress batch for processing, create the appropriate ACH entries, and automatically update this field with the in-progress batch number. This prevents double entries from occurring.

Note: In the case where Pre-ACH entries were already created for a batch, but this batch was later deleted and re-created (therefore giving it a new batch number), you must manually update this field with the new batch number. For example, assume a Pre-ACH prenote was sent for batch 202202, but for some reason you decided to delete that batch and create the next regular payroll batch to replace it. If the system assigns number 202205 to the new batch, you must change the value in the Pre-ACH Batch Number field from 202202 to 202205. This ensures that PrismHR does not re-transmit the Pre-ACH entry.

  1. Click Save.

 Annual

  1. PrismHR calculates the other values: • Minimum (Hourly): The minimum hourly pay, based on the minimum annual pay. • Maximum (Hourly): The maximum hourly pay, based on the maximum annual pay.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 151 Chapter 8 Establishing Other Client Setup Features

•    Midpoint: The calculated midpoint annual pay.
     Formula = (((Maximum – Minimum) / 2) + Minimum)
•    Percentage Range: The percentage range for the Midpoint value.
     Formula = (((Maximum - Minimum) / Minimum) * 100)

Field Description Position Code Enter or select a unique code that briefly describes the position. For example, OPER for vehicle operator. (Codes cannot contain spaces or special characters.) When this form opens, the position code, its title, classification, FLSA exempt status, and obsolete status display. The system displays the FLSA Exempt settings, EEO position group, and the EEO class, if they apply to this position. FLSA Exempt indicates whether the selected position classification is set to be exempt from both the minimum wage and overtime provisions of the FLSA. You cannot change it here. Remote Position Enter an alternative position classification for remote employees of the Classification same position. The system displays the FLSA Exempt settings, EEO position group, and the EEO class, if they apply to this remote position. FLSA Exempt indicates whether the selected remote position classification is set to be exempt from both the minimum wage and overtime provisions of the FLSA. You cannot change it here. Position Description Enter a description for this position. The second panel defines requirements for the position and the pay. Supervisory Select if this is a supervisory position. The system uses this field for statistical reports. Hierarchy Tier For future development. Does not currently impact the functionality of PrismHR. Pay Grade Select to use as a default for new hires assigned this job code, if applicable. The Special Requirements option identifies those positions that have physical or mental requirements. The Americans with Disabilities Act prohibits employers from discriminating against qualified individuals with disabilities. Not including a particular person in the applicant pool for a certain job is only nondiscriminatory if that person does not meet any physical or mental requirements identified as essential functions of the position. Applications for these jobs must be closely monitored for ADA compliance.

Field Description Union Code Select this override for table-based union calculations. If an override is not Override selected, the system uses a union code in Employee Details, if any.

Alaska Position Code If applicable, enter the Alaska Position Code sent to MasterTax for quarterly tax reporting to the state of Alaska. SOC Code Enter the Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Code, if appropriate. Enter only numbers, no dashes. This information is included in the MasterTax RTS file and the Employer and Client LA quarterly files in place of the position’s description. If you do not define a SOC code for the position, the files include the description.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 154 Chapter 8 Establishing Other Client Setup Features

Field Description TTO Code Define which positions are considered eligible tipped positions to comply with the tips requirements of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. You can enter the TTO Code (Tipped Taxable Occupation Code) manually or you can click the TTO Code hyperlink and select it from the TTO Codes dialog box. The TTO Description displays upon entering a valid TTO Code. The system will validate when you enter a TTO Code against the SOC Code during the creation or updation of a Position. • Invalid TTO/SOC combinations result in an error message: TTO code [] and SOC code [] are not related. • Invalid TTO code results in an error message: TTO Code [] does not exist. • Invalid entries cannot be saved. • Valid TTO code entry is allowed when the SOC code is blank. Indiana Seasonal Enter a two-digit code if the position is seasonal and located in Indiana. This Employee Code code is required for SUI electronic filing in Indiana. Prevailing Wage Enter the Prevailing Wage for this position. This can print on pay stubs as a pay detail field. Price Code Select a price code that overrides the Bundled Rate for any employee who has been assigned to this position. Note: Only use Price Code with Bundled Billing if an employee is granted special pricing rather than using the standard bundled rate and with an employee-specific add-on unbundled rule. Per Diem Percent Enter this percentage to allocate to non-taxable per diem when paid using the percentage method. W/C Time Sheet Loc Select to calculate workers’ compensation accruals for each employee’s Based actual work location. This overrides the setting in Client Details. Obsolete Select if this position is no longer used. Suppress Work State Select if employees in this position are subject to taxes in their state of Tax residence rather than state of work. During calculations, the system will use the employee’s residence for the basis of state taxes. Benefit Group Assign a default benefit group for employees hired in this position. Agricultural Worker Select if the employee is an agricultural worker and the employee’s income will be reported to the IRS on Form 943. (Note: All employees assigned to this position are auto-assigned this designation during the new hire process.)

Working with Miscellaneous GL Segments Use the Misc GL panel to review Misc GL Counts (predefined wildcards) for this position and enter replacement Misc GL Segments. Note: During payroll processing, the system substitutes the GL segments for wildcards in GL account codes. These wildcards must also be included in the following setups: • GL setup, which is processed into payroll accounting. (You can configure them in the G/L Setup form.) • PEO client accounting setup, which is processed into client accounting. (You can configure them in the PEO Client Accounting form.)

When working with miscellaneous GL segments: 1. The predefined wildcards display in rows in the Misc GL Count column, where the codes are always EEMJB01 through EEMJB99. (The program that evaluates the wildcards only looks for those values.) 2. If appropriate, enter the Misc GL Description. For example, EEMJB01 = Segment 1 and EEMJB02 = Segment 2. (You can apply these misc segments to account codes for other areas besides pay, such as taxes or deductions.) Important! Any changes made to the descriptions affect all positions in the active client. Note: The Misc GL Description column’s values are for reference only. (These descriptions are stored in the client’s record.) The system automatically loads these values each time a position record displays. 3. If appropriate, enter the Misc GL Segment value that replaces the Misc GL Count wildcard. Note: When the system evaluates the Misc GL Segments, they are always based on the “home” job, which is different from the way segments are evaluated for departments (that is, for account codes for payment, the system uses the timesheet “worked-for” department). 4. Click Save.

Creating Commission Structures Create complex commission structures that your organization can assign to salespeople at the client level with the Commission Plan Maintenance form. You can use a commission plan as a template. Organizations that use commissions often have a standard commission program for either all or a subset of its salespeople. Assigning a commission plan code to a salesperson rather than entering individual commission structures saves effort. Note: After creating a commission plan at the client level, if you make updates to that plan and click Save, the system cannot apply those updates. For example, if you create commission plan A and apply it to client 123, then update commission plan A and save the updates the system displays an error message, “This plan is assigned to a client and changes cannot be made. Either unassign from all clients to make changes or create a new plan.” Click OK to continue. In addition, existing commission plans already in use at the client level cannot be deleted. For example, if you click the Delete button for a client-level plan and then select Yes an error message displays, “This plan is in use and cannot be deleted.” Click OK to continue.

Grouping Commissions PrismHR’s commission plan grouping feature enables the system to compare the results of the commission calculations and, according to how you arrange the groups, apply only the commission structure with the lowest or highest result. The grouping feature also enables the system to choose between commission results that use the same basis for calculation. When the system calculates commissions, it totals the commission amounts within the same numbered group and compares the results against the results of other groups. The group with the highest or lowest commission amount (depending on what is indicated in the Commission Group Highest or Lowest field) is the one added to the commissions of the salespeople assigned to the commission plan. For example, this example shows that the salesperson’s commission is the total of the fourth commission line (benefit plans with the commission code MED) plus whichever group is the highest: • Gross wages or admin fees (Group 1) • Active lives (Group 2)

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 189 Chapter 8 Establishing Other Client Setup Features

For example:

To administer PTG commission types and generate invoice records: 1. Enter or select a mandatory Begin Date and an End Date in the Look Back Period panel. Note: You cannot enter Look Back Period dates or Target Period dates that contain a gap greater than one year. 2. Enter or select a mandatory Begin Date and an End Date in the Target Period panel. 3. Enable Active Clients (only) to limit the assessment to active clients only. 4. Click Run Process. (The system only enables the Run Process button after completing all date fields.) A message displays, “Are you sure you wish to start the Look-back process at this time?” Click Yes to continue. 5. A progress report displays on-screen. Click Report to view the report details or Close to return to the Commission Period Look-back form. 6. The system displays a printable/downloadable report titled Commission Period Look-back Report, which lists all invoices created during this process. (Otherwise, a message displays, “No invoices were Created.”) For example:

Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details Use the Client Details form to maintain company information and settings.

Most of the information is in the tabs of the form. Maintaining Client Information Set company information with the Detail tab on the Client Details form.

Establishing Client Information Specify basic information with the Name & Address panel.

To set client information, do the following: 1. Select Client. 2. From Client|Change, select Client Details. 3. Complete these fields in the Name & Address panel.

 Field                         Description

                                 record that was created when the client was entered in the system. The
                                 system assumes cost equals billed for taxes and workers’ compensation.
                            •    Corporate: This option provides a Corporate Accounting model that works
                                 best for corporate companies. In addition, using this option with the

                            •    Staffing: This option provides a Staffing Accounting model that works best

                                 Version field set to Professional in the Global Configuration form runs
                                 staffing accounting for this client in a professional product version for the

 Field                     Description
                                 the client should be billed, select a different service type.)
                            •    Professional Employer: Also known as PEO, this option indicates that the
                                 service provider manages human resources, employee benefits, payroll,
                                 workers’ compensation, accounts receivable, and COBRA administration
                                 for the new client. Cost is considered the PEO cost for taxes and workers’
                                 compensation rates, which are entered at the system/employer levels.
                                 Billed rates can be higher (for profit centers) or lower than cost if
                                 appropriate, and rates are specified at the client level.
                            •    HR Services Only: The service provider manages only human resources for
                                 the client’s employees: hiring, termination, performance, compensation,
                                 training, policy, and OSHA-related services. There is no payroll.
                            •    Payroll Services Only: The employer of record provides only payroll and
                                 payroll tax services for the client. The employer does not provide human
                                 resources services.
                            •    Admin. Service/Alt. Billing: This option is similar to an ASO in that the
                                 system creates an employer record automatically. The system treats the
                                 client as a PEO for billing purposes. The organization can open profit
                                 centers on taxes and workers’ compensation. The system does not assume
                                 cost equals billed.

If you specify one or more employee statuses in this panel, the client will only be able to see the specified statuses in the following forms: Reactivation, Rehire, Status Type Change, and Employee Termination.

Note: The settings configured here will apply to any Service Provider, Worksite Manager, and Worksite Trusted Advisor users associated with the client.

To enter employee statuses: 1. Locate the Employee Statuses panel. 2. Enter or select the appropriate Employee Statuses. A Description will populate next to each type. 3. Click Save.

Defining Reason Codes Enter or select the reason codes in this panel that you would like to display to this client. If you leave this table empty, the client can use any reason codes in the system. If you specify one or more reason codes in this panel, the client will only be able to use the specified codes in the following forms: Leave of Absence, Pay Rate Change, Reactivation, Rehire, Status Type Change, and Employee Termination.

Note: The settings configured here will apply to any Service Provider, Worksite Manager, and Worksite Trusted Advisor users associated with the client.

To define reason codes: 1. Locate the Reason Codes panel. 2. Enter or select the appropriate Reason Codes. A Description will populate next to each type. 3. Click Save.

The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will be: • Client State Tax ID when: • Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Client • Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Client • Employer State Tax ID: • Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Employer • Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Employer Note: If the State Tax ID is not available on the corresponding reporting entity, the Form W-2 will not be built, and an error will appear in the W2 Error Report stating State Employer ID not found for Client # for State XX OR State Employer ID not found for Employer for State XX

Recording External PTO Balances on Check Pay Stubs To accommodate service providers whose clients use time and labor systems with their own built-in PTO capabilities that are maintained outside of PrismHR, the system provides a process to record external PTO balances on check pay stubs for regularly scheduled, manual, and special payrolls. Important! This feature does not apply to checks created using the Manual Check Entry process or the On Demand Check creation process.

Enabling the External PTO Feature You can enable the External PTO feature using the External PTO used field, which displays on the Other tab in the Client Details form. For example:

The following message displays when you select the External PTO used field, “Selecting this option will ignore any PTO setup in Prism and should only be set when PTO is being tracked externally. Do you want to continue?” Selecting Yes keeps the External PTO used field enabled and ignores any PTO set up in PrismHR. (Select No to disable this field.) When you enable the External PTO used field, the following PTO set up in PrismHR is ignored during the payroll calculation process, including:

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 246 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

• PTO accruals • PTO requests, including leave requests • PTO set up in the following forms: PTO Benefit Plans, PTO Register Types, PTO Classes, PTO Absence Codes, Employee Time Off Register, and Planned Time Off Requests In addition, any PTO set up in PrismHR does not display on payroll vouchers or on PTO reports. Note: After you enable the External PTO used field and then save the form, if you try to disable this field the following message displays, “Warning: this setting should only be unchecked if PTO is no longer being tracked externally, and any PTO that is set up in Prism should be used. Are you sure you want to continue?” Selecting Yes disables the External PTO used field and reverts to using PTO set up in PrismHR. (Select No to keep the field enabled.)

Processing Payroll When processing payroll with the External PTO feature enabled, the system retrieves the following data from an external PTO file that the client provides to display on the check pay stub: • Plan description • PTO balance • Accrued plan year (total plan year total; not per pay period) • Used plan year (PTO taken) • Carryover PTO Note: The data that displays on the check pay stub matches the external PTO file by payroll number and employee ID. (If the employee does not have a check pay stub or is not in the payroll, the system ignores the data.) During the payroll process, the system attaches each external PTO file to a specific payroll in PrismHR, which displays the most current PTO data on the check pay stub and maintains compliance with state requirements. (If the client does not submit an external PTO file for each payroll they process, the check pay stubs will not display any PTO balances.) Note the following: • The system can retrieve the external PTO file multiple times before the payroll posts. • The system reads all data sent in the external PTO file. However, it does not validate the data. (The data is the client’s responsibility.) • After the payroll finalizes, no additional PTO data can post to that payroll. • Each employee is allowed up to 20 different PTO plans listed on their check pay stub.

Reprinting External Employee PTO Information on Check Pay Stubs When you reprint a check pay stub on the Reprint Payroll Checks form, either with or without selecting the Rebuild field, while using the External PTO feature, the check pay stub displays the external PTO file data that corresponds with the payroll number and employee ID.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 247 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

During this process, the system retrieves the most recent file data that was submitted prior to the payroll being finalized and posted. Note the following: • If there is no external PTO file that matches the payroll number and employee ID, no data displays on the check stub. • If you reprint a check stub for inclusion in the check print file for an employee who did not originally have a check stub produced in the check file, the external PTO data displays on this check stub as well.

Post-Payroll Processing Once you enable the External PTO used field, do not disable it after processing payroll. After processing, the system locks the payroll and verifies if the client has finished submitting the current PTO file associated with the payroll’s number (applies to regularly scheduled, manual, and special payrolls). If the file is still uploading the system displays the following error message in the Process Payroll or SuperBatch forms, “External PTO data is currently being uploaded and must be completed before payroll finalization can continue.” (This applies to any user type finalizing payroll, including self-service worksite managers/worksite trusted advisors.)

Setting Up Yearly Group-Term Life Tax Rates Set annual Group Term Life rates with the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To set rates:

  1. Click Back Office .

  3. From the Actions menu , select Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage.
  4. Click Tax Year to select the year to which coverage applies. The form fills with age ranges and monthly rate per thousand for these age ranges. If the year does not yet exist, enter the new year into the Tax Year field.
  5. Copy Rates - Once you enter a Tax Year (say 2023) on the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form, the Copy Rates option becomes visible. This allows you the convenience of copying existing rates from one tax year to another instead of manually completing the table. Only users with Full Access to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form will be able to see the Copy Rates option. You can also click the Tax Year hyperlink to select a tax year. If you manually enter a non-existing tax year then the Copy Rates option will not display. Click the Copy Rates hyperlink. A new selector named Copy Tax Rates opens as shown below. • On the Copy Tax Rates selector, the From field is already pre-populated with the tax year (2023) entered above. On the To field, select the tax year from the drop-down to which you want to copy the tax rates. You will see the current tax year and subsequent two tax years in the drop-down. Select 2024 if you want to copy

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 248 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

the 2023 tax rates to 2024. Once you select a value for To field from the drop-down, the Copy button
becomes selectable.
•    Click Copy. A warning message opens stating Warning! Overwrite existing tax rates for 2024?
     •    Click Yes - The 2023 tax rates are copied for the 2024 tax year in the system. You will receive a
          confirmation message stating Tax rates successfully copied. Do you want to view the tax rates for
          2024?
          •     Click Yes - The 2023 tax rates are copied to 2024. The Copy Tax Rates selector closes and you
                return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form. The tax year now reflects 2024 instead
                of 2023.
          •     Click No - The 2023 tax rates are copied to 2024. The Copy Tax Rates selector closes and you
                return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form. The tax year now reflects 2023.
     •    Click No - The 2023 tax rates are not copied to 2024. You return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life
          Coverage form. The tax year reflects 2023.
•    Click Close - The 2023 tax rates are not copied to 2024. You return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life
     Coverage form. The tax year reflects 2023.

Note: If you pull up an existing tax year record (say 2023), make changes but do not save the record and click the Copy Rates hyperlink, you will receive a warning message stating There are unsaved changes that will not be copied. Do you wish to continue? • Click Yes - The last saved record for the From Tax Year selected will be used when coping rates to the To Tax Year. Unsaved changes on the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form will be ignored. • Click No - You return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form with all the unsaved changes. The Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form now also has the following buttons: Cancel - Click Cancel to clear the form at any time. All unsaved changes will be lost. Close - This button is displayed when this form is opened in a modal. Click Close to close the form. All unsaved changes will be lost. 6. Change From Age/To Age as required, or click + to add a new age range. 7. Change the Monthly Rate per Thousand of Taxable Coverage if required, or create new rates for any new age ranges you created. 8. Click Save to save the record. 9. Click Delete to delete the record. 10. Click Cancel to clear the form at any time. All unsaved changes will be lost. 11. Click Close to close this form at any time

Setting Commission Levels You can set commission levels for service provider salespeople that earn commissions based on client activity using the Commission Maintenance form. You can enter more than one commission schedule for a salesperson, and those can be in effect during different time periods or simultaneously. For example, a salesperson can simultaneously receive commissions based on gross wages as well as active lives (active employees). The system calculates commissions during the specified date range. If the period covered by the From Date and To Date for one or more salespeople overlap, the system computes all those schedules during that time period. Note the following: • When setting up commissions on the client level, you cannot set up both client and system-level plans on the same line. If you attempt this setup and click Accept, an error message displays. • If both a client-level and a system-level plan are applied, then the system calculates the commissions based on the system-level plan.

To set commission levels, do the following: 1. Select Client. 2. From Client|Change, select Client Details. 3. Select Commissions from the Actions menu. 4. Complete these fields as required.

 Field Name                          Description
 Salesperson                         In the Salesperson field, enter the user ID of an employee at your
                                     organization who is a sales representative associated with the client.
 From Date                           Enter the From Date on which the commission level goes into effect.
 To Date                             Enter the To Date on which the commission level expires.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 254 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

 Field Name                          Description
 There are two ways to calculate commissions, simple or complex.
 To calculate simple commissions:
 Amount                              Enter the commission amount as a flat amount or a percentage.
 Flat or Percent                     Indicate if the commission amount is Flat or Percent.
 Based On                            Indicate what the commission is based on.
                                     The following Based On options work with the Percent option (see
                                     above):
                                         •   Gross Wages: Total gross wages of the client payroll invoice.
                                         •   Admin Fees: Total amount of administrative fees on the client
                                             payroll invoice.
                                         •   Benefit Commission Type: Benefits-based commission for a
                                             specific benefit type. (You must enter the benefit type code in the
                                             Based on Item field.)
                                         •   Benefit Commission Percentage: Percentage based on the benefit
                                             list. (You must enter the specific group benefit plan ID in the
                                             Based on Item field.)
                                         •   Workers Comp: Total amount of workers’ compensation billed to
                                             the client for the payroll period.
                                         •   Workers Compensation Profit: Checks bill code 005 and computes
                                             the profit, and also checks for information entered on losses.
                                         •   Average Number Lives: Average number of active employees as of
                                             the period end date of the payroll (regardless of whether the
                                             employees were paid in the payroll batch).
                                         •   Gross Profit: Sales items minus the direct cost items. The value is
                                             shown on the Profitability Report in the backend system.
                                         •   Tax Profit: Sales of tax-based items (such as FUTA and SUTA)
                                             minus the cost for those tax items. Tax profit is rarely used for
                                             commissions because when not passing shelter credits it can often
                                             show a loss for the month.
                                         •   Percent of Bill Code: Fixed percentage for the amount charged on
                                             a specific bill code. (You must enter the percentage in the Based
                                             on Item field.)
                                         •   Profits to Admin (Enter Bill Code in Based On): The system uses
                                             the specified Bill Code and then subtracts the cost associated with
                                             that Bill Code. That amount (profit or loss) is used in the percent

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 255 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

 Field Name                          Description
                                             computation. For example, if you choose Bill Code 004 (SUTA) and
                                             specify 5% of profits, and there was $1000 in sales and $960 in
                                             costs, the payout would be $2.00 ($40.00 x 0.05).
                                         •   Percent of Target Amount: Percent commission based on the
                                             amount set in the Target Amount field. (This option only works
                                             with the Percent commission amount option, see above. The Flat
                                             or Percent field automatically defaults to Percent.)
                                     The following Based On options work with the Flat option (see above):
                                         •   Fixed Amount Group 1–5: Sets a flat amount that a user can elect
                                             to include when running Compute Commissions.
                                         •   Fixed per Paid Employee: Flat commission based on the number of
                                             employees paid in the commission cycle.
                                     Note: If you select a Based On option that is invalid for the selected
                                     Flat or Percent option an error message displays, "<Based On Option>
                                     'based-on' codes will not support <XXX> Amounts." Click OK to
                                     continue.
 Based on Item                       Enter additional based-on types to the commission rule at the client
                                     level, such as Percent of Bill Code, Profits to Admin, Workers
                                     Compensation Profit, Benefit Commission Type, and Benefit
                                     Commission Percentage.
 For complex commission structures, enter a Based on Plan, which is the ID of the commission plan.
 Do not use the Amount, Flat or Percent, and Based On fields. (See Creating Commission Structures
 (page 185).)
 Target Amount                       Enter the commission's target amount, which is used in conjunction
                                     with the Percent of Target Amount option. (You can enter up to two
                                     decimals in this field. The system truncates values with more than two
                                     decimals.)
                                     The Target Amount field value is an overall dollar figure the system
                                     multiplies by the Amount Percent value to calculate the salesperson's
                                     commission payout amount. For example, a Target Amount set to
                                     100,000 for a 30% of Target Amount Commission setup would pay out
                                     $30,000 as the Commission amount for the defined commission period.
                                     The system calculates the total commission as the Target Amount x
                                     Amount (percentage) defined on the Commission Maintenance form,
                                     divided by the number of invoices in the applicable timeframe. The
                                     calculated commission is split across all invoices in the Compute
                                     Commissions period (Begin Date - End Date), which corresponds to the
                                     configuration dates on the Commission Maintenance form.

 Field Name                          Description
                                     Note: If the commission cannot be split evenly across all invoices, then
                                     the sum of all commission amounts across all invoices will still total the

Set a theme as follows: 1. Specify colors for these items: text and tiles, title bars, header bars, breadcrumb bar, and the background. Use a hexademical color code, or click the drop icon to select a palette color. The last column displays a color swatch. 2. Upload a company logo to display in EP. a. Click Choose File for the Logo Image. b. Navigate to the location of the logo image file and select it. c. Click Open. You return to the ESS Theme Designer. d. Click Upload. 3. You can also upload a background image to display in EP. a. Click Choose File for the Background Image. b. Navigate to the location of the background image file and select it. c. Click Open. You return to the ESS Theme Designer. d. Click Upload. 4. Click Save Theme.

Note: To remove a logo or background image from a theme, click the Delete button next to the image, then click Save Theme.

Using Report Parameters Feature The Report Parameters feature allows you to specify run-time parameters for some of the reports that print for this client when a user processes the payroll. The reports in the list are specified in the Client Details Payroll tab. Not all reports allow you to specify default parameters. The reports that do are listed below. The other reports have set parameters that you cannot customize for the client. • Defining Benefits Billing Report Parameters (page 269) • Setting Calculate Checks Report Parameters (page 271) • Setting Client Allocation Report Parameters (page 273) • Setting Deduction Register Report Parameters (page 276) • Setting Employee Check Acknowledgement Parameters (page 272) • Setting Fax Back Report Parameters (page 279) • Setting Payroll Allocation Report Parameters (page 280) • Setting Payroll Check Journal Report Parameters (page 272) • Setting Payroll Register Report Parameters (page 283) • Setting Payroll No Earnings Report Parameters (page 282)

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 268 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

• Setting Workers’ Compensation Report Parameters (page 285)

Note: If a report is set at the global level, users can edit the default parameters from the main Client menu.

Defining Certified Payroll Report Format Parameters You can set up the Certified Payroll Report to automatically run with payroll. Use the Certified Payroll Report Format Parameters form to define the format parameters for this report.

Note: This report executes only for regularly scheduled, weekly payrolls (AUTORUN version), and displays information about wages and payroll for all employees. It does not execute for the ON-DEMAND version.

To define the Certified Payroll Report format parameters: 1. Go to the Certified Payroll Report Format Parameters form and complete the following fields.

 Field Name                              Description
 Format                                  Select the Format from the drop-down.
                                         Note: Currently, this report only supports the Federal Government
                                         version.
 Include Gender on the Report            Select Include Gender on the Report, if needed.
 Include Ethnicity                       Select Include Ethnicity, if needed.
 Include Employee Address                Select Include Employee Address, if needed.
 Employee Identifier                     Select an Employee Identifier you want to use in the report: (Full Social
                                         Security Number, Last Four Digits of Social, Employee ID, or None).

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 269 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

 Field Name                              Description
 Show zero work weeks                    Select this field to include projects that did not have any work to display
                                         in the Certified Payroll Report, essentially providing you with a zero
                                         report (all amounts listed in the report display as zero). If you do not
                                         select this field and there was no project work during the requested
                                         date, an error message displays.
 Show extended rate of pay up            Select this field to display the pay rate in the same format that displays
 to 4 decimal places                     on vouchers, which display up to four decimal places.
 Allocate Deductions/Taxes by            Select Allocate Deductions/Taxes by Project to calculate deductions and
 Project                                 taxes. Selecting this field sets the calculation to allocate by project total.
                                         When unchecked, the allocation is based on gross pay.
  1. Click Save.

Managing Client Security Settings Use the Security form (accessed through the Client Details Actions menu ) to manage the client’s security settings.

Defining Client Security You can define the Data Security Entities that users can access by specifying the defaults and the settings to which you want to restrict access. Data Security Entities are entities and work assignments that users can set for employees in the Employee Details > Work tab, specifically Location, Division, Department, Shift, or Work Group. The Data Security Entities in the Client Security panel are the only ones by which your organization can restrict access for the client. If you do not list an item, you cannot restrict user access by that entity. As indicated below, you can restrict client access by location, division, and department. Because shift and work group are not listed, users can access all shift and work group information, if any.

If the client does not use an entity type (for example, they have only one location), there is probably no reason to include that entity. For example, if some employees have division assignments and should have access to one or more departments, select Department from Data Security Entity and set Default Access to Full Access. If other employees do not have any department assigned, and you do not want them to have access to department information, set Default Access when Blank to No Access.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 287 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

  1. For each entity:
    1. Select each Data Security Entity.
    2. Select the Default Access for the entity. This can be changed at the user level. • Full Access: Users can view, edit, and save data. • No Access: Users cannot see any information associated with the entity.
    3. Select the Default Access when Blank to indicate the default behavior if an employee user does not have a value for the entity. • Full Access: Employees that have nothing set for the entity can view, edit, and save data. • No Access: Employees that have nothing set for the entity cannot see any information associated with the entity.
  2. Click Accept.

Maintaining Worksite Users This panel allows you to manage the worksite users who have access to the client.

If available, you can: • Click the User ID link to edit the user account. (Note: The access information that displays is dependent on the user record’s current access for the selected client, which is available on the Users form.) • Click the Add User button to create a new user account to associate with the client. Refer to the System Administration Guide for information on editing and creating user accounts.

Associating User and Human Resource Roles with a Worksite Manager Select any role to associate with a worksite manager in the User Roles and Human Resource Roles panels, so managers who have access to set up other managers can only access these user and Human Resources roles for the client.

Suppressing Payroll Warnings Suppress payroll warnings by selecting a warning in the Payroll Suppress panel.

Maintaining Security Settings for the Client Use the options in the Access panel to maintain the client’s security settings.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 288 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

  1. Set sMFA Device Expiration to use the global setting, a different interval period from the global setting, or disable multi-factor authentication for this client. (Note: This setting automatically defaults to 30 Days.) When enabled, all users associated with this client who access the system will need to re-authenticate their access after the specified time interval, if any, for each device they use (computer, tablet, and so on). The system prompts them to request an authentication code, which it sends to the email address set on their user account (users must have email address). Then the user can enter the authentication code to regain access to the system.
  2. Select the sMFA Enabled for Trusted Advisor Password Reset option to enable multi-factor authentication for all worksite trusted advisors who have access to the client, requiring them to use multi-factor authentication when they use the Forgot Password link.
  3. Select Enable Security for Messages to restrict the users, companies, and so on, that the service provider can select in the New Message form to those that client users can access.
  4. Use the IP White List/Range table to restrict worksite users (managers, trusted advisors, and employees) to a specific IP address or range of addresses. See the examples below.

Using IP White List/Range Examples Your organization can use the white list to grant the client’s users access only at a specific location, such as an office or home, by specifying the IP addresses or the IP range. In the example below, those users can only access PrismHR from the listed IP addresses (123.123.123.101, 123.123.123.102, and 123.123.123.103).

Your organization can also specify a range of permitted IP addresses. • In the example below, those users can only access PrismHR from IP addresses that begin with 123.123.123.

• In the example below, those users can only access the system from IP addresses in the range (123.123.123.100, 123.123.123.101, 123.123.123.102, and so on). Note that if you enter a range, you must separate the first and last addresses with a dash and that the first three numbers must match. If the first three numbers do not match, that is not a valid IP address range and the system will ignore it.

Defining Payroll Shipping Methods for the Client Use the Special Delivery form to define methods that users can select for shipping the client’s payrolls. For example:

To define payroll shipping methods for the client: 1. Select All Locations if the delivery method applies to all locations. If this is selected, the system charges a single fee for the whole client. 2. If you did not select All Locations, click New and select one of the client’s worksite locations, or enter the code for a location that already has a delivery method defined for it. 3. Enter the Company Override Method, which is one of the delivery methods defined in your system. This overrides the default. 4. Enter the Method description, which is usually the name for the service (for example, US Postal Service or FedEx). 5. Enter the Days In Transit, which is the delivery method’s number of days in transit. 6. Enter the Bill Event Code, which is the ID of the billing event that the system uses to track this delivery method. If there is no charge for the delivery method, leave this field blank. 7. Enter the Special Bill Amt to override the standard billing amount for this client, if appropriate. 8. Use the Method Active drop-down to indicate the status of this delivery method: • Yes: This method is available for users to select. • No: Users cannot select this method. • Once: Select this if the method will be used only once. After it has been triggered, the system sets it to No.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 290 Chapter 9 Maintaining Client Details

  1. In the Method Until field, enter the date when delivery method should stop being used for the client. After this date, the system sets the Method Active to No.
  2. Select Create Spec Sheet to indicate that a special sheet will print during payroll processing. Do not select this option if a special sheet is not necessary.
  3. If a special sheet will print:
    1. Enter the Special Message that prints on the sheet.
    2. Enter the Name that should appear on the sheet.
    3. Enter the Address to print on the sheet.
    4. Enter the City, State, Zip Code to print on the sheet.
  4. Select the Delivery Sheet Format, which ensures that the address on the printed delivery sheet displays in the window envelopes your organization uses. You can select one of the following: • The Standard and Expanded options display no line or indent adjustment fields when selected, and the delivery sheet prints the entered data in a fixed position. • The Large Window, Large Window (Expanded), Large Window - 1 Page, and Large Window - 1 Page (Expanded) options display adjustment fields for Delivery Sheet Address Line and Deliver Sheet Address Indent. The delivery sheet prints the entered data using these specified adjustments. • The 2 Window, 2 Window (Expanded), 2 Window - 1 Page, and 2 Window - 1 Page (Expanded) options display adjustment fields for Delivery Sheet Address Line, Deliver Sheet Address Indent, Client Information Line, and Client Information Indent. The delivery sheet prints the entered data using the specified adjustments. • The 2 Window (Shipping on Page 2) and 2 Window (Expanded) (Shipping on Page 2) options, in addition to the adjustment fields described above, print the address on the first piece of paper and the Special Message on the second sheet. The purpose is that the person who is preparing the envelopes can insert the address into the envelope and then read the instructions on the second page (what type of envelope to use, which mail bin to place the envelope in, and so on). Note: If you select one of the 2 Window formats, you must enter the full address.
  5. Click Save. After changing these settings, you can rerun the delivery sheet report from the Payroll Summary form, if needed.

Setting Up Payroll Approval Your organization can set up the system so that the client can see the invoice and approve the payroll before it is complete. You can set approvals for both the initialization and finalization steps of the process.

Setting Up a Client for Payroll Calculation Approvals You do not need to define an approval policy to set the client to approve their payrolls.

To set up a client for payroll calculation approvals, do the following: 1. Go to the Client Details form (found in the Client menu under Client|Change). 2. Select the Control tab.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 309 Chapter 11 Using Client Payroll Processing Options

  1. Select the Worksite Payroll Approval option to send an approval email after a payroll is calculated (initialized).
  2. If appropriate, you can also specify that a Payroll Finalization Notification should be sent by email and, if so, who should receive those emails other than the payroll approver. This sends an email after the payroll is posted (finalized).

Note: This is simply a notice that the payroll was posted. It is not related to any approval policies for payroll finalization that your organization has defined at either the system level or for the client.

  1. Click Save.

Setting Up an Approval Policy for Payroll Posting To set up an approval policy for payroll posting, do the following: 1. You can set up approval policies for all clients or for the specific client. • To set up a system-level policy, go to the Global Approval Policies form. ( Click Back Office. Select System|Change.) • To set up a policy for the client, go to the Approval Policies form (found in the HR menu under HR|Change). Ensure that the correct client is selected. 2. If you are setting up a system-level policy, specify the Service Type. If you are setting up a client-level policy, continue to the next step. 3. From the Approval Type drop-down, select Payroll Finalization. 4. Define each of the users who need to approve the payroll when it is posted. (For example, you might specify the HR Role of Payroll Approver.) 5. Click Save.

Setting Up a User as a Payroll Approver To make a user the client’s payroll approver, do the following: 1. Go to the Users form. (Click Back Office. Select System|Change.) 2. Enter the User ID of the user who will approve payrolls.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 310 Chapter 11 Using Client Payroll Processing Options

If you are creating a new user account, enter the other information as needed. See the online help for the
form or refer to the System Administration Guide for detailed instructions.
  1. In Human Resources Roles, select Payroll Approver. You should also make sure that the Active User option is selected, that the user has access to the client, and that the user role assigned to the user has full access to the approval forms.
  2. Click Save.

After you complete this setup, when a payroll processor calculates and reviews the next payroll, the user will receive an email with the invoice details and a link to payroll approval in PrismHR.

Defining Custom Message Templates for Approvals You can set up message templates to send for each kind of payroll approval for your organization to use instead of the system default. This allows you to customize the message.

To create a message template, do the following: 1. Go to the Message Templates form. (Click Back Office. Select System|Change.) 2. Enter a unique Message ID for the template, for example, PAYCALCAPP. 3. Enter a Description of the template, for example, Payroll Calculation Approval. 4. Select the Content Type: TEXT or HTML. 5. Enter the Subject line for emails that use this template. 6. Enter the Body of the message. You can incorporate HTML in the body of the message if you select the HTML format. 7. Click Save.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 311 Chapter 11 Using Client Payroll Processing Options

To use the template for approvals or finalization notices, do the following: 1. Go to the System Parameters form. (Click Back Office. Select System|Change.) 2. Open the Actions menu and then select Email Services. 3. Click + to add a new row. 4. Select the appropriate email Template Type: • Payroll Approval: The email to send for approvals after the payroll is calculated. • Payroll Finalization: The email to send after the payroll is posted. 5. Adjusting Summary Time Sheet Columns Users specify the Summary Time Sheet Pay Codes in the Client Details Time Sheet tab. This determines the pay columns that display in Summary Time Sheet Entry.

Note: Client Details is found in the Client menu under Client|Change.

You can change or reorder the columns as needed and the system displays messages to alert you to the impact that your edits will have. Use one of the following procedures to change or reorder the columns and get the results you want: • Changing Columns (page 313) • Reordering Columns (page 313) • Changing to a Different Type of Pay (page 313)

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 312 Chapter 11 Using Client Payroll Processing Options

Changing Columns You can change the column from one pay code to another with the same earning type (such as cash). 1. In the Time Sheet tab of Client Details, edit one of the Pay Codes to change it to one for the same type of pay (for example, REG1 to REG2). 2. In the message “This action will replace pay code [REG1] with pay code [REG2] for all current summary time sheet records. These changes will occur when this form is saved. Do you wish to continue?” click the Yes button to reassign the values to the new pay code (for example, REG2).

Note: If you click No, the system does not change the pay code.

  1. Click Save.

Reordering Columns If you want to rearrange the columns and, ultimately, keep the current hours assigned to the same pay codes they were before you changed the columns, follow these steps. 1. In the Time Sheet tab of Client Details, edit one of the Pay Codes to change it to one for the same type of pay (for example, REG3 to REG4). 2. In the message “This action will replace pay code [REG3] with pay code [REG4] for all current summary time sheet records. These changes will occur when this form is saved. Do you wish to continue?” click the Yes button to (temporarily) reassign the values to the new pay code (for example, REG4).

Note: If you click No, the system does not change the pay code.

  1. Enter the original pay code (for example, REG3) in a new column.
  2. In the message, “You previously stated that you would like to replace [REG3] pay code on active time sheets with [REG4]. Do you still wish to do this [Yes], or move the values associated with the [REG3] to this new position [No]?”: • Click Yes to leave any values assigned to the new pay code (REG4). • Click No to assign any values back to the original pay code (REG3).
  3. Click Save.

Changing to a Different Type of Pay If you need to change a pay code from one type of pay to another, you can only do so if there are no values entered in an active payroll. Examples are when you change to a pay code with a different calculation method or pay reason. • If there are no values, you can simply change the pay code. • When there are values in an active payroll, the system displays a message informing you that you need to use Payroll Control to delete and recreate the payroll. If that is what you need to do: 1. Open Payroll Control (found in the Payroll menu under Payroll|Change).

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 313 Chapter 11 Using Client Payroll Processing Options

2. Enter the Payroll Number of the active payroll.
3. Click Delete.
4. In the confirmation message, click Yes.
5. Click Yes in the message to create a replacement payroll for the one you just deleted.
6. Return to the Client Details Time Sheet tab and change the pay code.
7. Users can proceed to enter data in the time sheet for the new pay code.

Note: If there are only a few values in the time sheet, you can simply delete them from the time sheet rather than deleting the entire payroll and creating a new one.

Chapter 12 Managing Pending Payday Notifications You can manage pending payday notifications using the Payday Notification Queue form, which is available on the Client|View menu. For example:

Note the following: • This form is only available for service providers. • After payrolls are completed, payday notifications are scheduled for delivery but are not sent until the pay date. These pending notifications display in the Payday Notification Queue, so you can view and manage them. • The queue displays all employees that have a pay date within the next seven days (default). • You can adjust the pay date to include vouchers up to 30 days in the future.

                                 after the form loads.)
                                 Note: The system uses the Pay Date on the voucher to trigger the payday
                                 notification.
 Employee                        To view and manage a specific employee, do one of the following:

                                  •      Enter the employee ID or name in the Employee field.
                                  •      Search for an employee by ID or name by selecting the Employee field. The
                                         Select Employee search dialog displays where you can enter the employee ID
                                         or name, which displays in the results list. You can click Reset Search and
                                         Filters to remove the search entry from the Employee ID or Name field.

 Processed Date                  Select the date when the payroll was processed (optional).

  1. The form loads all enabled payday notifications for the active client, if the employee has not opted out of their settings on EP. In addition, note the following: • Voided payrolls do not display. • Only regularly scheduled batches display (the system excludes special and manual batches). • If you update the delivery method, email address, or mobile number while the notification is still pending, the change immediately displays in the queue, and notifications are sent based on the updated information. • The system triggers payday notifications only when payroll is completed and the employee is opted into the notification.
  2. Select the checkbox for each pending payday notification you want to remove or click Select All to remove all displayed notifications.
  3. Click Remove from queue. In addition, you can obtain a list of payment notification transmission statuses by running the Payday Notification Transmission Report.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 322 Chapter 13 Maintaining Worksite Locations

Chapter 13 Maintaining Worksite Locations You can maintain the details for the client’s worksite locations in the Worksite Locations form.

Working with SUTA SUTA is based on the employee’s home location. Entering hours for a different state does not trigger the SUTA for that state. SUTA is based on the location code in the Employee Details form. You cannot have multiple SUTA states in a single payroll. If you have an employee who worked in multiple states for a single payroll and wants to calculate SUTA for each state, you must run a separate payroll to process the hours for each state where the employee works. You must change the employee’s home location in Employee Details for each payroll you run before processing.

Importing a Worksite Locations Template File Clicking the Import button displays the Data Import Tool form, which allows you to import a Worksite Locations template file that contains the following fields (this file must be in .txt format): • Client ID (Required). • Location Code (Required). • Location Name (Required). • Address One (Required). • Address Two. • Zip Code (Required). • Geocode (auto-fills based on zip code). • City/County/State (populates with geocode population and auto-fills based on zip code). • Latitude (auto-fills based on zip code). • Longitude (auto-fills based on zip code). • Work Comp State (Required): Enter a two-digit state name (do not enter the whole state name). For example, enter TX for the state of Texas. • G/L Segment Code 1. • G/L Segment Code 2.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 323 Chapter 13 Maintaining Worksite Locations

• G/L Segment Code 3. The Import button displays on the Worksite Locations form for all service provider user roles except the “Deny” and “Inquiry-only” roles. Imports can be performed for multiple clients at the operations level.

Note: For more information about the Data Import Tool form, refer to the Payroll Administration Guide.

Working with Miscellaneous GL Segments Use the Misc GL panel to review Misc GL Counts (predefined wildcards) for this worksite location and enter replacement Misc GL Segments. Note: During payroll processing, the system substitutes the GL segments for wildcards in GL account codes. These wildcards must also be included in the following setups: • GL setup, which is processed into payroll accounting. (You can configure them in the G/L Setup form.) • PEO client accounting setup, which is processed into client accounting. (You can configure them in the PEO Client Accounting form.)

When working with miscellaneous GL segments: 1. The predefined wildcards display in rows in the Misc GL Count column, where the codes are always EEMLC01 through EEMLC99. (The program that evaluates the wildcards only looks for those values.) 2. If appropriate, enter the Misc GL Description. For example, EEMLC01 = Segment 1 and EEMLC02 = Segment 2. (You can apply these misc segments to account codes for other areas besides pay, such as taxes or deductions.) Important! Any changes made to the descriptions affect all worksite locations in the active client. Note: The Misc GL Description column’s values are for reference only. (These descriptions are stored in the client’s record.) The system automatically loads these values each time a worksite location record displays. 3. If appropriate, enter the Misc GL Segment value that replaces the Misc GL Count wildcard. 4. Click Save.

Indicating Associated Taxpayer Entities/Employers Use the Eligible Employers panel if the client has alternate employers listed in the Client Details Other tab and you need to indicate which taxpayer entities/ employers are associated with the worksite location. This ensures that during the new hire process, employees can only be hired into locations for the specified employer and the worksite manager and trusted advisor users can select the appropriate employer. If you do not specify any employers, then service providers can select any of the client’s alternate employers in the New Hire form. In addition, worksite managers can only select the default employer unless an Alternate Employer is listed on the worksite location. Note: To change this behavior, enable the ALLOWWMNEWHIREALTEMP custom feature code, which allows a worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor to select an alternate employer on the New Hire form when the alternate employer’s Suppress Client Access is not set to Yes on the Client Details Other tab.

Managing Messages Manage messages with the Messages form, which displays messages sent through the system. For example:

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 337 Chapter 14 Sending and Receiving Messages

To Do this Read a message Click Date Received, From, or Subject. The Message Review form displays. A check mark displays in the Read column for each message read. Messages display on this panel as follows: • Unread messages display in bold text at the top of the list • Messages display in chronological date order, with the newest messages displaying first. Note: Pagination controls display for clients who have more than 26 messages. Change an item in the panel Click Refresh to update the display. Delete a message • For a single message, click the message’s box in the Select All column, then click Delete Selected Messages. Click Yes in the confirmation dialog that displays. • For multiple messages, click the box in the Select All column for every message you want to delete, then click Delete Selected Messages. Click Yes in the confirmation dialog that displays. • All messages at once: Click the box to the right of Select All, then click Delete Selected Messages. Click Yes in the confirmation dialog that displays.

Access other message-related features using the Actions menu: • Configuring New Messages (page 338) • Maintaining Custom Message Groups (page 336)

Configuring New Messages Send messages through the system or by e-mail with the New Message form. You can also search for and review previous messages.

Optional: Refine the work assignment by specifying Dept, Division, Location, Project, or Shift. 8. Click Send when the message is ready.

Defining and Applying Global PEO Accounting Templates The Global PEO Client Accounting Templates allow you the flexibility to define and apply a PEO accounting template for related clients globally without having to repeat the setup on a client-by-client basis. A service provider with a PEO Client that has sister companies might want all their accounting to be set up the same, for example, a chain of hotels. You can define a Global PEO Client Accounting Template and then select it in the Global Account Template field in the PEO Client Accounting form. Working with Bill Pending Data The Bill Pending Events panel, on the Bill Pending form, lists billing events that will occur during the next scheduled billing date (in other words, they are pending). These billing events can be created on this form or generated automatically by PrismHR.

Background There are three ways to create invoice line items: • As a scheduled bill, according to payroll dates and so on. • As an immediate bill, manually generated using the Miscellaneous Invoice Entry form. • As a future-dated or “pending” bill, which waits until the next scheduled billing date. Those items appear in the Bill Pending Events form.

• To view an existing event, click the event’s Bill Date. The Line Item Details form opens, where you can view the read-only information.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 347 Chapter 15 Setting Other Client Features

• To manually create a new event, click New Entry. The Line Item Details form opens, where you can enter the billing event.

System Billing Events Several events trigger PrismHR to generate a pending bill for clients. Here are two examples: • When you set up a new employee, the system creates a line item for the employee setup fee. • When you terminate benefits for an employee, the system searches for a billing event using the TB+ naming convention. For example, if a plan ID is HMOBLUE, the system searches for a billing event named TBHMOBLUE. If it does not find that billing event, the system uses TEBA.

Manual Billing Events Many reasons and situations exist in which you need to manually create a line item. In each case, PrismHR bills the client upon the next invoice, not an immediate invoice.

Importing Bill Pending Data You can access the Bill Pending import template in the Data Import Tool from this form to import bill pending

data by clicking Import . The Bill Pending import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Bill Pending form.

Note: You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Bill Pending import template option. Note the following when importing Bill Pending data: • Importing only creates new entries. It does not edit or update existing bill pending entries. • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company. • Users with a user role set to DENY for the Bill Pending form cannot import data using the Bill Pending import template. The Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form. • Users with a user role set to INQUIRY for the Bill Pending form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool, cannot view the Import icon on the Bill Pending form. • Users with a user role set to INQUIRY for the Bill Pending form can view the Bill Pending import template, but cannot import data. • Users with a user role set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.
