Avoiding Pitfalls Client Bill Pending is an extremely useful tool; at the same time, problems can occur if you are not careful. PrismHR does only what you tell it to do, so ensure your entries are correct. Client Bill Pending is both employee- sensitive and date-sensitive.

Employee Sensitivity For example, you set up a new employee named Joe, who is an active employee and is paid once a month on the first. You create a line item for Joe on the second day of the month. PrismHR does not convert the line item into a bill for the client until Joe’s next pay day, which is the first of the following month. If this feature was not employee-sensitive, you would bill the client on the next invoice, which could fall before the first of the month.

Date Sensitivity For example, you create a line item for January 1, 2024, but specify a billing date of January 1, 2026 by mistake. The line item remains dormant in PrismHR until the date you specified, then is included in the next invoice after that date.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 352 Chapter 15 Setting Other Client Features

Using Repeat Thru Date Correctly If you set up a recurring event, you must define the date limits of the event. The system uses the Repeat Thru Date field to know when the recurring event starts and when it stops. Be very aware of the dates you want to define and double-check your date entries. The system automatically calculates if any dates have been “missed” upon the first payroll run after you define the recurring event. For example, you have a weekly billing event for a payroll that you want to occur starting on or after January 1, 2024. You enter 12/31/24 in the Repeat Thru Date field. However, you mistakenly enter the start date (in the Bill Date field) as 1/1/23 instead of 1/1/24. Upon January 2, 2024 (the first business day of the year), PrismHR realizes it has not performed its weekly billing (based on the check date) since the starting date. Therefore, PrismHR creates 52 transactions in order to “catch up” to the present date.

Using Repeat Cycle Correctly If you set up a recurring event, you must define how often to repeat the event. The system uses the Repeat Cycle field to know how often it must run the recurring event. For example, you have a monthly billing event for an end-of-the-month payroll. The system reads what you enter literally: in other words, it is very exact. You mistakenly enter the billing date (in the Bill Date field) as 1/31/24 instead of 1/28/24. Upon February 29, 2024 (because of the leap year – otherwise February 28), PrismHR realizes it is not the 31st day of the month. Therefore, PrismHR skips the transaction.

Cost If you enter an amount in the cost section of Bill Pending, the cost is updated when a payroll is posted. For example, you need to set up a client bill pending for an overbilling on SUTA. The rate you charge your client is 2.7% and you mistakenly charged them 3.00% on $15,000 taxable wages. SUTA is not a profit center for this client so the billing should match the cost. The liability was calculated at the correct rate of 2.7%. When entering the client’s credit for $45.00, leave the cost column blank. There is no need to adjust cost. As another example, you bill your client for drug testing the employees. The arrangement you make with the client is they pay $28.00 per drug test. Your provider bills you $20.00 per employee. Enter the client bill pending as $20.00 in the cost field so that the system can calculate the income.

To deidentify files for an inactive employee: 1. Select Employees in the Data Type field. 2. In the Years Terminated field, select the minimum number of years an employee must be inactive to display. The employees matching this criteria display. In addition, a message displays, “Employee Inactive Data Deletion limited to 1000 employees per run.” Note the following: • Only employees who have been terminated for at least seven years can have their PII deidentified from active and inactive clients. (The tool tip ( ) displays this information.) • Employees display in the Inactive Data Deletion list when their last termination status date is more than the selected number of Years Terminated from the current date. 3. To narrow the search, enter or select the employee’s Client ID. After entering or selecting an ID and moving your cursor off the field, the search immediately displays all inactive employee data for that ID. Note: To narrow down the list of employees that displays, enter the employee ID or the employee’s first or last name in the Search box. After clicking the magnifying glass icon ( ) or pressing Enter, the employee list redisplays that criteria. (Searches can return up to 1,000 employees at a time since only 1,000 employees can be deidentified at a time.) 4. Select the employees to deidentify in the Employees table. (Click Employee ID to select all employees that display.)

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 365 Chapter 15 Setting Other Client Features

  1. After verifying the settings, click Deidentify Employee Data. A confirmation message displays, “Deidentify all data for the selected employees?” Confirm the action to remove data for the displayed employees. (The system replaces the attribute values in Column F.) Note: This action deidentifies employee data (that is, it removes the data instead of deleting it) and cannot be undone.
  2. Once the deidentify process is complete, click a link in the Employees column in the History panel to download a report of all employees removed from the system. Note: This downloadable report lists the company ID and the employee ID for all employees who were deidentified. However, no PII is shared.

To search for data deletions within a date range: 1. Open the History panel by clicking the plus sign ( ). 2. Enter or select the From and To date range. The system adjusts the display of data deletions or deidentifications to match the criteria. 3. The following columns display:

 Column                              Description
 Date Completed                      Timestamps when the deletion finished, displaying the date, hours,
                                     minutes, seconds, and the CST time zone.
 Data Type                           Displays the type of data that was deleted:
                                         •   Client: Displays if both client and employee data was deleted.
                                         •   Employee: Displays if only employee data was deleted.

 Clients                             Displays total number of clients deleted.
                                     Note: Displays a dash (-) if only employee data was deleted.
 Employees                           Displays total number of employees deleted.
                                     Note: Displays a dash (-) if only client data was deleted.
 Processed by User                   Displays the user ID of the person who performed the deletion.
 Clients                             Displays a link to the client deletion file that can be downloaded as a ZIP
                                     file.
 Employees                           Displays a link to the employee deidentification file that can be
                                     downloaded as a ZIP file.

Note: Searches can only return up to 1,000 employees at a time since only 1,000 employees at a time can be deidentified.

Chapter 16 Converting a PEO Client to an ASO Client Note: You should have a basic understanding of Employer Details and Client Details in PrismHR before completing this process.

To perform this conversion, complete the following steps: 1. Entering Employer Details (page 373): Create a new employer. 2. Establishing Employer SUTA Rate (page 374): Enter the SUTA cost for the new employer. 3. Establishing Employer W/C Accrual Mods (page 375): Set up the Workers’ Compensation cost for the new employer. 4. Entering Employer Bank Accounts (page 376): Set up the employer’s bank accounts for cutting checks and/or direct deposit. 5. Defining Employer Billing Templates (page 377): Set up billing templates for the ASO. 6. Selecting Client Details (page 377): Select the client that is changing to the ASO; update the Detail, Control, and Billing tabs.

Entering Employer Details Use the Employer Details form to enter a new employer ID and general information about the employer. For example:

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 373 Chapter 16 Converting a PEO Client to an ASO Client

To enter a new employer ID and general information about the employer, do the following: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details. 3. Enter the new Employer ID, which should be the same as the ASO’s current client ID. 4. Enter the Employer Print Name, which is the way the employer’s name should print on checks, reports, and so on. 5. Enter the Federal EIN issued to the employer by the IRS in the format ##-#######. Note: The accounting files put the company number before the account number. QuickBooks and PeachTree cannot process the numbers, so PrismHR removes the company number when it builds files for those programs. You can use the G/L Company Number for accounting purposes to group data, such as for an ASO. 6. Enter the G/L Company Number used as the prefix to the general ledger account number. 7. Refer to the online help or the Employer Administration User Guide for information on the other fields in Employee Details form. 8. Click Save.

 Employer                                Enter the Employer ID.

 Effective Date or New Date              Select an existing Effective Date, or click New Date and enter the

Establishing Employer W/C Accrual Mods Use the Employer W/C Accrual Mods form to establish the workers’ compensation rates for a selected employer and state. For example:

To establish the workers’ compensation rates, do the following: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Employer|Change, select Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers. 3. Enter the Employer ID. 4. Enter or select the State Code in which the employer does business. 5. Enter a new Effective Date, or select an existing date. 6. Enter the employer’s Discount/Debit rate for this state. 7. Entering Employer Bank Accounts If you are going to cut checks or direct deposit information from the client’s own bank account, enter the basic information about the account in the Bank Account panel of the Bank Accounts form. For example:

Note: The 00 Checking Account is a special purpose account, the master account for all transactions. Each file header shows the 00 Checking Account as the main file header, with the funds being transferred into the account from whatever checking account the individual ACH shows it is processed. This adds a level of abstraction to the process, but allows a single account to process all the ACH clearing with only summary transactions from each of the actual checking accounts.

To enter employer bank account information, do the following: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Bank Accounts. 3. Enter the bank Account ID for this account. It must be an integer. 4. Enter a Reference for the name of the financial institution where this account is maintained, as well as any other information. For example, ASO’s Payroll Cash Account at Fleet Bank. 5. Enter the Bank Name. 6. Enter the Bank Address and City, State & ZIP Code, which is the street or mailing address. 7. Enter the Transit Number assigned to this financial institution. This number prints on checks drawn on this bank unless you enter a different number in Transit Number (Chks) below. 8. Enter the client’s Account Number at this financial institution. This account is debited when an offsetting settlement entry is created. 9. Enter the Fractional Transit number that appears on checks. This number is the same for all checks drawn on a unique checking account, typically in the format NN/NNN. 10. Enter the Check Title.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 376 Chapter 16 Converting a PEO Client to an ASO Client

  1. Enter the Employer ID who is the owner of the checking account, from a general ledger point of view. (See See Entering Employer Details on page 373.)

Working with Data Retriever The Data Retriever form is a quick and flexible way to retrieve, export, and manipulate data from your system. You can quickly pull raw data from multiple clients and the entities within these clients. Data Retriever can give you access to aggregate system data for purposes of analysis or analytics.

Note: By default, the company tax and workers’ compensation data is available only to the service providers. Unless you enable client access to this data these items are restricted from view for worksite manager and worksite trusted advisor users.

Use the + to expand the categories in any column.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 401 Chapter 17 Using Reports

To create a Data Retriever report: 1. In the Step 1 column, select the clients you want to query. You can select as many clients as you want. 2. In the Step 2 column, select the fields you want to query. If you query Employment Status, you can click to select statuses on which to filter. 3. In the Step 3 column, select the totals you want, then select a date range from the calendar.

  1. To add another date range or to select additional data, click the date range link.

  2. Optionally, you can expand certain items and select a sort order for them.

  3. Click Save.

  4. Click Run. When your report is ready, the results display.

Note: Data retriever is configured to calculate up to four reports at one time. If a user attempts to generate a report while the four reports are calculating, the report will be placed in a queue. If you would like to view the

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 402 Chapter 17 Using Reports

status of any report that has been run or is currently in the queue, you can navigate to Data Retriever>Actions menu>View Run Report (Last 24 hours).

  1. To export the report to a spreadsheet format, click Export. The system exports your data to a .csv file. From the Actions menu , you can select: • Suppress/Do not suppress lines with zero totals • Save Report Template -To save a report as a template or edit and replace an existing template. For more information on saving report templates by user type, see See Save Report Template by User Type on page 406

Note: You can save report templates for yourself only or share them and provide access to specific user types.

Data Retriever Security By default, access to potentially sensitive data is restricted in Data Retriever. For example, company tax and workers’ compensation data is available only to service providers. Unless you enable client access to this data for worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor users, it does not display. Your organization should have a well-planned strategy for applying role-based security. Based on the role associated with a user account, you can define the forms and fields in PrismHR that users can view or edit. You can also define the fields that users can query.

Step 2 Data You can set the security for Step 2 of the Data Retriever query process on the User Roles form. Step 2 data is pulled from the following forms: • EMPLOYEE.PERMAINT • EMPLOYEE.PERMAINT.PERSONAL • EMPLOYEE.PER*MAINT.PAY Toggle the Access option to control access to the data. • Full and Inquiry access allows the user role to work with the data. • Deny access prevents the user role from viewing or querying the data.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 403 Chapter 17 Using Reports

For field-level security, click the Field link. The Field Security Maintenance form displays. Toggle the Enable/Disable/Hidden options for each field. • Enable access allows the user role to work with the data. • Disable access allows the user role to see that there is data, but prevents working with it. • Hidden access prevents the user role from even seeing that the data is in the system.

Step 3 Security For the calculated data that displays in Step 3, you also set security on the User Roles form. Full, Inquiry, or Deny access is set on AGG.DATA*GETIT. To set field-level security for Step 3 data, click the Field link.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 404 Chapter 17 Using Reports

The Field Security form displays. Use the toggle switch to enable or restrict access to each field.

You can also enable or restrict access to the expanded data items that display after you set the date rage.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 405 Chapter 17 Using Reports

For example, Invoiced items include Billing Format, Invoiced As and Detail Code. You must set security for each of these items. The Invoiced items in Step 3 include only amounts from billing vouchers that are associated with an employee ID. Miscellaneous charges (for example, delivery fees) are not included on the reports. If miscellaneous or bundled charges are included, client reports will not balance back to the invoice.

Note: Note that if a client changes billing format mid-year, Data Retriever shows the billing breakout formats. Once the data cube is rebuilt, the data will only break out based upon the current billing format.

Save Report Template by User Type When you save a report template in Data Retriever, you can specify which type of user can have access to it. 1. From the Actions menu in Data Retriever, select Save Report Template. 2. Enable the option to save the report for yourself only or select a user type to associate with the report: • Service Providers - only Service Providers can see the report. • Worksite Managers - Service Providers and Worksite Managers can see the report. • Trusted Advisers - Service Providers, Worksite Managers, and Trusted Advisers can see the report.

Client Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 406 Chapter 17 Using Reports

  1. Click Save. To edit an existing report template, load the template, make changes, and save it. Be sure to select Replace the existing report?. To create a new report template from an existing one, load the template, make changes, and save it. Be sure to change the Description of Report and clear the option to Replace the existing report?.

The report columns are: • Grade: The pay grade code. • Description: The pay grade code description. • Minimum Annual Pay: The minimum annual pay rate for that pay grade. • Minimum Hourly Pay: The minimum hourly pay rate for that pay grade. • Maximum Annual Pay: The maximum annual pay rate for that pay grade. • Maximum Hourly Pay: The maximum hourly pay rate for that pay grade. • Midpoint: The midpoint pay based on minimum and maximum pay rates. • Percent Rage: The midpoint percent.

Transfer Downloads File to PC Use this form to download files to a user’s system, from the server’s download directory generated by the PrismHR system.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

Note: A warning message displays on the User Role form if a user,

 •   who has access to the Transfer Downloads File to PC menu is switched to a new User Role, BUT
 •   is also restricted from clients via client access group security.
 The message states:
 The user role <new user role> has access to the Transfer Downloads File to PC menu. This form does not
 utilize client access group security so it is possible that <user id> maybe be able to download files that
 contain data they should not be allowed to access. Do you wish to continue?
 •   If Yes is selected, then the user record is saved, and the screen is cleared.
 •   If No is selected, then the user record is not saved, and the data is left as is on the screen.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu > Operations|Action > Transfer Downloads File to PC.

To transfer a Download File to a user’s PC: 1. Click the Filename link. A separate Select File window opens. 2. Scroll and select the Download File that you want to download from the list. You can also search for the Download File using Filename Description and Date. The File View shows the first 15 lines of the selected Download File. 3. Click Download.

Intended Audience This guide is intended for users who are involved in client and employee administration. Unless you have permission to access system-level features, you cannot view them or make changes. To effectively use this guide, you must also have background knowledge of systems, payroll, benefits, and human resources.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 11 Chapter 1 Employer-Level Setup

Chapter 1 Employer-Level Setup In PrismHR, employers can include your organization, divisions of your organization, and client companies that manage themselves to some extent. You must set up employers as part of your basic system configuration.

Maintaining Employer Details You can maintain employer information using the Employer Details form. Use this form to update federal and state tax processing settings, local tax information, and other important employer data.

Setting Employer Details Use the Employer Details panel to create new employer IDs and add basic employer information, or to edit information for an existing Employer ID.

Setup Procedure

Note about deleting employers Note: If you try to delete an employer who has active employees or employees on leave, the following confirmation message displays:

Do the following if this message displays: • Click Yes to permanently delete the employer record. The Employer Details form clears. • Click No to close the message and return to the form. The employer data remains on the form.

Changing Employer IDs Use the Change Employer IDs for a Client form to change employer IDs for pre-existing clients. You must rebuild registers after running this process.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To change employer IDs for preexisting clients: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Employer|Action, select Change Employer IDs for a Client. 3. Complete these fields as required:

 Field                                     Description
 Client ID                                 The client ID of the client whose status is to be changed.
 To Employer ID                            The employer ID to which historical tax registers will be moved.
  1. Click Update.
  2. Click Yes when prompted for confirmation. A message notifies you when the change is complete.
  3. Rebuild the registers. See the “Tax Register Rebuild” documentation for details.

Setting State Tax Information Maintain state tax information in Employer Details with the State Tax panel.

To set up tax information: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details and expand the State Tax panel. 3. In the State Tax ID Numbers table, set tax information for each state where an employer does business:

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 16 Chapter 1 Employer-Level Setup

Note: SUTA Rpt Entity and SIT Rpt Entity must have equivalent values. You cannot set one to report at the client level and the other to report on the employer level.

Field Description State Two-character postal code. States will display in alphabetical order once any changes are saved. State Name The full state name displays when you enter a postal code. For example, enter CA in the State field and the State Name of California displays. Licensed Select Yes if an employer is a licensed PEO in a specific state. Taxpayer ID/UI Account Employer Taxpayer ID number for a specific state. Enter APPLIED FOR if you are awaiting an ID. State Tax Nbr State number for reporting income taxes that appears on W-2 forms. Mag Authority ID Magnetic authorization number for a state. Misc ID1 • California: Enter the Wage Plan Code. • Iowa: Enter the 3 digit suffix location number. If an employer has multiple locations that requires the 3-digit suffix for the location they are filing from, they should enter the 3-digit suffix location number here to capture the employer 9 digit FEIN along with the 3 digit suffix when generating the Iowa New Hire Report. Iowa New Hire reporting file will be rejected if the FEIN is not 12 digits long. • New Jersey: Enter the Disability Insurance Private Plan Number. Misc ID2 • New Jersey: Enter the FLIPP Number. • Iowa: Enter the 8-digit Business E-File Number provided by the state. GL Segment EEHL Enter substitute data for the Employee Home Location ID.

SUTA Rpt Entity Select whether the PEO or Company (client) is the designated SUTA reporting entity in the state. This overrides the setting on the State Rules form. Rpt Entity Eff. Date Effective date for the SUTA reporting entity. SIT Rpt Entity Select whether the Employer or Client is the designated income tax reporting entity for the state. If you do not select an entity, or if the reporting date is in the future, state income tax accrues and reports according to any Tax Deduction settings. If no Tax Deduction settings exist, state income tax accrues and reports under the employer, by default.

Updates to Form W-2 build The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will now be pulled from the Client Details form or the Employer Details form based on the tax deduction code, unless an override exists on the Employer Details form on the SIT Rpt Entity field for that state under the State Tax section. The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will be: • Client State Tax ID when: • Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Client • Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Client

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 18 Chapter 1 Employer-Level Setup

• Employer State Tax ID: • Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Employer • Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Employer Note: If the State Tax ID is not available on the corresponding reporting entity, the Form W-2 will not be built, and an error will appear in the W2 Error Report stating State Employer ID not found for Client # for State XX OR State Employer ID not found for Employer for State XX

Setting Online Access for Form W-2 Set up employer online access to Form W-2, Form W-2c, and Form 1099 using the Form W-2/1099 Initialization Audit & Control panel under Employer Details.

To configure online tax form access: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details and expand the Form W-2/1099 Initialization Audit & Control panel. 3. Fill out these fields as required:

Field Description Year Enter a tax year. The grid displays the Last Init Date, Last Init Time, and Last Init By fields. Use the Create Employee W-2 Forms (found under Work Centers > W-2 Processing) to perform these initializations. Allow Web Access Provide web access permissions for Form W-2. Options include: l Yes - All employees can access Forms W-2 for the year. l No - No employees can access Forms W-2 for the year. l Electronic - Employees who elected early online access to their W-2s can see the forms. This is controlled by the Electronic Form W-2 option in the Employee Details > Tax tab.

                                           To see which employees have elected electronic Form W-2 access, use
                                           the Client Master report or the Employee General Information report in
                                           Report Center.

These steps make Form W-2c/Form 1099 accessible from both Employee Details and Employee Portal (EP): 1099 Web Access Set to Yes to allow employees to view and print Form 1099. W2C Web Access Set to Yes to allow employees to view and print Form W-2c.

Processing Form W-2 with a Common Pay Agent Common Pay Agents provide FICA consolidation and also handle income tax withholding, reporting and remittance under their Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN). Common Pay Agent Name Control is not applied to Form W-2’s built by Client Federal Entity Registers for SBEA W2 Reporting. Common Pay Agent PDF only applies to 2023 and forward. If an employer has registered with the IRS as using a common pay agent for remittance of federal withholding taxes, use the Employer Details > Common Pay Agent for Form W-2 Processing panel to identify the common pay agent contracted to process W-2s.

To set Common Pay Agent details: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details and expand the Common Pay Agent for Form W-2 Processing panel. 3. Complete the following fields:

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 20 Chapter 1 Employer-Level Setup

Field Name Description Year The year for which this setup will apply. For example, for 2023 you have a common pay agent and reporting option is Agent only. For every year starting 2023 the Form W-2 or Form W-2c will report only the common pay agent information until you change it. If you make any changes later, you will need to add a line, enter the year and make the changes. For example, for 2025 you change the Report Option to Agent|Employer. You would then see the Common Pay Agent information reported on the Form W-2 only for 2023, 2024, and in 2025 you would see the Agent|Employer information reported on the Form W-2 or Form W-2c. (It is not required to add the 2024 record for common pay agent to continue) Agent FEIN Enter the common pay agent’s FEIN (or Federal Tax Identification Number). FEIN format must be either ##-####### (two digits, dash, seven digits) or ######### (nine consecutive digits). Agent Name The name of the agent. Address The street address of the agent. City The city of the agent. State The two digit state of the agent. Zip The zip code of the agent. Report Option Select is the default option which will only report the employer information. You need to select one of the following options: • Agent|Employer - Select this option to report the Common Pay Agent and Agent for {Employer}. • Agent only - Select this option to report only the Common Pay Agent.

                                           Note: To display Common Pay Agent information on the Form
                                           W-2 or Form W-2c PDF, even if this was used in the past, you
                                           will need to select a Report Option and Save the changes on the
                                           Employer Details form.

Panel Description Miscellaneous override rates Enter the miscellaneous override rates for employer-paid taxes. If these fields are left blank, the system uses the default rate. • Enter the State Misc1 Rate (Tax ID 26). • Enter the State Misc2 Rate only to set employer tax rates for Vermont Childcare Employee Tax Rate (Tax Code 48-28). If no tax rate is entered for the employer, but a tax rate is entered for the employee using the State Misc 2 Employee Rate field below, you will see the full amount for the employer calculated at 0.44%. The employee tax rate below does not offset the employer tax rate here. So, you must enter the tax rates for both the employer and the employee in this form if using overrides. • Enter the State Misc3 Rate field to set employer tax rates for tax codes 22-41 (Massachusetts), 48-41 (Washington) and 51-41 (Wyoming). For example, you can increase the tax rate paid by the employer. • Enter the State Misc4 Rate here, for example for tax code 24-54 (Minnesota).

State Misc 2 Employee Rate Enter the State Misc 2 Employee Rate only to set employee tax rates for Vermont Childcare Employee Tax Rate (Tax Code 48-27). The employer tax rate above does not offset the employer tax rate here. So, you must enter the tax rates for both the employer and the employee in this form if using overrides. State Misc 3 Employee Rate Enter the State Misc 3 Employee Rate to set employee tax rates for codes 22-40 (Massachusetts) or 48-40 (Washington) paid family medical leave. For example, you can decrease the tax rate paid by employees. Note: If you adjust State Misc2 Rate or State Misc 2 Employee Rate and State Misc3 Rate or State Misc 3 Employee Rate, you must use both the corresponding fields. Do not assume one field will adjust automatically when a change is made to the other field.

Maintaining Employee Lock-in Information Employers and employees might receive a lock-in letter from the IRS if they are in debt to that organization. This letter states how much withholding allowance the employee can claim — typically zero. Employees who have a lock-in letter cannot change their allowances in Employee Portal. A lock-in can also be set for a particular state. When an IRS employee lock-in is set, any users who are not Service Providers will see the following message when they try to change their withholding amount: Note: Federal taxes for this employee are locked and may not be changed.

Lock-In Auth User Click the link and select a service provider who is authorized to change the withholding amount for an employee who has a lock-in letter. The system displays the ID and username of the service provider in the list. • Click + in the header or > in any row to display an additional row where you can select another service provider. • Click x to delete a service provider from the list.

Using the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool You can use the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool to quickly import a list of employees to transfer to new clients. Note the following: • This tool is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Mass Employee Transfer Import form. • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Mass Employee Transfer Import form displays the form in read- only format. • Users who do not have access to a particular client as configured in Client Access Groups cannot transfer employees into or out of the client using the Mass Employee Transfer Import form. • This process accomplishes the same results as executing the standard employee transfer process using the Transfer Employee to New Client form. (See Transferring Employees to New Clients.) The Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool is available from the Operations|Import Processing menu in the Back

Office . For example, the following form displays after you access the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool:

Before you can upload and import data, your source file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. When you open the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool form, the required file layout displays. The layout must match the requirements for number and order of columns, category descriptions, and the required fields.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 34 Chapter 1 Employer-Level Setup

In addition, you can use the sample header file before importing to avoid manually creating an import file that matches the import template type. Note the following when using a comma (,) in a description in your import file: • If you include a comma in a description field using the .csv file format, you must enclose the item in double quotes. For example, “Manager, Admin.” • If you include a comma in a description field using the .txt file format, no extra formatting is necessary.

Using the Sample Header File Before starting the import process, you can first download a sample header file by clicking that link on the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool form. For example:

  1. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.
  2. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.
  3. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File will display in the File Upload dialog box.
  4. Click Start Upload to upload the file.
  5. Click Close on the File Upload dialog box.
  6. The uploaded Import File name will display under the File Name field on the form. The content of the file will display under File Content tab. Errors, if any, will display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process. While processing the uploaded file, the following validation occurs: • If any mandatory field is missing from the file, the system displays an error message, “ is a required field.” • If the system does not associate the Employee ID with the From Client field, it displays an error message, “Employee not located in client .” • If the values in the Pay Group, To Retire Plan, To Position, and To Location fields are not valid for the To Client record, then the system displays an error message, “Record . is not on file in <field’s filename>.” • In the Termination Reason field, the system identifies a valid value only if the REASON.CODES contain “Termination.” If you provide any other value, the system displays an error message, “ is not a valid Term Reason Code.”
  7. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR. After the import finishes, the following occurs: • If Transfer YTD Check Stubs is enabled, the program transfers the YTD check stubs. • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is enabled, the program terminates the employee on the original client using the corresponding Termination Date and Termination Reason from the upload file. • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is disabled, the program does not terminate the employee on the original client. • If Terminate Benefit Coverage Today is enabled, the program terminates the employee’s benefit coverage. • If the uploaded file contains a mix of employees who are successfully validated and employees that fail the validations, those employees that are successfully validated are transferred appropriately and the employees that fail validation are documented in the error log and are not transferred or terminated.
  8. Click Report to view the transaction report. This report contains the following information: • Successfully transferred employees display “Success” in the Import Status column. • Employees that failed validation and could not be transferred display “Skipped” in the Import Status column. The “Comments” column for the failed transfer employees displays the error message for whichever failed validation event prevented the transfer.

  1. Click Generate File. A File Generation Process window opens. In case of any error, redo the field entries.
  2. Click Close. The data to be exported populates in the Preview section, which displays a maximum of 100 records. A message prompts you the total number of records.
  3. Click Download File to download the .csv file to a local system. Note: This export file contains one total line for each company, employer, employee, and W/C class code combination within the entered pay date range. Also, the check date that displays is the last check date for that employee.
  4. Click Clear to clear the form at any time.

Creating the ESAC Client Export The Employer Services Assurance Corporation (ESAC) is an independent non-profit corporation; it is the official accreditation and financial assurance organization for the PEO industry. The ESAC Client Export process creates a file that contains a list of clients for a specified PEO, which can be sent to ESAC for accreditation verification.

Note: This process does not use Client Access Group security.

To access this form, click the Back Office menu. Under Operations|Action, select ESAC Client Export.

To download the ESAC Client export: 1. Complete the following fields:

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 41 Chapter 1 Employer-Level Setup

 Field                                                 Description
 Start Date                                            Enter the start date of the export period.
 End Date                                              Enter the end date of the export period.

                                                       Note: The End Date must be after the Start Date and
                                                       must be the last day of the month.
 Include PEO Clients Only?                             This field is optional. Select one of the following options
                                                       from the drop-down:
                                                            •   Yes (Default) - Only PEO clients are included in
                                                                the export.
                                                            •   No - All clients
 Exclude Clients Terminated                            Enter the number of months in numbers. You can enter
                                                       any number of months. This will exclude clients who
                                                       were terminated the specified number of months
                                                       before the Start Date.
  1. Click Build. The ESAC Client Export processing starts. If errors occur, fix them and then rebuild the export file.
  2. When the process is complete, click Close to return to the ESAC Client Export page
  3. Click the Download link to download the export file.
  4. Click Clear to clear the screen at any time.

Exporting Retirement Contributions An export file contains data extracted from the system, often to provide to another party. The Retirement Exports form offers multiple retirement export types from a single page. These export types are shown in the Vendor/Template field. When you select an export type from the list, the fields relevant to that type display. Once the export file is generated, you can export it to your computer.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form. If client selection is left blank to run for all clients, only clients to which you have access are available.

To access the form, click Back Office. Under Operations|Action, click Retirement Exports.

To generate a retirement export: 1. Select a Vendor/Template from the following options, and complete the fields as required: • 401(k) Extended Download (page 44) • ADP (page 46) • Anico (page 46) • Boston Land (page 47)

401(k) Extended Download Use this form to generate a retirement export that shows both eligible and participants for 401(k) plans. This is not related to a 401(k) TPA, but is a generic export. See also: Exporting Retirement Contributions. To set up the 401(k) Extended Download retirement export, complete the following fields as required:

Field Description File Type The retirement export file type. This is read-only field. This is Generic 401(k) Download. File Format Select the appropriate file format from the following: • Eligible and Participants (Default) - This will return hours and pay values for everyone for the full Pay Date Range entered. • Participants Only - This will return hours and pay values only from Election Effective Date.

                                  Note: If you have employees that are new to the plan within the
                                  year and your carrier needs information for the full year even if the
                                  employee did not participate the full year, then you use the Eligible
                                  and Participants file format for the full year date range because if
                                  you use the Participants Only file format, it only returns pay and
                                  hours since election started.

Plan ID Enter the retirement plan ID, or click the Plan ID link to select the retirement plan from the Select Plan selector.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 44 Chapter 1 Employer-Level Setup

Field Description Start Pay Date Enter the starting pay date for which this download will be generated. End Pay Date Enter the ending pay date for which this download will be generated. Client ID This field is optional. If you want to limit this download to a specific client, enter that client ID, or click the Client ID link and select the client from the Select Client selector. Leave it blank to select all clients. Employer ID This field is optional. If you want to limit this download to a specific employer, enter that employer ID, or click the Employer ID link and select the employer from the Select employer selector. Leave it blank to select all employers. Service Type If you would like to limit the download to a specific employer type, select one of the following options from the drop-down: • All - This means include all employer types • Administrative Services Only • Professional Employer Services • Payroll Processing • Admin Services/Alt Billing Only • Corporate Payroll • HR Services (No Payroll)

Combine First and Last This is a check box. Use it in one of the following ways: Name into One Column • Checked - if you want the first and last name to be combined into one column.- This is the default option. • Unchecked - if you do not want the first and last name to be combined into one column. Exclude 1099 Employees This is a check box. Use it in one of the following ways: • Checked - if you want to exclude 1099 employees from the download. This is the default option. • Unchecked - if you want to include 1099 employees from the download.

The EMPLOYEE TOTAL would include these. • SUCCESSOR RETIREMENT DEFERRAL AMOUNT • SUCCESSOR CATCH-UP DEFERRAL AMOUNT • SUCCESSOR ROTH DEFERRAL AMOUNT • SUCCESSOR ROTH CATCH-UP DEFERRAL AMOUNT Status Codes This field is optional. Leave this field blank to include all employee statuses in the retirement export file. Periodic JSON Export This feature helps customers and Support teams quickly locate and re-download History previously generated Periodic Tax JSON/PTS export files, reducing the likelihood that processed files are lost. Previously, you had to navigate to Transfer Downloads to PC to retrieve periodic JSON exports. The export history is now available directly on the Periodic Tax JSON Export form. If no historical exports exist, the Periodic JSON Export History subsection displays an empty state message stating No export history found. This subsection renders a table with the following columns (left to right) : • Date/Time - The date and time the file was generated. • Created By - The username of the user who initiated the build. • File Name - The JSON file name is displayed as a hyperlink. Rebuilding the Tax Journal When PrismHR posts a payroll, it collects voucher data and writes it to the TAX.JOURNAL file. The Mastertax PTS export file is built based on values stored in the TAX.JOURNAL file. The final step of these processes is archiving voucher data from the file, so that voucher data is not reported twice. It is possible that either of these files can become corrupted, so you need to rebuild this file using historical payroll data. The Rebuild Tax Journal file completes this process.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To rebuild the journal: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Employer|Action, select Rebuild Tax Journal file. 3. Complete these fields as required.

There can be various reasons for this, including: • periodic review • concerns or issues regarding a particular form, or • the form was filled out before supporting features were fully integrated into PrismHR. For example, you might need to locate forms associated with: • Portland Metro (Oregon) SHS tax • Multnomah County (Oregon) Preschool For All tax • Colorado Annual Withholding Allowance elections, as specified on state form DR 0004 Document Management provides search and filter options for the documents stored in your system, including employee tax forms.

Building the Reconciliation Tax Summary The MasterTax RTS (Reconciliation Tax Summary) file build process reviews the various tax registers and generates a file in a specific format for a third party vendor called MasterTax. Run this process quarterly and use it to reconcile the check amounts that were imported throughout the previous three months. Now, positive and or negative adjustments made in the grid in the FUTA Credit Adjustment Entry form displays on the MasterTax Reconciliation Tax Summary (RTS). The values entered in the grid adjust the state XX-17 total YTD value in the RTS. This will not require a register rebuild, instead when you run the RTS, any value in the grid will offset either the E or F code record based on the Employet and/or Client setup. Adjustments to the xx-17 record will be saved and stored to the Futa Credit Adjustment Entry grid for each employee. The 501 record is reduced in statistic four (which is the employee count) by any employee in which an adjustment reduces their FUTA taxable wages to 0 for the state, or increase the 501 record by any employee in which an adjustment adds fUTA taxable wages that were not originally to be reported. There are multiple versions of this form as well as a NON SBEA and SBEA build that look to different tax registers when generating the values on the file. These build types are controlled by the MasterTax Interface parameter form.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To build the RTS file: 1. On the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing > File Exports > Mastertax RTS File Build. 2. Creating Payroll Tax Summary Export Files The MasterTax PTS (Payroll Tax Summary) File Build transmits data from the TAX.JOURNAL file to MasterTax. MasterTax is a third party vendor that handles the tax payments for many service providers. This file is typically generated once per day and uploaded to MasterTax. There are multiple versions of the PTS file. There are also SBEA and Non-SBEA versions of this file, depending on the settings on the MasterTax

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 105 Chapter 3 MasterTax Processing

Interface Parameter form. A process lock on the TAX.JOURNAL file prevents multiple users from running this file concurrently. In the past, PTS files contained deleted data. PTS files created out of PrismHR archive that data for 45 days, and then it is deleted.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To build the PTS file: 1. On the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing. > File Exports > Mastertax PTS File Build. 2. Select Build File by: • All Clients and Employers – When this option is selected, the Employer and Client options are disabled. • Employer – Click the Employer link and select an employer from the list that displays. • Client – Click the Client link and select a client from the list that displays. You can search by Client ID/Name, Service Type, Employer, or Status. • Re-process Previous File – Select a file from the drop-down. This regenerates data that was contained on that file using updated parameters from the MasterTax Interface Parameters form. 3. Click Build to generate the PTS file. A progress window opens and displays process steps and a date/time stamp. When the build is finished, it automatically downloads to a local drive and appears on the PTS File History list. If a PTS file is already being generated, a process lock is applied to prevent others from attempting builds. You can clear the lock, but it should be cleared only if the process is frozen. 4. Check the MasterTax version by expanding the Configuration Information panel. 5. Check the PTS File History for a build status. The system displays a time and date stamp, the user who ran the build, and what the file name is. 6. Click a File Name link to download that file. You can also view an audit report by clicking View next to one of the file names.

MasterTax PTS Clear Lock A process lock is applied to the Mastertax PTS (Payroll Tax Summary) file during its build process to prevent other users from attempting builds. However, it is possible that the process that generates the file can hang, preventing generation of a new file. This function removes the lock on the PTS generation process so the file can be recreated.

To remove the lock on a PTS file being built: 1. From the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing. 2. From File Exports, click Mastertax PTS File Build.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 106 Chapter 3 MasterTax Processing

  1. Click Build. If a PTS build is already in progress, this message displays:

  2. Click Yes to remove the lock.

  3. Click Build again to start the build process.

Government Exports This section explains how to build quarterly government export files.

BLS Multiple Worksite Electronic File Use this form to generate the BLS-3020 electronic file to be submitted to the federal or state Bureau of Labor Statistics. BLS Reports provide analytical information related to the labor force, consumer spending, earnings, and work injuries and illnesses. Typically, reports contain a few pages of written analysis followed by statistical tables, which allow you to gather detailed information on economic conditions. Most reports have an annual cycle.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group security.

To access this form, in the Work Centers panel, under Tax, click Quarterly Tax Processing. Under Government Exports, click BLS Multiple Worksite Electronic File.

                                 •    ASO

  5. The report is downloaded on your system in a .txt format.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 139 Chapter 5 W-2 Processing

Chapter 5 W-2 Processing The W-2 processing options provide everything needed in the life cycle of W-2 processing, from setup to printing. In addition, these menus provide the flexibility to perform small and specific adjustment processes, as well as to identify larger tax issues and use automated adjustment processes to correct them. The W-2 processes provide a straightforward user experience to handle the myriad of complicated tax-related processes and calculations needed to assure that you calculate and report your employees’ and clients’ taxes. A specific focus is on turning large, time-consuming projects into more automated procedures that require less time to complete. The options available in the W-2 Processing work center are organized under the following headings: • W-2 Processes • EFW2 Exports • 3rd Party W-2 Export Files • W-2 Reporting • W-2 Setup Reports • W-2 Setup • Parameter Setup • W-2 Printing

W-2 Processing Overview This section gives a summary overview of W-2 processing. It is best practice to read it completely before you begin.

W-2 Setup There are several setup forms for processing W2s.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 140 Chapter 5 W-2 Processing

Use this form To do this EFW2 Submitter Maintenance Specify where PEOs report their W-2 data on the electronic files they send to various government agencies. The process of generating the W-2 data starts with the Create Employee W-2 Forms option, which creates the W-2 data and registers. You can specify whether to create W-2 data for all employers or for selected employers. EFW2 Local List Maintenance Create and maintain local EFW2 codes. You then assign these codes to the relevant local tax authorities. When the W-2 data is created, the system places the code on the employee’s W-2 register and then reads it when building the EFW2 files for upload to the various local governments. Benefits W-2 Reporting Setup Specify the types of benefit plans that need to be reported on the W-2 in Box 12. Global W-2 Reporting Setup Set up the reporting codes for external benefit plans. For example, assume that the employee health insurance that needs to be in Box 12 is not a PEO based plan and is calculated outside of the PrismHR system. In this scenario the benefit plan type codes are set up so that the PEO can enter the premium amounts either manually or via an import. Client W2 Reporting Setup Creates an exclusion for clients to report their benefits in Box 12. Consult PrismHR Support before using this functionality.

W2 Processing The W2 Processing menu is where you build and verify the W-2 registers.

Use this form To do this Create Employee W-2 Forms Build the registers that subsequent steps in the W-2 process will use. Update W2 Record Manually add or edit data to the W-2 register. This form is also commonly used to verify the data contained in the employee’s W2 register. The system populates this form with the W2 register data that was created using the Create W2 form.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 141 Chapter 5 W-2 Processing

Use this form To do this Employee W2 Benefits Entry Manually enter external benefit premiums on an employee by employee basis. enter the benefit premium amounts monthly. l You can create an individual record for each month using a multi-value grid where you enter each month’s premium at one time. l You can also enter a year’s worth of premiums under one month to get total premiums for a year. Employee W2 Benefit Import Import data for external benefit premiums instead of entering it manually. This is typically used for a client who has external benefits and gets the information from a benefits administrator. Employee W2 Benefits Inquiry Look at the employee’s W2 benefit data. Typically you would run the employee W2 Benefit Report, which provides the same data for a client instead of an employee.

Electronic Files The system provides a variety of electronic file formats that you can generate for federal, state, and local governments. You can also generate electronic files for third party printers such as CIC and Solv. The files that the system generates are imported into one of the third party providers, who then print, stuff, and send them to PEOs to distribute to their employees.

Use this form To do this EFW2 Download Build the EFW2 data. When you open this form, you are prompted to specify whether it is for the federal, state, or local government. Create BDS/IBF W2 Download Send data to SOLV so that they can print, stuff, and mail the employee W-2 forms. Create CIC W2 Download Send the W2 information to CIC so that they can print, stuff, and mail the employee W-2 forms. CIC PR Download Provide additional information required for Puerto Rico employees. CIC Virgin Islands Download Provide additional information required for Virgin IIsland employees.

Handling Errors Since W-2 processing runs as a background task, the system provides various ways to inform you when errors occur, even if you are working on another task during W-2 processing. The type of notification method used depends on the severity of the errors that are encountered.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 142 Chapter 5 W-2 Processing

Pre-Processing Errors When you select Create Employee W-2 forms, the system runs a quick check and displays a list of errors that you must address before processing can occur. When processing is complete, you receive an email notification.

Non Fatal errors These are errors on employee related data or setup parameters. The system saves errors in the error log.

Fatal errors Fatal errors stop the W-2 build process. When a fatal occurs during processing, you receive an email notification. To see the error, open the error log from the Create W2 form.

Error Report The system records errors that are detected during W-2 processing in an error report that it generates when the build process is complete. You can see the errors by opening the W-2 Processing Status form. The error report shows the following information: • Number of errors found so far • Number of W-2s generated so far

Processing Flow for Errors The following charts show the process flow for each type of error.

Creating the Employee SSN Verification Service Download The Employee SSN Verification Service Download builds an electronic file that you can upload to the Social Security Number Verification Service, which verifies names and SSNs before generating Employee W-2s. It also

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 144 Chapter 5 W-2 Processing

updates employee records with an Eligibility Verification System (EVS) date. Once this process is complete, you are notified with a pop-up window.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access this form and run the report: 1. Open the Work Centers menu and select Work Centers|Tax > W-2 Processing. 2. Under W-2 Processes, select Create Employee SSN Verification Download. 3. Complete these fields as required:

 Field              Description
 Requester ID ID of the person requesting the file. This required field is limited to 4 alphanumeric
              characters (no special characters).
 Starting           Starting date of the date range for creating this file.
 Report Date
 Ending             Ending date of date range for creating this file.
 Report Date
 Client ID          Click the link to display a list from which you can select a specific client for the
                    report. If left blank, the file includes all clients.
  1. Click Generate File. If errors occur, fix them and then regenerate the download.
  2. Click Close to download the file. If you return to the Create Employee SSN Verification Download screen, a Re-Download Verification File option is available.

Clearing Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates Use this process to reset the Employment Verification Service (EVS) reporting dates. These Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates are used when processing the EVS download file that is generated from the W-2 work center (W-2 Processing > W-2 Processes > Create Employee SSN Verification Download). If a reporting date is entered in the Employment Verification Service (EVS) reporting date, the employee is not shown on the EVS download. This process resets the EVS reporting dates so that the employees will be shown on the EVS download file.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under the heading Complianceclick on New Hire and Termination Reporting. Then under the heading Reporting Date Overrides click on Clear Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 145 Chapter 5 W-2 Processing

To clear employee SSN verification reporting dates: 1. Enter Starting EVS Report Date which is a mandatory date field. Please enter the date from which you want to clear the employee SSN Verification reporting. 2. Enter Ending EVS Report Date which is a mandatory date field. Please enter the date upto which you want to clear the employee SSN Verification reporting. 3. Company ID is an optional free text field. Leave it blank to select all clients. 4. Click Process. A progress window opens that shows the number of records read and the number of records cleared and notifies you when the process is complete. The Close and Report buttons remain disabled while the report is being generated. 5. Click Close to close the window. 6. Click Report to display the Job Control Status Report window. 7. In the Job Control Status Report window, click the XLS link to download the report.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 165 Chapter 5 W-2 Processing

Field Description status of a file, click the status of that file to open the Edit EFW2C File Status form for that file and edit the status. For example, once you have submitted an unsent file to the Social Security Administration, you may want to change the status of that file from Unsent to In Process. A file will have one of the following statuses: • Unsent - Once you click Create Export File to generate a file for a batch for the first time for an original EFW2C submission, it will be listed as Unsent in the grid with a new file name. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you cannot edit information for any employee on this file. • In Process - A file that has been submitted to the Social Security Administration but is yet to be accepted by them. You can enter the Receipt ID received for that file submission on the Edit EFW2C File Status form for that file. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you cannot edit information for any employee on this file. • Accepted - A file that was submitted successfully to the Social Security Administration and accepted by them. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you cannot edit information for any employee on this file. • Rejected - A file that was rejected upon submission by the Social Security Administration. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can edit information for any employee on this file, and the values will be pre-populated for that employee. • Regenerate - A file that was regenerated prior to submission to the Social Security Administration. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can edit information for any employee on this file, and the values will be pre-populated for that employee. • Cancelled - A generated file that is not currently under submission the Social Security Administration and cancelled owing to some reason. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can edit information for any employee on this file. However,

Running the W-2 Reconciliation Report Social Security’s Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) program limits the amount of earnings subject to taxation for a given year. The W-2 Reconciliation Report compares OASDI with Medicare to determine whether the wage data processed by the SSA was less than the amount reported to the IRS. If the wage data is different, the SSA assumes that the processed earnings are incorrect.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

Maintaining Local EFW2 Codes EFW2 is a type of format that employers and payroll providers use to report W2 forms electronically with the SSA (Social Security Administration) and state and local governments. Each year, the SSA updates the W-2 electronic filing instructions through the EFW2 specification. Use the Local EFW2 form to generate and store local EFW2 codes. These codes are assigned to the tax authority for local government and used to build the W-2 registers. The codes are then used in the EFW2 build process to denote which taxes for the applicable tax authority should be included on the EFW2 that is sent to the local government. You can view, add, and delete codes.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To maintain local EFW2 codes: 1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > W-2 Processing > W-2 Setup > Parameter Setup > Local EFW2 Codes. The Local EFW2 Codes page opens. One column shows the list of codes and the other column shows the description of each code. 2. Select one of the following options: • To insert a blank row above the selected row, click > at the beginning of the row and then enter the code and description in the new row. • To insert a blank row at the end of the list, click + at the top of the list and then enter the code and description in the new row. • To delete a code, click X at the beginning of the row. The system deletes the row. 3. Click Save.

1099 Processes This section explains how to perform 1099 processing tasks.

Adding or Updating an Employee 1099 Record Use the Add/Update 1099 form to add or update an employee’s 1099 record.

Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To add or update an employee 1099: 1. On the Work Centers panel, select Tax > 1099 Processing > 1099 Processes > Add/Update Employee 1099. 2. In the Add/Update Employee 1099 section, complete these fields as required.

 Field                            Description
 Employer                         The Employer ID for whom to generate 1099 data.
 SBEA Entity                      An optional field that is available only when Build W2s from Client
                                  Federal Tax Registers is checked in the Global Configuration form. This is
                                  a client federal entity who represents a client of your organization that is
                                  included in SBEA reporting.
 Employee                         The employee whose record is being added or updated.
                                  If a 1099 record is found for the specified employer ID and employee ID,
                                  the record is displayed so that you can make the necessary changes.

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 196 Chapter 6 1099 Processing

                                  If a 1099 record is not found for the specified employer ID and employee

                                  before the current year.

                                  when you make manual changes to the record.

  1. In the Federal Form 1099 Misc section, add or change these fields as necessary.

    Field Description Recipient’s TIN The recipient’s tax ID number. Recipient’s Name The recipient’s name. Employee Address The employee’s street address. City, State & Zip The employee’s city, state, and zip code. Non-employee Compensation Whether the record was manually updated. The system selects this option when you make manual changes to the record. Federal Income Tax Withheld The amount of federal income tax withheld. Federal Income Taxable The amount of taxable federal income. State Tax Withheld The amount of state tax withheld. State Income The amount of state income. State/Payer’s State No. The number for the state or payer.

  3. Click Delete to delete the record.

Viewing the 1099 Record Change Log The 1099 Record Change Log captures changes made to a Form 1099 record. Display the change log by opening the Actions menu on the Add/Update Employee 1099 form and selecting Change Log. The change log displays information about each change in the following columns: • Field Name • Date • Time • Port • User • Changed From • Changed To

1099 Reporting This section explains how to perform 1099 reporting tasks.

Running the 1099 Forms Report The 1099 Forms report shows the data that was included on the employee 1099 forms that were generated for a specified tax year, employer, and zip code.

Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To run the 1099 Forms report: 1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > 1099 Processing > 1099 Reporting > 1099 Forms Report. 2. Select a tax year and employer ID and enter a zip code. If you leave the zip code blank, the report includes all zip codes for the selected tax year and employer. 3. Click Process. The report contains columns that display the following information:

Employer Administration Guide © 2026 PrismHR 201 Chapter 6 1099 Processing

• Employee Name • ID • Social Security Number • Employer • Company • Zip Code • Earnings You can navigate through the report by going to the next or previous page, going to a specific page, or searching for specific information. In the Actions list, you can print the report, convert it to PDF, or print specific PDF pages. You can also convert the report to XLS format by clicking the XLS link.

Printing Employee 1099 Forms Use this form to print 1099 forms for employees. Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form. To access this form, click Work Centers. In the Work Centers|Tax section, click 1099 Processing, then click Print Employee 1099 Forms.

To print 1099 forms for employees: 1. Complete the following fields:

Field Name Description Tax Year Select the tax year to be processed. The default tax year is the prior year based upon today’s date. Create Forms By Select an option if you want to generate 1099 forms for employees: • Employer: Select this option if you want to print Forms 1099 for employees for certain employers. Enter the employer IDs here or click the Employer ID link and select the employers from the Select Employer dialog box. • Client: Select this option if you want to print Forms 1099 for employees for certain clients. Enter the client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select the clients from the Select Clients list. • All (default) Employees This field is optional. If you want to restrict generating 1099 forms for certain employees, enter them here or click the Employee ID link and select them from the Select Employee list. Leave this field blank to generate 1099 forms for all as per selection above.

Chapter 1 Activating Onboarding The following are required system and client-level settings to activate Onboarding.

Enabling Onboarding To enable Onboarding, use the Global Configuration form in PrismHR. 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Global Configuration. The Global Configuration form opens. 3. Select Enable Onboarding. 4. Click Save.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 8 Chapter 2 Configuring System Settings

Chapter 2 Configuring System Settings The following are required system-level settings in Onboarding.

Setting Up Approval Policies Set up the I-9 Section 2 approval policies for your organization at the system or client level in the Global Approval Policies and the Approval Policies forms. An I-9 Approver role is available in both forms. You can use that role, or any other role, for I-9 Section 2 approvals. For more information about setting up approval policies at the system level, see the System Administration Guide or Approvals Guide. For more information about setting up approval policies at the client level, see the Human Resources User Guide or Approvals Guide.

Setting Up Form I-9 Approvers For Onboarding, you must set up an administrator as an I-9 Approver.

To define an administrator as an I-9 Approver: 1. Click Back Office. 1. From System|Change, select Users. 2. In User ID, enter the administrator ID. 3. In User Type: • For a service provider, in the Account Management Roles panel, select I-9 Approver. • For a worksite manager, in the Human Resource Roles panel, select I-9 Approver. 4. Click Save. For more information on editing user roles in PrismHR, see the System Administration Guide.

Approving Forms I-9 When an onboarding workflow contains the Form I-9, there must be a Form I-9 approval.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 9 Chapter 2 Configuring System Settings

For Onboarding, you must set up a user as an I-9 Approver. Employees are unable to submit their Form I-9 Section 1 without an I-9 Section 2 approver. The I-9 Section 2 approval is not created unless an approver exists. For more information, see the System Administration Guide.

Note: If E-Verification is enabled for an employee, it is flagged after Form I-9 Section 2 is completed.

The user set up with this role must approve the I-9 Forms for new hires to complete the onboarding process. For more information about processing approvals, see the Human Resources User Guide. After the new hire submits the I-9 Section 1, an I-9 Section 2 approval is created, and the approval displays in the approval queue of the Approvals Pending form in PrismHR. The approver can select one of the following options: • Deny the Form I-9 Section 1 • Complete and submit the Form I-9 Section 2 • Return the approval to the queue for another approver to complete For more information about pending approvals, see the Human Resources User Guide or Approvals Guide.

Working with the Manage Approvals Queue Important! The Manage Approvals Queue form has been retired. Instead, use the Manage Pending Approvals form (Refer to the PrismHR Human Resources Guide for more information.) When you select Manage Approvals Queue on the Operations|Utility Processing menu a message displays, “Managing pending approvals has been moved to the new Manage Pending Approvals form. You will be redirected.” Click OK to display the Manage Pending Approvals form for the active client.

Note: If you had access to the Manage Approvals Queue form but you do not have access to the Manage Pending Approvals form, when you access this form a message displays, “Managing pending approvals has been moved to the new Manage Pending Approvals form. Access to the Manage Pending Approvals form will need to be added to your user role.”

Using Substitution Variables Substitution variables are tags that you can use as placeholder text when building message template content. When generating the message, the system replaces the variable with data pulled from the system. Substitution variables are similar to mail merge fields in word processing programs. They give content a more personal impact and make it easier to customize and reuse content for multiple employees, clients, workflows, and enrollment periods. Substitution variables behave differently depending on where you use them: • Specifying Substitution Variables for Messages • Working with Substitution Variables for Onboarding • Working with Substitution Variables for Benefits Enrollment

Specifying Substitution Variables for Messages Substitution variables for messages behave differently based on the message type they are used for and only work in specific message types.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 14 Chapter 2 Configuring System Settings

For example, you might set up a form for a workflow that includes text using the substitution variable for the employee’s name: Welcome, <<EMPLOYEE.NAME>>! When the employee views the form, the substitution variable is replaced by the employee’s name and displays as: Welcome, Jane M. Smith! Users can include the following substitution variables in both notifications and custom forms. These variables are case-sensitive and you must type them exactly as shown in the Substitution Variable column.

Chapter 5 Setting Up Forms and Workflows A workflow is essentially a wizard—a script that presents employees with a series of forms to guide them through well-defined and highly customizable steps during onboarding and benefit enrollments. If you plan to include any media items in a workflow, such as documents or images, in forms or workflows, upload them to Document Management before you create the forms in the Form Library. In the Form Library, you can create custom versions of the forms or use the prebuilt versions provided with their default language and settings. Prebuilt forms display in bold. After you create the forms, you can use them as components to create workflows in the Workflow Library.

Managing Documents, Forms, and Workflows Use the following libraries to manage documents, forms, and workflows for onboarding.

Library Description Document Management Upload and maintain documents to use when creating forms (graphic files for logos, PDF files containing onboarding information, and so on). Form Library Configure forms to include in a workflow. PrismHR provides prebuilt forms that you can use as templates to create new forms. You can also build your own custom forms. Workflow Library Create workflows using forms from the Forms Library as components.

Managing Forms To create and maintain forms, use the Form Library. These forms are the components used to build workflows for Onboarding. PrismHR provides prebuilt forms that can be used with minimal customization and the ability to create custom forms for additional onboarding options.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 35 Chapter 5 Setting Up Forms and Workflows

To open the Form Library: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change, select Form Library. The Form Library displays.

Field Description Name The name of the form. ID The ID assigned to the form when the form was created on the Create New Custom Form form. Version The version number of the form. Form Type • Default: This indicates that the form is a prebuilt form. • Custom: This indicates that the form was created manually.

Workflow • Enrollment: This indicates that the form is used in Benefits Enrollment. Type • Onboarding: This indicates that the form is used in Onboarding.

Status • Active: This indicates that the form is available for use in a workflow. • Draft: This indicates that the form has been saved as a draft and can be viewed or edited. • Inactive: This indicates form is not available use.

Creation The date the form was created. Date Start Date The date the form was made available for use.
