Creating Forms from Prebuilt Forms To create customized copies of prebuilt forms, use the Form Library. You can edit the default text in the prebuilt form. The text varies depending on the form selected. The rest of the content is prebuilt for you.

To create a new form based on a prebuilt form: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From System|Change select Form Library. The Form Library opens. 3. In the row of the prebuilt form to use (medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and so on), select Duplicate. The Duplicate Form displays. 4. Enter a New ID and New Name for the form. 5. Click Duplicate. The Customize Prebuilt Form form opens. 6. On the General tab in the Form ID field, enter a unique ID for the form. Required. You can edit the Form Name, Description, and Form Symbol. On the Onboarding Tasks by Status Dashboard, form symbols are used to display a summary view of forms in the workflow. Form symbols allow characters A-Z and 0-9 only.

Note: Business rules and form sets are not available for prebuilt forms.

  2. Click Done and then click Save. The Submit Form dialog box opens and prompts you to specify when the change goes into effect.

    Option Description Immediately The system sets the form status to Active, and sets the current date as the Start Date. Since there can be only one active version of the form, the system changes the status of any prior active version to Inactive and sets the current date as its End Date. Future Date You are prompted to enter a Start Date. The system sets the form status to Inactive and changes it to Active on the specified start date. Save as Draft The system sets the form status to Draft. The system does not set a Start Date, version, or revision number for the form.

  3. Click Submit Form when the form is complete.

To modify the form layout: 1. Select the Layout tab. 2. From Field Type, drag field types to the layout on the right. Field types are customizable and vary depending on the type of form. Some field types, such as Textfield, Text Area, Checkbox, Select List, Radio Button, and E-signature, can be edited. Others are read-only. Editable field types allow employees to enter unique data.

Note: If a field type is configured for additional languages, the languages for which the field is available displays in the Languages column.

If PDF integration is used, the PDF Fields list displays. From here, the editable fields extracted from the PDF
can be selected for inclusion on the custom form. For more information, see PDF Integration.

Note: When PDF files are uploaded in an additional language, the file’s mappable fields are parsed and compared to the field map of the English PDF file. If there is a mismatch of fields and field IDs with the English field map, it is rejected by the system.

  1. Click Save. The Submit Form dialog box opens, prompting you to specify when the form should be made available.

    Option Description Immediately The system sets the form status to Active, and sets the current date as the Start Date. Since there can be only one active version of the form, the system changes the status of any prior active version to Inactive and sets the current date as its End Date. Future Date You are prompted to enter a Start Date. The system sets the form status to Inactive and changes it to Active on the specified start date. Save as Draft The system sets the form status to Draft. The system does not set a Start Date, version, or revision number for the form.

  2. Click Submit Form when the form is complete.

Setting Up Third-Party WOTC Form Integration Third-party Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) forms can be included in the onboarding process using custom forms. When creating a custom form, a hyperlink to the third-party WOTC form can be included, along with any additional information about the form and a field to confirm the employee has completed the form. Once information for the third-party WOTC form has been defined, the custom form can be added to a workflow, and employees can use the hyperlink on the custom form to access and complete the third-party WOTC form during the normal onboarding process.

Adding a Third-Party URL to a Custom Form 1. Create a custom form as normal and access the Layout tab on the Edit Custom Form. Refer to “Creating Custom Forms (Onboarding)” for more information. 2. From Field Type, drag the Third Party URL field type to the layout on the right. 3. Click on the Third Party URL field type to display the Field Details panel. 4. In the Field Label field, enter the text to display as a hyperlink on the form. For example, enter Click here to access the WOTC form. 5. In the Source URL field, enter the URL of the third-party WOTC form. When the employee clicks this hyperlink during onboarding, the employee’s prehire ID, the client ID, and the PEO ID are automatically appended to the URL, creating a unique URL for the employee. This unique URL allows the form provider to

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 44 Chapter 5 Setting Up Forms and Workflows

collect information about the employee using an API call and automatically enter that information in the
appropriate fields on the WOTC form, eliminating the need for the employee to manually enter their
information again.
  1. Click Done to close the Field Details panel.
  2. Optional: drag additional field types to the layout on the right as needed. For example, use the Paragraph field type to enter additional information about the form, or use the Checkbox field type to add a checkbox for the employee to confirm they have completed the form.
  3. Optional: to preview the form before saving, click Preview Form. If additional languages are enabled on your system, a form preview includes an additional language, such as Spanish.
  4. Click Save. The Submit Form dialog box opens, prompting you to specify when the change goes into effect. Refer to “Creating Custom Forms (Onboarding)” for more information.
  5. Click Submit Form when the form is complete.
  6. Add the form to a workflow as normal. Refer to “Creating a Workflow (Onboarding)” for more information.

Working with Substitution Variables Substitution variables are tags you can use as placeholder text when building content in custom forms and notifications in Onboarding. When generating the output, the system replaces the variable with data pulled from PrismHR. Substitution variables are similar to the mail merge fields used in word processing programs: they give content a more personal impact while also making it easier to customize and reuse content for multiple employees, clients, and workflows. For example, you might set up a form for a workflow that includes text using the substitution variable for the employee’s name: Welcome, <>! When the employee views the form, the substitution variable is replaced by the employee’s name and displays as: Welcome, Jane M. Smith! Users can include the following substitution variables in both notifications and custom forms. These variables are case-sensitive. You must type them exactly as shown.

Managing Versions and Revisions The Form Library and Workflow Library both maintain multiple versions and revisions for forms and workflows. The system sets revisions automatically when you submit a new form or workflow or modify an existing one. • When you create a new form or workflow, the system automatically sets the Version to 1.0. • If you change the form or workflow and select the option to have them go into effect immediately, the system adds a Revision number after the decimal point in the Version number (1.1, 1.2, and so on). The system also immediately sets the Status to Active, and sets the current date as the Start Date. Since there can be only one active version of the form, the system changes the Status of any prior active version to Inactive and sets the current date as its End Date. • If you change the form or workflow and select the option to have the changes go into effect at a future date, the system automatically sets the Version number to the next number in the sequence, and resets the revision number to zero (2.0, 3.0, and so on). The system sets the new version’s Status to Active on the Start Date, which you assign when you submit the form or workflow. Since there can be only one active version, the system changes the Status of any prior active version to Inactive and sets the current date as its End Date. You can view and compare different versions and revisions in both libraries by clicking the form or workflow ID in the table. The Versions form opens, displaying all versions and revisions that exist. • Click the ID if you want to modify a form or workflow version or revision. • To compare two versions or revisions of a form or workflow, select the two you want to compare and click Compare. The Comparison panel opens below the main table in the form (you must scroll down to view data) and displays settings for both.

Chapter 6 Setting Up Notifications The Notification Templates and Notification Recipients forms enable you to set up notifications you want to send and to specify recipients for notifications. For notifications to work, you must first set up Email Services. For more information, see the System Administration Guide. • You can set up content for notifications in the Notification Templates form. For more information, see Setting Up Notification Templates (Onboarding). • You can designate recipients for notifications in the Notification Recipients form. For more information, see Setting Up Notification Recipients (Onboarding). • Notifications are available in the Workflow Library where you can add them to workflows. For more information, see Creating a Workflow for Onboarding.

Managing Notifications To specify how often the system should send the notifications, to resend time-based notifications if needed, and to stop or start the notifications engine, use the Notification Control Panel. For more information, see Managing the Notification Control Panel (Onboarding).

Handling Bounced Notifications There are two possible circumstances that can result in notifications not reaching the recipient: • The email address is not entered correctly (for example, it is entered as @​example.com​ instead of j​ smith@example.com​). PrismHR logs this error but it is not accessible to the user. Users should contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team. • The email address is entered correctly, but is otherwise not deliverable (for example, the email address is no longer active). In this case, PrismHR simply sends the email. There is no error log, and in most cases, there is no way to know that it was not received. Many email servers are configured not to send notifications of undeliverable emails.

Tracking Notifications You can track notifications by setting up the Notification Recipients form to send copies of all notifications to an administrator in your organization. This also enables you to forward notifications.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 77 Chapter 6 Setting Up Notifications

Setting Up Notification Templates The Notification Templates form is used to create templates for the notifications that are sent to employees or groups during onboarding. Each template specifies the content that is included in the notification, such as the subject and message body, as well as the criteria for sending the notification and the communication method used to send the notification. When defining notification content, substitution variables can be used to replace generic information with specific information from PrismHR. Once the template has been created, the Notification Recipients form can be used to define the recipients who receive the notification. In addition, the notifications can be added to a workflow using the Workflow Library.

Note: Notification templates that have been attached to a workflow or a notification recipient record cannot be deleted.

Using the Notification Control Panel Use the OB Notify section in the Notification Control Panel to: • Start and stop the notification engine during onboarding • Determine the frequency at which the notifications engine sends notifications During onboarding, the system sends event and time-based notifications attached to the workflows to notification recipients. The system: • Sends time-based notifications daily, typically shortly after midnight. This applies only to incomplete forms in the onboarding workflow. • Sends event-based notifications when the event specified by the trigger condition occurs (for example, when the employee completes the workflow). The notification engine runs in the background and periodically checks to see whether there are notifications to send. If so, it sends event-based notifications when they turn up during the check.

Note: The options in the BE Notify section are only used in PrismHR Benefits Enrollment and do not affect Onboarding.

To check for and send available event-based notifications: 1. Click Back Office. 2. From Operations|Action select Notification Control Panel. The Notification Control Panel form opens. 3. In OB Notify Interval (mins), enter the number of minutes. You can enter values from 5 to 1440 minutes. Note: The state of the process, ENABLED or DISABLED, displays next to the OB Notify Interval (mins) field. OB Notify Date populates automatically with the date the system last sent time-based notifications. If you need to manually resend a notification (for example, if employees did not receive the notification, or if there is a change to the notification template), you can delete the displayed OB Notify Date, and click Save. The system resends time-based notifications for that day with the current date. When the notifications are resent, the current date displays. 4. To submit your settings and start the notifications engine, click Save.

Managing Notification Objects and Tasks You can specify sending Onboarding notifications based on the object specified in the Notification tab when setting up a workflow in the Workflow Library. For event based notifications an object can be a workflow, specific form, or the I-9 Section 2 form. The objects that display in the Object column differ depending on the notification Trigger Condition. For time based notifications, an object can be a task. A task is an action that an employee or administrator must completed by the employee (or an administrator) by a fixed due date. Notifications that have the time-based Trigger Type display tasks in the Object drop-down. The following tables lists all of the notification conditions and their associated objects or tasks you can select when attaching a notification to an onboarding workflow.

Trigger Type Trigger Condition Object or Task Options Available Event Based Workflow is launched Workflow (no additional objects or task list displays) Event Based Workflow is completed Workflow (no additional objects; no drop-down displays) Event Based Employee submits form • I-9 section 1 • Employee Information • Selected Forms • Submit

Event Based Approver confirms I-9 Section 2 (no additional approval policies or list displays)

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 83 Chapter 6 Setting Up Notifications

Trigger Type Trigger Condition Object or Task Options Available Event Based Approver rejects I-9 Section 2 (no additional approval policies or list displays) Time Based X Days before due date Tasks available: • I-9 section 1 • Employee Information • I-9 Section 2 • All Other Forms

Time Based X Days after due date Tasks available: • I-9 section 1 • Employee Information • I-9 Section 2 • All Other Forms

Onboarding includes the following tasks:

Task Due Date I-9 Section 1 Employee’s date of hire Employee Information Employee’s date of hire I-9 Section 2 Approval due 3 days after date of hire All Other Forms Onboarding end date

For example, if the task I-9 Section 1 is set up with the time based Trigger Condition X Days before due date, and the number Days are defined as 5, the notification is sent 5 days before the employee’s date of hire.

Note: The date of hire is defined as the later of Client Start Date and Employer Start Date. It is the day the new hire begins employment.

Conditional Notifications Conditional notifications are event-based notifications triggered by content in a form field or a business rule. This feature helps clients with custom forms ask questions of an employee, whose Yes response triggers a notification to previously specified recipients. For example, a custom form might ask if employees have received a COVID-19 vaccine. In the form library, fields need to be identified where these notifications apply. For instance, a new radio button is added with Yes or No options for response.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 84 Chapter 6 Setting Up Notifications

Additional attributes are needed to trigger a notification for a Form Field Response. Notification triggers are event-based, such as when a workflow is completed. When an employee submits a workflow, conditional notifications are triggered. A single notification template is allowed for each field type. The user is unable to choose a different notification template per response. There is one chosen template that is sent based on the responses selected. A user can choose multiple responses for sending the notification.

The conditional notifications workflow operates like this: 1. Notification logic is updated to account for the Send Notification configuration on the field type of a form. 2. When a trigger is enabled. employees submit a workflow and the system examines the notifications attached to a workflow to determine whether this form has field types that require notification. 3. If yes, the system then determines if an employee’s response is selected to send a notification. 4. If yes, the system sends the notification.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 110 Chapter 12 Cross Hiring Employees

Chapter 12 Cross Hiring Employees A cross hire employee works for multiple clients under the same service provider. If the system identifies a new hire employee as a cross hire and their employee information does not match the existing employee information, the system generates a conflict. Cross hire conflicts prevent the system from launching new hire onboarding workflows. The following outlines how the system identifies cross hire employees, checks for cross hire conflicts, and enables you to review or resolve those conflicts: 1. When entering a new hire, if the Social Security number (SSN) matches the SSN of an existing employee, the system identifies the employee as a cross hire. 2. After identifying the employee as a cross hire, the system checks for conflicts to determine if the new hire is the same person as the existing employee. However, system does not check for cross hire conflicts when a service provider enters a new hire on the New Hire form. For more information on these exceptions, see Service Providers and Worksite Managers. 3. If cross hire conflicts exist, they display on the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form. The following details how the system checks for cross hire conflicts.

Checking for Cross Hire Conflicts To identify cross hire conflicts, the system verifies that the new hire is the same person as the existing employee with three key fields - First Name, Last Name, and Date of Birth. If any of these values do not match, the onboarding workflow does not launch, the system creates a conflict, and an email sends to the service provider assigned to the client Human Resources and Payroll accounts (Client Details > Accounts tab). A message also displays in My Messages. Service providers must resolve the conflict on the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form. The system identifies cross hire conflicts when launching their onboarding workflow in the following scenarios: • Entering a new hire on the New Hire form. See Manually Entering a Cross Hire New Hire. • Importing a new hire with the Expanded Employee Import. See Importing Cross Hires with the Expanded Employee Import. • Importing a new hire with the API Import. See Importing Cross Hire Employees with the API Import. • Launching a new workflow for a new hire with the Launch New Workflow action on the Workflow Maintenance form. Launching a New Workflow for a Cross Hire New Hire. In some cases, when onboarding a new hire to more than one client at the same time, the system may not identify a cross hire until a workflow launches and the new hire is completing their onboarding forms. In this

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 111 Chapter 12 Cross Hiring Employees

scenario, the system performs a cross hire check on the Form I-9 Section 1 and the Employee Information form. See Employee Submits Forms in Onboarding Workflow.

Importing Cross Hires with the Expanded Employee Import The Expanded Employee Import in HRPyramid System Administration > Process > Conversion Processing > Expanded Employee Import) supports importing and converting cross hire employees set up for Onboarding into the backend system of PrismHR. First, you must import the employees (Expanded Employee Import > Import Employees).

Note: To import an employee as a cross hire, you must include the employee ID in column GQ (field 199). For more information, see Expanded Employee Import File Specifications on the Customer Resource Center.

The import process loads an external file and creates IMPORT.EMPLOYEE records you can import into the Employee Master file. During the import, the system checks for cross hire conflicts. If a conflict exists, a warning displays in the import report. You can fix it by correcting the data in the external file. After importing, you must convert the employees (Expanded Employee Import > Convert Employees). The conversion process moves valid employees from the IMPORT.EMPLOYEES file into the Employee Master file. If a conflict exists, the conflict displays on the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form, and their onboarding workflow does not launch. If a conflict does not exist, the system launches their onboarding workflow.

Importing Cross Hire Employees with the API Import The API Employee Import supports importing cross hire employees set up for Onboarding into the backend system of PrismHR. First, you must import the employees.

Note: To import an employee as a cross hire, you must include the employee ID.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 113 Chapter 12 Cross Hiring Employees

The import process checks the data and creates a Data Import Errors Report to identify any data issues. If a cross hire conflict exists, a warning displays in the import report. You can fix the conflict by correcting the data. After importing, you must commit the employees. The commit process updates the data in PrismHR. If a conflict exists, the conflict displays on the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form, and their onboarding workflow does not launch. If a conflict does not exist, the system launches their onboarding workflows.

Launching a New Workflow for a Cross Hire New Hire When you launch a new workflow on the Workflow Maintenance form, the system identifies whether the new hire is also a cross hire. If a cross hire conflict does not exist, the onboarding workflow launches. If there is a cross hire conflict, it displays on the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form, and the onboarding workflow does not launch.

Employee Submits Forms in Onboarding Workflow When an employee submits forms in their onboarding workflow, the system checks for cross hire conflicts at three points. When the employee: • Clicks Back or Next on the Form I-9 Section 1, Employee Information page. • Clicks Back or Next on the Employee Information form, Personal Information page. • Clicks Save and Continue on the Employee Information form, Emergency Contacts page. If a conflict exists, the system informs the employee they cannot proceed because either the First Name, Last Name, or Date of Birth does not match what is already in the system. The employee can resolve the conflict by entering the correct values. If the employee resolves the conflict, the system removes it from the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form and sends an email indicating that the conflict is resolved to the service provider. A message also displays in My Messages. If the employee cannot resolve the conflict, the service provider can correct it on the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form.

Reviewing Cross Hire Conflicts Note: On the User Roles form, you can only grant full access (Full) or deny access (Deny) to the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form. Currently, the Inquiry option functions the same as granting full access.

On the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form, you must review the conflict shown to decide whether the new hire is the same person as the existing employee. This may involve speaking with the manager who entered the new hire, the new hire, or the existing employee. To help you communicate with these people, the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form shows the person who entered the conflict, as well as contact information for the manager who entered the new hire, the new hire, and the existing employee. If the new hire is the same person as the existing employee, you can correct the mismatched fields so the system can automatically launch the workflow. If the data correction involves an active onboarding workflow, that workflow resets so the employee can resign all forms with the correct information. If the new hire is not the same person as the existing employee, you can delete the new hire.

To open the Review Cross Hire Conflicts form: 1. Click Back Office.

  1. From System|Action, select Review Cross Hire Conflicts. The Review Cross Hire Conflicts form opens.

Client Name The client’s name. Conflict Date The date the conflict was entered into the system. Data Entered By The person that entered the conflict in the system. For more information, see Fixing the Conflict. • Delete New Hire - If you determine that the new hire and the existing employee are not the same person, you can delete the new hire. For more information, see Deleting the New Hire.

Fixing the Conflict After identifying that the new hire is the same person, you can fix the conflict to make the existing employee and new hire records match.

To fix the conflict: 1. Click Fix Conflict. The Fix Conflicts dialog box displays. 2. In Update data for both records, correct the conflicts and click Update. 3. In the confirmation dialog box, click Yes, Update. The Review Cross Hire Conflicts form displays. Both records update to match correctly, and the conflict is removed from the list.

Deleting the Conflict After identifying that the new hires are not the same person, you can delete the new hire record.

To delete the new hire: 1. Click Delete New Hire. 2. In the confirmation dialog box, click Yes, Delete. The Review Cross Hire Conflicts form displays. The record deletes and the conflict is removed from the list.

Viewing Who Entered the Conflict To view the person that entered the conflict in the system, use the Conflict Entered By tab.

Viewing Contact Information To view contact information for the manager who entered the new hire, new hire, and existing employee in the system related to the conflict, use the Contact Information tab.

Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) To select a pay card account approval, use the Approvals Pending (Assigned to You) panel. The approval is used to assign the pay card account number.

  1. In Pay Card Account, enter the employee pay card account number. This is the account number on the pay card you are providing to the employee.
  2. To save the pay card account number, click Apply.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 125 Chapter 15 Working with Pay Card Direct Deposit Accounts

Note: If an employee removes the pay card account from their direct deposit during the approval process, an alert message displays informing the designated approvers that their approval is no longer necessary.

Chapter 16 Employee Process for Completing Form I-9 Section 1 To complete Section 1 of Form I-9: If necessary, the employee can click View Instructions to review instructions for completing Form I-9 directly on the USCIS website. 1. The employee logs in to Onboarding and selects I-9 in the navigation menu on the left. The Form I-9 Instructions Overview displays.

  1. After reviewing the information in each section, the employee clicks Next to proceed to the Preparer and Translator Certification.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 127 Chapter 16 Employee Process for Completing Form I-9 Section 1

 If the employee was assisted by a preparer or translator in completing the Form I-9, the employee selects
 Yes and an additional field displays to allow the employee to upload the Form I-9 provided by their
 preparer or translator. In addition, the employee can select the I have more than one preparer or
 translator option to indicate multiple preparers or translators were used and upload an I-9 Supplement
 form provided by their second preparer or translator.
 Otherwise, the employee selects No.

  1. Once a selection is made and documents have been uploaded as applicable, the employee clicks Next. The Attestation of Citizenship or Immigration Status displays.

    The employee selects the appropriate option for their citizenship or immigration status. Depending on the option selected, additional fields display to allow the employee to enter additional information such as their Alien Registration Number/USCIS Number.

  2. After making entries as necessary, the employee clicks Next. The Supporting Documents screen displays.

    Note: This screen only displays if the option for uploading supporting documents is enabled for the client. If uploading supporting documents is disabled, the Employee Information screen displays instead. Proceed to step 5.

    For more information about enabling this setting at the client level, refer to “Setting Control Parameters” in the PrismHR in-product help or in the Client Administration User Guide. For more information about

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 128 Chapter 16 Employee Process for Completing Form I-9 Section 1

  enabling this setting at the system level, refer to"Maintaining Global Onboarding Options" in the PrismHR
  in-product help or in the Onboarding User Guide.

 If the employee chooses to upload supporting documents at a later time, the employee selects No.
 If the employee chooses to upload supporting documents now, the employee selects Yes. Additional fields
 display to allow the employee to select the type of supporting documents to upload and then upload the
 documents.
  1. Once a selection is made and documents have been uploaded as applicable, the employee clicks Next. The Employee Information screen displays.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 129 Chapter 16 Employee Process for Completing Form I-9 Section 1

 The employee enters information in each field as appropriate. Once entries are made, the employee
 selects the checkbox in the Signature of Employee section to indicate that they consent to electronically
 signing the form. The employee's name and the current date are automatically entered in this section
 when the checkbox is selected. The employee's address is validated automatically to ensure accuracy.
  1. After selecting the checkbox in the Signature of Employee section, the employee clicks Next. The Review screen displays.

Onboarding User Guide © 2026 PrismHR 130 Chapter 16 Employee Process for Completing Form I-9 Section 1

 The employee can review a PDF copy of their completed Form I-9 and download a copy for their own
 records if necessary. If information on the form needs to be corrected or otherwise modified, the
 employee clicks Back to navigate back to the appropriate screen and correct the information.
  1. After reviewing the information on the form, the employee clicks Submit. A message window displays to confirm the form should be submitted. The employee clicks Yes, and the completed section of the Form I-9 is submitted for approval. The onboarding process then continues to the next form in the workflow.
